G10.definition: Ἀβιούδ Abioúd, ab-ee-ood'; of Hebrew origin (H31); Abihud, an Israelite:—Abiud.

G100.definition:
ἁδρότης hadrótēs, had-rot'-ace; from ἁδρός hadrós (stout); plumpness, i.e. (figuratively)
 liberality:—abundance.

G1000.definition: βολή bolḗ, bol-ay'; from G906; a throw (as a measure of distance):—cast.

G1001.definition: βολίζω bolízō, bol-id'-zo; from G1002; to heave the lead:—sound.

G1003.definition: †Βοόζ Boóz, bo-oz'; of Hebrew origin (H1162); Booz, (i.e. Boaz), an Israelite:—Booz.

G1004.definition: βόρβορος bórboros, bor'-bor-os; of uncertain derivation; mud:—mire.

G1005.definition: βοῤῥᾶς borrhâs, bor-hras'; of uncertain derivation; the north (properly, wind):—north.

G1006.definition:
βόσκω bóskō, bos'-ko; a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare G977, G1016); to pasture; by
 extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze:—feed, keep.

G1008.definition: βοτάνη botánē, bot-an'-ay; from G1006; herbage (as if for grazing):—herb.

G1009.definition:
βότρυς bótrys, bot'-rooce; of uncertain derivation; a bunch (of grapes):—(vine) cluster (of the
 vine).

G101.definition: ἀδυνατέω adynatéō, ad-oo-nat-eh'-o; from G102; to be unable, i.e. (passively) impossible:—be impossible.

G1010.definition:
βουλευτής bouleutḗs, bool-yoo-tace'; from G1011; an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the
 Jewish Sanhedrin:—counsellor.

G1011.definition:
†βουλεύω bouleúō, bool-yoo'-o; from G1012; to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by
 implication) resolve:—consult, take counsel, determine, be minded,
 purpose.

G1012.definition:
βουλή boulḗ, boo-lay'; from G1014; volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication)
 purpose:—+ advise, counsel, will.

G1013.definition: βούλημα boúlēma, boo'-lay-mah; from G1014; a resolve:—purpose, will.

G1014.definition:
βούλομαι boúlomai, boo'-lom-ahee; middle voice of a primary verb; to "will," i.e. (reflexively) be
 willing:—be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing). 
 Compare G2309.

G1015.definition: βουνός bounós, boo-nos'; probably of foreign origin; a hillock:—hill.

G1016.definition:
βοῦς boûs, booce; probably from the base of G1006; an ox (as grazing), i.e. an animal of
 that species ("beef"):—ox.

G1017.definition:
βραβεῖον brabeîon, brab-i'-on; from βραβεύς brabeús (an umpire of uncertain derivation); an award (of
 arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games:—prize.

G1018.definition:
βραβεύω brabeúō, brab-yoo'-o; from the same as G1017; to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern
 (figuratively, prevail):—rule.

G1019.definition: βραδύνω bradýnō, brad-oo'-no; from G1021; to delay:—be slack, tarry.

G102.definition:
ἀδύνατος adýnatos, ad-oo'-nat-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1415; unable, i.e. weak (literally
 or figuratively); passively, impossible:—could not do, impossible,
 impotent, not possible, weak.

G1020.definition: βραδυπλοέω bradyploéō, brad-oo-plo-eh'-o; from G1021 and a prolonged form of G4126; to sail slowly:—sail slowly.

G1021.definition: βραδύς bradýs, brad-ooce'; of uncertain affinity; slow; figuratively, dull:—slow.

G1022.definition: βραδύτης bradýtēs, brad-oo'-tace; from G1021; tardiness:—slackness.

G1023.definition:
βραχίων brachíōn, brakh-ee'-own; properly, comparative of G1024, but apparently in the sense of
 βράσσω brássō (to wield); the arm, i.e. (figuratively)
 strength:—arm.

G1024.definition:
βραχύς brachýs, brakh-ooce'; of uncertain affinity; short (of time, place, quantity, or
 number):—few words, little (space, while).

G1025.definition:
βρέφος bréphos, bref'-os; of uncertain affinity; an infant (properly, unborn) literally or
 figuratively:—babe, (young) child, infant.

G1026.definition:
βρέχω bréchō, brekh'-o; a primary verb; to moisten (especially by a shower):—(send) rain,
 wash.

G1027.definition: βροντή brontḗ, bron-tay'; akin to βρέμω brémō (to roar); thunder:—thunder(-ing).

G1028.definition: βροχή brochḗ, brokh-ay'; from G1026; rain:—rain.

G1029.definition: βρόχος bróchos, brokh'-os; of uncertain derivation; a noose:—snare.

G103.definition: ᾄδω áidō, ad'-o; a primary verb; to sing:—sing.

G1030.definition: βρυγμός brygmós, broog-mos'; from G1031; a grating (of the teeth):—gnashing.

G1031.definition: βρύχω brýchō, broo'-kho; a primary verb; to grate the teeth (in pain or rage):—gnash.

G1032.definition:
βρύω brýō, broo'-o; a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush:—send
 forth.

G1033.definition:
βρῶμα brōma, bro'-mah; from the base of G977; food (literally or figuratively), especially
 (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law:—meat,
 victuals.

G1034.definition: βρώσιμος brṓsimos, bro'-sim-os; from G1035; eatable:—meat.

G1036.definition: βυθίζω bythízō, boo-thid'-zo; from G1037; to sink; by implication, to drown:—begin to sink, drown.

G1037.definition: βυθός bythós, boo-thos'; a variation of G899; depth, i.e. (by implication) the sea:—deep.

G1038.definition: βυρσεύς byrseús, boorce-yooce'; from βύρσα býrsa (a hide); a tanner:—tanner.

G1039.definition: βύσσινος býssinos, boos'-see-nos; from G1040; made of linen (neuter a linen cloth):—fine linen.

G104.definition:
ἀεί aeí, ah-eye'; from an obsolete primary noun (apparently meaning continued duration); 
 "ever," by qualification regularly; by implication, earnestly:—always, ever.

G1040.definition: βύσσος býssos, boos'-sos; of Hebrew origin (H948); white linen:—fine linen.

G1041.definition:
βωμός bōmós, bo'-mos; from the base of G939; properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an
 altar:—altar.

G1042.definition:
†γαββαθά gabbathá, gab-bath-ah'; of Chaldee origin (compare H1355); the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular
 term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem:—Gabbatha.

G1043.definition: Γαβριήλ Gabriḗl, gab-ree-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H1403); Gabriel, an archangel:—Gabriel.

G1044.definition: γάγγραινα gángraina, gang'-grahee-nah; from γραίνω graínō (to gnaw); an ulcer ("gangrene"):—canker.

G1045.definition: Γάδ Gád, gad; of Hebrew origin (H1410); Gad, a tribe of Israelites:—Gad.

G1046.definition:
†Γαδαρηνός Gadarēnós, gad-ar-ay-nos'; from Γαδαρά Gadará (a town east of the Jordan); a Gadarene or inhabitant of
 Gadara:—Gadarene.

G1047.definition: γάζα gáza, gad'-zah; of foreign origin; a treasure:—treasure.

G1048.definition:
Γάζα Gáza, gad'-zah; of Hebrew origin (H5804); Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in
 Palestine:—Gaza.

G1049.definition:
γαζοφυλάκιον gazophylákion, gad-zof-oo-lak'-ee-on; from G1047 and G5438; a treasure-house, i.e. a court in the temple for
 the collection-boxes:—treasury.

G105.definition: ἀετός aetós, ah-et-os'; from the same as; an eagle (from its wind-like flight):—eagle.

G1050.definition: Γάϊος Gáïos, gah'-ee-os; of Latin origin; Gaius (i.e. Caius), a Christian:—Gaius.

G1051.definition: γάλα gála, gal'-ah; of uncertain affinity; milk (figuratively):—milk.

G1052.definition: Γαλάτης Galátēs, gal-at'-ace; from G1053; a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia:—Galatian.

G1053.definition: Γαλατία Galatía, gal-at-ee'-ah; of foreign origin; Galatia, a region of Asia:—Galatia.

G1054.definition: Γαλατικός Galatikós, gal-at-ee-kos'; from G1053; Galatic or relating to Galatia:—of Galatia.

G1055.definition: γαλήνη galḗnē, gal-ay'-nay; of uncertain derivation; tranquillity:—calm.

G1056.definition:
Γαλιλαία Galilaía, gal-il-ah'-yah; of Hebrew origin (H1551); Galilæa (i.e. the heathen circle), a region
 of Palestine:—Galilee.

G1057.definition: Γαλιλαῖος Galilaîos, gal-ee-lah'-yos; from G1056; Galilean or belonging to Galilea:—Galilean, of Galilee.

G1058.definition: Γαλλίων Gallíōn, gal-lee'-own; of Latin origin; Gallion (i.e. Gallio), a Roman officer:—Gallio.

G1059.definition:
Γαμαλιήλ Gamaliḗl, gam-al-ee-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H1583); Gamaliel (i.e. Gamliel), an
 Israelite:—Gamaliel.

G106.definition:
ἄζυμος ázymos, ad'-zoo-mos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2219; unleavened, i.e.
 (figuratively) uncorrupted; (in the neutral plural) specially (by
 implication) the Passover week:—unleavened (bread).

G1060.definition: γαμέω gaméō, gam-eh'-o; from G1062; to wed (of either sex):—marry (a wife).

G1061.definition: †γαμίσκω gamískō, gam-is'-ko; from G1062; to espouse (a daughter to a husband):—give in marriage.

G1062.definition: γάμος gámos, gam'-os; of uncertain affinity; nuptials:—marriage, wedding.

G1063.definition:
γάρ gár, gar; a primary particle; properly, assigning a reason (used in argument,
 explanation or intensification; often with other particles):—and, as,
 because (that), but, even, for, indeed, no doubt, seeing, then,
 therefore, verily, what, why, yet.

G1064.definition:
γαστήρ gastḗr, gas-tare'; of uncertain derivation; the stomach; by analogy, the matrix;
 figuratively, a gourmand:—belly, + with child, womb.

G1065.definition:
γέ gé, gheh; a primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other
 particles prefixed):—and besides, doubtless, at least, yet.

G1066.definition:
Γεδεών Gedeṓn, ghed-eh-own'; of Hebrew origin (H1439); Gedeon (i.e. Gid(e)on), an Israelite:—Gedeon
 (in the King James Version).

G1069.definition:
γείτων geítōn, ghi'-tone; from G1093; a neighbour (as adjoining one's ground); by implication, a
 friend:—neighbour.

G107.definition: Ἀζώρ Azṓr, ad-zore'; of Hebrew origin (compare H5809); Azor, an Israelite:—Azorigin

G1070.definition:
γελάω geláō, ghel-ah'-o; of uncertain affinity; to laugh (as a sign of joy or
 satisfaction):—laugh.

G1071.definition: γέλως gélōs, ghel'-os; from G1070; laughter (as a mark of gratification):—laughter.

G1072.definition: γεμίζω gemízō, ghem-id'-zo; transitive from G1073; to fill entirely:—fill (be) full.

G1073.definition: γέμω gémō, ghem'-o; a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. be full:—be full.

G1074.definition:
γενεά geneá, ghen-eh-ah'; from (a presumed derivative of) G1085; a generation; by implication, an
 age (the period or the persons):—age, generation, nation, time.

G1075.definition:
γενεαλογέω genealogéō, ghen-eh-al-og-eh'-o; from G1074 and G3056; to reckon by generations, i.e. trace in
 genealogy:—count by descent.

G1076.definition:
γενεαλογία genealogía, ghen-eh-al-og-ee'-ah; from the same as G1075; tracing by generations, i.e.
 "genealogy":—genealogy.

G1077.definition: γενέσια genésia, ghen-es'-ee-ah; neuter plural of a derivative of G1078; birthday ceremonies:—birthday.

G1078.definition:
γένεσις génesis, ghen'-es-is; from the same as G1074; nativity; figuratively, nature:—generation,
 nature(-ral).

G1079.definition: γενετή genetḗ, ghen-et-ay; feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G1074; birth:—birth.

G108.definition:
Ἄζωτος Ázōtos, ad'-zo-tos; of Hebrew origin (H795); Azotus (i.e. Ashdod), a place in
 Palestine:—Azotus.

G1080.definition:
γεννάω gennáō, ghen-nah'-o; from a variation of G1085; to procreate (properly, of the father, but
 by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate:—bear,
 beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make,
 spring.

G1081.definition:
†γέννημα génnēma, ghen'-nay-mah; from G1080; offspring; by analogy, produce (literally or
 figuratively):—fruit, generation.

G1082.definition:
Γεννησαρέτ Gennēsarét, ghen-nay-sar-et'; of Hebrew origin (compare H3672); Gennesaret (i.e. Kinnereth), a lake
 and plain in Palestine:—Gennesaret.

G1084.definition: γεννητός gennētós, ghen-nay-tos'; from G1080; born:—they that are born.

G1085.definition:
γένος génos, ghen'-os; from G1096; "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative,
 individual or collective):—born, country(-man), diversity,
 generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock.

G1086.definition:
Γεργεσηνός Gergesēnós, gher-ghes-ay-nos'; of Hebrew origin (H1622); a Gergesene (i.e. Girgashite) or one of the
 aborigines of Palestine:—Gergesene.

G1087.definition:
γερουσία gerousía, gher-oo-see'-ah; from G1088; the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish
 Sanhedrin:—senate.

G1088.definition: γέρων gérōn, gher'-own; of uncertain affinity (compare G1094); aged:—old.

G1089.definition:
γεύομαι geúomai, ghyoo'-om-ahee; a primary verb; to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to
 experience (good or ill):—eat, taste.

G109.definition:
ἀήρ aḗr, ah-ayr'; from ἄημι áēmi (to breathe unconsciously, i.e. respire; by analogy, to
 blow); "air" (as naturally circumambient):—air. Compare G5594.

G1090.definition: γεωργέω geōrgéō, gheh-or-gheh'-o; from G1092; to till (the soil):—dress.

G1091.definition:
γεώργιον geṓrgion, gheh-ore'-ghee-on; neuter of a (presumed) derivative of G1092; cultivable, i.e. a
 farm:—husbandry.

G1092.definition:
γεωργός geōrgós, gheh-ore-gos'; from G1093 and the base of G2041; a land-worker, i.e.
 farmer:—husbandman.

G1093.definition:
γῆ gē, ghay; contracted from a primary word; soil; by extension a region, or the
 solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants
 in each application):—country, earth(-ly), ground, land, world.

G1094.definition: γῆρας gēras, ghay'-ras; akin to G1088; senility:—old age.

G1095.definition: γηράσκω gēráskō, ghay-ras'-ko; from G1094; to be senescent:—be (wax) old.

G1096.definition:
γίνομαι gínomai, ghin'-om-ahee; a prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb; to cause to be
 ("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used
 with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.):—arise, be
 assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be)
 come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be
 finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen,
 have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass,
 be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, × soon as it
 was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought.

G1097.definition:
γινώσκω ginṓskō, ghin-oce'-ko; a prolonged form of a primary verb; to "know" (absolutely) in a great
 variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with
 others not thus clearly expressed):—allow, be aware (of), feel,
 (have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure,
 understand.

G1098.definition:
γλεῦκος gleûkos, glyoo'-kos; akin to G1099; sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used
 of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented
 wine:—new wine.

G1099.definition:
γλυκύς glykýs, gloo-koos'; of uncertain affinity; sweet (i.e. not bitter nor salt):—sweet,
 fresh.

G11.definition:
Ἀβραάμ Abraám, ab-rah-am'; of Hebrew origin (H85); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch:—Abraham. (In
 Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.)

G110.definition:
ἀθανασία athanasía, ath-an-as-ee'-ah; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and G2288; 
 deathlessness:—immortality.

G1100.definition:
γλῶσσα glōssa, gloce-sah'; of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication, a language
 (specially, one naturally unacquired):—tongue.

G1101.definition:
γλωσσόκομον glōssókomon, gloce-sok'-om-on; from G1100 and the base of G2889; properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces
 of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially)
 purse:—bag.

G1102.definition:
γναφεύς gnapheús, gnaf-yuce'; by variation for a derivative from κνάπτω knáptō (to tease cloth); a
 cloth-dresser:—fuller.

G1103.definition:
γνήσιος gnḗsios, gnay'-see-os; from the same as G1077; legitimate (of birth), i.e. genuine:—own,
 sincerity, true.

G1104.definition: γνησίως gnēsíōs, gnay-see'-ose; adverb from G1103; genuinely, i.e. really:—naturally.

G1105.definition: γνόφος gnóphos, gnof'-os; akin to G3509; gloom (as of a storm):—blackness.

G1106.definition:
γνώμη gnṓmē, gno'-may; from G1097; cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively)
 resolve (counsel, consent, etc.):—advice, + agree, judgment, mind,
 purpose, will.

G1107.definition:
γνωρίζω gnōrízō, gno-rid'-zo; from a derivative of G1097; to make known; subjectively, to
 know:—certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit,
 wot.

G1108.definition:
γνῶσις gnōsis, gno'-sis; from G1097; knowing (the act), i.e. (by implication)
 knowledge:—knowledge, science.

G1109.definition: γνώστης gnṓstēs, gnoce'-tace; from G1097; a knower:—expert.

G1110.definition: γνωστός gnōstós, gnoce-tos'; from G1097; well-known:—acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable.

G1111.definition: γογγύζω gongýzō, gong-good'-zo; of uncertain derivation; to grumble:—murmur.

G1112.definition: γογγυσμός gongysmós, gong-goos-mos'; from G1111; a grumbling:—grudging, murmuring.

G1113.definition: γογγυστής gongystḗs, gong-goos-tace'; from G1111; a grumbler:—murmurer.

G1114.definition:
γόης góēs, go'-ace; from γοάω goáō (to wail); properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e.
 (by implication) an imposter:—seducer.

G1115.definition:
Γολγοθᾶ Golgothâ, gol-goth-ah'; of Chaldee origin (compare H1538); the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near
 Jerusalem:—Golgotha.

G1116.definition:
Γόμοῤῥα Gómorrha, gom'-or-hrhah; of Hebrew origin (H6017); Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead
 Sea:—Gomorrha.

G1117.definition:
γόμος gómos, gom'-os; from G1073; a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by
 extension) wares:—burden, merchandise.

G1118.definition: γονεύς goneús, gon-yooce'; from the base of G1096; a parent:—parent.

G1119.definition: γόνυ góny, gon-oo'; of uncertain affinity; the "knee":—knee(X -l).

G112.definition: ἄθεος átheos, ath'-eh-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2316; godless:—without God.

G1120.definition:
γονυπετέω gonypetéō, gon-oo-pet-eh'-o; from a compound of G1119 and the alternate of G4098; to fall on the
 knee:—bow the knee, kneel down.

G1121.definition:
γράμμα grámma, gram'-mah; from G1125; a writing, i.e. a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural
 learning:—bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.

G1122.definition:
γραμματεύς grammateús, gram-mat-yooce'; from G1121. a writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or
 secretary:—scribe, town-clerk.

G1123.definition: γραπτός graptós, grap-tos'; from G1125; inscribed (figuratively):—written.

G1124.definition:
γραφή graphḗ, graf-ay'; from G1125; a document, i.e. holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in
 it):—scripture.

G1125.definition:
†γράφω gráphō, graf'-o; a primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to
 describe:—describe, write(-ing, -ten).

G1126.definition:
γραώδης graṓdēs, grah-o'-dace; from γραύς graús (an old woman) and G1491; crone-like, i.e. silly:—old
 wives'.

G1127.definition:
γρηγορεύω grēgoreúō, gray-gor-yoo'-o; from G1453; to keep awake, i.e. watch (literally or figuratively):—be
 vigilant, wake, (be) watch(-ful).

G1128.definition:
γυμνάζω gymnázō, goom-nad'-zo; from G1131; to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train
 (figuratively):—exercise.

G1129.definition: γυμνασία gymnasía, goom-nas-ee'-ah; from G1128; training, i.e. (figuratively) asceticism:—exercise.

G113.definition:
ἄθεσμος áthesmos, ath'-es-mos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5087 (in the sense
 of enacting); lawless, i.e. (by implication) criminal:—wicked.

G1130.definition:
γυμνητεύω gymnēteúō, goom-nayt-yoo'-o; from a derivative of G1131; to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly
 clad:—be naked.

G1131.definition:
γυμνός gymnós, goom-nos'; of uncertain affinity; nude (absolute or relative, literal or
 figurative):—naked.

G1132.definition: γυμνότης gymnótēs, goom-not'-ace; from G1131; nudity (absolute or comparative):—nakedness.

G1133.definition: γυναικάριον gynaikárion, goo-nahee-kar'-ee-on; a diminutive from G1135; a little (i.e. foolish) woman:—silly woman.

G1134.definition: γυναικεῖος gynaikeîos, goo-nahee-ki'-os; from G1135; feminine:—wife.

G1135.definition:
γυνή gynḗ, goo-nay'; probably from the base of G1096; a woman; specially, a wife:—wife,
 woman.

G1136.definition:
Γώγ Gṓg, gogue; of Hebrew origin (H1463); Gog, a symbolic name for some future
 Antichrist:—Gog.

G1137.definition: γωνία gōnía, go-nee'-ah; probably akin to G1119; an angle:—corner, quarter.

G1138.definition:
†Δαβίδ Dabíd, dab-eed'; of Hebrew origin (H1732); Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite
 king:—David.

G1139.definition:
δαιμονίζομαι daimonízomai, dahee-mon-id'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G1142; to be exercised by a dæmon:—have a (be vexed
 with, be possessed with) devil(-s).

G114.definition:
ἀθετέω athetéō, ath-et-eh'-o; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of
 G5087; to set aside, i.e. (by implication) to disesteem, neutralize or
 violate:—cast off, despise, disannul, frustrate, bring to nought,
 reject.

G1140.definition:
δαιμόνιον daimónion, dahee-mon'-ee-on; neuter of a derivative of G1142; a dæmonic being; by extension a
 deity:—devil, god.

G1141.definition: δαιμονιώδης daimoniṓdēs, dahee-mon-ee-o'-dace; from G1140 and G1142; dæmon-like:—devilish.

G1142.definition:
δαίμων daímōn, dah'-ee-mown; from δαίω daíō (to distribute fortunes); a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of
 a bad nature):—devil.

G1143.definition:
δάκνω dáknō, dak'-no; a prolonged form of a primary root; to bite, i.e. (figuratively)
 thwart:—bite.

G1144.definition: δάκρυ dákry, dak'-roo; of uncertain affinity; a tear:—tear.

G1145.definition: δακρύω dakrýō, dak-roo'-o; from G1144; to shed tears:—weep. Compare G2799.

G1146.definition: δακτύλιος daktýlios, dak-too'-lee-os; from G1147; a finger-ring:—ring.

G1147.definition: δάκτυλος dáktylos, dak'-too-los; probably from G1176; a finger:—finger.

G1148.definition:
Δαλμανουθά Dalmanouthá, dal-man-oo-thah'; probably of Chaldee origin; Dalmanutha, a place in
 Palestine:—Dalmanutha.

G1149.definition:
Δαλματία Dalmatía, dal-mat-ee'-ah; probably of foreign derivation; Dalmatia, a region of
 Europe:—Dalmatia.

G115.definition:
ἀθέτησις athétēsis, ath-et'-ay-sis; from G114; cancellation (literally or figuratively):—disannulling, put
 away.

G1150.definition:
δαμάζω damázō, dam-ad'-zo; a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to
 tame:—tame.

G1151.definition: δάμαλις dámalis, dam'-al-is; probably from the base of G1150; a heifer (as tame):—heifer.

G1152.definition:
Δάμαρις Dámaris, dam'-ar-is; probably from the base of G1150; perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian
 woman:—Damaris.

G1153.definition: Δαμασκηνός Damaskēnós, dam-as-kay-nos'; from G1154; a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus:—Damascene.

G1154.definition: Δαμασκός Damaskós, dam-as-kos'; of Hebrew origin (H1834); Damascus, a city of Syria:—Damascus.

G1155.definition: †δανείζω daneízō, dan-ide'-zo; from G1156; to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow:—borrow, lend.

G1156.definition: δάνειον dáneion, dan'-i-on; from δάνος dános (a gift); probably akin to the base of G1325; a loan:—debt.

G1157.definition: †δανειστής daneistḗs, dan-ice-tace'; from G1155; a lender:—creditor.

G1158.definition: Δανιήλ Daniḗl, dan-ee-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H1840); Daniel, an Israelite:—Daniel.

G1159.definition:
δαπανάω dapanáō, dap-an-ah'-o; from G1160; to expend, i.e. (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a
 bad one) to waste:—be at charges, consume, spend.

G116.definition:
Ἀθῆναι Athēnai, ath-ay-nahee; plural of Ἀθήνη Athḗnē (the goddess of wisdom, who was reputed to have
 founded the city); Athenæ, the capitol of Greece:—Athens.

G1160.definition: δαπάνη dapánē, dap-an'-ay; from δάπτω dáptō (to devour); expense (as consuming):—cost.

G1161.definition:
δέ dé, deh; a primary particle (adversative or continuative); but, and,
 etc.:—also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English).

G1162.definition: δέησις déēsis, deh'-ay-sis; from G1189; a petition:—prayer, request, supplication.

G1163.definition:
†δεῖ deî, die; 3rd person singular active present of G1210; also deon deh-on'; neuter
 active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was,
 etc.) necessary (as binding):—behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be)
 need(-ful), ought, should.

G1164.definition: δεῖγμα deîgma, digh'-mah; from the base of G1166; a specimen (as shown):—example.

G1165.definition: δειγματίζω deigmatízō, digh-mat-id'-zo; from G1164; to exhibit:—make a shew.

G1166.definition:
†δεικνύω deiknýō, dike-noo'-o; a prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to show
 (literally or figuratively):—shew.

G1167.definition: δειλία deilía, di-lee'-ah; from G1169; timidity:—fear.

G1168.definition: δειλιάω deiliáō, di-lee-ah'-o; from G1167; to be timid:—be afraid.

G1169.definition: δειλός deilós, di-los'; from δεός deós (dread); timid, i.e. (by implication) faithless:—fearful.

G117.definition: Ἀθηναῖος Athēnaîos, ath-ay-nah'-yos; from G116; an Athenæan or inhabitant of Athenæ:—Athenian.

G1170.definition:
δεῖνα deîna, di'-nah; probably from the same as G1171 (through the idea of forgetting the
 name as fearful, i.e. strange); so and so (when the person is not
 specified):—such a man.

G1171.definition:
δεινῶς deinōs, di-noce'; adverb from a derivative of the same as G1169; terribly, i.e.
 excessively:—grievously, vehemently.

G1172.definition:
δειπνέω deipnéō, dipe-neh'-o; from G1173; to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal:—sup (X
 -er).

G1173.definition:
δεῖπνον deîpnon, dipe'-non; from the same as G1160; dinner, i.e. the chief meal (usually in the
 evening):—feast, supper.

G1174.definition:
†δεισιδαιμονέστερος deisidaimonésteros, dice-ee-dahee-mon-es'-ter-os; the compound of a derivative of the base of G1169 and G1142; more
 religious than others:—too superstitious.

G1175.definition: δεισιδαιμονία deisidaimonía, dice-ee-dahee-mon-ee'-ah; from the same as G1174; religion:—superstition.

G1176.definition: δέκα déka, dek'-ah; a primary number; ten:—(eight-)een, ten.

G1177.definition: δεκαδύο dekadýo, dek-ad-oo'-o; from G1176 and G1417; two and ten, i.e. twelve:—twelve.

G1178.definition: δεκαπέντε dekapénte, dek-ap-en'-teh; from G1176 and G4002; ten and five, i.e. fifteen:—fifteen.

G1179.definition:
Δεκάπολις Dekápolis, dek-ap'-ol-is; from G1176 and G4172; the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in
 Syria:—Decapolis.

G118.definition:
ἀθλέω athléō, ath-leh'-o; from ἄθλος áthlos (a contest in the public lists); to contend in the
 competitive games:—strive.

G1180.definition: δεκατέσσαρες dekatéssares, dek-at-es'-sar-es; from G1176 and G5064; ten and four, i.e. fourteen:—fourteen.

G1182.definition: δέκατος dékatos, dek'-at-os; ordinal from G1176; tenth:—tenth.

G1183.definition:
δεκατόω dekatóō, dek-at-o'-o; from G1181; to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth:—pay (receive)
 tithes.

G1184.definition: δεκτός dektós, dek-tos'; from G1209; approved; (figuratively) propitious:—accepted(-table).

G1185.definition:
δελεάζω deleázō, del-eh-ad'-zo; from the base of G1388; to entrap, i.e. (figuratively) delude:—allure,
 beguile, entice.

G1186.definition: δένδρον déndron, den'-dron; probably from δρύς drýs (an oak); a tree:—tree.

G1187.definition:
δεξιολάβος dexiolábos, dex-ee-ol-ab'-os; from G1188 and G2983; a guardsman (as if taking the right) or
 light-armed soldier:—spearman.

G1188.definition:
δεξιός dexiós, dex-ee-os'; from G1209; the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually
 takes):—right (hand, side).

G1189.definition:
δέομαι déomai, deh'-om-ahee; middle voice of G1210; to beg (as binding oneself), i.e.
 petition:—beseech, pray (to), make request. Compare G4441.

G119.definition: ἄθλησις áthlēsis, ath'-lay-sis; from G118; a struggle (figuratively):—fight.

G1190.definition: Δερβαῖος Derbaîos, der-bah'-ee-os; from G1191; a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe:—of Derbe.

G1191.definition: Δέρβη Dérbē, der-bay'; of foreign origin; Derbe, a place in Asia Minor:—Derbe.

G1192.definition: δέρμα dérma, der'-mah; from G1194; a hide:—skin.

G1193.definition: δερμάτινος dermátinos, der-mat'-ee-nos; from G1192; made of hide:—leathern, of a skin.

G1194.definition:
δέρω dérō, der'-o; a primary verb; properly, to flay, i.e. (by implication) to scourge,
 or (by analogy) to thrash:—beat, smite.

G1195.definition:
δεσμεύω desmeúō, des-myoo'-o; from a (presumed) derivative of G1196; to be a binder (captor), i.e. to
 enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load):—bind.

G1197.definition: δέσμη désmē, des-may'; from G1196; a bundle:—bundle.

G1198.definition: δέσμιος désmios, des'-mee-os; from G1199; a captive (as bound):—in bonds, prisoner.

G1199.definition:
δεσμόν desmón, des-mon'; neuter and masculine respectively from G1210; a band, i.e. ligament (of
 the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively, an impediment or
 disability:—band, bond, chain, string.

G12.definition:
ἄβυσσος ábyssos, ab'-us-sos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a variation of G1037; depthless,
 i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss":—deep, (bottomless) pit.

G120.definition:
ἀθυμέω athyméō, ath-oo-meh'-o; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and G2372; to be
 spiritless, i.e. disheartened:—be dismayed.

G1200.definition:
δεσμοφύλαξ desmophýlax, des-mof-oo'-lax; from G1199 and G5441; a jailer (as guarding the prisoners):—jailor,
 keeper of the prison.

G1201.definition:
δεσμωτήριον desmōtḗrion, des-mo-tay'-ree-on; from a derivative of G1199 (equivalent to G1196); a place of bondage,
 i.e. a dungeon:—prison.

G1202.definition: δεσμώτης desmṓtēs, des-mo'-tace; from the same as G1201; (passively) a captive:—prisoner.

G1203.definition:
δεσπότης despótēs, des-pot'-ace; perhaps from G1210 and πόσις pósis (a husband); an absolute ruler
 ("despot"):—Lord, master.

G1204.definition:
δεῦρο deûro, dyoo'-ro; of uncertain affinity; here; used also imperative hither!; and of
 time, hitherto:—come (hither), hither(-to).

G1205.definition:
δεῦτε deûte, dyoo'-teh; from G1204 and an imperative form of εἶμι eîmi (to go); come hither!:—come,
 × follow.

G1206.definition: δευτεραῖος deuteraîos, dyoo-ter-ah'-yos; from G1208; secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day:—next day.

G1208.definition:
δεύτερος deúteros, dyoo'-ter-os; as the comparative of G1417; (ordinal) second (in time, place, or rank;
 also adverb):—afterward, again, second(-arily, time).

G1209.definition:
δέχομαι déchomai, dekh'-om-ahee; middle voice of a primary verb; to receive (in various applications,
 literally or figuratively):—accept, receive, take. Compare G2983.

G121.definition:
†ἄθωος áthōos, ath'-o-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and probably a derivative of G5087
 (meaning a penalty); not guilty:—innocent.

G1210.definition:
δέω déō, deh'-o; a primary verb; to bind (in various applications, literally or
 figuratively):—bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind. See also G1163,
 G1189.

G1211.definition:
δή dḗ, day; probably akin to G1161; a particle of emphasis or explicitness; now,
 then, etc.:—also, and, doubtless, now, therefore.

G1212.definition: δῆλος dēlos, day'-los; of uncertain derivation; clear:—+ bewray, certain, evident, manifest.

G1213.definition: δηλόω dēlóō, day-lo'-o; from G1212; to make plain (by words):—declare, shew, signify.

G1214.definition: Δημᾶς Dēmâs, day-mas'; probably for G1216; Demas, a Christian:—Demas.

G1215.definition:
δημηγορέω dēmēgoréō, day-may-gor-eh'-o; from a compound of G1218 and G58; to be a people-gatherer, i.e. to
 address a public assembly:—make an oration.

G1216.definition:
Δημήτριος Dēmḗtrios, day-may'-tree-os; from Δημήτηρ Dēmḗtēr (Ceres); Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a
 Christian:—Demetrius.

G1217.definition:
δημιουργός dēmiourgós, day-me-oor-gos'; from G1218 and G2041; a worker for the people, i.e. mechanic (spoken of
 the Creator):—maker.

G1218.definition: δῆμος dēmos, day'-mos; from G1210; the public (as bound together socially):—people.

G1219.definition:
δημόσιος dēmósios, day-mos'ee-os; from G1218; public; (feminine singular dative case as adverb) in
 public:—common, openly, publickly.

G122.definition: αἴγειος aígeios, ah'-ee-ghi-os; from αἴξ aíx (a goat); belonging to a goat:—goat.

G1220.definition: δηνάριον dēnárion, day-nar'-ee-on; of Latin origin; a denarius (or ten asses):—pence, penny(-worth).

G1222.definition:
δήπου dḗpou, day'-poo; from G1211 and G4225; a particle of asseveration; indeed
 doubtless:—verily.

G1223.definition:
διά diá, dee-ah'; a primary preposition denoting the channel of an act; through (in very
 wide applications, local, causal, or occasional):—after, always,
 among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause) …
 fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that,
 thereby, therefore, × though, through(-out), to, wherefore, with
 (-in).

G1224.definition: διαβαίνω diabaínō, dee-ab-ah'-ee-no; from G1223 and the base of G939; to cross:—come over, pass (through).

G1225.definition: διαβάλλω diabállō, dee-ab-al'-lo; from G1223 and G906; (figuratively) to traduce:—accuse.

G1226.definition:
διαβεβαιόομαι diabebaióomai, dee-ab-eb-ahee-o'-om-ahee; middle voice of a compound of G1223 and G950; to confirm thoroughly (by
 words), i.e. asseverate:—affirm constantly.

G1227.definition:
διαβλέπω diablépō, dee-ab-lep'-o; from G1223 and G991; to look through, i.e. recover full vision:—see
 clearly.

G1228.definition:
διάβολος diábolos, dee-ab'-ol-os; from G1225; a traducer; specially, Satan (compare H7854):—false
 accuser, devil, slanderer.

G1229.definition:
διαγγέλλω diangéllō, de-ang-gel'-lo; from G1223 and the base of G32; to herald thoroughly:—declare, preach,
 signify.

G123.definition:
αἰγιαλός aigialós, ahee-ghee-al-os'; from ἀΐσσω aḯssō (to rush) and G251 (in the sense of the sea; a beach (on
 which the waves dash):—shore.

G1230.definition: διαγίνομαι diagínomai, dee-ag-in'-om-ahee; from G1223 and G1096; to elapse meanwhile:—X after, be past, be spent.

G1231.definition:
διαγινώσκω diaginṓskō, dee-ag-in-o'-sko; from G1223 and G1097; to know thoroughly, i.e. ascertain
 exactly:—(would) enquire, know the uttermost.

G1233.definition: διάγνωσις diágnōsis, dee-ag'-no-sis; from G1231; (magisterial) examination ("diagnosis"):—hearing.

G1234.definition: διαγογγύζω diagongýzō, dee-ag-ong-good'-zo; from G1223 and G1111; to complain throughout a crowd:—murmur.

G1235.definition: διαγρηγορέω diagrēgoréō, dee-ag-ray-gor-eh'-o; from G1223 and G1127; to waken thoroughly:—be awake.

G1236.definition: διάγω diágō, dee-ag'-o; from G1223 and G71; to pass time or life:—lead life, living.

G1237.definition:
διαδέχομαι diadéchomai, dee-ad-ekh'-om-ahee; from G1223 and G1209; to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed
 to:—come after.

G1238.definition:
διάδημα diádēma, dee-ad'-ay-mah; from a compound of G1223 and G1210; a "diadem" (as bound about the
 head):—crown. Compare G4735.

G1239.definition:
διαδίδωμι diadídōmi, dee-ad-id'-o-mee; from G1223 and G1325; to give throughout a crowd, i.e. deal out; also to
 deliver over (as to a successor):—(make) distribute(-ion), divide,
 give.

G124.definition: Αἰγύπτιος Aigýptios, ahee-goop'-tee-os; from G125; an Ægyptian or inhabitant of Ægyptus:—Egyptian.

G1240.definition: διάδοχος diádochos, dee-ad'-okh-os; from G1237; a successor in office:—room.

G1241.definition: διαζώννυμι diazṓnnymi, dee-az-own'-noo-mee; from G1223 and G2224; to gird tightly:—gird.

G1242.definition:
διαθήκη diathḗkē, dee-ath-ay'-kay; from G1303; properly, a disposition, i.e. (specially) a contract
 (especially a devisory will):—covenant, testament.

G1243.definition:
διαίρεσις diaíresis, dee-ah'-ee-res-is; from G1244; a distinction or (concretely) variety:—difference,
 diversity.

G1244.definition: διαιρέω diairéō, dee-ahee-reh'-o; from G1223 and G138; to separate, i.e. distribute:—divide.

G1245.definition:
†διακαθαρίζω diakatharízō, dee-ak-ath-ar-id'-zo; from G1223 and G2511; to cleanse perfectly, i.e. (specially)
 winnow:—thoroughly purge.

G1246.definition:
διακατελέγχομαι diakatelénchomai, dee-ak-at-el-eng'-khom-ahee; middle voice from G1223 and a compound of G2596 and G1651; to prove
 downright, i.e. confute:—convince.

G1247.definition:
διακονέω diakonéō, dee-ak-on-eh'-o; from G1249; to be an attendant, i.e. wait upon (menially or as a host,
 friend, or (figuratively) teacher); technically, to act as a Christian
 deacon:—(ad-)minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon.

G1248.definition:
διακονία diakonía, dee-ak-on-ee'-ah; from G1249; attendance (as a servant, etc.); figuratively
 (eleemosynary) aid, (official) service (especially of the Christian
 teacher, or technically of the diaconate):—(ad-)minister(-ing,
 -tration, -try), office, relief, service(-ing).

G1249.definition:
διάκονος diákonos, dee-ak'-on-os; probably from an obsolete διάκω diákō (to run on errands; compare G1377); an
 attendant, i.e. (genitive case) a waiter (at table or in other menial
 duties); specially, a Christian teacher and pastor (technically, a
 deacon or deaconess):—deacon, minister, servant.

G125.definition: Αἴγυπτος Aígyptos, ah'-ee-goop-tos; of uncertain derivation; Ægyptus, the land of the Nile:—Egypt.

G1250.definition: διακόσιοι diakósioi, dee-ak-os'-ee-oy; from G1364 and G1540; two hundred:—two hundred.

G1251.definition:
†διακούομαι diakoúomai, dee-ak-oo'-om-ahee; middle voice from G1223 and G191; to hear throughout, i.e. patiently
 listen (to a prisoner's plea):—hear.

G1252.definition:
διακρίνω diakrínō, dee-ak-ree'-no; from G1223 and G2919; to separate thoroughly, i.e. (literally and
 reflexively) to withdraw from, or (by implication) oppose;
 figuratively, to discriminate (by implication, decide), or
 (reflexively) hesitate:—contend, make (to) differ(-ence), discern,
 doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver.

G1253.definition: διάκρισις diákrisis, dee-ak'-ree-sis; from G1252; judicial estimation:—discern(-ing), disputation.

G1254.definition:
διακωλύω diakōlýō, dee-ak-o-loo'-o; from G1223 and G2967; to hinder altogether, i.e. utterly
 prohibit:—forbid.

G1255.definition:
διαλαλέω dialaléō, dee-al-al-eh'-o; from G1223 and G2980; to talk throughout a company, i.e. converse or
 (genitive case) publish:—commune, noise abroad.

G1256.definition:
διαλέγομαι dialégomai, dee-al-eg'-om-ahee; middle voice from G1223 and G3004; to say thoroughly, i.e. discuss (in
 argument or exhortation):—dispute, preach (unto), reason (with),
 speak.

G1257.definition: διαλείπω dialeípō, dee-al-i'-po; from G1223 and G3007; to leave off in the middle, i.e. intermit:—cease.

G1258.definition: διάλεκτος diálektos, dee-al'-ek-tos; from G1256; a (mode of) discourse, i.e. "dialect":—language, tongue.

G1259.definition:
διαλλάσσω diallássō, dee-al-las'-so; from G1223 and G236; to change thoroughly, i.e. (mentally) to
 conciliate:—reconcile.

G126.definition:
ἀΐδιος aḯdios, ah-id'-ee-os; from G104; everduring (forward and backward, or forward
 only):—eternal, everlasting.

G1260.definition:
διαλογίζομαι dialogízomai, dee-al-og-id'-zom-ahee; from G1223 and G3049; to reckon thoroughly, i.e. (genitive case) to
 deliberate (by reflection or discussion):—cast in mind, consider,
 dispute, muse, reason, think.

G1261.definition:
διαλογισμός dialogismós, dee-al-og-is-mos'; from G1260; discussion, i.e. (internal) consideration (by implication,
 purpose), or (external) debate:—dispute, doubtful(-ing), imagination,
 reasoning, thought.

G1262.definition: διαλύω dialýō, dee-al-oo'-o; from G1223 and G3089; to dissolve utterly:—scatter.

G1263.definition:
διαμαρτύρομαι diamartýromai, dee-am-ar-too'-rom-ahee; from G1223 and G3140; to attest or protest earnestly, or (by
 implication) hortatively:—charge, testify (unto), witness.

G1264.definition: διαμάχομαι diamáchomai, dee-am-akh'-om-ahee; from G1223 and G3164; to fight fiercely (in altercation):—strive.

G1265.definition:
διαμένω diaménō, dee-am-en'-o; from G1223 and G3306; to stay constantly (in being or
 relation):—continue, remain.

G1266.definition:
διαμερίζω diamerízō, dee-am-er-id'-zo; from G1223 and G3307; to partition thoroughly (literally in
 distribution, figuratively in dissension):—cloven, divide, part.

G1267.definition: διαμερισμός diamerismós, dee-am-er-is-mos'; from G1266; disunion (of opinion and conduct):—division.

G1268.definition:
διανέμω dianémō, dee-an-em'-o; from G1223 and the base of G3551; to distribute, i.e. (of information)
 to disseminate:—spread.

G1269.definition:
διανεύω dianeúō, dee-an-yoo'-o; from G1223 and G3506; to nod (or express by signs) across an intervening
 space:—beckon.

G127.definition:
†αἰδώς aidṓs, ahee-doce'; perhaps from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1492 (through the idea of
 downcast eyes); bashfulness, i.e. (towards men), modesty or (towards
 God) awe:—reverence, shamefacedness.

G1270.definition:
διανόημα dianóēma, dee-an-o'-ay-mah; from a compound of G1223 and G3539; something thought through, i.e. a
 sentiment:—thought.

G1271.definition:
διάνοια diánoia, dee-an'-oy-ah; from G1223 and G3563; deep thought, properly, the faculty (mind or its
 disposition), by implication, its exercise:—imagination, mind,
 understanding.

G1272.definition:
διανοίγω dianoígō, dee-an-oy'-go; from G1223 and G455; to open thoroughly, literally (as a first-born) or
 figuratively (to expound):—open.

G1273.definition:
διανυκτερεύω dianyktereúō, dee-an-ook-ter-yoo'-o; from G1223 and a derivative of G3571; to sit up the whole
 night:—continue all night.

G1274.definition: διανύω dianýō, dee-an-oo'-o; from G1223 and ἀνύω anýō (to effect); to accomplish thoroughly:—finish.

G1275.definition:
διαπαντός diapantós, dee-ap-an-tos'; from G1223 and the genitive case of G3956; through all time, i.e.
 (adverbially) constantly:—alway(-s), continually.

G1276.definition:
διαπεράω diaperáō, dee-ap-er-ah'-o; from G1223 and a derivative of the base of G4008; to cross entirely:—go
 over, pass (over), sail over.

G1277.definition: διαπλέω diapléō, dee-ap-leh'-o; from G1223 and G4126; to sail through:—sail over.

G1278.definition:
†διαπονέω diaponéō, dee-ap-on-eh'-o; from G1223 and a derivative of G4192; to toil through, i.e. (passively)
 be worried:—be grieved.

G1279.definition:
διαπορεύομαι diaporeúomai, dee-ap-or-yoo'-om-ahee; from G1223 and G4198; to travel through:—go through, journey in, pass
 by.

G128.definition:
Αἰθίοψ Aithíops, ahee-thee'-ops; from αἴθω aíthō (to scorch) and ὤψ ṓps (the face, from G3700); an Æthiopian (as
 a blackamoor):—Ethiopian.

G1280.definition:
διαπορέω diaporéō, dee-ap-or-eh'-o; from G1223 and G639; to be thoroughly nonplussed:—(be in) doubt, be
 (much) perplexed.

G1281.definition:
διαπραγματεύομαι diapragmateúomai, dee-ap-rag-mat-yoo'-om-ahee; from G1223 and G4231; to thoroughly occupy oneself, i.e. (transitively
 and by implication) to earn in business:—gain by trading.

G1282.definition:
διαπρίω diapríō, dee-ap-ree'-o; from G1223 and the base of G4249; to saw asunder, i.e. (figuratively) to
 exasperate:—cut (to the heart).

G1283.definition: διαρπάζω diarpázō, dee-ar-pad'-zo; from G1223 and G726; to seize asunder, i.e. plunder:—spoil.

G1284.definition: †διαῤῥήσσω diarrhḗssō, dee-ar-hrayce'-so; from G1223 and G4486; to tear asunder:—break, rend.

G1285.definition:
διασαφέω diasaphéō, dee-as-af-eh'-o; from G1223 and σαφής saphḗs (clear); to clear thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively)
 declare:—tell unto.

G1286.definition:
διασείω diaseíō, dee-as-i'-o; from G1223 and G4579; to shake thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to
 intimidate:—do violence to.

G1287.definition:
διασκορπίζω diaskorpízō, dee-as-kor-pid'-zo; from G1223 and G4650; to dissipate, i.e. (genitive case) to rout or
 separate; specially, to winnow; figuratively, to squander:—disperse,
 scatter (abroad), strew, waste.

G1288.definition:
διασπάω diaspáō, dee-as-pah'-o; from G1223 and G4685; to draw apart, i.e. sever or dismember:—pluck
 asunder, pull in pieces.

G1289.definition:
διασπείρω diaspeírō, dee-as-pi'-ro; from G1223 and G4687; to sow throughout, i.e. (figuratively) distribute
 in foreign lands:—scatter abroad.

G129.definition:
αἷμα haîma, hah'-ee-mah; of uncertain derivation; blood, literally (of men or animals),
 figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of
 Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred:—blood.

G1290.definition:
διασπορά diasporá, dee-as-por-ah'; from G1289; dispersion, i.e. (specially and concretely) the (converted)
 Israelite resident in Gentile countries:—(which are) scattered
 (abroad).

G1291.definition:
†διαστέλλομαι diastéllomai, dee-as-tel'-lom-ahee; middle voice from G1223 and G4724; to set (oneself) apart (figuratively,
 distinguish), i.e. (by implication) to enjoin:—charge, that which was
 (give) commanded(-ment).

G1292.definition: διάστημα diástēma, dee-as'-tay-mah; from G1339; an interval:—space.

G1293.definition: διαστολή diastolḗ, dee-as-tol-ay'; from G1291; a variation:—difference, distinction.

G1294.definition:
διαστρέφω diastréphō, dee-as-tref'-o; from G1223 and G4762; to distort, i.e. (figuratively) misinterpret, or
 (morally) corrupt:—perverse(-rt), turn away.

G1295.definition:
†διασώζω diasṓzō, dee-as-odze'-o; from G1223 and G4982; to save thoroughly, i.e. (by implication or
 analogy) to cure, preserve, rescue, etc.:—bring safe, escape (safe),
 heal, make perfectly whole, save.

G1296.definition: διαταγή diatagḗ, dee-at-ag-ay'; from G1299; arrangement, i.e. institution:—instrumentality.

G1297.definition: διάταγμα diátagma, dee-at'-ag-mah; from G1299; an arrangement, i.e. (authoritative) edict:—commandment.

G1298.definition:
διαταράσσω diatarássō, dee-at-ar-as'-so; from G1223 and G5015; to disturb wholly, i.e. agitate (with
 alarm):—trouble.

G1299.definition:
διατάσσω diatássō, dee-at-as'-so; from G1223 and G5021; to arrange thoroughly, i.e. (specially) institute,
 prescribe, etc.:—appoint, command, give, (set in) order, ordain.

G13.definition: Ἄγαβος Ágabos, ag'-ab-os; of Hebrew origin (compare H2285); Agabus, an Israelite:—Agabus.

G130.definition:
αἱματεκχυσία haimatekchysía, hahee-mat-ek-khoo-see'-ah; from G129 and a derivative of G1632; an effusion of blood:—shedding of
 blood.

G1300.definition:
διατελέω diateléō, dee-at-el-eh'-o; from G1223 and G5055; to accomplish thoroughly, i.e. (subjectively) to
 persist:—continue.

G1301.definition:
διατηρέω diatēréō, dee-at-ay-reh'-o; from G1223 and G5083; to watch thoroughly, i.e. (positively and
 transitively) to observe strictly, or (negatively and reflexively) to
 avoid wholly:—keep.

G1303.definition:
†διατίθεμαι diatíthemai, dee-at-ith'-em-ahee; middle voice from G1223 and G5087; to put apart, i.e. (figuratively)
 dispose (by assignment, compact, or bequest):—appoint, make,
 testator.

G1304.definition:
διατρίβω diatríbō, dee-at-ree'-bo; from G1223 and the base of G5147; to wear through (time), i.e.
 remain:—abide, be, continue, tarry.

G1305.definition: διατροφή diatrophḗ, dee-at-rof-ay'; from a compound of G1223 and G5142; nourishment:—food.

G1306.definition: διαυγάζω diaugázō, dee-ow-gad'-zo; from G1223 and G826; to glimmer through, i.e. break (as day):—dawn.

G1308.definition:
διαφέρω diaphérō, dee-af-er'-o; from G1223 and G5342; to bear through, i.e. (literally) transport;
 usually to bear apart, i.e. (objectively) to toss about (figuratively,
 report); subjectively, to "differ", or (by implication) surpass:—be
 better, carry, differ from, drive up and down, be (more) excellent,
 make matter, publish, be of more value.

G1309.definition: διαφεύγω diapheúgō, dee-af-yoo'-go; from G1223 and G5343; to flee through, i.e. escape:—escape.

G131.definition:
αἱμοῤῥέω haimorrhéō, hahee-mor-hreh'-o; from G129 and G4482; to flow blood, i.e. have a hæmorrhage:—diseased
 with an issue of blood.

G1310.definition:
διαφημίζω diaphēmízō, dee-af-ay-mid'-zo; from G1223 and a derivative of G5345; to report thoroughly, i.e.
 divulgate:—blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame.

G1311.definition:
διαφθείρω diaphtheírō, dee-af-thi'-ro; from G1225 and G5351; to rot thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to ruin
 (passively, decay utterly, figuratively, pervert):—corrupt, destroy,
 perish.

G1312.definition: διαφθορά diaphthorá, dee-af-thor-ah'; from G1311; decay:—corruption.

G1313.definition:
διάφορος diáphoros, dee-af'-or-os; from G1308; varying; also surpassing:—differing, divers, more
 excellent.

G1314.definition: διαφυλάσσω diaphylássō, dee-af-oo-las'-so; from G1223 and G5442; to guard thoroughly, i.e. protect:—keep.

G1315.definition:
†διαχειρίζομαι diacheirízomai, dee-akh-i-rid'-zom-ahee; from G1223 and a derivative of G5495; to handle thoroughly, i.e. lay
 violent hands upon:—kill, slay.

G1316.definition:
διαχωρίζομαι diachōrízomai, dee-akh-o-rid'-zom-ahee; from G1223 and the middle voice of G5563; to remove (oneself) wholly,
 i.e. retire:—depart.

G1317.definition: διδακτικός didaktikós, did-ak-tik-os'; from G1318; instructive ("didactic"):—apt to teach.

G1318.definition:
διδακτός didaktós, did-ak-tos'; from G1321; (subjectively) instructed, or (objectively) communicated by
 teaching:—taught, which … teacheth.

G1319.definition:
διδασκαλία didaskalía, did-as-kal-ee'-ah; from G1320; instruction (the function or the information):—doctrine,
 learning, teaching.

G132.definition: Αἰνέας Ainéas, ahee-neh'-as; of uncertain derivation; Ænĕas, an Israelite:—Æneas.

G1320.definition:
διδάσκαλος didáskalos, did-as'-kal-os; from G1321; an instructor (genitive case or specially):—doctor,
 master, teacher.

G1321.definition:
διδάσκω didáskō, did-as'-ko; a prolonged (causative) form of a primary verb δάω dáō (to learn); to
 teach (in the same broad application):—teach.

G1322.definition:
διδαχή didachḗ, did-akh-ay'; from G1321; instruction (the act or the matter):—doctrine, hath been
 taught.

G1323.definition: δίδραχμον dídrachmon, did'-rakh-mon; from G1364 and G1406; a double drachma (didrachm):—tribute.

G1324.definition:
Δίδυμος Dídymos, did'-oo-mos; prolongation from G1364; double, i.e. twin; Didymus, a
 Christian:—Didymus.

G1325.definition:
δίδωμι dídōmi, did'-o-mee; a prolonged form of a primary verb (which is used as an alternative in
 most of the tenses); to give (used in a very wide application,
 properly, or by implication, literally or figuratively; greatly
 modified by the connection):—adventure, bestow, bring forth, commit,
 deliver (up), give, grant, hinder, make, minister, number, offer, have
 power, put, receive, set, shew, smite (+ with the hand), strike (+
 with the palm of the hand), suffer, take, utter, yield.

G1326.definition:
διεγείρω diegeírō, dee-eg-i'-ro; from G1223 and G1453; to wake fully; i.e. arouse (literally or
 figuratively):—arise, awake, raise, stir up.

G1327.definition:
διέξοδος diéxodos, dee-ex'-od-os; from G1223 and G1841; an outlet through, i.e. probably an open square
 (from which roads diverge):—highway.

G1328.definition: διερμηνευτής diermēneutḗs, dee-er-main-yoo-tace'; from G1329; an explainer:—interpreter.

G1329.definition:
διερμηνεύω diermēneúō, dee-er-main-yoo'-o; from G1223 and G2059; to explain thoroughly, by implication, to
 translate:—expound, interpret(-ation).

G133.definition:
αἴνεσις aínesis, ah'-ee-nes-is; from G134; a praising (the act), i.e. (specially) a
 thank(-offering):—praise.

G1330.definition:
διέρχομαι diérchomai, dee-er'-khom-ahee; from G1223 and G2064; to traverse (literally):—come, depart, go (about,
 abroad, everywhere, over, through, throughout), pass (by, over,
 through, throughout), pierce through, travel, walk through.

G1331.definition:
διερωτάω dierōtáō, dee-er-o-tah'-o; from G1223 and G2065; to question throughout, i.e. ascertain by
 interrogation:—make enquiry for.

G1332.definition: διετής dietḗs, dee-et-ace'; from G1364 and G2094; of two years (in age):—two years old.

G1333.definition: διετία dietía, dee-et-ee'-a; from G1332; a space of two years (biennium):—two years.

G1334.definition: διηγέομαι diēgéomai, dee-ayg-eh'-om-ahee; from G1223 and G2233; to relate fully:—declare, shew, tell.

G1335.definition: †διήγεσις diḗgesis, dee-ayg'-es-is; from G1334; a recital:—declaration.

G1337.definition:
διθάλασσος dithálassos, dee-thal'-as-sos; from G1364 and G2281; having two seas, i.e. a sound with a double
 outlet:—where two seas meet.

G1338.definition:
διϊκνέομαι diïknéomai, dee-ik-neh'-om-ahee; from G1223 and the base of G2425; to reach through, i.e.
 penetrate:—pierce.

G1339.definition:
διΐστημι diḯstēmi, dee-is'-tay-mee; from G1223 and G2476; to stand apart, i.e. (reflexively) to remove,
 intervene:—go further, be parted, after the space of.

G134.definition: αἰνέω ainéō, ahee-neh'-o; from G136; to praise (God):—praise.

G1340.definition:
διϊσχυρίζομαι diïschyrízomai, dee-is-khoo-rid'-zom-ahee; from G1223 and a derivative of G2478; to stout it through, i.e.
 asservate:—confidently (constantly) affirm.

G1341.definition: δικαιοκρισία dikaiokrisía, dik-ah-yok-ris-ee'-ah; from G1342 and G2920; a just sentence:—righteous judgment.

G1342.definition:
δίκαιος díkaios, dik'-ah-yos; from G1349; equitable (in character or act); by implication, innocent,
 holy (absolutely or relatively):—just, meet, right(-eous).

G1343.definition:
δικαιοσύνη dikaiosýnē, dik-ah-yos-oo'-nay; from G1342; equity (of character or act); specially (Christian)
 justification:—righteousness.

G1344.definition:
δικαιόω dikaióō, dik-ah-yo'-o; from G1342; to render (i.e. show or regard as) just or innocent:—free,
 justify(-ier), be righteous.

G1345.definition:
δικαίωμα dikaíōma, dik-ah'-yo-mah; from G1344; an equitable deed; by implication, a statute or
 decision:—judgment, justification, ordinance, righteousness.

G1346.definition: δικαίως dikaíōs, dik-ah'-yoce; adverb from G1342; equitably:—justly, (to) righteously(-ness).

G1347.definition: δικαίωσις dikaíōsis, dik-ah'-yo-sis; from G1344; aquittal (for Christ's sake):—justification.

G1348.definition: δικαστής dikastḗs, dik-as-tace'; from a derivative of G1349; a judger:—judge.

G1349.definition:
†δίκη díkē, dee'-kay; probably from G1166; right (as self-evident), i.e. justice (the
 principle, a decision, or its execution):—judgment, punish,
 vengeance.

G135.definition:
αἴνιγμα aínigma, ah'-ee-nig-ma; from a derivative of G136 (in its primary sense); an obscure saying
 ("enigma"), i.e. (abstractly) obscureness:—X darkly.

G1350.definition:
δίκτυον díktyon, dik'-too-on; probably from a primary verb δίκω díkō (to cast); a seine (for
 fishing):—net.

G1351.definition:
δίλογος dílogos, dil'-og-os; from G1364 and G3056; equivocal, i.e. telling a different
 story:—double-tongued.

G1352.definition:
διό dió, dee-o'; from G1223 and G3739; through which thing, i.e. consequently:—for which
 cause, therefore, wherefore.

G1353.definition: διοδεύω diodeúō, dee-od-yoo'-o; from G1223 and G3593; to travel through:—go throughout, pass through.

G1354.definition: Διονύσιος Dionýsios, dee-on-oo'-see-os; from Διόνυσος Diónysos (Bacchus); reveller; Dionysius, an Athenian:—Dionysius.

G1355.definition: διόπερ dióper, dee-op'-er; from G1352 and G4007; on which very account:—wherefore.

G1356.definition:
διοπετής diopetḗs, dee-op-et'-ace; from the alternate of G2203 and the alternate of G4098; sky-fallen (i.e.
 an aerolite):—which fell down from Jupiter.

G1357.definition:
διόρθωσις diórthōsis, dee-or'-tho-sis; from a compound of G1223 and a derivative of G3717, meaning to
 straighten thoroughly; rectification, i.e. (specially) the Messianic
 restauration:—reformation.

G1358.definition: διορύσσω diorýssō, dee-or-oos'-so; from G1223 and G3736; to penetrate burglariously:—break through (up).

G1359.definition:
Διόσκουροι Dióskouroi, dee-os'-koo-roy; from the alternate of G2203 and a form of the base of G2877; sons of
 Jupiter, i.e. the twins Dioscuri:—Castor and Pollux.

G136.definition:
αἶνος aînos, ah'-ee-nos; apparently a prime word; properly, a story, but used in the sense of
 G1868; praise (of God):—praise.

G1360.definition:
διότι dióti, dee-ot'-ee; from G1223 and G3754; on the very account that, or inasmuch as:—because
 (that), for, therefore.

G1361.definition:
Διοτρεφής Diotrephḗs, dee-ot-ref-ace'; from the alternate of G2203 and G5142; Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an
 opponent of Christianity:—Diotrephes.

G1362.definition:
†διπλοῦς diploûs, dip-looce'; from G1364 and (probably) the base of G4119; two-fold:—double, two-fold
 more.

G1363.definition: διπλόω diplóō, dip-lo'-o; from G1362; to render two-fold:—double.

G1364.definition: δίς dís, dece; adverb from G1417; twice:—again, twice.

G1365.definition:
διστάζω distázō, dis-tad'-zo; from G1364; properly, to duplicate, i.e. (mentally) to waver (in
 opinion):—doubt.

G1366.definition: δίστομος dístomos, dis'-tom-os; from G1364 and G4750; double-edged:—with two edges, two-edged.

G1367.definition: δισχίλιοι dischílioi, dis-khil'-ee-oy; from G1364 and G5507; two thousand:—two thousand.

G1368.definition:
†διϋλίζω diÿlízō, dee-oo-lid'-zo; from G1223 and ὑλίζω hylízō hoo-lid'-zo (to filter); to strain out:—strain
 at (probably by misprint).

G1369.definition:
διχάζω dicházō, dee-khad'-zo; from a derivative of G1364; to make apart, i.e. sunder (figuratively,
 alienate):—set at variance.

G137.definition: Αἰνών Ainṓn, ahee-nohn'; of Hebrew origin (a derivative of H5869, place of springs); Ænon, a place in Palestine:—Ænon.

G1370.definition:
διχοστασία dichostasía, dee-khos-tas-ee'-ah; from a derivative of G1364 and G4714; disunion, i.e. (figuratively)
 dissension:—division, sedition.

G1371.definition:
διχοτομέω dichotoméō, dee-khot-om-eh'-o; from a compound of a derivative of G1364 and a derivative of
 τέμνω témnō (to cut); to bisect, i.e. (by extension) to flog
 severely:—cut asunder (in sunder).

G1372.definition:
διψάω dipsáō, dip-sah'-o; from a variation of G1373; to thirst for (literally or
 figuratively):—(be, be a-)thirst(-y).

G1373.definition: δίψος dípsos, dip'-sos; of uncertain affinity; thirst:—thirst.

G1374.definition:
δίψυχος dípsychos, dip'-soo-khos; from G1364 and G5590; two-spirited, i.e. vacillating (in opinion or
 purpose):—double minded.

G1375.definition: διωγμός diōgmós, dee-ogue-mos'; from G1377; persecution:—persecution.

G1376.definition: διώκτης diṓktēs, dee-oke'-tace; from G1377; a persecutor:—persecutor.

G1377.definition:
διώκω diṓkō, dee-o'-ko; a prolonged (and causative) form of a primary verb δίω díō (to flee; 
 compare the base of G1169 and G1249); to pursue (literally or
 figuratively); by implication, to persecute:—ensue, follow (after),
 given to, (suffer) persecute(-ion), press forward.

G1378.definition:
δόγμα dógma, dog'-mah; from the base of G1380; a law (civil, ceremonial or
 ecclesiastical):—decree, ordinance.

G1379.definition:
δογματίζω dogmatízō, dog-mat-id'-zo; from G1378; to prescribe by statute, i.e. (reflexively) to submit to,
 ceremonially rule:—be subject to ordinances.

G1380.definition:
δοκέω dokéō, dok-eh'-o; a prolonged form of a primary verb, δόκω dókō dok'-o (used only in an
 alternate in certain tenses; compare the base of G1166) of the same
 meaning; to think; by implication, to seem (truthfully or
 uncertainly):—be accounted, (of own) please(-ure), be of reputation,
 seem (good), suppose, think, trow.

G1381.definition:
†δοκιμάζω dokimázō, dok-im-ad'-zo; from G1384; to test (literally or figuratively); by implication, to
 approve:—allow, discern, examine, × like, (ap-)prove, try.

G1382.definition:
δοκιμή dokimḗ, dok-ee-may'; from the same as G1384; test (abstractly or concretely); by
 implication, trustiness:—experience(-riment), proof, trial.

G1383.definition:
δοκίμιον dokímion, dok-im'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G1382; a testing; by implication,
 trustworthiness:—trial, trying.

G1384.definition:
δόκιμος dókimos, dok'-ee-mos; from G1380; properly, acceptable (current after assayal), i.e.
 approved:—approved, tried.

G1385.definition: δοκός dokós, dok-os'; from G1209 (through the idea of holding up); a stick of timber:—beam.

G1386.definition: δόλιος dólios, dol'-ee-os; from G1388; guileful:—deceitful.

G1387.definition: δολιόω dolióō, dol-ee-o'-o; from G1386; to be guileful:—use deceit.

G1389.definition:
δολόω dolóō, dol-o'-o; from G1388; to ensnare, i.e. (figuratively) adulterate:—handle
 deceitfully.

G139.definition:
αἵρεσις haíresis, hah'-ee-res-is; from G138; properly, a choice, i.e. (specially) a party or (abstractly)
 disunion:—heresy (which is the Greek word itself), sect.

G1390.definition: δόμα dóma, dom'-ah; from the base of G1325; a present:—gift.

G1391.definition:
δόξα dóxa, dox'-ah; from the base of G1380; glory (as very apparent), in a wide application
 (literal or figurative, objective or subjective):—dignity,
 glory(-ious), honour, praise, worship.

G1392.definition:
δοξάζω doxázō, dox-ad'-zo; from G1391; to render (or esteem) glorious (in a wide
 application):—(make) glorify(-ious), full of (have) glory, honour,
 magnify.

G1393.definition: Δορκάς Dorkás, dor-kas'; gazelle; Dorcas, a Christian woman:—Dorcas.

G1394.definition:
δόσις dósis, dos'-is; from the base of G1325; a giving; by implication, (concretely) a
 gift:—gift, giving.

G1395.definition: δότης dótēs, dot'-ace; from the base of G1325; a giver:—giver.

G1396.definition:
δουλαγωγέω doulagōgéō, doo-lag-ogue-eh'-o; from a presumed compound of G1401 and G71; to be a slave-driver, i.e. to
 enslave (figuratively, subdue):—bring into subjection.

G1397.definition: δουλεία douleía, doo-li'-ah; from G1398; slavery (ceremonially or figuratively):—bondage.

G1398.definition:
δουλεύω douleúō, dool-yoo'-o; from G1401; to be a slave to (literal or figurative, involuntary or
 voluntary):—be in bondage, (do) serve(-ice).

G1399.definition:
δούλη doúlē, doo'-lay; feminine of G1401; a female slave (involuntarily or
 voluntarily):—handmaid(-en).

G14.definition: ἀγαθοεργέω agathoergéō, ag-ath-er-gheh'-o; from G18 and G2041; to work good:—do good.

G140.definition: αἱρετίζω hairetízō, hahee-ret-id'-zo; from a derivative of G138; to make a choice:—choose.

G1400.definition: δοῦλον doûlon, doo'-lon; neuter of G1401; subservient:—servant.

G1402.definition:
δουλόω doulóō, doo-lo'-o; from G1401; to enslave (literally or figuratively):—bring into (be
 under) bondage, × given, become (make) servant.

G1403.definition: δοχή dochḗ, dokh-ay'; from G1209; a reception, i.e. convivial entertainment:—feast.

G1404.definition:
δράκων drákōn, drak'-own; probably from an alternate form of δέρκομαι dérkomai (to look); a fabulous kind
 of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate):—dragon.

G1405.definition:
δράσσομαι drássomai, dras'-som-ahee; perhaps akin to the base of G1404 (through the idea of capturing); to
 grasp, i.e. (figuratively) entrap:—take.

G1406.definition:
δραχμή drachmḗ, drakh-may'; from G1405; a drachma or (silver) coin (as handled):—piece (of
 silver).

G1407.definition:
δρέπανον drépanon, drep'-an-on; from δρέπω drépō (to pluck); a gathering hook (especially for
 harvesting):—sickle.

G1408.definition:
δρόμος drómos, drom'-os; from the alternate of G5143; a race, i.e. (figuratively)
 career:—course.

G1409.definition:
Δρούσιλλα Droúsilla, droo'-sil-lah; a feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name); Drusilla, a member of
 the Herodian family:—Drusilla.

G141.definition: αἱρετικός hairetikós, hahee-ret-ee-kos'; from the same as G140; a schismatic:—heretic (the Greek word itself).

G1410.definition:
δύναμαι dýnamai, doo'-nam-ahee; of uncertain affinity; to be able or possible:—be able, can (do, +
 -not), could, may, might, be possible, be of power.

G1411.definition:
δύναμις dýnamis, doo'-nam-is; from G1410; force (literally or figuratively); specially, miraculous
 power (usually by implication, a miracle itself):—ability, abundance,
 meaning, might(-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle(-s), power,
 strength, violence, mighty (wonderful) work.

G1412.definition: δυναμόω dynamóō, doo-nam-o'-o; from G1411; to enable:—strengthen.

G1413.definition: δυνάστης dynástēs, doo-nas'-tace; from G1410; a ruler or officer:—of great authority, mighty, potentate.

G1414.definition: δυνατέω dynatéō, doo-nat-eh'-o; from G1415; to be efficient (figuratively):—be mighty.

G1415.definition:
δυνατός dynatós, doo-nat-os'; from G1410; powerful or capable (literally or figuratively); neuter
 possible:—able, could, (that is) mighty (man), possible, power,
 strong.

G1417.definition: δύο dýo, doo'-o; a primary numeral; "two":—both, twain, two.

G1419.definition: δυσβάστακτος dysbástaktos, doos-bas'-tak-tos; from G1418 and a derivative of G941; oppressive:—grievous to be borne.

G142.definition:
αἴρω aírō, ah'-ee-ro; a primary root; to lift up; by implication, to take up or away;
 figuratively, to raise (the voice), keep in suspense (the mind),
 specially, to sail away (i.e. weigh anchor); by Hebraism (compare
 H5375) to expiate sin:—away with, bear (up), carry, lift up, loose,
 make to doubt, put away, remove, take (away, up).

G1420.definition:
†δυσεντερία dysentería, doos-en-ter-ee'-ah; from G1418 and a comparative of G1787 (meaning a bowel); a
 "dysentery":—bloody flux.

G1421.definition:
δυσερμήνευτος dysermḗneutos, doos-er-mane'-yoo-tos; from G1418 and a presumed derivative of G2059; difficult of
 explanation:—hard to be uttered.

G1422.definition:
δύσκολος dýskolos, doo'-kol-os; from G1418 and κόλον kólon (food); properly, fastidious about eating
 (peevish), i.e. (genitive case) impracticable:—hard.

G1423.definition: δυσκόλως dyskólōs, doos-kol'-oce; adverb from G1422; impracticably:—hardly.

G1424.definition:
δυσμή dysmḗ, doos-may'; from G1416; the sun-set, i.e. (by implication) the western
 region:—west.

G1425.definition:
δυσνόητος dysnóētos, doos-no'-ay-tos; from G1418 and a derivative of G3539; difficult of perception:—hard to
 be understood.

G1426.definition: δυσφημία dysphēmía, doos-fay-mee'-ah; from a compound of G1418 and G5345; defamation:—evil report.

G1427.definition: †δώδεκα dṓdeka, do'-dek-ah; from G1417 and G1176; two and ten, i.e. a dozen:—twelve.

G1428.definition: δωδέκατος dōdékatos, do-dek'-at-os; from G1427; twelfth:—twelfth.

G1429.definition: δωδεκάφυλον dōdekáphylon, do-dek-af'-oo-lon; from G1427 and G5443; the commonwealth of Israel:—twelve tribes.

G143.definition:
αἰσθάνομαι aisthánomai, ahee-sthan'-om-ahee; of uncertain derivation; to apprehend (properly, by the
 senses):—perceive.

G1430.definition:
δῶμα dōma, do'-mah; from δέμω démō (to build); properly, an edifice, i.e. (specially) a
 roof:—housetop.

G1431.definition: δωρεά dōreá, do-reh-ah'; from G1435; a gratuity:—gift.

G1432.definition:
δωρεάν dōreán, do-reh-an'; accusative case of G1431 as adverb; gratuitously (literally or
 figuratively):—without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain.

G1433.definition: δωρέομαι dōréomai, do-reh'-om-ahee; middle voice from G1435; to bestow gratuitously:—give.

G1434.definition: δώρημα dṓrēma, do'-ray-mah; from G1433; a bestowment:—gift.

G1435.definition: δῶρον dōron, do'-ron; a present; specially, a sacrifice:—gift, offering.

G1436.definition:
ἔα éa, eh'-ah; apparent imperative of G1439; properly, let it be, i.e. (as
 interjection) aha!:—let alone.

G1437.definition:
†ἐάν eán, eh-an'; from G1487 and G302; a conditional particle; in case that, provided,
 etc.; often used in connection with other particles to denote
 indefiniteness or uncertainty:—before, but, except, (and) if, (if)
 so, (what-, whither-)soever, though, when (-soever), whether (or), to
 whom, (who-)so(-ever). See G3361.

G1438.definition:
ἑαυτοῦ heautoû, heh-ow-too'; from a reflexive pronoun otherwise obsolete and the genitive case
 (dative case or accusative case) of G846; him- (her-, it-, them-, also
 (in conjunction with the personal pronoun of the other persons) my-,
 thy-, our-, your-) self (selves), etc.:—alone, her (own, -self), (he)
 himself, his (own), itself, one (to) another, our (thine)
 own(-selves), + that she had, their (own, own selves), (of)
 them(-selves), they, thyself, you, your (own, own conceits, own
 selves, -selves).

G1439.definition:
ἐάω eáō, eh-ah'-o; of uncertain affinity; to let be, i.e. permit or leave alone:—commit,
 leave, let (alone), suffer. See also G1436.

G144.definition: αἴσθησις aísthēsis, ah'-ee-sthay-sis; from G143; perception, i.e. (figuratively) discernment:—judgment.

G1440.definition:
†ἑβδομήκοντα hebdomḗkonta, heb-dom-ay'-kon-tah; from G1442 and a modified form of G1176; seventy:—seventy, three score
 and ten.

G1441.definition: ἑβδομηκοντάκις hebdomēkontákis, heb-dom-ay-kon-tak-is; multiple adverb from G1440; seventy times:—seventy times.

G1442.definition: ἕβδομος hébdomos, heb'-dom-os; ordinal from G2033; seventh:—seventh.

G1443.definition: Ἐβέρ Ebér, eb-er'; of Hebrew origin (H5677); Eber, a patriarch:—Eber.

G1445.definition: Ἑβραῖος Hebraîos, heb-rah'-yos; from G1443; a Hebræan (i.e. Hebrew) or Jew:—Hebrew.

G1446.definition:
Ἑβραΐς Hebraḯs, heb-rah-is'; from G1443; the Hebraistic (Hebrew) or Jewish (Chaldee)
 language:—Hebrew.

G1447.definition:
Ἑβραϊστί Hebraïstí, heb-rah-is-tee'; adverb from G1446; Hebraistically or in the Jewish (Chaldee)
 language:—in (the) Hebrew (tongue).

G1448.definition:
ἐγγίζω engízō, eng-id'-zo; from G1451; to make near, i.e. (reflexively) approach:—approach, be at
 hand, come (draw) near, be (come, draw) nigh.

G1449.definition: ἐγγράφω engráphō, eng-graf'-o; from G1722 and G1125; to "engrave", i.e. inscribe:—write (in).

G145.definition:
αἰσθητήριον aisthētḗrion, ahee-sthay-tay'-ree-on; from a derivative of G143; properly, an organ of perception, i.e.
 (figuratively) judgment:—senses.

G1450.definition:
ἔγγυος éngyos, eng'-goo-os; from G1722 and γυῖον guîon (a limb); pledged (as if articulated by a member),
 i.e. a bondsman:—surety.

G1451.definition:
ἐγγύς engýs, eng-goos'; from a primary verb ἄγχω ánchō (to squeeze or throttle; akin to the base of
 G43); near (literally or figuratively, of place or time):—from , at
 hand, near, nigh (at hand, unto), ready.

G1453.definition:
ἐγείρω egeírō, eg-i'-ro; probably akin to the base of G58 (through the idea of collecting one's
 faculties); to waken (transitively or intransitively), i.e. rouse
 (literally, from sleep, from sitting or lying, from disease, from
 death; or figuratively, from obscurity, inactivity, ruins,
 nonexistence):—awake, lift (up), raise (again, up), rear up, (a-)rise
 (again, up), stand, take up.

G1454.definition: ἔγερσις égersis, eg'-er-sis; from G1453; a resurgence (from death):—resurrection.

G1455.definition:
ἐγκάθετος enkáthetos, eng-kath'-et-os; from G1722 and a derivative of G2524; subinduced, i.e. surreptitiously
 suborned as a lier-in-wait:—spy.

G1456.definition:
ἐγκαίνια enkaínia, eng-kah'-ee-nee-ah; neuter plural of a presumed compound from G1722 and G2537; innovatives,
 i.e. (specially) renewal (of religious services after the Antiochian
 interruption):—dedication.

G1457.definition: ἐγκαινίζω enkainízō, eng-kahee-nid'-zo; from G1456; to renew, i.e. inaugurate:—consecrate, dedicate.

G1458.definition:
ἐγκαλέω enkaléō, eng-kal-eh'-o; from G1722 and G2564; to call in (as a debt or demand), i.e. bring to
 account (charge, criminate, etc.):—accuse, call in question, implead,
 lay to the charge.

G1459.definition:
ἐγκαταλείπω enkataleípō, eng-kat-al-i'-po; from G1722 and G2641; to leave behind in some place, i.e. (in a good
 sense) let remain over, or (in a bad sense) to desert:—forsake,
 leave.

G146.definition:
αἰσχροκερδής aischrokerdḗs, ahee-skhrok-er-dace'; from G150 and κέρδος kérdos (gain); sordid:—given to (greedy of) filthy
 lucre.

G1460.definition:
ἐγκατοικέω enkatoikéō, eng-kat-oy-keh'-o; from G1722 and G2730; to settle down in a place, i.e. reside:—dwell
 among.

G1461.definition:
ἐγκεντρίζω enkentrízō, eng-ken-trid'-zo; from G1722 and a derivative of G2759; to prick in, i.e. ingraft:—graff
 in(-to).

G1462.definition:
ἔγκλημα énklēma, eng'-klay-mah; from G1458; an accusation, i.e. offence alleged:—crime laid against,
 laid to charge.

G1463.definition:
ἐγκομβόομαι enkombóomai, eng-kom-bo'-om-ahee; middle voice from G1722 and κομβόω kombóō (to gird); to engirdle oneself (for
 labor), i.e. figuratively (the apron as being a badge of servitude) to
 wear (in token of mutual deference):—be clothed with.

G1464.definition: ἐγκοπή enkopḗ, eng-kop-ay'; from G1465; a hindrance:—X hinder.

G1465.definition:
ἐγκόπτω enkóptō, eng-kop'-to; from G1722 and G2875; to cut into, i.e. (figuratively) impede,
 detain:—hinder, be tedious unto.

G1466.definition: ἐγκράτεια enkráteia, eng-krat'-i-ah; from G1468; self-control (especially continence):—temperance.

G1467.definition:
ἐγκρατεύομαι enkrateúomai, eng-krat-yoo'-om-ahee; middle voice from G1468; to exercise self-restraint (in diet and
 chastity):—can(-not) contain, be temperate.

G1468.definition:
ἐγκρατής enkratḗs, eng-krat-ace'; from G1722 and G2904; strong in a thing (masterful), i.e. (figuratively
 and reflexively) self-controlled (in appetite, etc.):—temperate.

G1469.definition:
ἐγκρίνω enkrínō, eng-kree'-no; from G1722 and G2919; to judge in, i.e. count among:—make of the
 number.

G147.definition: αἰσχροκερδῶς aischrokerdōs, ahee-skhrok-er-doce'; adverb from G146; sordidly:—for filthy lucre's sake.

G1470.definition: ἐγκρύπτω enkrýptō, eng-kroop'-to; from G1722 and G2928; to conceal in, i.e. incorporate with:—hid in.

G1471.definition:
ἔγκυος énkyos, eng'-koo-os; from G1722 and the base of G2949; swelling inside, i.e. pregnant:—great
 with child.

G1472.definition: ἐγχρίω enchríō, eng-khree'-o; from G1722 and G5548; to rub in (oil), i.e. besmear:—anoint.

G1473.definition:
ἐγώ egṓ, eg-o'; a primary pronoun of the first person I (only expressed when
 emphatic):—I, me. For the other cases and the plural see G1691, G1698,
 G1700, G2248, G2249, G2254, G2257, etc.

G1474.definition: ἐδαφίζω edaphízō, ed-af-id'-zo; from G1475; to raze:—lay even with the ground.

G1475.definition: ἔδαφος édaphos, ed'-af-os; from the base of G1476; a basis (bottom), i.e. the soil:—ground.

G1476.definition:
ἑδραῖος hedraîos, hed-rah'-yos; from a derivative of ἕζομαι hézomai (to sit); sedentary, i.e. (by
 implication) immovable:—settled, stedfast.

G1477.definition:
ἑδραίωμα hedraíōma, hed-rah'-yo-mah; from a derivative of G1476; a support, i.e. (figuratively)
 basis:—ground.

G1478.definition:
Ἐζεκίας Ezekías, ed-zek-ee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H2396); Ezekias (i.e. Hezekeiah), an
 Israelite:—Ezekias.

G1479.definition:
†ἐθελοθρησκεία ethelothrēskeía, eth-el-oth-race-ki'-ah; from G2309 and G2356; voluntary (arbitrary and unwarranted) piety, i.e.
 sanctimony:—will worship.

G148.definition: αἰσχρολογία aischrología, ahee-skhrol-og-ee'-ah; from G150 and G3056; vile conversation:—filthy communication.

G1480.definition:
ἐθίζω ethízō, eth-id'-zo; from G1485; to accustom, i.e. (neuter passive participle)
 customary:—custom.

G1481.definition: ἐθνάρχης ethnárchēs, eth-nar'-khace; from G1484 and G746; the governor (not king) of a district:—ethnarch.

G1482.definition:
ἐθνικός ethnikós, eth-nee-kos'; from G1484; national ("ethnic"), i.e. (specially) a Gentile:—heathen
 (man).

G1483.definition: ἐθνικῶς ethnikōs, eth-nee-koce'; adverb from G1482; as a Gentile:—after the manner of Gentiles.

G1485.definition:
ἔθος éthos, eth'-os; from G1486; a usage (prescribed by habit or law):—custom, manner, be
 wont.

G1487.definition:
εἰ ei, i; a primary particle of conditionality; if, whether, that,
 etc.:—forasmuch as, if, that, (al-)though, whether. Often used in
 connection or composition with other particles, especially as in G1489,
 G1490, G1499, G1508, G1509, G1512, G1513, G1536, G1537. See also G1437.

G1490.definition:
εἰ δὲ μή(γε) ei dè mḗ(ge), i deh may'-(gheh); from G1487, G1161, and G3361 (sometimes with G1065 added); but if
 not:—(or) else, if (not, otherwise), otherwise.

G1491.definition:
εἶδος eîdos, i'-dos; from G1492; a view, i.e. form (literally or figuratively):—appearance,
 fashion, shape, sight.

G1492.definition:
†εἴδω eídō, i'-do; a primary verb; used only in certain past tenses, the others being
 borrowed from the equivalent G3700 and G3708; properly, to see
 (literally or figuratively); by implication, (in the perfect tense
 only) to know:—be aware, behold, × can (+ not tell), consider, (have)
 know(-ledge), look (on), perceive, see, be sure, tell, understand,
 wish, wot. Compare G3700.

G1493.definition:
εἰδωλεῖον eidōleîon, i-do-li'-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G1497; an image-fane:—idol's
 temple.

G1494.definition:
†εἰδωλόθυτον eidōlóthyton, i-do-loth'-oo-ton; neuter of a compound of G1497 and a presumed derivative of G2380; an
 image-sacrifice, i.e. part of an idolatrous offering:—(meat, thing
 that is) offered (in sacrifice, sacrificed) to (unto) idols.

G1495.definition:
†εἰδωλολατρεία eidōlolatreía, i-do-lol-at-ri'-ah; from G1497 and G2999; image-worship (literally or
 figuratively):—idolatry.

G1496.definition:
εἰδωλολάτρης eidōlolátrēs, i-do-lol-at'-race; from G1497 and the base of G3000; an image- (servant or) worshipper
 (literally or figuratively):—idolater.

G1497.definition:
εἴδωλον eídōlon, i'-do-lon; from G1491; an image (i.e. for worship); by implication, a heathen god,
 or (plural) the worship of such:—idol.

G1498.definition:
†εἴην eíēn, i'-ane; optative (i.e. English subjunctive) present of G1510 (including the
 other person); might (could, would, or should) be:—mean, + perish,
 should be, was, were.

G15.definition:
ἀγαθοποιέω agathopoiéō, ag-ath-op-oy-eh'-o; from G17; to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty):—(when) do good
 (well).

G150.definition: αἰσχρός aischrós, ahee-skhros'; from the same as G153; shameful, i.e. base (specially, venal):—filthy.

G1500.definition:
εἰκῆ eikē, i-kay'; probably from G1502 (through the idea of failure); idly, i.e. without
 reason (or effect):—without a cause, (in) vain(-ly).

G1501.definition: εἴκοσι eíkosi, i'-kos-ee; of uncertain affinity; a score:—twenty.

G1502.definition:
εἴκω eíkō, i'-ko; apparently a primary verb; properly, to be weak, i.e. yield:—give
 place.

G1504.definition:
εἰκών eikṓn, i-kone'; from G1503; a likeness, i.e. (literally) statue, profile, or
 (figuratively) representation, resemblance:—image.

G1505.definition:
εἰλικρίνεια eilikríneia, i-lik-ree'-ni-ah; from G1506; clearness, i.e. (by implication) purity
 (figuratively):—sincerity.

G1506.definition:
εἰλικρινής eilikrinḗs, i-lik-ree-nace'; from εἵλη heílē (the sun's ray) and G2919; judged by sunlight, i.e. tested
 as genuine (figuratively):—pure, sincere.

G151.definition: αἰσχρότης aischrótēs, ahee-skhrot'-ace; from G150; shamefulness, i.e. obscenity:—filthiness.

G1510.definition:
εἰμί eimí, i-mee'; the first person singular present indicative; a prolonged form of a
 primary and defective verb; I exist (used only when emphatic):—am,
 have been, × it is I, was. See also G1488, G1498, G1511, G1527, G2258,
 G2071, G2070, G2075, G2076, G2771, G2468, G5600.

G1511.definition:
εἶναι eînai, i'-nahee; present infinitive from G1510; to exist:—am, was. come, is, × lust
 after, × please well, there is, to be, was.

G1512.definition: εἴ περ eí per, i per; from G1487 and G4007; if perhaps:—if so be (that), seeing, though.

G1514.definition:
εἰρηνεύω eirēneúō, i-rane-yoo'-o; from G1515; to be (act) peaceful:—be at (have, live in) peace, live
 peaceably.

G1515.definition:
εἰρήνη eirḗnē, i-ray'-nay; probably from a primary verb εἴρω eírō (to join); peace (literally or
 figuratively); by implication, prosperity:—one, peace, quietness,
 rest, + set at one again.

G1516.definition: εἰρηνικός eirēnikós, i-ray-nee-kos'; from G1515; pacific; by implication, salutary:—peaceable.

G1517.definition:
εἰρηνοποιέω eirēnopoiéō, i-ray-nop-oy-eh'-o; from G1518; to be a peace-maker, i.e. (figuratively) to
 harmonize:—make peace.

G1518.definition:
εἰρηνοποιός eirēnopoiós, i-ray-nop-oy-os'; from G1515 and G4160; pacificatory, i.e. (subjectively)
 peaceable:—peacemaker.

G1519.definition:
εἰς eis, ice; a primary preposition; to or into (indicating the point reached or
 entered), of place, time, or (figuratively) purpose (result, etc.);
 also in adverbial phrases:—(abundant-)ly, against, among, as, at,
 (back-)ward, before, by, concerning, + continual, + far more
 exceeding, for (intent, purpose), fore,
 + forth, in (among, at, unto, -so much that, -to), to the
 intent that, + of one mind, + never, of, (up-)on, + perish, + set at
 one again, (so) that, therefore(-unto), throughout, til, to (be, the
 end, -ward), (here-)until(-to), …ward, (where-)fore, with.

G152.definition:
αἰσχύνη aischýnē, ahee-skhoo'-nay; from G153; shame or disgrace (abstractly or concretely):—dishonesty,
 shame.

G1520.definition:
