G2035.definition: ἑπτακισχίλιοι heptakischílioi, hep-tak-is-khil'-ee-oy; from G2034 and G5507; seven times a thousand:—seven thousand.

G2036.definition:
ἔπω épō, ep'-o; a primary verb (used only in the definite past tense, the others being
 borrowed from G2046, G4483, and G5346); to speak or say (by word or
 writing):—answer, bid, bring word, call, command, grant, say (on),
 speak, tell. Compare G3004.

G2037.definition: Ἔραστος Érastos, er'-as-tos; from ἐράω eráō (to love); beloved; Erastus, a Christian:—Erastus.

G2038.definition:
ἐργάζομαι ergázomai, er-gad'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G2041; to toil (as a task, occupation, etc.), (by
 implication) effect, be engaged in or with, etc.:—commit, do, labor
 for, minister about, trade (by), work.

G2039.definition:
ἐργασία ergasía, er-gas-ee'-ah; from G2040; occupation; by implication, profit, pains:—craft,
 diligence, gain, work.

G204.definition: ἀκρογωνιαῖος akrogōniaîos, ak-rog-o-nee-ah'-yos; from G206 and G1137; belonging to the extreme corner:—chief corner.

G2040.definition: ἐργάτης ergátēs, er-gat'-ace; from G2041; a toiler; figuratively, a teacher:—labourer, worker(-men).

G2041.definition:
ἔργον érgon, er'-gon; from a primary (but obsolete) ἔργω érgō (to work); toil (as an effort or
 occupation); by implication, an act:—deed, doing, labour, work.

G2042.definition:
ἐρεθίζω erethízō, er-eth-id'-zo; from a presumed prolonged form of G2054; to stimulate (especially to
 anger):—provoke.

G2043.definition:
ἐρείδω ereídō, er-i'-do; of obscure affinity; to prop, i.e. (reflexively) get fast:—stick
 fast.

G2044.definition:
ἐρεύγομαι ereúgomai, er-yoog'-om-ahee; of uncertain affinity; to belch, i.e. (figuratively) to speak
 out:—utter.

G2047.definition: ἐρημία erēmía, er-ay-mee'-ah; from G2048; solitude (concretely):—desert, wilderness.

G2048.definition:
ἔρημος érēmos, er'-ay-mos; of uncertain affinity; lonesome, i.e. (by implication) waste (usually
 as a noun, G5561 being implied):—desert, desolate, solitary,
 wilderness.

G2049.definition:
ἐρημόω erēmóō, er-ay-mo'-o; from G2048; to lay waste (literally or figuratively):—(bring to, make)
 desolate(-ion), come to nought.

G205.definition:
ἀκροθίνιον akrothínion, ak-roth-in'-ee-on; from G206 and θίς thís (a heap); properly (in the plural) the top of the
 heap, i.e. (by implication) best of the booty:—spoils.

G2050.definition: ἐρήμωσις erḗmōsis, er-ay'-mo-sis; from G2049; despoliation:—desolation.

G2051.definition: ἐρίζω erízō, er-id'-zo; from G2054; to wrangle:—strive.

G2052.definition:
ἐριθεία eritheía, er-ith-i'-ah; perhaps as the same as G2042; properly, intrigue, i.e. (by implication)
 faction:—contention(-ious), strife.

G2053.definition: ἔριον érion, er'-ee-on; of obscure affinity; wool:—wool.

G2054.definition:
ἔρις éris, er'-is; of uncertain affinity; a quarrel, i.e. (by implication)
 wrangling:—contention, debate, strife, variance.

G2055.definition:
ἐρίφιον eríphion, er-if'-ee-on; from G2056; a kidling, i.e. (genitive case) goat (symbolically, wicked
 person):—goat.

G2056.definition:
ἔριφος ériphos, er'-if-os; perhaps from the same as G2053 (through the idea of hairiness); a kid
 or (genitive case) goat:—goat, kid.

G2057.definition: Ἑρμᾶς Hermâs, her-mas'; probably from G2060; Hermas, a Christian:—Hermas.

G2058.definition: ἑρμηνεία hermēneía, her-may-ni'-ah; from the same as G2059; translation:—interpretation.

G2059.definition:
ἑρμηνεύω hermēneúō, her-mayn-yoo'-o; from a presumed derivative of G2060 (as the god of language); to
 translate:—interpret.

G206.definition:
ἄκρον ákron, ak'-ron; neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of G188; the
 extremity:—one end… other, tip, top, uttermost participle

G2060.definition:
Ἑρμῆς Hermēs, her-mace'; perhaps from G2046; Hermes, the name of the messenger of the Greek
 deities; also of a Christian:—Hermes, Mercury.

G2061.definition:
Ἑρμογένης Hermogénēs, her-mog-en'-ace; from G2060 and G1096; born of Hermes; Hermogenes, an apostate
 Christian:—Hermogenes.

G2062.definition:
ἑρπετόν herpetón, her-pet-on'; neuter of a derivative of ἕρπω hérpō (to creep); a reptile, i.e. (by
 Hebraism (compare H7431)) a small animal:—creeping thing, serpent.

G2063.definition: ἐρυθρός erythrós, er-oo-thros'; of uncertain affinity; red, i.e. (with G2281) the Red Sea:—red.

G2064.definition:
ἔρχομαι érchomai, er'-khom-ahee; middle voice of a primary verb 

 (used only in the present and imperfect tenses, the others being 
 supplied by a kindred (middle voice)
    
    ἐλεύθομαι eleúthomai  el-yoo'-thom-ahee,  or (active)
    ἔλθω élthō  el'-tho,
    
 which do not otherwise occur); 

 to come or go (in a great variety of applications, literally and 
 figuratively):—accompany, appear, bring, come, enter, fall out, go,
 grow, × light, × next, pass, resort, be set.

G2065.definition:
ἐρωτάω erōtáō, er-o-tah'-o; apparently from G2046 (compare G2045); to interrogate; by implication,
 to request:—ask, beseech, desire, intreat, pray. Compare G4441.

G2066.definition: ἐσθής esthḗs, es-thace'; from ἕννυμι hénnymi (to clothe); dress:—apparel, clothing, raiment, robe.

G2068.definition:
†ἐσθίω esthíō, es-thee'-o; strengthened for a primary ἔδω édō (to eat); used only in certain tenses,
 the rest being supplied by G5315; to eat (usually literal):—devour,
 eat, live.

G2069.definition: Ἐσλί Eslí, es-lee'; of Hebrew origin (probably for H454); Esli, an Israelite:—Esli.

G207.definition: Ἀκύλας Akýlas, ak-oo'-las; probably for Latin aquila (an eagle); Akulas, an Israelite:—Aquila.

G2070.definition:
ἐσμέν esmén, es-men'; first person plural indicative of G1510; we are:—are, be, have our
 being, × have hope, + (the gospel) was (preached unto) us.

G2071.definition:
ἔσομαι ésomai, es'-om-ahee; future of G1510; will be:—shall (should) be (have), (shall) come (to
 pass), × may have, × fall, what would follow, × live long, × sojourn.

G2072.definition:
ἔσοπτρον ésoptron, es'-op-tron; from G1519 and a presumed derivative of G3700; a mirror (for looking
 into):—glass. Compare G2734.

G2073.definition:
ἑσπέρα hespéra, hes-per'-ah; feminine of an adjective hesperos (evening); the eve (G5610 being
 implied):—evening(-tide).

G2074.definition: Ἐσρώμ Esrṓm, es-rome; of Hebrew origin (H2696); Esrom (i.e. Chetsron), an Israelite:—Esrom.

G2075.definition:
ἐστέ esté, es-teh'; second person plural present indicative of G1510; ye are:—be, have
 been, belong.

G2076.definition:
ἐστί estí, es-tee'; third person singular present indicative of G1510; he (she or it) is;
 also (with neuter plural) they are:—are, be(-long), call, X
 can(-not), come, consisteth, × dure for a while, + follow, × have,
 (that) is (to say), make, meaneth, × must needs, + profit, +
 remaineth, + wrestle.

G2079.definition:
ἐσχάτως eschátōs, es-khat'-oce; adverb from G2078; finally, i.e. (with G2192) at the extremity of
 life:—point of death.

G208.definition:
ἀκυρόω akyróō, ak-oo-ro'-o; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2964; to invalidate:—disannul,
 make of none effect.

G2080.definition:
ἔσω ésō, es'-o; from G1519; inside (as preposition or adjective):—(with-)in(-ner,
 -to, -ward).

G2081.definition:
ἔσωθεν ésōthen, es'-o-then; from G2080; from inside; also used as equivalent to G2080
 (inside):—inward(-ly), (from) within, without.

G2082.definition: ἐσώτερος esṓteros, es-o'-ter-os; comparative of G2080; interior:—inner, within.

G2083.definition: ἑταῖρος hetaîros, het-ah'-ee-ros; from ἔτης étēs (a clansman); a comrade:—fellow, friend.

G2084.definition:
ἑτερόγλωσσος heteróglōssos, het-er-og'-loce-sos; from G2087 and G1100; other- tongued, i.e. a foreigner:—man of other
 tongue.

G2085.definition:
ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω heterodidaskaléō, het-er-od-id-as-kal-eh'-o; from G2087 and G1320; to instruct differently:—teach other
 doctrine(-wise).

G2086.definition:
ἑτεροζυγέω heterozygéō, het-er-od-zoog-eh'-o; from a compound of G2087 and G2218; to yoke up differently, i.e.
 (figuratively) to associate discordantly:—unequally yoke together
 with.

G2087.definition:
ἕτερος héteros, het'-er-os; of uncertain affinity; (an-, the) other or different:—altered, else,
 next (day), one, (an-)other, some, strange.

G2088.definition: ἑτέρως hetérōs, het-er'-oce; adverb from G2087; differently:—otherwise.

G2089.definition:
ἔτι éti, et'-ee; perhaps akin to G2094; "yet," still (of time or degree):—after that,
 also, ever, (any) further, (t-)henceforth (more), hereafter, (any)
 longer, (any) more(-one), now, still, yet.

G209.definition:
ἀκωλύτως akōlýtōs, ak-o-loo'-toce; adverb from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative
 of G2967; in an unhindered manner, i.e. freely:—no man forbidding him.

G2090.definition: ἑτοιμάζω hetoimázō, het-oy-mad'-zo; from G2092; to prepare:—prepare, provide, make ready. Compare G2680.

G2091.definition: ἑτοιμασία hetoimasía, het-oy-mas-ee'-ah; from G2090; preparation:—preparation.

G2092.definition:
ἕτοιμος hétoimos, het-oy'-mos; from an old noun ἐτεός eteós (fitness); adjusted, i.e. ready:—prepared,
 (made) ready(-iness, to our hand).

G2093.definition: ἑτοίμως hetoímōs, het'-oy-moce; adverb from G2092; in readiness:—ready.

G2094.definition: ἔτος étos, et'-os; apparently a primary word; a year:—year.

G2095.definition:
†εὖ eû, yoo; neuter of a primary εὖς eûs (good); (adverbially) well:—good, well
 (done).

G2096.definition:
†Εὖα Eûa, yoo'-ah; of Hebrew origin (H2332); Eua (or Eva, i.e. Chavvah), the first
 woman:—Eve.

G2097.definition:
εὐαγγελίζω euangelízō, yoo-ang-ghel-id'-zo; from G2095 and G32; to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the
 gospel:—declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach
 (the gospel).

G2098.definition: εὐαγγέλιον euangélion, yoo-ang-ghel'-ee-on; from the same as G2097; a good message, i.e. the gospel:—gospel.

G2099.definition: εὐαγγελιστής euangelistḗs, yoo-ang-ghel-is-tace'; from G2097; a preacher of the gospel:—evangelist.

G21.definition:
ἀγαλλιάω agalliáō, ag-al-lee-ah'-o; from agan (much) and G242; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult:—be
 (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly).

G210.definition:
ἄκων ákōn, ak'-ohn; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1635; unwilling:—against the
 will.

G2100.definition: εὐαρεστέω euarestéō, yoo-ar-es-teh'-o; from G2101; to gratify entirely:—please (well).

G2101.definition: εὐάρεστος euárestos, yoo-ar'-es-tos; from G2095 and G701; fully agreeable:—acceptable(-ted), wellpleasing.

G2102.definition: εὐαρέστως euaréstōs, yoo-ar-es'-toce; adverb from G2101; quite agreeably:—acceptably, + please well.

G2103.definition: Εὔβουλος Eúboulos, yoo'-boo-los; from G2095 and G1014; good-willer; Eubulus, a Christian:—Eubulus.

G2104.definition:
†εὐγενής eugenḗs, yoog-en'-ace; from G2095 and G1096; well born, i.e. (literally) high in rank, or
 (figuratively) generous:—more noble, nobleman.

G2105.definition:
εὐδία eudía, yoo-dee'-ah; feminine from G2095 and the alternate of G2203 (as the god of the
 weather); a clear sky, i.e. fine weather:—fair weather.

G2107.definition:
εὐδοκία eudokía, yoo-dok-ee'-ah; from a presumed compound of G2095 and the base of G1380; satisfaction,
 i.e. (subjectively) delight, or (objectively) kindness, wish,
 purpose:—desire, good pleasure (will), × seem good.

G2108.definition:
εὐεργεσία euergesía, yoo-erg-es-ee'-ah; from G2110; beneficence (genitive case or specially):—benefit, good
 deed done.

G2109.definition: εὐεργετέω euergetéō, yoo-erg-et-eh'-o; from G2110; to be philanthropic:—do good.

G2110.definition:
εὐεργέτης euergétēs, yoo-erg-et'-ace; from G2095 and the base of G2041; a worker of good, i.e. (specially) a
 philanthropist:—benefactor.

G2111.definition:
εὔθετος eúthetos, yoo'-thet-os; from G2095 and a derivative of G5087; well placed, i.e. (figuratively)
 appropriate:—fit, meet.

G2112.definition:
εὐθέως euthéōs, yoo-theh'-oce; adverb from G2117; directly, i.e. at once or soon:—anon, as soon as,
 forthwith, immediately, shortly, straightway.

G2113.definition:
εὐθυδρομέω euthydroméō, yoo-thoo-drom-eh'-o; from G2117 and G1408; to lay a straight course, i.e. sail
 direct:—(come) with a straight course.

G2114.definition:
εὐθυμέω euthyméō, yoo-thoo-meh'-o; from G2115; to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter
 comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully:—be of good cheer (merry).

G2115.definition:
†εὔθυμος eúthymos, yoo'-thoo-mos; from G2095 and G2372; in fine spirits, i.e. cheerful:—of good cheer,
 the more cheerfully.

G2116.definition:
εὐθύνω euthýnō, yoo-thoo'-no; from G2117; to straighten (level); technically, to steer:—governor,
 make straight.

G2117.definition:
†εὐθύς euthýs, yoo-thoos'; perhaps from G2095 and G5087; straight, i.e. (literally) level, or
 (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once:—anon, by and by,
 forthwith, immediately, straightway.

G2118.definition: εὐθύτης euthýtēs, yoo-thoo'-tace; from G2117; rectitude:—righteousness.

G2119.definition:
εὐκαιρέω eukairéō, yoo-kahee-reh'-o; from G2121; to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure:—have
 leisure (convenient time), spend time.

G212.definition:
ἀλαζονεία alazoneía, al-ad-zon-i'-a; from G213; braggadocio, i.e. (by implication)
 self-confidence:—boasting, pride.

G2120.definition: εὐκαιρία eukairía, yoo-kahee-ree'-ah; from G2121; a favorable occasion:—opportunity.

G2121.definition:
εὔκαιρος eúkairos, yoo'-kahee-ros; from G2095 and G2540; well-timed, i.e. opportune:—convenient, in time
 of need.

G2122.definition: εὐκαίρως eukaírōs, yoo-kah'-ee-roce; adverb from G2121; opportunely:—conveniently, in season.

G2123.definition:
εὐκοπώτερος eukopṓteros, yoo-kop-o'-ter-os; comparative of a compound of G2095 and G2873; better for toil, i.e. more
 facile:—easier.

G2124.definition:
εὐλάβεια eulábeia, yoo-lab'-i-ah; from G2126; properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by
 implication, dread (concretely):—fear(-ed).

G2125.definition:
εὐλαβέομαι eulabéomai, yoo-lab-eh'-om-ahee; middle voice from G2126; to be circumspect, i.e. (by implication) to be
 apprehensive; religiously, to reverence:—(moved with) fear.

G2126.definition:
εὐλαβής eulabḗs, yoo-lab-ace'; from G2095 and G2983; taking well (carefully), i.e. circumspect
 (religiously, pious):—devout.

G2127.definition:
†εὐλογέω eulogéō, yoo-log-eh'-o; from a compound of G2095 and G3056; to speak well of, i.e. (religiously)
 to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper):—bless,
 praise.

G2128.definition: εὐλογητός eulogētós, yoo-log-ay-tos'; from G2127; adorable:—blessed.

G2129.definition:
εὐλογία eulogía, yoo-log-ee'-ah; from the same as G2127; fine speaking, i.e. elegance of language;
 commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously,
 benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or
 largess:—blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech.

G213.definition: ἀλαζών alazṓn, al-ad-zone'; from ἄλη álē (vagrancy); braggart:—boaster.

G2130.definition:
εὐμετάδοτος eumetádotos, yoo-met-ad'-ot-os; from G2095 and a presumed derivative of G3330; good at imparting, i.e.
 liberal:—ready to distribute.

G2131.definition: Εὐνίκη Euníkē, yoo-nee'-kay; from G2095 and G3529; victorious; Eunice, a Jewess:—Eunice.

G2132.definition:
εὐνοέω eunoéō, yoo-no-eh'-o; from a compound of G2095 and G3563; to be well- minded, i.e.
 reconcile:—agree.

G2133.definition:
εὔνοια eúnoia, yoo'-noy-ah; from the same as G2132; kindness; euphemistically, conjugal
 duty:—benevolence, good will.

G2134.definition: εὐνουχίζω eunouchízō, yoo-noo-khid'-zo; from G2135; to castrate (figuratively, live unmarried):—make…eunuch.

G2135.definition:
εὐνοῦχος eunoûchos, yoo-noo'-khos; from εὐνή eunḗ (a bed) and G2192; a castrated person (such being employed in
 Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by
 implication, a chamberlain (state-officer):—eunuch.

G2136.definition:
†Εὐοδία Euodía, yoo-od-ee'-ah; from the same as G2137; fine travelling; Euodia, a Christian
 woman:—Euodias.

G2137.definition:
εὐοδόω euodóō, yoo-od-o'-o; from a compound of G2095 and G3598; to help on the road, i.e.
 (passively) succeed in reaching; figuratively, to succeed in business
 affairs:—(have a) prosper(-ous journey).

G2138.definition:
εὐπειθής eupeithḗs, yoo-pi-thace'; from G2095 and G3982; good for persuasion, i.e. (intransitively)
 compliant:—easy to be intreated.

G2139.definition:
εὐπερίστατος euperístatos, yoo-per-is'-tat-os; from G2095 and a derivative of a presumed compound of G4012 and G2476; 
 well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every
 direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case):—which doth so
 easily beset.

G214.definition:
ἀλαλάζω alalázō, al-al-ad'-zo; from ἀλαλή alalḗ ( a shout, "halloo"); to vociferate, i.e. (by implication)
 to wail; figuratively, to clang:—tinkle, wail.

G2140.definition:
εὐποιΐα eupoiḯa, yoo-poy-ee'-ah; from a compound of G2095 and G4160; well-doing, i.e. beneficence:—to do
 good.

G2141.definition:
εὐπορέω euporéō, yoo-por-eh'-o; from a compound of G2090 and the base of G4197; (intransitively) to be
 good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary
 means:—ability.

G2142.definition: εὐπορία euporía, yoo-por-ee'-ah; from the same as G2141; pecuniary resources:—wealth.

G2143.definition:
εὐπρέπεια euprépeia, yoo-prep'-i-ah; from a compound of G2095 and G4241; good suitableness, i.e.
 gracefulness:—grace.

G2144.definition:
εὐπρόσδεκτος euprósdektos, yoo-pros'-dek-tos; from G2095 and a derivative of G4327; well-received, i.e. approved,
 favorable:—acceptable(-ted).

G2146.definition:
εὐπροσωπέω euprosōpéō, yoo-pros-o-peh'-o; from a compound of G2095 and G4383; to be of good countenance, i.e.
 (figuratively) to make a display:—make a fair show.

G2147.definition:
εὑρίσκω heurískō, hyoo-ris'-ko; a prolonged form of a primary
    
    εὕρω heúrō  hyoo'-ro,   which 
                (together with another cognate form)
    
    εὑρέω heuréō  hyoo-reh'-o  is used for it in all the tenses
                except the present and imperfect; 

 to find (literally or figuratively):—find, get, obtain, perceive,
 see.

G2149.definition: εὐρύχωρος eurýchōros, yoo-roo'-kho-ros; from εὐρύς eurýs (wide) and G5561; spacious:—broad.

G215.definition:
ἀλάλητος alálētos, al-al'-ay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2980; 
 unspeakable:—unutterable, which cannot be uttered.

G2150.definition: εὐσέβεια eusébeia, yoo-seb'-i-ah; from G2152; piety; specially, the gospel scheme:—godliness, holiness.

G2151.definition:
εὐσεβέω eusebéō, yoo-seb-eh'-o; from G2152; to be pious, i.e. (towards God) to worship, or (towards
 parents) to respect (support):—show piety, worship.

G2152.definition: εὐσεβής eusebḗs, yoo-seb-ace'; from G2095 and G4576; well-reverent, i.e. pious:—devout, godly.

G2153.definition: εὐσεβῶς eusebōs, yoo-seb-oce'; adverb from G2152; piously:—godly.

G2154.definition:
εὔσημος eúsēmos, yoo'-say-mos; from G2095 and the base of G4591; well indicated, i.e. (figuratively)
 significant:—easy to be understood.

G2155.definition:
εὔσπλαγχνος eúsplanchnos, yoo'-splangkh-nos; from G2095 and G4698; well compassioned, i.e. sympathetic:—pitiful,
 tender-hearted.

G2156.definition: εὐσχημόνως euschēmónōs, yoo-skhay-mon'-ose; adverb from G2158; decorously:—decently, honestly.

G2157.definition: εὐσχημοσύνη euschēmosýnē, yoo-skhay-mos-oo'-nay; from G2158; decorousness:—comeliness.

G2158.definition:
εὐσχήμων euschḗmōn, yoo-skhay'-mone; from G2095 and G4976; well-formed, i.e. (figuratively) decorous, noble
 (in rank):—comely, honourable.

G216.definition: ἄλαλος álalos, al'-al-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2980; mute:—dumb.

G2160.definition:
εὐτραπελία eutrapelía, yoo-trap-el-ee'-ah; from a compound of G2095 and a derivative of the base of G5157 (meaning
 well-turned, i.e. ready at repartee, jocose); witticism, i.e. (in a
 vulgar sense) ribaldry:—jesting.

G2161.definition:
Εὔτυχος Eútychos, yoo'-too-khos; from G2095 and a derivative of G5177; well- fated, i.e. fortunate;
 Eutychus, a young man:—Eutychus.

G2162.definition:
εὐφημία euphēmía, yoo-fay-mee'-ah; from G2163; good language ("euphemy"), i.e. praise (repute):—good
 report.

G2163.definition: εὔφημος eúphēmos, yoo'-fay-mos; from G2095 and G5345; well spoken of, i.e. reputable:—of good report.

G2164.definition:
εὐφορέω euphoréō, yoo-for-eh'-o; from G2095 and G5409; to bear well, i.e. be fertile:—bring forth
 abundantly.

G2165.definition:
εὐφραίνω euphraínō, yoo-frah'-ee-no; from G2095 and G5424; to put (middle voice or passively, be) in a good
 frame of mind, i.e. rejoice:—fare, make glad, be (make) merry,
 rejoice.

G2166.definition:
Εὐφράτης Euphrátēs, yoo-frat'-ace; of foreign origin (compare H6578); Euphrates, a river of
 Asia:—Euphrates.

G2167.definition: εὐφροσύνη euphrosýnē, yoo-fros-oo'-nay; from the same as G2165; joyfulness:—gladness, joy.

G2168.definition:
εὐχαριστέω eucharistéō, yoo-khar-is-teh'-o; from G2170; to be grateful, i.e. (actively) to express gratitude
 (towards); specially, to say grace at a meal:—(give) thank(-ful, -s).

G2169.definition:
εὐχαριστία eucharistía, yoo-khar-is-tee'-ah; from G2170; gratitude; actively, grateful language (to God, as an act
 of worship):—thankfulness, (giving of) thanks(-giving).

G217.definition: †ἅλας hálas, hal'-as; from G251; salt; figuratively, prudence:—salt.

G2170.definition:
εὐχάριστος eucháristos, yoo-khar'-is-tos; from G2095 and a derivative of G5483; well favored, i.e. (by
 implication) grateful:—thankful.

G2171.definition:
εὐχή euchḗ, yoo-khay'; from G2172; properly, a wish, expressed as a petition to God, or in
 votive obligation:—prayer, vow.

G2172.definition:
εὔχομαι eúchomai, yoo'-khom-ahee; middle voice of a primary verb; to wish; by implication, to pray to
 God:—pray, will, wish.

G2173.definition:
εὔχρηστος eúchrēstos, yoo'-khrays-tos; from G2095 and G5543; easily used, i.e. useful:—profitable, meet for
 use.

G2174.definition:
εὐψυχέω eupsychéō, yoo-psoo-kheh'-o; from a compound of G2095 and G5590; to be in good spirits, i.e. feel
 encouraged:—be of good comfort.

G2175.definition:
εὐωδία euōdía, yoo-o-dee'-ah; from a compound of G2095 and a derivative of G3605; good-scentedness,
 i.e. fragrance:—sweet savour (smell, -smelling).

G2176.definition:
εὐώνυμος euṓnymos, yoo-o'-noo-mos; from G2095 and G3686; properly, well-named (good-omened), i.e. the left
 (which was the lucky side among the pagan Greeks); neuter as
 adverbial, at the left hand:—(on the) left.

G2177.definition: ἐφάλλομαι ephállomai, ef-al'-lom-ahee; from G1909 and G242; to spring upon:—leap on.

G2178.definition: ἐφάπαξ ephápax, ef-ap'-ax; from G1909 and G530; upon one occasion (only):—(at) once (for all).

G218.definition:
ἀλείφω aleíphō, al-i'-fo; from G1 (as particle of union) and the base of G3045; to oil (with
 perfume):—anoint.

G2180.definition:
Ἐφέσιος Ephésios, ef-es'-ee-os; from G2181; an Ephesian or inhabitant of Ephesus:—Ephesian, of
 Ephesus.

G2181.definition: Ἔφεσος Éphesos, ef'-es-os; probably of foreign origin; Ephesus, a city of Asia Minor:—Ephesus.

G2182.definition:
ἐφευρετής epheuretḗs, ef-yoo-ret'-ace; from a compound of G1909 and G2147; a discoverer, i.e.
 contriver:—inventor.

G2183.definition:
ἐφημερία ephēmería, ef-ay-mer-ee'-ah; from G2184; diurnality, i.e. (specially) the quotidian rotation or
 class of the Jewish priests' service at the Temple, as distributed by
 families:—course.

G2184.definition: ἐφήμερος ephḗmeros, ef-ay'-mer-os; from G1909 and G2250; for a day ("ephemeral"), i.e. diurnal:—daily.

G2185.definition:
ἐφικνέομαι ephiknéomai, ef-ik-neh'-om-ahee; from G1909 and a cognate of G2240; to arrive upon, i.e. extend
 to:—reach.

G2186.definition:
ἐφίστημι ephístēmi, ef-is'-tay-mee; from G1909 and G2476; to stand upon, i.e. be present (in various
 applications, friendly or otherwise, usually literal); --assault, come
 (in, to, unto, upon), be at hand (instant), present, stand (before,
 by, over).

G2187.definition:
†Ἐφραίμ Ephraím, ef-rah-im'; of Hebrew origin (H669 or better H6085); Ephraim, a place in
 Palestine:—Ephraim.

G2188.definition: ἐφφαθά ephphathá, ef-fath-ah'; of Chaldee origin (H6606); be opened!:—Ephphatha.

G2189.definition:
ἔχθρα échthra, ekh'-thrah; feminine of G2190; hostility; by implication, a reason for
 opposition:—enmity, hatred.

G219.definition:
ἀλεκτοροφωνία alektorophōnía, al-ek-tor-of-o-nee'-ah; from G220 and G5456; cock-crow, i.e. the third
 night-watch:—cockcrowing.

G2190.definition:
ἐχθρός echthrós, ech-thros'; from a primary ἔχθω échthō (to hate); hateful (passively, odious, or
 actively, hostile); usually as a noun, an adversary (especially
 Satan):—enemy, foe.

G2191.definition:
ἔχιδνα échidna, ekh'-id-nah; of uncertain origin; an adder or other poisonous snake (literally or
 figuratively):—viper.

G2192.definition:
ἔχω échō, ekh'-o; a primary verb; to hold (used in very various applications, literally
 or figuratively, direct or remote; such as possession; ability,
 contiuity, relation, or condition):—be (able, × hold, possessed
 with), accompany, + begin to amend, can(+ -not), × conceive, count,
 diseased, do + eat, + enjoy, + fear, following, have, hold, keep, +
 lack, + go to law, lie, + must needs, + of necessity, + need, next, +
 recover, + reign, + rest, + return, × sick, take for, + tremble, +
 uncircumcised, use.

G2193.definition:
ἕως héōs, heh'-oce; of uncertain affinity; a conjunction, preposition and adverb of
 continuance, until (of time and place):—even (until, unto), (as) far
 (as), how long, (un-)til(-l), (hither-, un-, up) to, while(-s).

G2194.definition:
Ζαβουλών Zaboulṓn, dzab-oo-lone'; of Hebrew origin (H2074); Zabulon (i.e. Zebulon), a region of
 Palestine:—Zabulon.

G2195.definition: Ζακχαῖος Zakchaîos, dzak-chah'-ee-yos; of Hebrew origin (compare H2140); Zacchæus, an Israelite:—Zacchæus.

G2196.definition: Ζαρά Zará, dzar-ah'; of Hebrew origin (H2226); Zara, (i.e. Zerach), an Israelite:—Zara.

G2197.definition:
Ζαχαρίας Zacharías, dzakh-ar-ee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H2148); Zacharias (i.e. Zechariah), the name of two
 Israelites:—Zacharias.

G2198.definition:
ζάω záō, dzah'-o; a primary verb; to live (literally or figuratively):—life(-time),
 (a-)live(-ly), quick.

G2199.definition: Ζεβεδαῖος Zebedaîos, dzeb-ed-ah'-yos; of Hebrew origin (compare H2067); Zebedæus, an Israelite:—Zebedee.

G22.definition: ἄγαμος ágamos, ag'-am-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1062; unmarried:—unmarried.

G220.definition: ἀλέκτωρ aléktōr, al-ek'-tore; from ἀλέκω alékō (to ward off); a cock or male fowl:—cock.

G2200.definition:
ζεστός zestós, dzes-tos'; from G2204; boiled, i.e. (by implication) calid (figuratively,
 fervent):—hot.

G2201.definition:
ζεῦγος zeûgos, dzyoo'-gos; from the same as G2218; a couple, i.e. a team (of oxen yoked together)
 or brace (of birds tied together):—yoke, pair.

G2202.definition:
ζευκτηρία zeuktēría, dzook-tay-ree'-ah; feminine of a derivative (at the second stage) from the same as G2218; 
 a fastening (tiller-rope):—band.

G2203.definition:
Ζεύς Zeús, dzyooce; of uncertain affinity; in the oblique cases there is used instead of
 it a (probably cognate) name

    Δίς Dís  deece, which is otherwise obsolete;
    
 Zeus or Dis (among the Latins, Jupiter or Jove), the supreme deity of
 the Greeks:—Jupiter.

G2204.definition:
ζέω zéō, dzeh'-o; a primary verb; to be hot (boil, of liquids; or glow, of solids), i.e.
 (figuratively) be fervid (earnest):—be fervent.

G2205.definition:
ζῆλος zēlos, dzay'-los; from G2204; properly, heat, i.e. (figuratively) "zeal" (in a favorable
 sense, ardor; in an unfavorable one, jealousy, as of a husband
 (figuratively, of God), or an enemy, malice):—emulation, envy(-ing),
 fervent mind, indignation, jealousy, zeal.

G2206.definition:
†ζηλόω zēlóō, dzay-lo'-o; from G2205; to have warmth of feeling for or against:—affect, covet
 (earnestly), (have) desire, (move with) envy, be jealous over, (be)
 zealous(-ly affect).

G2207.definition: ζηλωτής zēlōtḗs, dzay-lo-tace'; from G2206; a "zealot":—zealous.

G2209.definition:
ζημία zēmía, dzay-mee'-ah; probably akin to the base of G1150 (through the idea of violence); 
 detriment:—damage, loss.

G221.definition:
Ἀλεξανδρεύς Alexandreús, al-ex-and-reuce'; from Ἀλεξάνδρεια Alexándreia (the city so called); an Alexandreian or inhabitant
 of Alexandria:—of Alexandria, Alexandrian.

G2210.definition:
ζημιόω zēmióō, dzay-mee-o'-o; from G2209; to injure, i.e. (reflexively or passively) to experience
 detriment:—be cast away, receive damage, lose, suffer loss.

G2211.definition:
Ζηνᾶς Zēnâs, dzay-nas'; probably contracted from a poetic form of G2203 and G1435; Jove-given;
 Zenas, a Christian:—Zenas.

G2212.definition:
ζητέω zētéō, dzay-teh'-o; of uncertain affinity; to seek (literally or figuratively); specially,
 (by Hebraism) to worship (God), or (in a bad sense) to plot (against
 life):—be (go) about, desire, endeavour, enquire (for), require, (X
 will) seek (after, for, means). Compare G4441.

G2213.definition:
ζήτημα zḗtēma, dzay'-tay-mah; from G2212; a search (properly concretely), i.e. (in words) a
 debate:—question.

G2214.definition:
†ζήτησις zḗtēsis, dzay'-tay-sis; from G2212; a searching (properly, the act), i.e. a dispute or its
 theme:—question.

G2215.definition: ζιζάνιον zizánion, dziz-an'-ee-on; of uncertain origin; darnel or false grain:—tares.

G2216.definition:
Ζοροβάβελ Zorobábel, dzor-ob-ab'-el; of Hebrew origin (H2216); Zorobabel (i.e. Zerubbabel), an
 Israelite:—Zorobabel.

G2217.definition:
ζόφος zóphos, dzof'-os; akin to the base of G3509; gloom (as shrouding like a
 cloud):—blackness, darkness, mist.

G2218.definition:
ζυγός zygós, dzoo-gos'; from the root of ζεύγνυμι zeúgnymi (to join, especially by a "yoke"); a
 coupling, i.e. (figuratively) servitude (a law or obligation); also
 (literally) the beam of the balance (as connecting the scales):—pair
 of balances, yoke.

G2219.definition: ζύμη zýmē, dzoo'-may; probably from G2204; ferment (as if boiling up):—leaven.

G222.definition:
Ἀλεξανδρῖνος Alexandrînos, al-ex-an-dree'-nos; from the same as G221; Alexandrine, or belonging to Alexandria:—of
 Alexandria.

G2220.definition: ζυμόω zymóō, dzoo-mo'-o; from G2219; to cause to ferment:—leaven.

G2221.definition:
ζωγρέω zōgréō, dzogue-reh'-o; from the same as G2226 and G64; to take alive (make a prisoner of war),
 i.e. (figuratively) to capture or ensnare:—take captive, catch.

G2222.definition:
ζωή zōḗ, dzo-ay'; from G2198; life (literally or figuratively):—life(-time). Compare
 G5590.

G2223.definition:
ζώνη zṓnē, dzo'-nay; probably akin to the base of G2218; a belt; by implication, a
 pocket:—girdle, purse.

G2224.definition: ζώννυμι zṓnnymi, dzone'-noo-mi; from G2223; to bind about (especially with a belt):—gird.

G2225.definition:
†ζωογονέω zōogonéō, dzo-og-on-eh'-o; from the same as G2226 and a derivative of G1096; to engender alive,
 i.e. (by analogy) to rescue (passively, be saved) from death:—live,
 preserve.

G2226.definition: †ζῶον zōon, dzo'-on; neuter of a derivative of G2198; a live thing, i.e. an animal:—beast.

G2227.definition:
†ζωοποιέω zōopoiéō, dzo-op-oy-eh'-o; from the same as G2226 and G4160; to (re-)vitalize (literally or
 figuratively):—make alive, give life, quicken.

G2228.definition:
ἤ ḗ, ay; a primary particle of distinction between two connected terms; 
 disjunctive, or; comparative, than:—and, but (either), (n-)either,
 except it be, (n-)or (else), rather, save, than, that, what, yea. 
 Often used in connection with other particles. Compare especially
 G2235, G2260, G2273.

G2229.definition:
ἦ ē, ay; an adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of G2228; used only (in
 the New Testament) before G3303; assuredly:—surely.

G223.definition:
Ἀλέξανδρος Aléxandros, al-ex'-an-dros; from the same as (the first part of) G220 and G435; man-defender;
 Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man:—Alexander.

G2230.definition: ἡγεμονεύω hēgemoneúō, hayg-em-on-yoo'-o; from G2232; to act as ruler:—be governor.

G2231.definition: ἡγεμονία hēgemonía, hayg-em-on-ee'-ah; from G2232; government, i.e. (in time) official term:—reign.

G2232.definition:
ἡγεμών hēgemṓn, hayg-em-ohn'; from G2233; a leader, i.e. chief person (or figuratively, place) of a
 province:—governor, prince, ruler.

G2233.definition:
ἡγέομαι hēgéomai, hayg-eh'-om-ahee; middle voice of a (presumed) strengthened form of G71; to lead, i.e.
 command (with official authority); figuratively, to deem, i.e.
 consider:—account, (be) chief, count, esteem, governor, judge, have
 the rule over, suppose, think.

G2234.definition:
ἡδέως hēdéōs, hay-deh'-oce; adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237; sweetly, i.e.
 (figuratively) with pleasure:—gladly.

G2235.definition:
ἤδη ḗdē, ay'-day; apparently from G2228 (or possibly G2229) and G1211; even now:—already,
 (even) now (already), by this time.

G2237.definition:
ἡδονή hēdonḗ, hay-don-ay'; from ἁνδάνω handánō (to please); sensual delight; by implication,
 desire:—lust, pleasure.

G2238.definition:
ἡδύοσμον hēdýosmon, hay-doo'-os-mon; neuter of the compound of the same as G2234 and G3744; a sweet-scented
 plant, i.e. mint:—mint.

G2239.definition:
ἦθος ēthos, ay'-thos; a strengthened form of G1485; usage, i.e. (plural) moral
 habits:—manners.

G224.definition: ἄλευρον áleuron, al'-yoo-ron; from ἀλέω aléō(to grind); flour:—meal.

G2240.definition:
ἥκω hḗkō, hay'-ko; a primary verb; to arrive, i.e. be present (literally or
 figuratively):—come.

G2241.definition: ἠλί ēlí, ay-lee'; of Hebrew origin (H410 with pronominal suffix); my God:—Eli.

G2242.definition: Ἡλί Hēlí, hay-lee'; of Hebrew origin (H5941); Heli (i.e. Eli), an Israelite:—Heli.

G2243.definition: †Ἡλίας Hēlías, hay-lee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H452); Helias (i.e. Elijah), an Israelite:—Elias.

G2244.definition: ἡλικία hēlikía, hay-lik-ee'-ah; from the same as G2245; maturity (in years or size):—age, stature.

G2245.definition:
ἡλίκος hēlíkos, hay-lee'-kos; from ἧλιξ hēlix (a comrade, i.e. one of the same age); as big as, i.e.
 (interjectively) how much:—how (what) great.

G2246.definition:
ἥλιος hḗlios, hay'-lee-os; from ἕλη hélē (a ray; perhaps akin to the alternate of G138); the sun; by
 implication, light:—+ east, sun.

G2247.definition: ἧλος hēlos, hay'-los; of uncertain affinity; a stud, i.e. spike:—nail.

G2248.definition: ἡμᾶς hēmâs, hay-mas'; accusative case plural of G1473; us:—our, us, we.

G2249.definition:
ἡμεῖς hēmeîs, hay-mice'; nominative plural of G1473; we (only used when emphatic):—us, we
 (ourselves).

G225.definition: ἀλήθεια alḗtheia, al-ay'-thi-a; from G227; truth:—true, × truly, truth, verity.

G2250.definition:
ἡμέρα hēméra, hay-mer'-ah; feminine (with G5610 implied) of a derivative of ἧμαι hēmai (to sit; akin to
 the base of G1476) meaning tame, i.e. gentle; day, i.e. (literally) the
 time space between dawn and dark, or the whole 24 hours (but several
 days were usually reckoned by the Jews as inclusive of the parts of
 both extremes); figuratively, a period (always defined more or less
 clearly by the context):—age, + alway, (mid-)day (by day, (-ly)), +
 for ever, judgment, (day) time, while, years.

G2251.definition: ἡμέτερος hēméteros, hay-met'-er-os; from G2249; our:—our, your (by a different reading).

G2252.definition: ἤμην ḗmēn, ay'-mane; a prolonged form of G2258; I was:—be, was. (Sometimes unexpressed).

G2253.definition:
ἡμιθανής hēmithanḗs, hay-mee-than-ace'; from a presumed compound of the base of G2255 and G2348; half dead, i.e.
 entirely exhausted:—half dead.

G2254.definition:
ἡμῖν hēmîn, hay-meen'; dative case plural of G1473; to (or for, with, by) us:—our, (for) us,
 we.

G2255.definition:
†ἥμισυ hḗmisy, hay'-mee-soo; neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to G260 (through
 the idea of partition involved in connection) and meaning semi-; (as
 noun) half:—half.

G2256.definition: ἡμιώριον hēmiṓrion, hay-mee-o'-ree-on; from the base of G2255 and G5610; a half-hour:—half an hour.

G2257.definition: ἡμῶν hēmōn, hay-mone'; genitive case plural of G1473; of (or from) us:—our (company), us, we.

G2258.definition:
ἦν ēn, ane; imperfect of G1510; I (thou, etc.) was (wast or were):—+ agree, be, X
 have (+ charge of), hold, use, was(-t), were.

G2259.definition: ἡνίκα hēníka, hay-nee'-kah; of uncertain affinity; at which time:—when.

G226.definition:
ἀληθεύω alētheúō, al-ayth-yoo'-o; from G227; to be true (in doctrine and profession):—speak (tell) the
 truth.

G2260.definition: ἤπερ ḗper, ay'-per; from G2228 and G4007; than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed):—than.

G2261.definition: ἤπιος ḗpios, ay'-pee-os; probably from G2031; properly, affable, i.e. mild or kind:—gentle.

G2262.definition: Ἤρ Ḗr, ayr; of Hebrew origin (H6147); Er, an Israelite:—Er.

G2263.definition:
ἤρεμος ḗremos, ay'-rem-os; perhaps by transposition from G2048 (through the idea of stillness); 
 tranquil:—quiet.

G2264.definition:
†Ἡρώδης Hērṓdēs, hay-ro'-dace; compound of ἥρως hḗrōs (a "hero") and G1491; heroic; Herod, the name of four
 Jewish kings:—Herod.

G2265.definition:
†Ἡρωδιανοί Hērōdianoí, hay-ro-dee-an-oy'; plural of a derivative of G2264; Herodians, i.e. partisans of
 Herod:—Herodians.

G2266.definition: †Ἡρωδιάς Hērōdiás, hay-ro-dee-as'; from G2264; Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family:—Herodias.

G2267.definition: †Ἡρωδίων Hērōdíōn, hay-ro-dee'-ohn; from G2264; Herodion, a Christian:—Herodion.

G2268.definition:
Ἡσαΐας Hēsaḯas, hay-sah-ee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H3470); Hesaias (i.e. Jeshajah), an
 Israelite:—Esaias.

G2269.definition: Ἠσαῦ Ēsaû, ay-sow'; of Hebrew origin (H6215); Esau, an Edomite:—Esau.

G227.definition:
ἀληθής alēthḗs, al-ay-thace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2990; true (as not
 concealing):—true, truly, truth.

G2271.definition:
ἡσυχία hēsychía, hay-soo-khee'-ah; feminine of G2272; (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or
 language:—quietness, silence.

G2272.definition:
ἡσύχιος hēsýchios, hay-soo'-khee-os; a prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of
 G1476 and perhaps G2192; properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e.
 (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing):—peaceable, quiet.

G2273.definition: ἤτοι ḗtoi, ay'-toy; from G2228 and G5104; either indeed:—whether.

G2274.definition:
†ἡττάω hēttáō, hayt-tah'-o; from the same as G2276; to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or
 figuratively); by implication, to rate lower:—be inferior, overcome.

G2275.definition:
ἥττημα hḗttēma, hayt'-tay-mah; from G2274; a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or
 (subjectively) loss:—diminishing, fault.

G2277.definition:
ἤτω ḗtō, ay'-to; third person singular imperative of G1510; let him (or it) be:—let …
 be.

G2278.definition: ἠχέω ēchéō, ay-kheh'-o; from G2279; to make a loud noise, i.e. reverberate:—roar, sound.

G2279.definition:
†ἦχος ēchos, ay'-khos; of uncertain affinity; a loud or confused noise ("echo"), i.e. roar;
 figuratively, a rumor:—fame, sound.

G228.definition: ἀληθινός alēthinós, al-ay-thee-nos'; from G227; truthful:—true.

G2280.definition: Θαδδαῖος Thaddaîos, thad-dah'-yos; of uncertain origin; Thaddæus, one of the Apostles:—Thaddæus.

G2281.definition:
θάλασσα thálassa, thal'-as-sah; probably prolonged from G251; the sea (genitive case or
 specially):—sea.

G2282.definition:
θάλπω thálpō, thal'-po; probably akin to θάλλω thállō (to warm); to brood, i.e. (figuratively) to
 foster:—cherish.

G2283.definition: Θάμαρ Thámar, tham'-ar; of Hebrew origin (H8559); Thamar (i.e. Tamar), an Israelitess:—Thamar.

G2284.definition: θαμβέω thambéō, tham-beh'-o; from G2285; to stupefy (with surprise), i.e. astound:—amaze, astonish.

G2285.definition:
θάμβος thámbos, tham'-bos; akin to an obsolete τάφω táphō (to dumbfound); stupefaction (by surprise),
 i.e. astonishment:—X amazed, + astonished, wonder.

G2286.definition: θανάσιμος thanásimos, than-as'-ee-mos; from G2288; fatal, i.e. poisonous:—deadly.

G2287.definition:
θανατήφορος thanatḗphoros, than-at-ay'-for-os; from (the feminine form of) G2288 and G5342; death-bearing, i.e.
 fatal:—deadly.

G2288.definition:
θάνατος thánatos, than'-at-os; from G2348; (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or
 figuratively):—X deadly, (be…) death.

G2289.definition:
θανατόω thanatóō, than-at-o'-o; from G2288 to kill (literally or figuratively):—become dead, (cause to
 be) put to death, kill, mortify.

G229.definition: ἀλήθω alḗthō, al-ay'-tho; from the same as G224; to grind:—grind.

G2290.definition: θάπτω tháptō, thap'-to; a primary verb; to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. inter:—bury.

G2291.definition:
Θάρα Thára, thar'-ah; of Hebrew origin (H8646); Thara (i.e. Terach), the father of
 Abraham:—Thara.

G2292.definition:
θαῤῥέω tharrhéō, thar-hreh'-o; another form for G2293; to exercise courage:—be bold, × boldly, have
 confidence, be confident. Compare G5111.

G2293.definition: θαρσέω tharséō, thar-seh'-o; from G2294; to have courage:—be of good cheer (comfort). Compare G2292.

G2294.definition:
θάρσος thársos, thar'-sos; akin (by transposition) to θράσος thrásos (daring); boldness
 (subjectively):—courage.

G2295.definition:
θαῦμα thaûma, thos'-mah; apparently from a form of G2300; wonder (properly concrete; but by
 implication, abstract):—admiration.

G2296.definition:
†θαυμάζω thaumázō, thou-mad'-zo; from G2295; to wonder; by implication, to admire:—admire, have in
 admiration, marvel, wonder.

G2297.definition:
θαυμάσιος thaumásios, thow-mas'-ee-os; from G2295; wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle:—wonderful
 thing.

G2298.definition:
θαυμαστός thaumastós, thow-mas-tos'; from G2296; wondered at, i.e. (by implication)
 wonderful:—marvel(-lous).

G2299.definition: θεά theá, theh-ah'; feminine of G2316; a female deity:—goddess.

G23.definition:
ἀγανακτέω aganaktéō, ag-an-ak-teh'-o; from ἄγαν ágan (much) and ἄχθος áchthos (grief; akin to the base of G43); to be
 greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant:—be much (sore)
 displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation.

G230.definition:
ἀληθῶς alēthōs, al-ay-thoce'; adverb from G227; truly:—indeed, surely, of a surety, truly, of a (in)
 truth, verily, very.

G2300.definition:
θεάομαι theáomai, theh-ah'-om-ahee; a prolonged form of a primary verb; to look closely at, i.e. (by
 implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to
 visit:—behold, look (upon), see. Compare G3700.

G2301.definition: †θεατρίζω theatrízō, theh-at-rid'-zo; from G2302; to expose as a spectacle:—make a gazing stock.

G2302.definition:
θέατρον théatron, theh'-at-ron; from G2300; a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. general
 audience-room; by implication, a show itself
 (figuratively):—spectacle, theatre.

G2303.definition:
θεῖον theîon, thi'-on; probably neuter of G2304 (in its original sense of flashing); 
 sulphur:—brimstone.

G2304.definition: θεῖος theîos, thi'-os; from G2316; godlike (neuter as noun, divinity):—divine, godhead.

G2305.definition: θειότης theiótēs, thi-ot'-ace; from G2304; divinity (abstractly):—godhead.

G2306.definition: θειώδης theiṓdēs, thi-o'-dace; from G2303 and 1491; sulphur-like, i.e. sulphurous:—brimstone.

G2307.definition:
θέλημα thélēma, thel'-ay-mah; from the prolonged form of G2309; a determination (properly, the
 thing), i.e. (actively) choice (specially, purpose, decree;
 abstractly, volition) or (passively) inclination:—desire, pleasure,
 will.

G2308.definition: θέλησις thélēsis, thel'-ay-sis; from G2309; determination (properly, the act), i.e. option:—will.

G2309.definition:
†θέλω thélō, thel'-o; apparently strengthened from the alternate form of G138; to determine
 (as an active option from subjective impulse; whereas G1014 properly
 denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations),
 i.e. choose or prefer (literally or figuratively); by implication, to
 wish, i.e. be inclined to (sometimes adverbially, gladly);
 impersonally for the future tense, to be about to; by Hebraism, to
 delight in:—desire, be disposed (forward), intend, list, love, mean,
 please, have rather, (be) will (have, -ling, - ling(-ly)).

G231.definition:
ἁλιεύς halieús, hal-ee-yoos'; from G251; a sailor (as engaged on the salt water), i.e. (by
 implication) a fisher:—fisher(-man).

G2310.definition:
†θεμέλιος themélios, them-el'-ee-os; from a derivative of G5087; something put down, i.e. a substruction (of
 a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively):—foundation.

G2311.definition:
θεμελιόω themelióō, them-el-ee-o'-o; from G2310; to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or
 (figuratively) consolidate:—(lay the) found(- ation), ground, settle.

G2312.definition: θεοδίδακτος theodídaktos, theh-od-id'-ak-tos; from G2316 and G1321; divinely instructed:—taught of God.

G2314.definition: θεομάχος theomáchos, theh-om'-akh-os; from G2316 and G3164; an opponent of deity:—to fight against God.

G2315.definition:
θεόπνευστος theópneustos, theh-op'-nyoo-stos; from G2316 and a presumed derivative of G4154; divinely breathed
 in:—given by inspiration of God.

G2316.definition:
θεός theós, theh'-os; of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with G3588) the supreme
 Divinity; figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very:—X exceeding,
 God, god(-ly, -ward).

G2317.definition: θεοσέβεια theosébeia, theh-os-eb'-i-ah; from G2318; devoutness, i.e. piety:—godliness.

G2318.definition: θεοσεβής theosebḗs, theh-os-eb-ace'; from G2316 and G4576; reverent of God, i.e. pious:—worshipper of God.

G2319.definition:
θεοστυγής theostygḗs, theh-os-too-gace'; from G2316 and the base of G4767; hateful to God, i.e. impious:—hater
 of God.

G232.definition:
ἁλιεύω halieúō, hal-ee-yoo'-o; from G231; to be a fisher, i.e. (by implication) to fish:—go
 a-fishing.

G2320.definition: θεότης theótēs, theh-ot'-ace; from G2316; divinity (abstractly):—godhead.

G2321.definition:
Θεόφιλος Theóphilos, theh-of'-il-os; from G2316 and G5384; friend of God; Theophilus, a
 Christian:—Theophilus.

G2322.definition:
θεραπεία therapeía, ther-ap-i'-ah; from G2323; attendance (specially, medical, i.e. cure); figuratively
 and collectively, domestics:—healing, household.

G2323.definition:
θεραπεύω therapeúō, ther-ap-yoo'-o; from the same as G2324; to wait upon menially, i.e. (figuratively) to
 adore (God), or (specially) to relieve (of disease):—cure, heal,
 worship.

G2324.definition:
θεράπων therápōn, ther-ap'-ohn; apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the
 base of G2330; a menial attendant (as if cherishing):—servant.

G2325.definition: θερίζω therízō, ther-id'-zo; from G2330 (in the sense of the crop); to harvest:—reap.

G2326.definition: θερισμός therismós, ther-is-mos'; from G2325; reaping, i.e. the crop:—harvest.

G2327.definition: θεριστής theristḗs, ther-is-tace'; from G2325; a harvester:—reaper.

G2328.definition: θερμαίνω thermaínō, ther-mah'-ee-no; from G2329; to heat (oneself):—(be) warm(-ed, self).

G2329.definition: θέρμη thérmē, ther'-may; from the base of G2330; warmth:—heat.

G233.definition: ἁλίζω halízō, hal-id'-zo; from G251; to salt:—salt.

G2330.definition: θέρος théros, ther'-os; from a primary θέρω thérō (to heat); properly, heat, i.e. summer:—summer.

G2331.definition:
Θεσσαλονικεύς Thessalonikeús, thes-sal-on-ik-yoos'; from G2332; a Thessalonican, i.e. inhabitant of
 Thessalonice:—Thessalonian.

G2332.definition:
Θεσσαλονίκη Thessaloníkē, thes-sal-on-ee'-kay; from Θεσσαλός Thessalós (a Thessalian) and G3529; Thessalonice, a place in Asia
 Minor:—Thessalonica.

G2333.definition: Θευδᾶς Theudâs, thyoo-das'; of uncertain origin; Theudas, an Israelite:—Theudas.

G2334.definition:
θεωρέω theōréō, theh-o-reh'-o; from a derivative of G2300 (perhaps by addition of G3708); to be a
 spectator of, i.e. discern, (literally, figuratively (experience) or
 intensively (acknowledge)):—behold, consider, look on, perceive, see. 
 Compare G3700.

G2335.definition:
θεωρία theōría, theh-o-ree'-ah; from the same as G2334; spectatorship, i.e. (concretely) a
 spectacle:—sight.

G2336.definition: θήκη thḗkē, thay'-kay; from G5087; a receptacle, i.e. scabbard:—sheath.

G2337.definition:
θηλάζω thēlázō, thay-lad'-zo; from θηλή thēlḗ (the nipple); to suckle, (by implication) to suck:—(give)
 suck(-ling).

G2338.definition: θῆλυς thēlys, thay'-loos; from the same as G2337; female:—female, woman.

G2339.definition:
θήρα thḗra, thay'-rah; from θήρ thḗr (a wild animal, as game); hunting, i.e. (figuratively)
 destruction:—trap.

G234.definition: †ἀλίσγεμα alísgema, al-is'-ghem-ah; from ἀλισγέω alisgéō (to soil); (ceremonially) defilement:—pollution.

G2340.definition:
θηρεύω thēreúō, thay-ryoo'-o; from G2339; to hunt (an animal), i.e. (figuratively) to carp
 at:—catch.

G2341.definition:
θηριομαχέω thēriomachéō, thay-ree-om-akh-eh'-o; from a compound of G2342 and G3164; to be a beast-fighter (in the
 gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious
 men):—fight with wild beasts.

G2342.definition:
θηρίον thēríon, thay-ree'-on; diminutive from the same as G2339; a dangerous animal:—(venomous,
 wild) beast.

G2343.definition:
θησαυρίζω thēsaurízō, thay-sow-rid'-zo; from G2344; to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively):—lay up
 (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up).

G2344.definition:
θησαυρός thēsaurós, thay-sow-ros'; from G5087; a deposit, i.e. wealth (literally or
 figuratively):—treasure.

G2345.definition:
θιγγάνω thingánō, thing-gan'-o; a prolonged form of an obsolete primary θίγω thígō (to finger); to
 manipulate, i.e. have to do with; by implication, to injure:—handle,
 touch.

G2346.definition:
θλίβω thlíbō, thlee'-bo; akin to the base of G5147; to crowd (literally or
 figuratively):—afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble.

G2347.definition:
†θλῖψις thlîpsis, thlip'-sis; from G2346; pressure (literally or figuratively):—afflicted(-tion),
 anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble.

G2348.definition:
θνήσκω thnḗskō, thnay'-sko; a strengthened form of a simpler primary θάνω thánō than'-o (which is used
 for it only in certain tenses); to die (literally or
 figuratively):—be dead, die.

G2349.definition: θνητός thnētós, thnay-tos'; from G2348; liable to die:—mortal(-ity).

G235.definition:
ἀλλά allá, al-lah'; neuter plural of G243; properly, other things, i.e. (adverbially)
 contrariwise (in many relations):—and, but (even), howbeit, indeed,
 nay, nevertheless, no, notwithstanding, save, therefore, yea, yet.

G2350.definition:
θορυβέω thorybéō, thor-oo-beh'-o; from G2351; to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor:—make ado (a noise),
 trouble self, set on an uproar.

G2351.definition: θόρυβος thórybos, thor'-oo-bos; from the base of G2360; a disturbance:—tumult, uproar.

G2352.definition: θραύω thraúō, throw'-o; a primary verb; to crush:—bruise. Compare G4486.

G2353.definition: θρέμμα thrémma, threm'-mah; from G5142; stock (as raised on a farm):—cattle.

G2354.definition: θρηνέω thrēnéō, thray-neh'-o; from G2355; to bewail:—lament, mourn.

G2356.definition:
θρησκεία thrēskeía, thrace-ki'-ah; from a derivative of G2357; ceremonial observance:—religion,
 worshipping.

G2357.definition:
θρησκός thrēskós, thrace'-kos; probably from the base of G2360; ceremonious in worship (as
 demonstrative), i.e. pious:—religious.

G2358.definition:
θριαμβεύω thriambeúō, three-am-byoo'-o; from a prolonged compound of the base of G2360; and a derivative of G680
 (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an
 acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by
 Hebraism) to give victory:—(cause) to triumph (over).

G2359.definition:
θρίξ thríx, threeks; genitive case τριχός trichós, etc.; of uncertain derivation; hair:—hair. 
 Compare G2864.

G236.definition: ἀλλάσσω allássō, al-las'-so; from G243; to make different:—change.

G2360.definition:
θροέω throéō, thro-eh'-o; from θρέομαι thréomai to wail; to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to
 frighten:—trouble.

G2361.definition: θρόμβος thrómbos, throm'-bos; perhaps from G5142 (in the sense of thickening); a clot:—great drop.

G2362.definition:
θρόνος thrónos, thron'-os; from θράω thráō (to sit); a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power
 or (concretely) a potentate:—seat, throne.

G2363.definition: Θυάτειρα Thyáteira, thoo-at'-i-rah; of uncertain derivation; Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor:—Thyatira.

G2364.definition:
θυγάτηρ thygátēr, thoo-gat'-air; apparently a primary word (compare "daughter"); a female child, or (by
 Hebraism) descendant (or inhabitant):—daughter.

G2365.definition: θυγάτριον thygátrion, thoo-gat'-ree-on; from G2364; a daughterling:—little (young) daughter.

G2366.definition: θύελλα thýella, thoo'-el-lah; from G2380 (in the sense of blowing) a storm:—tempest.

G2367.definition:
θύϊνος thýïnos, thoo'-ee-nos; from a derivative of G2380 (in the sense of blowing; denoting a certain
 fragrant tree); made of citron-wood:—thyine.

G2368.definition:
θυμίαμα thymíama, thoo-mee'-am-ah; from G2370; an aroma, i.e. fragrant powder burnt in religious service;
 by implication, the burning itself:—incense, odour.

G2369.definition:
θυμιαστήριον thymiastḗrion, thoo-mee-as-tay'-ree-on; from a derivative of G2370; a place of fumigation, i.e. the alter of
 incense (in the Temple):—censer.

G237.definition: ἀλλαχόθεν allachóthen, al-lakh-oth'-en; from G243; from elsewhere:—some other way.

G2370.definition:
θυμιάω thymiáō, thoo-mee-ah'-o; from a derivative of G2380 (in the sense of smoking); to fumigate, i.e.
 offer aromatic fumes:—burn incense.

G2371.definition:
θυμομαχέω thymomachéō, thoo-mom-akh-eh'-o; from a presumed compound of G2372 and G3164; to be in a furious fight,
 i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated:—be highly displeased.

G2372.definition:
θυμός thymós, thoo-mos'; from G2380; passion (as if breathing hard):—fierceness, indignation,
 wrath. Compare G5590.

G2373.definition: θυμόω thymóō, tho-mo'-o; from G2372; to put in a passion, i.e. enrage:—be wroth.

G2374.definition:
θύρα thýra, thoo'-rah; apparently a primary word (compare "door"); a portal or entrance (the
 opening or the closure, literally or figuratively):—door, gate.

G2375.definition: θυρεός thyreós, thoo-reh-os'; from G2374; a large shield (as door-shaped):—shield.

G2376.definition: θυρίς thyrís, thoo-rece'; from G2374; an aperture, i.e. window:—window.

G2377.definition:
θυρωρός thyrōrós, thoo-ro-ros'; from G2374 and οὖρος oûros (a watcher); a gate- warden:—that kept the door,
 porter.

G2378.definition:
θυσία thysía, thoo-see'-ah; from G2380; sacrifice (the act or the victim, literally or
 figuratively):—sacrifice.

G2379.definition:
θυσιαστήριον thysiastḗrion, thoo-see-as-tay'-ree-on; from a derivative of G2378; a place of sacrifice, i.e. an altar
 (special or genitive case, literal or figurative):—altar.

G238.definition:
ἀλληγορέω allēgoréō, al-lay-gor-eh'-o; from G243 and ἀγορέω agoréō (to harangue (compare G58)); to allegorize:—be an
 allegory (the Greek word itself).

G2380.definition:
θύω thýō, thoo'-o; a primary verb; properly, to rush (breathe hard, blow, smoke), i.e.
 (by implication) to sacrifice (properly, by fire, but genitive case);
 by extension to immolate (slaughter for any purpose):—kill, (do)
 sacrifice, slay.

G2381.definition:
Θωμᾶς Thōmâs, tho-mas'; of Chaldee origin (compare H8380); the twin; Thomas, a
 Christian:—Thomas.

G2382.definition:
θώραξ thṓrax, tho'-rax; of uncertain affinity; the chest ("thorax"), i.e. (by implication) a
 corslet:—breast-plate.

G2383.definition: †Ἰάειρος Iáeiros, ee-ah'-i-ros; of Hebrew origin (H2971); Jairus (i.e. Jair), an Israelite:—Jairus.

G2384.definition:
Ἰακώβ Iakṓb, ee-ak-obe'; of Hebrew origin (H3290); Jacob (i.e. Ja`akob), the progenitor of the
 Israelites:—also an Israelite:—Jacob.

G2385.definition:
Ἰάκωβος Iákōbos, ee-ak'-o-bos; the same as G2384 Græcized; Jacobus, the name of three
 Israelites:—James.

G2386.definition: ἴαμα íama, ee'-am-ah; from G2390; a cure (the effect):—healing.

G2387.definition: Ἰαμβρῆς Iambrēs, ee-am-brace'; of Egyptian origin; Jambres, an Egyptian:—Jambres.

G2388.definition: Ἰαννά Ianná, ee-an-nah'; probably of Hebrew origin (compare H3238); Janna, an Israelite:—Janna.

G2389.definition: Ἰαννῆς Iannēs, ee-an-nace'; of Egyptian origin; Jannes, an Egyptian:—Jannes.

G239.definition:
ἀλληλουϊα allēlouïa, al-lay-loo'-ee-ah; of Hebrew origin (imperative of H1984 and H3050); praise ye Jah!, an
 adoring exclamation:—alleluiah.

G2390.definition:
ἰάομαι iáomai, ee-ah'-om-ahee; middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to cure (literally or
 figuratively):—heal, make whole.

G2391.definition: †Ἰάρεδ Iáred, ee-ar'-ed; of Hebrew origin (H3382); Jared (i.e. Jered), an antediluvian:—Jared.

G2392.definition: ἴασις íasis, ee'-as-is; from G2390; curing (the act):—cure, heal(-ing).

G2393.definition: ἴασπις íaspis, ee'-as-pis; probably of foreign origin (see H3471); "jasper", a gem:—jasper.

G2394.definition:
Ἰάσων Iásōn, ee-as'-oan; future active participle masculine of G2390; about to cure; Jason, a
 Christian:—Jason.

G2395.definition: ἰατρός iatrós, ee-at-ros'; from G2390; a physician:—physician.

G2396.definition:
ἴδε íde, id'-eh; second person singular imperative active of G1492; used as an
 interjection to denote surprise; lo!:—behold, lo, see.

G2398.definition:
ἴδιος ídios, id'-ee-os; of uncertain affinity; pertaining to self, i.e. one's own; by
 implication, private or separate:—X his acquaintance, when they were
 alone, apart, aside, due, his (own, proper, several), home, (her, our,
 thine, your) own (business), private(-ly), proper, severally, their
 (own).

G2399.definition:
ἰδιώτης idiṓtēs, id-ee-o'-tace; from G2398; a private person, i.e. (by implication) an ignoramus
 (compare "idiot"):—ignorant, rude, unlearned.

G24.definition: ἀγανάκτησις aganáktēsis, ag-an-ak'-tay-sis; from G23; indignation:—indignation.

G240.definition:
ἀλλήλων allḗlōn, al-lay'-lone; Genitive plural from G243 reduplicated; one another:—each other,
 mutual, one another, (the other), (them-, your-)selves, (selves)
 together (sometimes with G3326 or G4314).

G2400.definition:
ἰδού idoú, id-oo'; second person singular imperative middle voice of G1492; used as
 imperative lo!; --behold, lo, see.

G2401.definition:
Ἰδουμαία Idoumaía, id-oo-mah'-yah; of Hebrew origin (H123); Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South)
 of Palestine:—Idumæa.

G2402.definition: ἱδρώς hidrṓs, hid-roce'; a strengthened form of a primary idos (sweat); perspiration:—sweat.

G2403.definition:
†Ἰεζαβήλ Iezabḗl, ee-ed-zab-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H348); Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used
 as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher):—Jezabel.

G2404.definition:
Ἱεράπολις Hierápolis, hee-er-ap'-ol-is; from G2413 and G4172; holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia
 Minor:—Hierapolis.

G2405.definition:
ἱερατεία hierateía, hee-er-at-i'-ah; from G2407; priestliness, i.e. the sacerdotal function:—office of the
 priesthood, priest's office.

G2406.definition:
ἱεράτευμα hieráteuma, hee-er-at'-yoo-mah; from G2407; the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order
 (figuratively):—priesthood.

G2407.definition:
ἱερατεύω hierateúō, hee-er-at-yoo'-o; prolongation from G2409; to be a priest, i.e. perform his
 functions:—execute the priest's office.

G2408.definition:
Ἱερεμίας Hieremías, hee-er-em-ee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H3414); Hieremias (i.e. Jermijah), an
 Israelite:—Jeremiah.

G2409.definition: ἱερεύς hiereús, hee-er-yooce'; from G2413; a priest (literally or figuratively):—(high) priest.

G241.definition: ἀλλογενής allogenḗs, al-log-en-ace'; from G243 and G1085; foreign, i.e. not a Jew:—stranger.

G2410.definition: Ἱεριχώ Hierichṓ, hee-er-ee-kho'; of Hebrew origin (H3405); Jericho, a place in Palestine:—Jericho.

G2411.definition:
ἱερόν hierón, hee-er-on'; neuter of G2413; a sacred place, i.e. the entire precincts (whereas
 G3485 denotes the central sanctuary itself) of the Temple (at Jerusalem
 or elsewhere):—temple.

G2412.definition: ἱεροπρεπής hieroprepḗs, hee-er-op-rep-ace'; from G2413 and the same as G4241; reverent:—as becometh holiness.

G2413.definition: ἱερός hierós, hee-er-os'; of uncertain affinity; sacred:—holy.

G2414.definition:
Ἱεροσόλυμα Hierosólyma, hee-er-os-ol'-oo-mah; of Hebrew origin (H3389); Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim), the capitol
 of Palestine:—Jerusalem. Compare G2419.

G2415.definition:
Ἱεροσολυμίτης Hierosolymítēs, hee-er-os-ol-oo-mee'-tace; from G2414; a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma:—of
 Jerusalem.

G2416.definition: ἱεροσυλέω hierosyléō, hee-er-os-ool-eh'-o; from G2417; to be a temple-robber (figuratively):—commit sacrilege.

G2417.definition: ἱερόσυλος hierósylos, hee-er-os'-oo-los; from G2411 and G4813; a temple-despoiler:—robber of churches.

G2418.definition:
ἱερουργέω hierourgéō, hee-er-oorg-eh'-o; from a compound of G2411 and the base of G2041; to be a temple-worker,
 i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively):—minister.

G2419.definition:
†Ἱερουσαλήμ Hierousalḗm, hee-er-oo-sal-ame'; of Hebrew origin (H3389); Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of
 Palestine:—Jerusalem. Compare G2414.

G242.definition:
ἅλλομαι hállomai, hal'-lom-ahee; middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to jump; figuratively, to
 gush:—leap, spring up.

G2420.definition:
ἱερωσύνη hierōsýnē, hee-er-o-soo'-nay; from G2413; sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly
 office:—priesthood.

G2421.definition: Ἰεσσαί Iessaí, es-es-sah'-ee; of Hebrew origin (H3448); Jessæ (i.e. Jishai), an Israelite:—Jesse.

G2422.definition:
Ἰεφθάε Iephtháe, ee-ef-thah'-eh; of Hebrew origin (H3316); Jephthaë (i.e. Jiphtach), an
 Israelite:—Jephthah.

G2423.definition:
Ἰεχονίας Iechonías, ee-ekh-on-ee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H3204); Jechonias (i.e. Jekonjah), an
 Israelite:—Jechonias.

G2424.definition:
Ἰησοῦς Iēsoûs, ee-ay-sooce'; of Hebrew origin (H3091); Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord
 and two (three) other Israelites:—Jesus.

G2425.definition:
ἱκανός hikanós, hik-an-os'; from ἵκω híkō ( ἱκάνω hikánō or ἱκνέομαι hiknéomai, akin to G2240) (to arrive); competent
 (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in
 character):—able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long
 (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy.

G2426.definition: ἱκανότης hikanótēs, hik-an-ot'-ace; from G2425; ability:—sufficiency.

G2427.definition: ἱκανόω hikanóō, hik-an-o'-o; from G2425; to enable, i.e. qualify:—make able (meet).

G2428.definition:
ἱκετηρία hiketēría, hik-et-ay-ree'-ah; from a derivative of the base of G2425 (through the idea of approaching
 for a favor); intreaty:—supplication.

G2429.definition: †ἱκμάς hikmás, hik-mas'; of uncertain affinity; dampness:—moisture.

G243.definition:
ἄλλος állos, al'-los; a primary word; "else," i.e. different (in many applications):—more,
 one (another), (an-, some an-)other(-s, -wise).

G2430.definition:
Ἰκόνιον Ikónion, ee-kon'-ee-on; perhaps from G1504; image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia
 Minor:—Iconium.

G2431.definition:
ἱλαρός hilarós, hil-ar-os'; from the same as G2436; propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt
 or willing:—cheerful.

G2432.definition: ἱλαρότης hilarótēs, hil-ar-ot'-ace; from G2431; alacrity:—cheerfulness.

G2433.definition:
ἱλάσκομαι hiláskomai, hil-as'-kom-ahee; middle voice from the same as G2436; to conciliate, i.e. (transitively)
 to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious:—be merciful,
 make reconciliation for.

G2434.definition: ἱλασμός hilasmós, hil-as-mos'; atonement, i.e. (concretely) an expiator:—propitiation.

G2435.definition:
†ἱλαστήριον hilastḗrion, hil-as-tay'-ree-on; neuter of a derivative of G2433; an expiatory (place or thing), i.e.
 (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in
 the Temple):—mercyseat, propitiation.

G2436.definition:
ἵλεως híleōs, hil'-eh-oce; perhaps from the alternate form of G138; cheerful (as attractive), i.e.
 propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in
 averting some calamity) far be it:—be it far, merciful.

G2437.definition:
Ἰλλυρικόν Illyrikón, il-loo-ree-kon'; neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation; (the)
 Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of
 Europe:—Illyricum.

G2438.definition:
ἱμάς himás, hee-mas'; perhaps from the same as G260; a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a
 sandal) or the lash (of a scourge):—latchet, thong.

G2439.definition: ἱματίζω himatízō, him-at-id'-zo; from G2440; to dress:—clothe.

G244.definition:
ἀλλοτριεπίσκοπος allotriepískopos, al-lot-ree-ep-is'-kop-os; from G245 and G1985; overseeing others' affairs, i.e. a meddler
 (specially, in Gentile customs):—busybody in other men's matters.

G2440.definition:
ἱμάτιον himátion, him-at'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of ennumi (to put on); a dress (inner
 or outer):—apparel, cloke, clothes, garment, raiment, robe, vesture.

G2441.definition: ἱματισμός himatismós, him-at-is-mos'; from G2439; clothing:—apparel (X -led), array, raiment, vesture.

G2443.definition:
ἵνα hína, hin'-ah; probably from the same as the former part of G1438 (through the
 demonstrative idea; compare G3588); in order that (denoting the purpose
 or the result):—albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as,
 (so) that, (for) to. Compare G3363.

G2445.definition:
Ἰόππη Ióppē, ee-op'-pay; of Hebrew origin (H3305); Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in
 Palestine:—Joppa.

G2446.definition:
Ἰορδάνης Iordánēs, ee-or-dan'-ace; of Hebrew origin (H3383); the Jordanes (i.e. Jarden), a river of
 Palestine:—Jordan.

G2447.definition:
ἰός iós, ee-os'; perhaps from εἶμι eîmi (to go) or ἵημι híēmi (to send); rust (as if emitted by
 metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents):—poison, rust.

G2449.definition:
Ἰουδαία Ioudaía, ee-oo-dah'-yah; feminine of G2453 (with G1093 implied); the Judæan land (i.e. Judæa),
 a region of Palestine:—Judæa.

G245.definition:
ἀλλότριος allótrios, al-lot'-ree-os; from G243; another's, i.e. not one's own; by extension foreign, not
 akin, hostile:—alien, (an-)other (man's, men's), strange(-r).

G2450.definition: Ἰουδαΐζω Ioudaḯzō, ee-oo-dah-id'-zo; from G2453; to become a Judæan, i.e. "Judaize":—live as the Jews.

G2451.definition: Ἰουδαϊκός Ioudaïkós, ee-oo-dah-ee-kos'; from G2453; Judaïc, i.e. resembling a Judæan:—Jewish.

G2452.definition:
Ἰουδαϊκῶς Ioudaïkōs, ee-oo-dah-ee-koce'; adverb from G2451; Judaïcally or in a manner resembling a Judæan:—as
 do the Jews.

G2453.definition:
Ἰουδαῖος Ioudaîos, ee-oo-dah'-yos; from G2448 (in the sense of G2455 as a country); Judæan, i.e. belonging
 to Jehudah:—Jew(-ess), of Judæa.

G2454.definition:
Ἰουδαϊσμός Ioudaïsmós, ee-oo-dah-is-mos'; from G2450; "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages:—Jews'
 religion.

G2455.definition:
Ἰούδας Ioúdas, ee-oo-das'; of Hebrew origin (H3063); Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten
 Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its
 region:—Juda(-h, -s); Jude.

G2456.definition: Ἰουλία Ioulía, ee-oo-lee'-ah; feminine of the same as G2457; Julia, a Christian woman:—Julia.

G2457.definition: Ἰούλιος Ioúlios, ee-oo'-lee-os; of Latin origin; Julius, a centurion:—Julius.

G2458.definition: †Ἰουνιᾶς Iouniâs, ee-oo-nee'-as; of Latin origin; Junias, a Christian:—Junias.

G2459.definition:
Ἰοῦστος Ioûstos, ee-ooce'-tos; of Latin origin ("just"); Justus, the name of three
 Christian:—Justus.

G246.definition:
ἀλλόφυλος allóphylos, al-lof'-oo-los; from G243 and G5443; foreign, i.e. (specially) Gentile:—one of another
 nation.

G2460.definition: ἱππεύς hippeús, hip-yooce'; from G2462; an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps:—horseman.

G2461.definition: †ἱππικόν hippikón, hip-pee-kon'; neuter of a derivative of G2462; the cavalry force:—horse(-men).

G2462.definition: ἵππος híppos, hip'-pos; of uncertain affinity; a horse:—horse.

G2463.definition:
ἶρις îris, ee'-ris; perhaps from G2046 (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan
 deities); a rainbow ("iris"):—rainbow.

G2464.definition:
Ἰσαάκ Isaák, ee-sah-ak'; of Hebrew origin (H3327); Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of
 Abraham:—Isaac.

G2465.definition: ἰσάγγελος isángelos, ee-sang'-el-los; from G2470 and G32; like an angel, i.e. angelic:—equal unto the angels.

G247.definition: ἄλλως állōs, al'-loce; adverb from G243; differently:—otherwise.

G2470.definition:
ἴσος ísos, ee'-sos; probably from G1492 (through the idea of seeming); similar (in amount
 and kind):—+ agree, as much, equal, like.

G2471.definition:
ἰσότης isótēs, ee-sot'-ace; likeness (in condition or proportion); by implication,
 equity:—equal(-ity).

G2472.definition: ἰσότιμος isótimos, ee-sot'-ee-mos; from G2470 and G5092; of equal value or honor:—like precious.

G2473.definition: ἰσόψυχος isópsychos, ee-sop'-soo-khos; from G2470 and G5590; of similar spirit:—likeminded.

G2474.definition:
Ἰσραήλ Israḗl, is-rah-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H3478); Israel (i.e. Jisrael), the adopted name of
 Jacob, including his descendants (literally or figuratively):—Israel.

G2475.definition:
Ἰσραηλίτης Israēlítēs, is-rah-ale-ee'-tace; from G2474; an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or
 figuratively):—Israelite.

G2476.definition:
†ἵστημι hístēmi, his'-tay-mee; a prolonged form of a primary στάω stáō stah'-o (of the same meaning, and
 used for it in certain tenses); to stand (transitively or
 intransitively), used in various applications (literally or
 figuratively):—abide, appoint, bring, continue, covenant, establish,
 hold up, lay, present, set (up), stanch, stand (by, forth, still, up). 
 Compare G5087.

G2477.definition:
ἱστορέω historéō, his-tor-eh'-o; from a derivative of G1492; to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by
 implication) to visit for information (interview):—see.

G2478.definition:
ἰσχυρός ischyrós, is-khoo-ros'; from G2479; forcible (literally or figuratively):—boisterous,
 mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant.

G248.definition: ἀλοάω aloáō, al-o-ah'-o; from the same as G257; to tread out grain:—thresh, tread out the corn.

G2480.definition:
ἰσχύω ischýō, is-khoo'-o; from G2479; to have (or exercise) force (literally or
 figuratively):—be able, avail, can do(-not), could, be good, might,
 prevail, be of strength, be whole, + much work.

G2481.definition: ἴσως ísōs, ee'-soce; adverb from G2470; likely, i.e. perhaps:—it may be.

G2482.definition: Ἰταλία Italía, ee-tal-ee'-ah; probably of foreign origin; Italia, a region of Europe:—Italy.

G2483.definition: Ἰταλικός Italikós, ee-tal-ee-kos'; from G2482; Italic, i.e. belonging to Italia:—Italian.

G2484.definition:
†Ἰτουραΐα Itouraḯa, ee-too-rah'-yah; of Hebrew origin (H3195); Ituræa (i.e. Jetur), a region of
 Palestine:—Ituræa.

G2485.definition: ἰχθύδιον ichthýdion, ikh-thoo'-dee-on; diminutive from G2486; a petty fish:—little (small) fish.

G2486.definition: ἰχθύς ichthýs, ikh-thoos'; of uncertain affinity; a fish:—fish.

G2487.definition:
ἴχνος íchnos, ikh'-nos; from ἰκνέομαι iknéomai (to arrive; compare G2240); a track
 (figuratively):—step.

G2488.definition:
†Ἰωάθαμ Iōátham, ee-o-ath'-am; of Hebrew origin (H3147); Joatham (i.e. Jotham), an
 Israelite:—Joatham.

G2489.definition: Ἰωάννα Iōánna, ee-o-an'-nah; feminine of the same as G2491; Joanna, a Christian:—Joanna.

G249.definition:
ἄλογος álogos, al'-og-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3056; irrational:—brute,
 unreasonable.

G2491.definition:
Ἰωάννης Iōánnēs, ee-o-an'-nace; of Hebrew origin (H3110); Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four
 Israelites:—John.

G2492.definition: Ἰώβ Iṓb, ee-obe'; of Hebrew origin (H347); Job (i.e. Ijob), a patriarch:—Job.

G2493.definition: Ἰωήλ Iōḗl, ee-o-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H3100); Joel, an Israelite:—Joel.

G2494.definition: †Ἰωνάν Iōnán, ee-o-nan'; probably for G2491 or G2495; Jonan, an Israelite:—Jonan.

G2495.definition:
Ἰωνᾶς Iōnâs, ee-o-nas'; of Hebrew origin (H3124); Jonas (i.e. Jonah), the name of two
 Israelites:—Jonas.

G2496.definition: †Ἰωράμ Iōrám, ee-o-ram'; of Hebrew origin (H3141); Joram, an Israelite:—Joram.

G2497.definition: †Ἰωρείμ Iōreím, ee-o-rime'; perhaps for G2496; Jorim, an Israelite:—Jorim.

G2498.definition:
Ἰωσαφάτ Iōsaphát, ee-o-saf-at'; of Hebrew origin (H3092); Josaphat (i.e. Jehoshaphat), an
 Israelite:—Josaphat.

G25.definition: ἀγαπάω agapáō, ag-ap-ah'-o; perhaps from ἄγαν ágan (much) (or compare H5689); to love (in a social or moral sense):—(be-)love(-ed). Compare G5368.

G250.definition: ἀλόη alóē, al-o-ay'; of foreign origin (compare G174); aloes (the gum):—aloes.

G2500.definition:
Ἰωσῆς Iōsēs, ee-o-sace'; perhaps for G2501; Joses, the name of two Israelites:—Joses. Compare
 G2499.

G2501.definition:
†Ἰωσήφ Iōsḗph, ee-o-safe'; of Hebrew origin (H3130); Joseph, the name of seven
 Israelites:—Joseph.

G2502.definition: Ἰωσίας Iōsías, ee-o-see'-as; of Hebrew origin (H2977); Josias (i.e. Joshiah), an Israelite:—Josias.

G2503.definition:
ἰῶτα iōta, ee-o'-tah; of Hebrew origin (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet); "iota",
 the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put
 (figuratively) for a very small part of anything:—jot.

G2504.definition:
κἀγώ kagṓ, kag-o'; from G2532 and G1473;  so also the dative case
 
    κἀμοί kamoí  kam-oy', and accusative case
    κἀμέ kamé  kam-eh'
    
 and (or also, even, etc.) I, (to) me:—(and, even, even so, so) I 
 (also, in like wise), both me, me also.

G2505.definition:
καθά kathá, kath-ah'; from G2596 and the neuter plural of G3739; according to which things,
 i.e. just as:—as.

G2506.definition:
καθαίρεσις kathaíresis, kath-ah'-ee-res-is; from G2507; demolition; figuratively, extinction:—destruction, pulling
 down.

G2507.definition:
καθαιρέω kathairéō, kath-ahee-reh'-o; from G2596 and G138 (including its alternate); to lower (or with
 violence) demolish (literally or figuratively):—cast (pull, put,
 take) down, destroy.

G2508.definition:
καθαίρω kathaírō, kath-ah'-ee-ro; from G2513; to cleanse, i.e. (specially) to prune; figuratively, to
 expiate:—purge.

G2509.definition: †καθάπερ katháper, kath-ap'-er; from G2505 and G4007; exactly as:—(even, as well) as.

G2510.definition: καθάπτω katháptō, kath-ap'-to; from G2596 and G680; to seize upon:—fasten on.

G2511.definition:
καθαρίζω katharízō, kath-ar-id'-zo; from G2513; to cleanse (literally or figuratively):—(make) clean(-se),
 purge, purify.

G2512.definition:
καθαρισμός katharismós, kath-ar-is-mos'; from G2511; a washing off, i.e. (ceremonially) ablution, (morally)
 expiation:—cleansing, + purge, purification(-fying).

G2513.definition:
καθαρός katharós, kath-ar-os'; of uncertain affinity; clean (literally or figuratively):—clean,
 clear, pure.

G2514.definition: καθαρότης katharótēs, kath-ar-ot'-ace; from G2513; cleanness (ceremonially):—purification.

G2515.definition:
καθέδρα kathédra, kath-ed'-rah; from G2596 and the same as G1476; a bench (literally or
 figuratively):—seat.

G2516.definition: καθέζομαι kathézomai, kath-ed'-zom-ahee; from G2596 and the base of G1476; to sit down:—sit.

G2517.definition:
καθεξῆς kathexēs, kath-ex-ace'; from G2596 and G1836; thereafter, i.e. consecutively; as a noun (by
 ellipsis of noun) a subsequent person or time:—after(-ward), by (in)
 order.

G2518.definition:
καθεύδω katheúdō, kath-yoo'-do; from G2596 and εὕδω heúdō (to sleep); to lie down to rest, i.e. (by
 implication) to fall asleep (literally or figuratively):—(be
 a-)sleep.

G2519.definition:
καθηγητής kathēgētḗs, kath-ayg-ay-tace'; from a compound of G2596 and G2233; a guide, i.e. (figuratively) a
 teacher:—master.

G252.definition: ἁλυκός halykós, hal-oo-kos'; from G251; briny:—salt.

G2520.definition:
καθήκω kathḗkō, kath-ay'-ko; from G2596 and G2240; to reach to, i.e. (neuter of present active
 participle, figuratively as adjective) becoming:—convenient, fit.

G2521.definition:
κάθημαι káthēmai, kath'-ay-mahee; from G2596; and ἧμαι hēmai (to sit; akin to the base of G1476); to sit down;
 figuratively, to remain, reside:—dwell, sit (by, down).

G2522.definition: καθημερινός kathēmerinós, kath-ay-mer-ee-nos'; from G2596 and G2250; quotidian:—daily.

G2523.definition:
καθίζω kathízō, kath-id'-zo; another (active) form for G2516; to seat down, i.e. set (figuratively,
 appoint); intransitively, to sit (down); figuratively, to settle
 (hover, dwell):—continue, set, sit (down), tarry.

G2524.definition: καθίημι kathíēmi, kath-ee'-ay-mee; from G2596; and ἵημι híēmi (to send); to lower:—let down.

G2525.definition:
καθίστημι kathístēmi, kath-is'-tay-mee; from G2596 and G2476; to place down (permanently), i.e. (figuratively)
 to designate, constitute, convoy:—appoint, be, conduct, make, ordain,
 set.

G2526.definition:
†καθό kathó, kath-o'; from G2596 and G3739; according to which thing, i.e. precisely as, in
 proportion as:—according to that, (inasmuch) as.

G2527.definition: καθόλου kathólou, kath-ol'-oo; from G2596 and G3650; on the whole, i.e. entirely:—at all.

G2528.definition: καθοπλίζω kathoplízō, kath-op-lid'-zo; from G2596; and G3695; to equip fully with armor:—arm.

G2529.definition:
καθοράω kathoráō, kath-or-ah'-o; from G2596 and G3708; to behold fully, i.e. (figuratively) distinctly
 apprehend:—clearly see.

G253.definition:
†ἀλυπότερος alypóteros, al-oo-pot'-er-os; comparative of a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and G3077; more
 without grief:—less sorrowful.

G2530.definition:
καθότι kathóti, kath-ot'-ee; from G2596; and G3739 and G5100; according to which certain thing, i.e.
 as far (or inasmuch) as:—(according, forasmuch) as, because (that).

G2531.definition:
καθώς kathṓs, kath-oce'; from G2596 and G5613; just (or inasmuch) as, that:—according to,
 (according, even) as, how, when.

G2532.definition:
καί kaí, kahee; apparently, a primary particle, having a copulative and sometimes also
 a cumulative force; and, also, even, so then, too, etc.; often used in
 connection (or composition) with other particles or small words:—and,
 also, both, but, even, for, if, or, so, that, then, therefore, when,
 yet.

G2533.definition:
Καϊάφας Kaïáphas, kah-ee-af'-as; of Chaldee origin; the dell; Caiaphas (i.e. Cajepha), an
 Israelite:—Caiaphas.

G2535.definition: Κάϊν Káïn, kah'-in; of Hebrew origin (H7014); Cain, (i.e. Cajin), the son of Adam:—Cain.

G2536.definition:
†Καϊνάν Kaïnán, kah-ee-nan'; of Hebrew origin (H7018); Cainan (i.e. Kenan), the name of two
 patriarchs:—Cainan.

G2537.definition:
†καινός kainós, kahee-nos'; of uncertain affinity; new (especially in freshness; while G3501 is
 properly so with respect to age:—new.

G2538.definition: καινότης kainótēs, kahee-not'-ace; from G2537; renewal (figuratively):—newness.

G2539.definition:
καίπερ kaíper, kah'-ee-per; from G2532 and G4007; and indeed, i.e. nevertheless or
 notwithstanding:—and yet, although.

G254.definition: ἅλυσις hálysis, hal'-oo-sis; of uncertain derivation; a fetter or manacle:—bonds, chain.

G2540.definition:
καιρός kairós, kahee-ros'; of uncertain affinity; an occasion, i.e. set or proper time:—X
 always, opportunity, (convenient, due) season, (due, short, while)
 time, a while. Compare G5550.

G2541.definition: Καῖσαρ Kaîsar, kah'-ee-sar; of Latin origin; Cæsar, a title of the Roman emperor:—Cæsar.

G2542.definition: Καισάρεια Kaisáreia, kahee-sar'-i-a; from G2541; Cæsaria, the name of two places in Palestine:—Cæsarea.

G2543.definition: καίτοι kaítoi, kah'-ee-toy; from G2532 and G5104; and yet, i.e. nevertheless:—although.

G2545.definition:
καίω kaíō, kah'-yo; apparently a primary verb; to set on fire, i.e. kindle or (by
 implication) consume:—burn, light.

G2546.definition:
κἀκεῖ kakeî, kak-i'; from G2532 and G1563; likewise in that place:—and there, there
 (thither) also.

G2547.definition:
κἀκεῖθεν kakeîthen, kak-i'-then; from G2532 and G1564; likewise from that place (or time):—and afterward
 (from) (thence), thence also.

G2548.definition:
κἀκεῖνος kakeînos, kak-i'-nos; from G2532 and G1565; likewise that (or those):—and him (other, them),
 even he, him also, them (also), (and) they.

G2549.definition:
κακία kakía, kak-ee'-ah; from G2556; badness, i.e. (subjectively) depravity, or (actively)
 malignity, or (passively) trouble:—evil, malice(-iousness),
