 naughtiness, wickedness.

G255.definition:
ἀλυσιτελής alysitelḗs, al-oo-sit-el-ace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G3081; gainless, i.e.
 (by implication) pernicious:—unprofitable.

G2550.definition:
κακοήθεια kakoḗtheia, kak-o-ay'-thi-ah; from a compound of G2556 and G2239; bad character, i.e. (specially)
 mischievousness:—malignity.

G2551.definition: κακολογέω kakologéō, kak-ol-og-eh'-o; from a compound of G2556 and G3056; to revile:—curse, speak evil of.

G2552.definition: κακοπάθεια kakopátheia, kak-op-ath'-i-ah; from a compound of G2256 and G3806; hardship:—suffering affliction.

G2553.definition:
κακοπαθέω kakopathéō, kak-op-ath-eh'-o; from the same as G2552; to undergo hardship:—be afflicted, endure
 afflictions (hardness), suffer trouble.

G2554.definition:
κακοποιέω kakopoiéō, kak-op-oy-eh'-o; from G2555; to be a bad-doer, i.e. (objectively) to injure, or
 (genitive) to sin:—do(ing) evil.

G2555.definition:
κακοποιός kakopoiós, kak-op-oy-os'; from G2556 and G4160; a bad-doer; (specially), a criminal:—evil-doer,
 malefactor.

G2556.definition:
κακός kakós, kak-os'; apparently a primary word; worthless (intrinsically, such; whereas
 G4190 properly refers to effects), i.e. (subjectively) depraved, or
 (objectively) injurious:—bad, evil, harm, ill, noisome, wicked.

G2557.definition:
κακοῦργος kakoûrgos, kak-oor'-gos; from G2556 and the base of G2041; a wrong-doer, i.e.
 criminal:—evil-doer, malefactor.

G2558.definition:
κακουχέω kakouchéō, kak-oo-kheh'-o; from a presumed compound of G2556 and G2192; to maltreat:—which suffer
 adversity, torment.

G2559.definition:
κακόω kakóō, kak-o'-o; from G2556; to injure; figuratively, to exasperate:—make evil
 affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex.

G256.definition: Ἀλφαῖος Alphaîos, al-fah'-yos; of Hebrew origin (compare H2501); Alphæus, an Israelite:—Alpheus.

G2560.definition:
κακῶς kakōs, kak-oce'; from G2556; badly (physically or morally):—amiss, diseased, evil,
 grievously, miserably, sick, sore.

G2561.definition: κάκωσις kákōsis, kak'-o-sis; from G2559; maltreatment:—affliction.

G2562.definition:
καλάμη kalámē, kal-am'-ay; feminine of G2563; a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively)
 stubble:—stubble.

G2563.definition:
κάλαμος kálamos, kal'-am-os; of uncertain affinity; a reed (the plant or its stem, or that of a
 similar plant); by implication, a pen:—pen, reed.

G2564.definition:
καλέω kaléō, kal-eh'-o; akin to the base of G2753; to "call" (properly, aloud, but used in a
 variety of applications, directly or otherwise):—bid, call (forth),
 (whose, whose sur-)name (was (called)).

G2565.definition:
καλλιέλαιος kalliélaios, kal-le-el'-ah-yos; from the base of G2566 and G1636; a cultivated olive tree, i.e. a
 domesticated or improved one:—good olive tree.

G2567.definition: καλοδιδάσκαλος kalodidáskalos, kal-od-id-as'-kal-os; from G2570 and G1320; a teacher of the right:—teacher of good things.

G2569.definition: καλοποιέω kalopoiéō, kal-op-oy-eh'-o; from G2570 and G4160; to do well, i.e. live virtuously:—well doing.

G257.definition:
ἅλων hálōn, hal'-ohn; probably from the base of G1507; a threshing-floor (as rolled hard),
 i.e. (figuratively) the grain (and chaff, as just threshed):—floor.

G2570.definition:
καλός kalós, kal-os'; of uncertain affinity; properly, beautiful, but chiefly (figuratively)
 good (literally or morally), i.e. valuable or virtuous (for appearance
 or use, and thus distinguished from G18, which is properly
 intrinsic):—X better, fair, good(-ly), honest, meet, well, worthy.

G2571.definition: †κάλυμα kályma, kal'-oo-mah; from G2572; a cover, i.e. veil:—vail.

G2572.definition:
καλύπτω kalýptō, kal-oop'-to; akin to G2813 and G2928; to cover up (literally or
 figuratively):—cover, hide.

G2573.definition:
καλῶς kalōs, kal-oce'; adverb from G2570; well (usually morally):—(in a) good (place),
 honestly, + recover, (full) well.

G2574.definition: κάμηλος kámēlos, kam'-ay-los; of Hebrew origin (H1581); a "camel":—camel.

G2575.definition: κάμινος káminos, kam'-ee-nos; probably from G2545; a furnace:—furnace.

G2576.definition:
καμμύω kammýō, kam-moo'-o; from a compound of G2596 and the base of G3466; to shut down, i.e. close
 the eyes:—close.

G2577.definition:
κάμνω kámnō, kam'-no; apparently a primary verb; properly, to toil, i.e. (by implication) to
 tire (figuratively, faint, sicken):—faint, sick, be wearied.

G2578.definition: κάμπτω kámptō, kamp'-to; apparently a primary verb; to bend:—bow.

G2579.definition:
κἄν kán, kan; from G2532 and G1437; and (or even) if:—and (also) if (so much as), if
 but, at the least, though, yet.

G258.definition:
ἀλώπηξ alṓpēx, al-o'-pakes; of uncertain derivation; a fox, i.e. (figuratively) a cunning
 person:—fox.

G2580.definition: †Κανᾶ Kanâ, kan-ah'; of Hebrew origin (compare H7071); Cana, a place in Palestine:—Cana.

G2582.definition: Κανδάκη Kandákē, kan-dak'-ay; of foreign origin; Candacè, an Egyptian queen:—Candace.

G2583.definition:
κανών kanṓn, kan-ohn'; from κάνη kánē (a straight reed, i.e. rod); a rule ("canon"), i.e.
 (figuratively) a standard (of faith and practice); by implication, a
 boundary, i.e. (figuratively) a sphere (of activity):—line, rule.

G2585.definition:
καπηλεύω kapēleúō, kap-ale-yoo'-o; from κάπηλος kápēlos (a huckster); to retail, i.e. (by implication) to
 adulterate (figuratively):—corrupt.

G2586.definition: καπνός kapnós, kap-nos'; of uncertain affinity; smoke:—smoke.

G2587.definition: Καππαδοκία Kappadokía, kap-pad-ok-ee'-ah; of foreign origin; Cappadocia, a region of Asia Minor:—Cappadocia.

G2588.definition:
καρδία kardía, kar-dee'-ah; prolonged from a primary κάρ kár (Latin cor, "heart"); the heart, i.e.
 (figuratively) the thoughts or feelings (mind); also (by analogy) the
 middle:—(+ broken-)heart(-ed).

G2589.definition: καρδιογνώστης kardiognṓstēs, kar-dee-og-noce'-tace; from G2588 and G1097; a heart-knower:—which knowest the hearts.

G259.definition: ἅλωσις hálōsis, hal'-o-sis; from a collateral form of G138; capture, be taken.

G2590.definition:
καρπός karpós, kar-pos'; probably from the base of G726; fruit (as plucked), literally or
 figuratively:—fruit.

G2591.definition: Κάρπος Kárpos, kar'-pos; perhaps for G2590; Carpus, probably a Christian:—Carpus.

G2592.definition:
καρποφορέω karpophoréō, kar-pof-or-eh'-o; from G2593; to be fertile (literally or figuratively):—be (bear, bring
 forth) fruit(-ful).

G2593.definition: καρποφόρος karpophóros, kar-pof-or'-os; from G2590 and G5342; fruitbearing (figuratively):—fruitful.

G2594.definition:
καρτερέω karteréō, kar-ter-eh'-o; from a derivative of G2904 (transposed); to be strong, i.e.
 (figuratively) steadfast (patient):—endure.

G2595.definition: κάρφος kárphos, kar'-fos; from κάρφω kárphō (to wither); a dry twig or straw:—mote.

G2596.definition:
κατά katá, kat-ah'; a primary particle; (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in
 varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or
 accusative) with which it is joined):—about, according as (to),
 after, against, (when they were) × alone, among, and, × apart, (even,
 like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), × aside, at, before,
 beyond, by, to the charge of, (charita-)bly, concerning, + covered,
 (dai-)ly, down, every, (+ far more) exceeding, × more excellent, for,
 from … to, godly, in(-asmuch, divers, every, -to, respect of), …
 by, after the manner of, + by any means, beyond (out of) measure, X
 mightily, more, × natural, of (up-)on (X part), out (of every), over
 against, (+ your) × own, + particularly, so, through(-oughout,
 -oughout every), thus, (un-)to(-gether, -ward), × uttermost,
 where(-by), with.

G2597.definition:
καταβαίνω katabaínō, kat-ab-ah'-ee-no; from G2596 and the base of G939; to descend (literally or
 figuratively):—come (get, go, step) down, fall (down).

G2598.definition: καταβάλλω katabállō, kat-ab-al'-lo; from G2596 and G906; to throw down:—cast down, lay.

G2599.definition: καταβαρέω katabaréō, kat-ab-ar-eh'-o; from G2596 and G916; to impose upon:—burden.

G26.definition:
ἀγάπη agápē, ag-ah'-pay; from G25; love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a
 love-feast:—(feast of) charity(-ably), dear, love.

G260.partOfSpeech: absolute state masculine plural intensive noun
G260.definition:
ἅμα háma, ham'-ah; a primary particle; properly, at the "same" time, but freely used as a
 preposition or adverb denoting close association:—also, and,
 together, with(-al).

G2600.definition: κατάβασις katábasis, kat-ab'-as-is; from G2597; a declivity:—descent.

G2601.definition:
καταβιβάζω katabibázō, kat-ab-ib-ad'-zo; from G2596 and a derivative of the base of G939; to cause to go down,
 i.e. precipitate:—bring (thrust) down.

G2602.definition:
καταβολή katabolḗ, kat-ab-ol-ay'; from G2598; a deposition, i.e. founding; figuratively,
 conception:—conceive, foundation.

G2603.definition:
καταβραβεύω katabrabeúō, kat-ab-rab-yoo'-o; from G2596 and G1018 (in its original sense); to award the price
 against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation):—beguile of
 reward.

G2604.definition: καταγγελεύς katangeleús, kat-ang-gel-yooce'; from G2605; a proclaimer:—setter forth.

G2605.definition:
καταγγέλλω katangéllō, kat-ang-gel'-lo; from G2596 and the base of G32; to proclaim, promulgate:—declare,
 preach, shew, speak of, teach.

G2606.definition: καταγελάω katageláō, kat-ag-el-ah'-o; to laugh down, i.e. deride:—laugh to scorn.

G2607.definition:
καταγινώσκω kataginṓskō, kat-ag-in-o'-sko; from G2596 and G1097; to note against, i.e. find fault with:—blame,
 condemn.

G2608.definition:
κατάγνυμι katágnymi, kat-ag'-noo-mee; from G2596 and the base of G4486; to rend in pieces, i.e. crack
 apart:—break.

G2609.definition:
κατάγω katágō, kat-ag'-o; from G2596 and G71; to lead down; specially, to moor a vessel:—bring
 (down, forth), (bring to) land, touch.

G261.definition: ἀμαθής amathḗs, am-ath-ace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3129; ignorant:—unlearned.

G2610.definition:
καταγωνίζομαι katagōnízomai, kat-ag-o-nid'-zom-ahee; from G2596 and G75; to struggle against, i.e. (by implication) to
 overcome:—subdue.

G2611.definition: καταδέω katadéō, kat-ad-eh'-o; from G2596 and G1210; to tie down, i.e. bandage (a wound):—bind up.

G2612.definition: κατάδηλος katádēlos, kat-ad'-ay-los; from G2596 intensive and G1212; manifest:—far more evident.

G2613.definition:
καταδικάζω katadikázō, kat-ad-ik-ad'-zo; from G2596 and a derivative of G1349; to adjudge against, i.e. pronounce
 guilty:—condemn.

G2614.definition: καταδιώκω katadiṓkō, kat-ad-ee-o'-ko; from G2596 and G1377; to hunt down, i.e. search for:—follow after.

G2615.definition: καταδουλόω katadoulóō, kat-ad-oo-lo'-o; from G2596 and G1402; to enslave utterly:—bring into bondage.

G2616.definition:
καταδυναστεύω katadynasteúō, kat-ad-oo-nas-tyoo'-o; from G2596 and a derivative of G1413; to exercise dominion against, i.e.
 oppress:—oppress.

G2617.definition:
καταισχύνω kataischýnō, kat-ahee-skhoo'-no; from G2596 and G153; to shame down, i.e. disgrace or (by implication)
 put to the blush:—confound, dishonour, (be a-, make a-)shame(-d).

G2618.definition:
κατακαίω katakaíō, kat-ak-ah'-ee-o; from G2596 and G2545; to burn down (to the ground), i.e. consume
 wholly:—burn (up, utterly).

G2619.definition: κατακαλύπτω katakalýptō, kat-ak-al-oop'-to; from G2596 and G2572; to cover wholly, i.e. veil:—cover, hide.

G262.definition:
ἀμαράντινος amarántinos, am-ar-an'-tee-nos; from G263; "amaranthine", i.e. (by implication) fadeless:—that fadeth
 not away.

G2620.definition:
†κατακαυχάομαι katakaucháomai, kat-ak-ow-khah'-om-ahee; from G2596 and G2744; to exult against (i.e. over):—boast (against),
 glory, rejoice against.

G2621.definition:
κατάκειμαι katákeimai, kat-ak'-i-mahee; from G2596 and G2749; to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick;
 specially, to recline at a meal:—keep, lie, sit at meat (down).

G2622.definition: κατακλάω katakláō, kat-ak-lah'-o; from G2596 and G2806; to break down, i.e. divide:—break.

G2623.definition:
κατακλείω katakleíō, kat-ak-li'-o; from G2596 and G2808; to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e.
 incarcerate:—shut up.

G2624.definition:
†κατακληροδοτέω kataklērodotéō, kat-ak-lay-rod-ot-eh'-o; from G2596 and a derivative of a compound of G2819 and G1325; to be a
 giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an
 estate:—divide by lot.

G2625.definition:
κατακλίνω kataklínō, kat-ak-lee'-no; from G2596 and G2827; to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place
 at table:—(make) sit down (at meat).

G2626.definition:
κατακλύζω kataklýzō, kat-ak-lood'-zo; from G2596 and the base of G2830; to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by
 implication) to deluge:—overflow.

G2627.definition: κατακλυσμός kataklysmós, kat-ak-looce-mos'; from G2626; an inundation:—flood.

G2628.definition: κατακολουθέω katakolouthéō, kat-ak-ol-oo-theh'-o; from G2596 and G190; to accompany closely:—follow (after).

G2629.definition: κατακόπτω katakóptō, kat-ak-op'-to; from G2596 and G2875; to chop down, i.e. mangle:—cut.

G263.definition:
ἀμάραντος amárantos, am-ar'-an-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3133; 
 unfading, i.e. (by implication) perpetual:—that fadeth not away.

G2630.definition:
κατακρημνίζω katakrēmnízō, kat-ak-rame-nid'-zo; from G2596 and a derivative of G2911; to precipitate down:—cast down
 headlong.

G2631.definition: κατάκριμα katákrima, kat-ak'-ree-mah; from G2632; an adverse sentence (the verdict):—condemnation.

G2632.definition: κατακρίνω katakrínō, kat-ak-ree'-no; from G2596 and G2919; to judge against, i.e. sentence:—condemn, damn.

G2633.definition: κατάκρισις katákrisis, kat-ak'-ree-sis; from G2632; sentencing adversely (the act):—condemn(-ation).

G2634.definition:
κατακυριεύω katakyrieúō, kat-ak-oo-ree-yoo'-o; from G2596 and G2961; to lord against, i.e. control,
 subjugate:—exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome.

G2635.definition:
καταλαλέω katalaléō, kat-al-al-eh'-o; from G2637; to be a traducer, i.e. to slander:—speak against (evil
 of).

G2636.definition: †καταλαλία katalalía, kat-al-al-ee'-ah; from G2637; defamation:—backbiting, evil speaking.

G2637.definition:
κατάλαλος katálalos, kat-al'-al-os; from G2596 and the base of G2980; talkative against, i.e. a
 slanderer:—backbiter.

G2638.definition:
καταλαμβάνω katalambánō, kat-al-am-ban'-o; from G2596 and G2983; to take eagerly, i.e. seize, possess, etc.
 (literally or figuratively):—apprehend, attain, come upon,
 comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take.

G2639.definition:
καταλέγω katalégō, kat-al-eg'-o; from G2596 and G3004 (in its original meaning); to lay down, i.e.
 (figuratively) to enrol:—take into the number.

G264.definition:
ἁμαρτάνω hamartánō, ham-ar-tan'-o; perhaps from G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G3313; 
 properly, to miss the mark (and so not share in the prize), i.e.
 (figuratively) to err, especially (morally) to sin:—for your faults,
 offend, sin, trespass.

G2641.definition:
καταλείπω kataleípō, kat-al-i'-po; from G2596 and G3007; to leave down, i.e. behind; by implication, to
 abandon, have remaining:—forsake, leave, reserve.

G2642.definition: καταλιθάζω katalitházō, kat-al-ith-ad'-zo; from G2596 and G3034; to stone down, i.e. to death:—stone.

G2643.definition:
καταλλαγή katallagḗ, kat-al-lag-ay'; from G2644; exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. restoration to
 (the divine) favor:—atonement, reconciliation(-ing).

G2644.definition:
καταλλάσσω katallássō, kat-al-las'-so; from G2596 and G236; to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound
 a difference:—reconcile.

G2645.definition:
κατάλοιπος katáloipos, kat-al'-oy-pos; from G2596 and G3062; left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the
 rest):—residue.

G2646.definition:
κατάλυμα katályma, kat-al'-oo-mah; from G2647; properly, a dissolution (breaking up of a journey), i.e.
 (by implication) a lodging-place:—guestchamber, inn.

G2647.definition:
καταλύω katalýō, kat-al-oo'-o; from G2596 and G3089; to loosen down (disintegrate), i.e. (by
 implication) to demolish (literally or figuratively); specially
 (compare G2646) to halt for the night:—destroy, dissolve, be guest,
 lodge, come to nought, overthrow, throw down.

G2648.definition:
καταμανθάνω katamanthánō, kat-am-an-than'-o; from G2596 and G3129; to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note
 carefully:—consider.

G2649.definition: καταμαρτυρέω katamartyréō, kat-am-ar-too-reh'-o; from G2596 and G3140; to testify against:—witness against.

G265.definition: ἁμάρτημα hamártēma, ham-ar'-tay-mah; from G264; a sin (properly concrete):—sin.

G2650.definition: καταμένω kataménō, kat-am-en'-o; from G2596 and G3306; to stay fully, i.e. reside:—abide.

G2654.definition: καταναλίσκω katanalískō, kat-an-al-is'-ko; from G2596 and G355; to consume utterly:—consume.

G2655.definition:
καταναρκάω katanarkáō, kat-an-ar-kah'-o; from G2596 and ναρκάω narkáō (to be numb); to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by
 implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive):—be burdensome
 (chargeable).

G2656.definition:
κατανεύω kataneúō, kat-an-yoo'-o; from G2596 and G3506; to nod down (towards), i.e. (by analogy) to make
 signs to:—beckon.

G2657.definition:
κατανοέω katanoéō, kat-an-o-eh'-o; from G2596 and G3539; to observe fully:—behold, consider, discover,
 perceive.

G2658.definition:
καταντάω katantáō, kat-an-tah'-o; from G2596 and a derivative of G473; to meet against, i.e. arrive at
 (literally or figuratively):—attain, come.

G2659.definition:
κατάνυξις katányxis, kat-an'-oox-is; from G2660; a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by
 implication, (perhaps by some confusion with G3506 or even with G3571))
 stupor (lethargy):—slumber.

G266.definition: ἁμαρτία hamartía, ham-ar-tee'-ah; from G264; a sin (properly abstract):—offence, sin(-ful).

G2660.definition:
κατανύσσω katanýssō, kat-an-oos'-so; from G2596 and G3572; to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to
 agitate violently ("sting to the quick"):—prick.

G2661.definition: καταξιόω kataxióō, kat-ax-ee-o'-o; from G2596 and G515; to deem entirely deserving:—(ac-)count worthy.

G2662.definition:
καταπατέω katapatéō, kat-ap-at-eh'-o; from G2596 and G3961; to trample down; figuratively, to reject with
 disdain:—trample, tread (down, underfoot).

G2663.definition: κατάπαυσις katápausis, kat-ap'-ow-sis; from G2664; reposing down, i.e. (by Hebraism) abode:—rest.

G2664.definition:
καταπαύω katapaúō, kat-ap-ow'-o; from G2596 and G3973; to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or
 (figuratively) to (cause to) desist:—cease, (give) rest(-rain).

G2665.definition:
καταπέτασμα katapétasma, kat-ap-et'-as-mah; from a compound of G2596 and a congener of G4072; something spread
 thoroughly, i.e. (specially) the door screen (to the Most Holy Place)
 in the Jewish Temple:—vail.

G2666.definition:
καταπίνω katapínō, kat-ap-ee'-no; from G2596 and G4095; to drink down, i.e. gulp entire (literally or
 figuratively):—devour, drown, swallow (up).

G2667.definition: καταπίπτω katapíptō, kat-ap-ip'-to; from G2596 and G4098; to fall down:—fall (down).

G2668.definition:
καταπλέω katapléō, kat-ap-leh'-o; from G2596 and G4126; to sail down upon a place, i.e. to land
 at:—arrive.

G2669.definition:
καταπονέω kataponéō, kat-ap-on-eh'-o; from G2596 and a derivative of G4192; to labor down, i.e. wear with toil
 (figuratively, harass):—oppress, vex.

G267.definition:
ἀμάρτυρος amártyros, am-ar'-too-ros; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a form of G3144; 
 unattested:—without witness.

G2670.definition:
καταποντίζω katapontízō, kat-ap-on-tid'-zo; from G2596 and a derivative of the same as G4195; to plunge down, i.e.
 submerge:—drown, sink.

G2671.definition:
κατάρα katára, kat-ar'-ah; from G2596 (intensive) and G685; imprecation, execration:—curse(-d,
 ing).

G2672.definition: καταράομαι kataráomai, kat-ar-ah'-om-ahee; middle voice from G2671; to execrate; by analogy, to doom:—curse.

G2673.definition:
καταργέω katargéō, kat-arg-eh'-o; from G2596 and G691; to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally
 or figuratively:—abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away,
 become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come)
 to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void.

G2674.definition: καταριθμέω katarithméō, kat-ar-ith-meh'-o; from G2596 and G705; to reckon among:—number with.

G2675.definition:
καταρτίζω katartízō, kat-ar-tid'-zo; from G2596 and a derivative of G739; to complete thoroughly, i.e. repair
 (literally or figuratively) or adjust:—fit, frame, mend, (make)
 perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore.

G2676.definition: κατάρτισις katártisis, kat-ar'-tis-is; from G2675; thorough equipment (subjectively):—perfection.

G2677.definition: καταρτισμός katartismós, kat-ar-tis-mos'; from G2675; complete furnishing (objectively):—perfecting.

G2678.definition: κατασείω kataseíō, kat-as-i'-o; from G2596 and G4579; to sway downward, i.e. make a signal:—beckon.

G2679.definition:
κατασκάπτω kataskáptō, kat-as-kap'-to; from G2596 and G4626; to undermine, i.e. (by implication) destroy:—dig
 down, ruin.

G268.definition: ἁμαρτωλός hamartōlós, ham-ar-to-los'; from G264; sinful, i.e. a sinner:—sinful, sinner.

G2680.definition:
κατασκευάζω kataskeuázō, kat-ask-yoo-ad'-zo; from G2596 and a derivative of G4632; to prepare thoroughly (properly,
 by external equipment; whereas G2090 refers rather to internal
 fitness); by implication, to construct, create:—build, make, ordain,
 prepare.

G2681.definition:
κατασκηνόω kataskēnóō, kat-as-kay-no'-o; from G2596 and G4637; to camp down, i.e. haunt; figuratively, to
 remain:—lodge, rest.

G2682.definition: κατασκήνωσις kataskḗnōsis, kat-as-kay'-no-sis; from G2681; an encamping, i.e. (figuratively) a perch:—nest.

G2683.definition: κατασκιάζω kataskiázō, kat-as-kee-ad'-zo; from G2596 and a derivative of G4639; to overshade, i.e. cover:—shadow.

G2684.definition: κατασκοπέω kataskopéō, kat-as-kop-eh'-o; from G2685; to be a sentinel, i.e. to inspect insidiously:—spy out.

G2685.definition:
κατάσκοπος katáskopos, kat-as'-kop-os; from G2596 (intensive) and G4649 (in the sense of a watcher); a
 reconnoiterer:—spy.

G2686.definition:
κατασοφίζομαι katasophízomai, kat-as-of-id'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G2596 and G4679; to be crafty against, i.e.
 circumvent:—deal subtilly with.

G2687.definition: καταστέλλω katastéllō, kat-as-tel'-lo; from G2596 and G4724; to put down, i.e. quell:—appease, quiet.

G2688.definition:
κατάστημα katástēma, kat-as'-tay-mah; from G2525; properly, a position or condition, i.e. (subjectively)
 demeanor:—behaviour.

G2689.definition: καταστολή katastolḗ, kat-as-tol-ay'; from G2687; a deposit, i.e. (specially) costume:—apparel.

G269.definition: ἄμαχος ámachos, am'-akh-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3163; peaceable:—not a brawler.

G2690.definition: καταστρέφω katastréphō, kat-as-tref'-o; from G2596 and G4762; to turn upside down, i.e. upset:—overthrow.

G2691.definition:
καταστρηνιάω katastrēniáō, kat-as-tray-nee-ah'-o; from G2596 and G4763; to become voluptuous against:—begin to wax wanton
 against.

G2692.definition:
καταστροφή katastrophḗ, kat-as-trof-ay'; from G2690; an overturn ("catastrophe"), i.e. demolition; figuratively,
 apostasy:—overthrow, subverting.

G2693.definition:
καταστρώννυμι katastrṓnnymi, kat-as-trone'-noo-mee; from G2596 and G4766; to strew down, i.e. (by implication) to prostrate
 (slay):—overthrow.

G2694.definition: κατασύρω katasýrō, kat-as-oo'-ro; from G2596 and G4951; to drag down, i.e. arrest judicially:—hale.

G2695.definition: †κατασφάττω kataspháttō, kat-as-fat'-to; from G2596 and G4969; to kill down, i.e. slaughter:—slay.

G2696.definition: κατασφραγίζω katasphragízō, kat-as-frag-id'-zo; from G2596 and G4972; to seal closely:—seal.

G2697.definition: κατάσχεσις katáschesis, kat-as'-khes-is; from G2722; a holding down, i.e. occupancy:—possession.

G2698.definition:
κατατίθημι katatíthēmi, kat-at-ith'-ay-mee; from G2596 and G5087; to place down, i.e. deposit (literally or
 figuratively):—do, lay, shew.

G2699.definition:
κατατομή katatomḗ, kat-at-om-ay'; from a compound of G2596 and τέμνω témnō (to cut); a cutting down (off), i.e.
 mutilation (ironically):—concision. Compare G609.

G27.definition: ἀγαπητός agapētós, ag-ap-ay-tos'; from G25; beloved:—(dearly, well) beloved, dear.

G270.definition:
ἀμάω amáō, am-ah'-o; from G260; properly, to collect, i.e. (by implication) reap:—reap
 down.

G2701.definition: κατατρέχω katatréchō, kat-at-rekh'-o; from G2596 and G5143; to run down, i.e. hasten from a tower:—run down.

G2702.definition:
καταφέρω kataphérō, kat-af-er'-o; from G2596 and G5342 (including its alternate); to bear down, i.e.
 (figuratively) overcome (with drowsiness); specially, to cast a
 vote:—fall, give, sink down.

G2703.definition: καταφεύγω katapheúgō, kat-af-yoo'-go; from G2596 and G5343; to flee down (away):—flee.

G2704.definition:
καταφθείρω kataphtheírō, kat-af-thi'-ro; from G2596 and G5351; to spoil entirely, i.e. (literally) to destroy; or
 (figuratively) to deprave; --corrupt, utterly perish.

G2705.definition: καταφιλέω kataphiléō, kat-af-ee-leh'-o; from G2596 and G5368; to kiss earnestly:—kiss.

G2706.definition: καταφρονέω kataphronéō, kat-af-ron-eh'-o; from G2596 and G5426; to think against, i.e. disesteem:—despise.

G2707.definition: †καταφροντής kataphrontḗs, kat-af-ron-tace'; from G2706; a contemner:—despiser.

G2708.definition: καταχέω katachéō, kat-akh-eh'-o; from G2596 and cheo (to pour); to pour down (out):—pour.

G2709.definition:
καταχθόνιος katachthónios, kat-akh-thon'-ee-os; from G2596 and χθών chthṓn (the ground); subterranean, i.e. infernal
 (belonging to the world of departed spirits):—under the earth.

G271.definition:
†ἀμέθυστος améthystos, am-eth'-oos-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3184; the
 "amethyst" (supposed to prevent intoxication):—amethyst.

G2710.definition: καταχράομαι katachráomai, kat-akh-rah'-om-ahee; from G2596 and G5530; to overuse, i.e. misuse:—abuse.

G2711.definition: καταψύχω katapsýchō, kat-ap-soo'-kho; from G2596 and G5594; to cool down (off), i.e. refresh:—cool.

G2712.definition:
κατείδωλος kateídōlos, kat-i'-do-los; from G2596 (intensively) and G1497; utterly idolatrous:—wholly given to
 idolatry.

G2713.definition: κατέναντι katénanti, kat-en'-an-tee; from G2596 and G1725; directly opposite:—before, over against.

G2714.definition:
κατενώπιον katenṓpion, kat-en-o'-pee-on; from G2596 and G1799; directly in front of:—before (the presence of),
 in the sight of.

G2715.definition:
κατεξουσιάζω katexousiázō, kat-ex-oo-see-ad'-zo; from G2596 and G1850; to have (wield) full privilege over:—exercise
 authority.

G2716.definition:
κατεργάζομαι katergázomai, kat-er-gad'-zom-ahee; from G2596 and G2038; to work fully, i.e. accomplish; by implication, to
 finish, fashion:—cause, to (deed), perform, work (out).

G2718.definition:
κατέρχομαι katérchomai, kat-er'-khom-ahee; from G2596 and G2064 (including its alternate); to come (or go) down
 (literally or figuratively):—come (down), depart, descend, go down,
 land.

G2719.definition:
κατεσθίω katesthíō, kat-es-thee'-o; from G2596 and G2068 (including its alternate); to eat down, i.e. devour
 (literally or figuratively):—devour.

G272.definition:
ἀμελέω ameléō, am-el-eh'-o; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3199; to be careless of:—make
 light of, neglect, be negligent, no regard.

G2720.definition:
κατευθύνω kateuthýnō, kat-yoo-thoo'-no; from G2596 and G2116; to straighten fully, i.e. (figuratively)
 direct:—guide, direct.

G2721.definition:
κατεφίστημι katephístēmi, kat-ef-is'-tay-mee; from G2596 and G2186; to stand over against, i.e. rush upon
 (assault):—make insurrection against.

G2722.definition:
κατέχω katéchō, kat-ekh'-o; from G2596 and G2192; to hold down (fast), in various applications
 (literally or figuratively):—have, hold (fast), keep (in memory),
 let, × make toward, possess, retain, seize on, stay, take, withhold.

G2723.definition:
κατηγορέω katēgoréō, kat-ay-gor-eh'-o; from G2725; to be a plaintiff, i.e. to charge with some
 offence:—accuse, object.

G2724.definition:
κατηγορία katēgoría, kat-ay-gor-ee'-ah; from G2725; a complaint ("category"), i.e. criminal charge:—accusation
 (X -ed).

G2725.definition:
†κατήγορος katḗgoros, kat-ay'-gor-os; from G2596 and G58; against one in the assembly, i.e. a complainant at
 law; specially, Satan:—accuser.

G2726.definition:
κατήφεια katḗpheia, kat-ay'-fi-ah; from a compound of G2596 and perhaps a derivative of the base of G5316
 (meaning downcast in look); demureness, i.e. (by implication)
 sadness:—heaviness.

G2727.definition:
κατηχέω katēchéō, kat-ay-kheh'-o; from G2596 and G2279; to sound down into the ears, i.e. (by implication)
 to indoctrinate ("catechize") or (genitive case) to apprise
 of:—inform, instruct, teach.

G2728.definition:
κατιόω katióō, kat-ee-o'-o; from G2596 and a derivative of G2447; to rust down, i.e.
 corrode:—canker.

G2729.definition: κατισχύω katischýō, kat-is-khoo'-o; from G2596 and G2480; to overpower:—prevail (against).

G273.definition:
ἄμεμπτος ámemptos, am'-emp-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3201; 
 irreproachable:—blameless, faultless, unblamable.

G2730.definition:
†κατοικέω katoikéō, kat-oy-keh'-o; from G2596 and G3611; to house permanently, i.e. reside (literally or
 figuratively):—dwell(-er), inhabitant(-ter).

G2731.definition:
κατοίκησις katoíkēsis, kat-oy'-kay-sis; from G2730; residence (properly, the act; but by implication,
 concretely, the mansion):—dwelling.

G2732.definition: κατοικητήριον katoikētḗrion, kat-oy-kay-tay'-ree-on; from a derivative of G2730; a dwelling-place:—habitation.

G2733.definition:
κατοικία katoikía, kat-oy-kee'-ah; residence (properly, the condition; but by implication, the
 abode itself):—habitation.

G2734.definition:
†κατοπτρίζομαι katoptrízomai, kat-op-trid'-zom-ahee; middle voice from a compound of G2596 and a derivative of G3700 (compare
 G2072); to mirror oneself, i.e. to see reflected
 (figuratively):—behold as in a glass.

G2736.definition:
†κάτω kátō, kat'-o; (compare G2737); adverb from G2596; downwards:—beneath, bottom, down,
 under.

G2737.definition: κατώτερος katṓteros, kat-o'-ter-os; comparative from G2736; inferior (locally, of Hades):—lower.

G2738.definition:
καῦμα kaûma, kow'-mah; from G2545; properly, a burn (concretely), but used (abstractly) of a
 glow:—heat.

G2739.definition: καυματίζω kaumatízō, kow-mat-id'-zo; from G2738; to burn:—scorch.

G274.definition: ἀμέμπτως amémptōs, am-emp'-toce; adverb from G273; faultlessly:—blameless, unblamably.

G2740.definition: καῦσις kaûsis, kow'-sis; from G2545; burning (the act):—be burned.

G2741.definition: †καυσόω kausóō, kow-so'-o; from G2740; to set on fire:—fervent heat.

G2742.definition: καύσων kaúsōn, kow'-sone; from G2741; a glare:—(burning) heat.

G2745.definition:
καύχημα kaúchēma, kow'-khay-mah; from G2744; a boast (properly, the object; by implication, the act) in
 a good or a bad sense:—boasting, (whereof) to glory (of), glorying,
 rejoice(-ing).

G2746.definition:
καύχησις kaúchēsis, kow'-khay-sis; from G2744; boasting (properly, the act; by implication, the object),
 in a good or a bad sense:—boasting, whereof I may glory, glorying,
 rejoicing.

G2747.definition:
†Κεγχρεαί Kenchreaí, keng-khreh-a'-hee; probably from kegchros (millet); Cenchreæ, a port of
 Corinth:—Cencrea.

G2748.definition:
†Κεδρών Kedrṓn, ked-rone'; of Hebrew origin (H6939); Cedron (i.e. Kidron), a brook near
 Jerusalem:—Cedron.

G2749.definition:
κεῖμαι keîmai, ki'-mahee; middle voice of a primary verb; to lie outstretched (literally or
 figuratively):—be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie. Compare
 G5087.

G275.definition:
ἀμέριμνος amérimnos, am-er'-im-nos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3308; not anxious:—without
 care(-fulness), secure.

G2750.definition: κειρία keiría, ki-ree'-ah; of uncertain affinity; a swathe, i.e. winding-sheet:—graveclothes.

G2751.definition: κείρω keírō, ki'-ro; a primary verb; to shear:—shear(-er).

G2752.definition: †κέλευμα kéleuma, kel'-yoo-mah; from G2753; a cry of incitement:—shout.

G2753.definition:
κελεύω keleúō, kel-yoo'-o; from a primary κέλλω kéllō (to urge on); "hail"; to incite by word, i.e.
 order:—bid, (at, give) command(-ment).

G2754.definition: κενοδοξία kenodoxía, ken-od-ox-ee'-ah; from G2755; empty glorying, i.e. self-conceit:—vain-glory.

G2755.definition:
κενόδοξος kenódoxos, ken-od'-ox-os; from G2756 and G1391; vainly glorifying, i.e. self-conceited:—desirous
 of vain-glory.

G2756.definition:
κενός kenós, ken-os'; apparently a primary word; empty (literally or figuratively):—empty,
 (in) vain.

G2757.definition:
κενοφωνία kenophōnía, ken-of-o-nee'-ah; from a presumed compound of G2756 and G5456; empty sounding, i.e.
 fruitless discussion:—vain.

G2758.definition:
κενόω kenóō, ken-o'-o; from G2756; to make empty, i.e. (figuratively) to abase, neutralize,
 falsify:—make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain.

G2759.definition:
κέντρον kéntron, ken'-tron; from κεντέω kentéō (to prick); a point ("centre"), i.e. a sting
 (figuratively, poison) or goad (figuratively, divine impulse):—prick,
 sting.

G2760.definition:
κεντυρίων kentyríōn, ken-too-ree'-ohn; of Latin origin; a centurion, i.e. captain of one hundred
 soldiers:—centurion.

G2761.definition: κενῶς kenōs, ken-oce'; adverb from G2756; vainly, i.e. to no purpose:—in vain.

G2762.definition:
κεραία keraía, ker-ah'-yah; feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G2768; something
 horn-like, i.e. (specially) the apex of a Hebrew letter (figuratively,
 the least particle):—tittle.

G2763.definition: κεραμεύς kerameús, ker-am-yooce'; from G2766; a potter:—potter.

G2764.definition: κεραμικός keramikós, ker-am-ik-os'; from G2766; made of clay, i.e. earthen:—of a potter.

G2765.definition:
κεράμιον kerámion, ker-am'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G2766; an earthenware vessel, i.e.
 jar:—pitcher.

G2766.definition:
κέραμος kéramos, ker'-am-os; probably from the base of G2767 (through the idea of mixing clay and
 water); earthenware, i.e. a tile (by analogy, a thin roof or
 awning):—tiling.

G2767.definition:
κεράννυμι keránnymi, ker-an'-noo-mee; prolonged form of a more primary κεράω keráō ker-ah'-o (which is used in
 certain tenses); to mingle, i.e. (by implication) to pour out (for
 drinking):—fill, pour out. Compare G3396.

G2768.definition:
κέρας kéras, ker'-as; from a primary κάρ kár (the hair of the head); a horn (literally or
 figuratively):—horn.

G2769.definition:
κεράτιον kerátion, ker-at'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G2768; something horned, i.e.
 (specially) the pod of the carob-tree:—husk.

G277.definition:
ἀμετακίνητος ametakínētos, am-et-ak-in'-ay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3334; 
 immovable:—unmovable.

G2770.definition: κερδαίνω kerdaínō, ker-dah'-ee-no; from G2771; to gain (literally or figuratively):—(get) gain, win.

G2771.definition:
κέρδος kérdos, ker'-dos; of uncertain affinity; gain (pecuniary or genitive case):—gain,
 lucre.

G2772.definition: κέρμα kérma, ker'-mah; from G2751; a clipping (bit), i.e. (specially) a coin:—money.

G2773.definition:
κερματιστής kermatistḗs, ker-mat-is-tace'; from a derivative of G2772; a handler of coins, i.e.
 money-broker:—changer of money.

G2774.definition:
κεφάλαιον kephálaion, kef-al'-ah-yon; neuter of a derivative of G2776; a principal thing, i.e. main point;
 specially, an amount (of money):—sum.

G2776.definition:
κεφαλή kephalḗ, kef-al-ay'; from the primary κάπτω káptō (in the sense of seizing); the head (as the
 part most readily taken hold of), literally or figuratively:—head.

G2777.definition:
κεφαλίς kephalís, kef-al-is'; from G2776; properly, a knob, i.e. (by implication) a roll (by
 extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was
 rolled):—volume.

G2778.definition:
κῆνσος kēnsos, kane'-sos; of Latin origin; properly, an enrollment ("census"), i.e. (by
 implication) a tax:—tribute.

G2779.definition: κῆπος kēpos, kay'-pos; of uncertain affinity; a garden:—garden.

G278.definition:
ἀμεταμέλητος ametamélētos, am-et-am-el'-ay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3338; 
 irrevocable:—without repentance, not to be repented of.

G2780.definition:
κηπουρός kēpourós, kay-poo-ros'; from G2779 and οὖρος oûros (a warden); a garden-keeper, i.e.
 gardener:—gardener.

G2782.definition:
κήρυγμα kḗrygma, kay'-roog-mah; from G2784; a proclamation (especially of the gospel; by implication,
 the gospel itself):—preaching.

G2783.definition:
κῆρυξ kēryx, kay'-roox; from G2784; a herald, i.e. of divine truth (especially of the
 gospel):—preacher.

G2784.definition:
κηρύσσω kērýssō, kay-roos'-so; of uncertain affinity; to herald (as a public crier), especially
 divine truth (the gospel):—preacher(-er), proclaim, publish.

G2785.definition:
κῆτος kētos, kay'-tos; probably from the base of G5490; a huge fish (as gaping for
 prey):—whale.

G2786.definition:
Κηφᾶς Kēphâs, kay-fas'; of Chaldee origin (compare H3710); the Rock; Cephas (i.e. Kepha), a
 surname of Peter:—Cephas.

G2787.definition:
κιβωτός kibōtós, kib-o-tos'; of uncertain derivation; a box, i.e. the sacred ark and that of
 Noah:—ark.

G2788.definition: κιθάρα kithára, kith-ar'-ah; of uncertain affinity; a lyre:—harp.

G2789.definition: κιθαρίζω kitharízō, kith-ar-id'-zo; from G2788; to play on a lyre:—harp.

G279.definition:
ἀμετανόητος ametanóētos, am-et-an-o'-ay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3340; 
 unrepentant:—impenitent.

G2790.definition:
κιθαρῳδός kitharōidós, kith-ar-o'-dos; from G2788 and a derivative of the same as G5603; a
 lyre-singer(-player), i.e. harpist:—harper.

G2791.definition: Κιλικία Kilikía, kil-ik-ee'-ah; probably of foreign origin; Cilicia, a region of Asia Minor:—Cilicia.

G2793.definition: κινδυνεύω kindyneúō, kin-doon-yoo'-o; from G2794; to undergo peril:—be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy.

G2794.definition: κίνδυνος kíndynos, kin'-doo-nos; of uncertain derivation; danger:—peril.

G2795.definition:
κινέω kinéō, kin-eh'-o; from κίω kíō (poetic for εἶμι eîmi, to go); to stir (transitively), literally
 or figuratively:—(re-)move(-r), way.

G2796.definition: κίνησις kínēsis, kin'-ay-sis; from G2795; a stirring:—moving.

G2797.definition: Κίς Kís, kis; of Hebrew origin (H7027); Cis (i.e. Kish), an Israelite:—Cis.

G2798.definition: κλάδος kládos, klad'-os; from G2806; a twig or bough (as if broken off):—branch.

G2799.definition: κλαίω klaíō, klah'-yo; of uncertain affinity; to sob, i.e. wail aloud (whereas G1145 is rather to cry silently):—bewail, weep.

G28.definition: †Ἄγαρ Ágar, ag'-ar; of Hebrew origin (H1904); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham:—Hagar.

G280.definition:
ἄμετρος ámetros, am'-et-ros; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3358; immoderate:—(thing) without
 measure.

G2800.definition: κλάσις klásis, klas'-is; from G2806; fracture (the act):—breaking.

G2801.definition: κλάσμα klásma, klas'-mah; from G2806; a piece (bit):—broken, fragment.

G2803.definition: Κλαυδία Klaudía, klow-dee'-ah; feminine of G2804; Claudia, a Christian woman:—Claudia.

G2804.definition: Κλαύδιος Klaúdios, klow'-dee-os; of Latin origin; Claudius, the name of two Romans:—Claudius.

G2805.definition: κλαυθμός klauthmós, klowth-mos'; from G2799; lamentation:—wailing, weeping, × wept.

G2806.definition: κλάω kláō, klah'-o; a primary verb; to break (specially, of bread):—break.

G2807.definition:
κλείς kleís, klice; from G2808; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or
 figuratively:—key.

G2808.definition: κλείω kleíō, kli'-o; a primary verb; to close (literally or figuratively):—shut (up).

G2809.definition:
κλέμμα klémma, klem'-mah; from G2813; stealing (properly, the thing stolen, but used of the
 act):—theft.

G281.definition:
ἀμήν amḗn, am-ane'; of Hebrew origin (H543); properly, firm, i.e. (figuratively)
 trustworthy; adverbially, surely (often as interjection, so be
 it):—amen, verily.

G2810.definition:
Κλεόπας Kleópas, kleh-op'-as; probably contracted from Κλεόπατρος Kleópatros (compound of G2811 and G3962); 
 Cleopas, a Christian:—Cleopas.

G2811.definition: κλέος kléos, kleh'-os; from a shorter form of G2564; renown (as if being called):—glory.

G2812.definition:
κλέπτης kléptēs, klep'-tace; from G2813; a stealer (literally or figuratively):—thief. Compare
 G3027.

G2813.definition: κλέπτω kléptō, klep'-to; a primary verb; to filch:—steal.

G2814.definition: κλῆμα klēma, kaly'-mah; from G2806; a limb or shoot (as if broken off):—branch.

G2815.definition:
Κλήμης Klḗmēs, klay'-mace; of Latin origin; merciful; Clemes (i.e. Clemens), a
 Christian:—Clement.

G2816.definition:
κληρονομέω klēronoméō, klay-ron-om-eh'-o; from G2818; to be an heir to (literally or figuratively):—be heir,
 (obtain by) inherit(-ance).

G2817.definition:
κληρονομία klēronomía, klay-ron-om-ee'-ah; from G2818; heirship, i.e. (concretely) a patrimony or (genitive case)
 a possession:—inheritance.

G2818.definition:
κληρονόμος klēronómos, klay-ron-om'-os; from G2819 and the base of G3551 (in its original sense of partitioning,
 i.e. (reflexively) getting by apportionment); a sharer by lot, i.e.
 inheritor (literally or figuratively); by implication, a
 possessor:—heir.

G2819.definition:
κλῆρος klēros, klay'-ros; probably from G2806 (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for
 the purpose; a die (for drawing chances); by implication, a portion
 (as if so secured); by extension, an acquisition (especially a
 patrimony, figuratively):—heritage, inheritance, lot, part.

G282.definition:
ἀμήτωρ amḗtōr, am-ay'-tore; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3384; motherless, i.e. of unknown
 maternity:—without mother.

G2820.definition:
κληρόω klēróō, klay-ro'-o; from G2819; to allot, i.e. (figuratively) to assign (a
 privilege):—obtain an inheritance.

G2821.definition: κλῆσις klēsis, klay'-sis; from a shorter form of G2564; an invitation (figuratively):—calling.

G2822.definition:
κλητός klētós, klay-tos'; from the same as G2821; invited, i.e. appointed, or (specially), a
 saint:—called.

G2823.definition: κλίβανος klíbanos, klib'-an-os; of uncertain derivation; an earthen pot used for baking in:—oven.

G2824.definition:
κλίμα klíma, klee'-mah; from G2827; a slope, i.e. (specially) a "clime" or tract of
 country:—part, region.

G2825.definition:
†κλίνη klínē, klee'-nay; from G2827; a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating):—bed,
 table.

G2826.definition:
κλινίδιον klinídion, klin-id'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G2825; a pallet or little
 couch:—bed.

G2827.definition:
κλίνω klínō, klee'-no; a primary verb; to slant or slope, i.e. incline or recline (literally
 or figuratively):—bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear
 away.

G2828.definition:
κλισία klisía, klee-see'-ah; from a derivative of G2827; properly, reclination, i.e. (concretely and
 specially), a party at a meal:—company.

G2829.definition: κλοπή klopḗ, klop-ay'; from G2813; stealing:—theft.

G283.definition:
ἀμίαντος amíantos, am-ee'-an-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3392; unsoiled,
 i.e. (figuratively) pure:—undefiled.

G2830.definition:
κλύδων klýdōn, kloo'-dohn; from κλύζω klýzō (to billow or dash over); a surge of the sea (literally or
 figuratively):—raging, wave.

G2831.definition:
κλυδωνίζομαι klydōnízomai, kloo-do-nid'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G2830; to surge, i.e. (figuratively) to
 fluctuate:—toss to and fro.

G2832.definition:
Κλωπᾶς Klōpâs, klo-pas'; of Chaldee origin (corresponding to H256); Clopas, an
 Israelite:—Cleophas.

G2833.definition:
κνήθω knḗthō, knay'-tho; from a primary κνάω knáō (to scrape); to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to
 tickle:—X itching.

G2834.definition: Κνίδος Knídos, knee'-dos; probably of foreign origin; Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor:—Cnidus.

G2835.definition: κοδράντης kodrántēs, kod-ran'-tace; of Latin origin; a quadrans, i.e. the fourth part of an as:—farthing.

G2836.definition:
κοιλία koilía, koy-lee'-ah; from κοῖλος koîlos ("hollow"); a cavity, i.e. (especially) the abdomen; by
 implication, the matrix; figuratively, the heart:—belly, womb.

G2837.definition:
κοιμάω koimáō, koy-mah'-o; from G2749; to put to sleep, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to
 slumber; figuratively, to decease:—(be a-, fall a-, fall on) sleep,
 be dead.

G2838.definition: κοίμησις koímēsis, koy'-may-sis; from G2837; sleeping, i.e. (by implication) repose:—taking of rest.

G2839.definition:
κοινός koinós, koy-nos'; probably from G4862; common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several,
 or (ceremonially) profane:—common, defiled, unclean, unholy.

G284.definition: Ἀμιναδάβ Aminadáb, am-ee-nad-ab'; of Hebrew origin (H5992); Aminadab, an Israelite:—Aminadab.

G2840.definition:
κοινόω koinóō, koy-no'-o; from G2839; to make (or consider) profane (ceremonially):—call common,
 defile, pollute, unclean.

G2841.definition:
κοινωνέω koinōnéō, koy-no-neh'-o; from G2844; to share with others (objectively or
 subjectively):—communicate, distribute, be partaker.

G2842.definition:
κοινωνία koinōnía, koy-nohn-ee'-ah; from G2844; partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social)
 intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction:—(to) communicate(-ation),
 communion, (contri-)distribution, fellowship.

G2843.definition:
κοινωνικός koinōnikós, koy-no-nee-kos'; from G2844; communicative, i.e. (pecuniarily) liberal:—willing to
 communicate.

G2844.definition:
κοινωνός koinōnós, koy-no-nos'; from G2839; a sharer, i.e. associate:—companion, × fellowship,
 partaker, partner.

G2845.definition:
κοίτη koítē, koy'-tay; from G2749; a couch; by extension, cohabitation; by implication, the
 male sperm:—bed, chambering, × conceive.

G2846.definition: κοιτών koitṓn, koy-tone'; from G2845; a bedroom:—+ chamberlain.

G2847.definition:
κόκκινος kókkinos, kok'-kee-nos; from G2848 (from the kernel-shape of the insect); 
 crimson-colored:—scarlet (colour, coloured).

G2848.definition: κόκκος kókkos, kok'-kos; apparently a primary word; a kernel of seed:—corn, grain.

G2849.definition:
κολάζω kolázō, kol-ad'-zo; from κόλος kólos (dwarf); properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to
 chastise (or reserve for infliction):—punish.

G285.definition: ἄμμος ámmos, am'-mos; perhaps from G260; sand (as heaped on the beach):—sand.

G2850.definition: κολακεία kolakeía, kol-ak-i'-ah; from a derivative of κόλαξ kólax (a fawner); flattery:—× flattering.

G2851.definition: κόλασις kólasis, kol'-as-is; from G2849; penal infliction:—punishment, torment.

G2852.definition: κολαφίζω kolaphízō, kol-af-id'-zo; from a derivative of the base of G2849; to rap with the fist:—buffet.

G2853.definition:
κολλάω kolláō, kol-lah'-o; from κόλλα kólla ("glue"); to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick
 (figuratively):—cleave, join (self), keep company.

G2854.definition:
†κολλούριον kolloúrion, kol-loo'-ree-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of κολλύρα kollýra (a cake; prob akin to the
 base of G2853); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of
 crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster:—eyesalve.

G2855.definition:
κολλυβιστής kollybistḗs, kol-loo-bis-tace'; from a presumed derivative of κόλλυβος kóllybos (a small coin; probably akin to
 G2854); a coin-dealer:—(money-)changer.

G2856.definition:
κολοβόω kolobóō, kol-ob-o'-o; from a derivative of the base of G2849; to dock, i.e. (figuratively)
 abridge:—shorten.

G2857.definition:
†Κολοσσαί Kolossaí, kol-os-sah'-ee; apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); Colossæ, a place
 in Asia Minor:—Colosse.

G2859.definition:
κόλπος kólpos, kol'-pos; apparently a primary word; the bosom; by analogy, a bay:—bosom,
 creek.

G286.definition: ἀμνός amnós, am-nos'; apparently a primary word; a lamb:—lamb.

G2860.definition: κολυμβάω kolymbáō, kol-oom-bah'-o; from κόλυμβος kólymbos (a diver); to plunge into water:—swim.

G2861.definition:
κολυμβήθρα kolymbḗthra, kol-oom-bay'-thrah; from G2860; 

 a diving-place, i.e. pond for bathing (or swimming):—pool.

G2862.definition: κολωνία kolōnía, kol-o-nee'-ah; of Latin origin; a Roman "colony" for veterans:—colony.

G2863.definition: κομάω komáō, kom-ah'-o; from G2864; to wear tresses of hair:—have long hair.

G2864.definition:
κόμη kómē, kom'-ay; apparently from the same as G2865; the hair of the head (locks, as
 ornamental, and thus differing from G2359; which properly denotes
 merely the scalp):—hair.

G2866.definition:
κομψότερον kompsóteron, komp-sot'-er-on; neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of 2865 (meaning,
 properly, well dressed, i.e. nice); figuratively, convalescent:—+
 began to amend.

G2867.definition: κονιάω koniáō, kon-ee-ah'-o; from κονία konía (dust; by analogy, lime); to whitewash:—whiten.

G2868.definition:
κονιορτός koniortós, kon-ee-or-tos'; from the base of G2867 and ornumi (to "rouse"); pulverulence (as blown
 about):—dust.

G2869.definition: κοπάζω kopázō, kop-ad'-zo; from G2873; to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax:—cease.

G287.definition: ἀμοιβή amoibḗ, am-oy-bay'; from ἀμείβω ameíbō (to exchange); requital:—requite.

G2870.definition: κοπετός kopetós, kop-et-os'; from G2875; mourning (properly, by beating the breast):—lamentation.

G2871.definition: κοπή kopḗ, kop-ay'; from G2875; cutting, i.e. carnage:—slaughter.

G2872.definition:
κοπιάω kopiáō, kop-ee-ah'-o; from a derivative of G2873; to feel fatigue; by implication, to work
 hard:—(bestow) labour, toil, be wearied.

G2873.definition:
κόπος kópos, kop'-os; from G2875; a cut, i.e. (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength),
 literally or figuratively; by implication, pains:—labour, + trouble,
 weariness.

G2874.definition: †κοπρία kopría, kop-ree'-ah; from κόπρος kópros (ordure; perhaps akin to G2875); manure:—dung(-hill).

G2875.definition:
κόπτω kóptō, kop'-to; a primary verb; to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in
 grief:—cut down, lament, mourn, (be-)wail. Compare the base of G5114.

G2876.definition: κόραξ kórax, kor'-ax; perhaps from G2880; a crow (from its voracity):—raven.

G2877.definition:
κοράσιον korásion, kor-as'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of κόρη kórē (a maiden); a (little)
 girl:—damsel, maid.

G2878.definition:
†κορβᾶν korbân, kor-ban'; of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (H7133); a votive offering
 and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by
 extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. the room where
 the contribution boxes stood:—Corban, treasury.

G2879.definition: Κορέ Koré, kor-eh'; of Hebrew origin (H7141); Core (i.e. Korach), an Israelite:—Core.

G288.definition:
ἄμπελος ámpelos, am'-pel-os; probably from the base of G297 and that of G257; a vine (as coiling
 about a support):—vine.

G2880.definition: κορέννυμι korénnymi, kor-en'-noo-mee; a primary verb; to cram, i.e. glut or sate:—eat enough, full.

G2881.definition: Κορίνθιος Korínthios, kor-in'-thee-os; from G2882; a Corinthian, i.e. inhabitant of Corinth:—Corinthian.

G2882.definition: Κόρινθος Kórinthos, kor'-in-thos; of uncertain derivation; Corinthus, a city of Greece:—Corinth.

G2883.definition: Κορνήλιος Kornḗlios, kor-nay'-lee-os; of Latin origin; Cornelius, a Roman:—Cornelius.

G2884.definition: κόρος kóros, kor'-os; of Hebrew origin (H3734); a cor, i.e. a specific measure:—measure.

G2885.definition:
κοσμέω kosméō, kos-meh'-o; from G2889; to put in proper order, i.e. decorate (literally or
 figuratively); specially, to snuff (a wick):—adorn, garnish, trim.

G2886.definition:
κοσμικός kosmikós, kos-mee-kos'; from G2889 (in its secondary sense); terrene ("cosmic"), literally
 (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt):—worldly.

G2887.definition:
κόσμιος kósmios, kos'-mee-os; from G2889 (in its primary sense); orderly, i.e. decorous:—of good
 behaviour, modest.

G2888.definition: κοσμοκράτωρ kosmokrátōr, kos-mok-fat'-ore; from G2889 and G2902; a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan:—ruler.

G289.definition: ἀμπελουργός ampelourgós, am-pel-oor-gos'; from G288 and G2041; a vine-worker, i.e. pruner:—vine-dresser.

G2890.definition: Κούαρτος Koúartos, koo'-ar-tos; of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian:—Quartus.

G2891.definition: †κοῦμι koûmi, koo'-mee; of Chaldee origin (H6966); cumi (i.e. rise!):—cumi.

G2892.definition: κουστωδία koustōdía, koos-to-dee'-ah; of Latin origin; "custody", i.e. a Roman sentry:—watch.

G2893.definition: κουφίζω kouphízō, koo-fid'-zo; from κοῦφος koûphos (light in weight); to unload:—lighten.

G2894.definition: κόφινος kóphinos, kof'-ee-nos; of uncertain derivation; a (small) basket:—basket.

G2895.definition: †κράββατος krábbatos, krab'-bat-os; probably of foreign origin; a mattress:—bed.

G2896.definition:
κράζω krázō, krad'-zo; a primary verb; properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e.
 (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat):—cry (out).

G2897.definition:
κραιπάλη kraipálē, krahee-pal'-ay; probably from the same as G726; properly, a headache (as a seizure of
 pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a
 glut):—surfeiting.

G2898.definition:
κρανίον kraníon, kran-ee'-on; diminutive of a derivative of the base of G2768; a skull
 ("cranium"):—Calvary, skull.

G2899.definition:
κράσπεδον kráspedon, kras'-ped-on; of uncertain derivation; a margin, i.e. (specially), a fringe or
 tassel:—border, hem.

G29.definition:
ἀγγαρεύω angareúō, ang-ar-yew'-o; of foreign origin (compare H104); properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by
 implication) to press into public service:—compel (to go).

G290.definition: ἀμπελών ampelṓn, am-pel-ohn'; from G288; a vineyard:—vineyard.

G2900.definition: κραταιός krataiós, krat-ah-yos'; from G2904; powerful:—mighty.

G2901.definition:
κραταιόω krataióō, krat-ah-yo'-o; from G2900; to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor:—be
 strengthened, be (wax) strong.

G2902.definition:
κρατέω kratéō, krat-eh'-o; from G2904; to use strength, i.e. seize or retain (literally or
 figuratively):—hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain,
 retain, take (by).

G2903.definition:
κράτιστος krátistos, krat'-is-tos; superlative of a derivative of G2904; strongest, i.e. (in dignity) very
 honorable:—most excellent (noble).

G2904.definition:
κράτος krátos, krat'-os; perhaps a primary word; vigor ("great") (literally or
 figuratively):—dominion, might(-ily), power, strength.

G2905.definition: κραυγάζω kraugázō, krow-gad'-zo; from G2906; to clamor:—cry out.

G2906.definition:
κραυγή kraugḗ, krow-gay'; from G2896; an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief):—clamour,
 cry(-ing).

G2907.definition: κρέας kréas, kreh'-as; perhaps a primary word; (butcher's) meat:—flesh.

G2909.definition:
κρείττων kreíttōn, krite'-tohn; comparative of a derivative of G2904; stronger, i.e. (figuratively)
 better, i.e. nobler:—best, better.

G291.definition:
†Ἀμπλίας Amplías, am-plee'-as; contracted for Latin ampliatus (enlarged); Amplias, a Roman
 Christian:—Amplias.

G2910.definition: κρεμάννυμι kremánnymi, krem-an'-noo-mee; a prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang:—hang.

G2911.definition: κρημνός krēmnós, krame-nos'; from G2910; overhanging, i.e. a precipice:—steep place.

G2912.definition: Κρής Krḗs, krace; from G2914; a Cretan, i.e. inhabitant of Crete:—Crete, Cretian.

G2913.definition:
Κρήσκης Krḗskēs, krace'-kace; of Latin origin; growing; Cresces (i.e. Crescens), a
 Christian:—Crescens.

G2914.definition:
Κρήτη Krḗtē, kray'-tay; of uncertain derivation; Crete, an island in the
 Mediterranean:—Crete.

G2915.definition: κριθή krithḗ, kree-thay'; of uncertain derivation; barley:—barley.

G2916.definition: κρίθινος kríthinos, kree'-thee-nos; from G2915; consisting of barley:—barley.

G2917.definition:
κρίμα kríma, kree'-mah; from G2919; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against
 ("crime")):—avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law,
 judgment.

G2918.definition: κρίνον krínon, kree'-non; perhaps a prim word; a lily:—lily.

G2919.definition:
κρίνω krínō, kree'-no; properly, to distinguish, i.e. decide (mentally or judicially); by
 implication, to try, condemn, punish:—avenge, conclude, condemn,
 damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law,
 ordain, call in question, sentence to, think.

G292.definition:
†ἀμύνομαι amýnomai, am-oo'-nom-ahee; middle voice of a primary verb; to ward off (for oneself), i.e.
 protect:—defend.

G2920.definition:
κρίσις krísis, kree'-sis; decision (subjectively or objectively, for or against); by
 extension, a tribunal; by implication, justice (especially, divine
 law):—accusation, condemnation, damnation, judgment.

G2921.definition: Κρίσπος Kríspos, kris'-pos; of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian:—Crispus.

G2922.definition:
κριτήριον kritḗrion, kree-tay'-ree-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G2923; a rule of judging
 ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal:—to judge, judgment
 (seat).

G2923.definition: κριτής kritḗs, kree-tace'; from G2919; a judge (genitive case or specially):—judge.

G2924.definition: κριτικός kritikós, krit-ee-kos'; from G2923; decisive ("critical"), i.e. discriminative:—discerner.

G2925.definition: κρούω kroúō, kroo'-o; apparently a primary verb; to rap:—knock.

G2926.definition: κρύπτη krýptē, kroop-tay'; feminine of G2927; a hidden place, i.e. cellar ("crypt"):—secret.

G2927.definition: κρυπτός kryptós, kroop-tos'; from G2928; concealed, i.e. private:—hid(-den), inward(-ly), secret.

G2928.definition:
κρύπτω krýptō, kroop'-to; a primary verb; to conceal (properly, by covering):—hide (self), keep
 secret, secret(-ly).

G2929.definition:
κρυσταλλίζω krystallízō, kroos-tal-lid'-zo; from G2930; to make (i.e. intransitively, resemble) ice
 ("crystallize"):—be clear as crystal.

G293.definition:
ἀμφίβληστρον amphíblēstron, am-fib'-lace-tron; from a compound of the base of G297 and G906; a (fishing) net (as thrown
 about the fish):—net.

G2930.definition:
κρύσταλλος krýstallos, kroos'-tal-los; from a derivative of κρύος krýos (frost); ice, i.e. (by analogy) rock
 "crystal":—crystal.

G2931.definition: κρυφῆ kryphē, kroo-fay'; adverb from G2928; privately:—in secret.

G2932.definition:
κτάομαι ktáomai, ktah'-om-ahee; a primary verb; to get, i.e. acquire (by any means; own):—obtain,
 possess, provide, purchase.

G2933.definition: κτῆμα ktēma, ktay'-mah; from G2932; an acquirement, i.e. estate:—possession.

G2934.definition: κτῆνος ktēnos, ktay'-nos; from G2932; property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal:—beast.

G2935.definition: κτήτωρ ktḗtōr, ktay'-tore; from G2932; an owner:—possessor.

G2936.definition:
κτίζω ktízō, ktid'-zo; probably akin to G2932 (through the idea of proprietorship of the
 manufacturer); to fabricate, i.e. found (form originally):—create,
 Creator, make.

G2937.definition:
κτίσις ktísis, ktis'-is; from G2936; original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the
 thing, literally or figuratively):—building, creation, creature,
 ordinance.

G2938.definition:
κτίσμα ktísma, ktis'-mah; from G2936; an original formation (concretely), i.e. product (created
 thing):—creature.

G2939.definition: †κτίστης ktístēs, ktis-tace'; from G2936; a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things):—Creator.

G294.definition: †ἀμφιέννυμι amphiénnymi, am-fee-en'-noo-mee; from the base of G297 and ἕννυμι hénnymi (to invest); to enrobe:—clothe.

G2940.definition:
κυβεία kybeía, koo-bi'-ah; from κύβος kýbos (a "cube", i.e. die for playing); gambling, i.e.
 (figuratively) artifice or fraud:—sleight.

G2941.definition:
κυβέρνησις kybérnēsis, koo-ber'-nay-sis; from κυβερνάω kybernáō (of Latin origin, to steer); pilotage, i.e.
 (figuratively) directorship (in the church):—government.

G2942.definition:
κυβερνήτης kybernḗtēs, koo-ber-nay'-tace; from the same as G2941; helmsman, i.e. (by implication)
 captain:—(ship) master.

G2943.definition:
κυκλόθεν kyklóthen, koo-kloth'-en; adverb from the same as G2945; from the circle, i.e. all
 around:—(round) about.

G2944.definition:
†κυκλόω kyklóō, koo-klo'-o; from the same as G2945; to encircle, i.e. surround:—compass (about),
 come (stand) round about.

G2945.definition:
†κύκλῳ kýklōi, koo'-klo; as if dative case of κύκλος kýklos (a ring, "cycle"; akin to G2947); i.e. in a
 circle (by implication, of G1722), i.e. (adverbially) all
 around:—round about.

G2946.definition: †κύλισμα kýlisma, koo'-lis-mah; from G2947; a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. filth:—wallowing.

G2947.definition:
†κυλιόω kylióō, koo-lee-o'-o; from the base of G2949 (through the idea of circularity; compare G2945,
 G1507); to roll about:—wallow.

G2948.definition:
κυλλός kyllós, kool-los'; from the same as G2947; rocking about, i.e. crippled (maimed, in feet
 or hands):—maimed.

G2949.definition:
κῦμα kŷma, koo'-mah; from κύω kýō (to swell (with young), i.e. bend, curve); a billow (as
 bursting or toppling):—wave.

G295.definition:
Ἀμφίπολις Amphípolis, am-fip'-ol-is; from the base of G297 and G4172; a city surrounded by a river;
 Amphipolis, a place in Macedonia:—Amphipolis.

G2950.definition:
κύμβαλον kýmbalon, koom'-bal-on; from a derivative of the base of G2949; a "cymbal" (as
 hollow):—cymbal.

G2951.definition: κύμινον kýminon, koo'-min-on; of foreign origin (compare H3646); dill or fennel ("cummin"):—cummin.

G2952.definition: κυνάριον kynárion, koo-nar'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G2965; a puppy:—dog.

G2953.definition: Κύπριος Kýprios, koo'-pree-os; from G2954; a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. inhabitant of Cyprus:—of Cyprus.

G2954.definition: Κύπρος Kýpros, koo'-pros; of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean:—Cyprus.

G2955.definition: †κύπτω kýptō, koop'-to; probably from the base of G2949; to bend forward:—stoop (down).

G2956.definition:
Κυρηναῖος Kyrēnaîos, koo-ray-nah'-yos; from G2957; i.e. Cyrenæan, i.e. inhabitant of Cyrene:—of Cyrene,
 Cyrenian.

G2957.definition: Κυρήνη Kyrḗnē, koo-ray'-nay; of uncertain derivation; Cyrene, a region of Africa:—Cyrene.

G2958.definition: Κυρήνιος Kyrḗnios, koo-ray'-nee-os; of Latin origin; Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman:—Cyrenius.

G2959.definition: Κυρία Kyría, koo-ree'-ah; feminine of G2962; Cyria, a Christian woman:—lady.

G296.definition:
ἄμφοδον ámphodon, am'-fod-on; from the base of G297 and G3598; a fork in the road:—where two ways
 meet.

G2960.definition: κυριακός kyriakós, koo-ree-ak-os'; from G2962; belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus):—Lord's.

G2961.definition:
κυριεύω kyrieúō, ko-ree-yoo'-o; from G2962; to rule:—have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise
 lordship over.

G2962.definition:
κύριος kýrios, koo'-ree-os; from κῦρος kŷros (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun)
 controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title):—God,
 Lord, master, Sir.

G2963.definition:
κυριότης kyriótēs, koo-ree-ot'-ace; from G2962; mastery, i.e. (concretely and collectively)
 rulers:—dominion, government.

G2964.definition: κυρόω kyróō, koo-ro'-o; from the same as G2962; to make authoritative, i.e. ratify:—confirm.

G2965.definition: κύων kýōn, koo'-ohn; a primary word; a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively):—dog.

G2966.definition: κῶλον kōlon, ko'-lon; from the base of G2849; a limb of the body (as if lopped):—carcase.

G2967.definition:
κωλύω kōlýō, ko-loo'-o; from the base of G2849; to estop, i.e. prevent (by word or
 act):—forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand.

G2968.definition: κώμη kṓmē, ko'-may; from G2749; a hamlet (as if laid down):—town, village.

G2969.definition: κωμόπολις kōmópolis, ko-mop'-ol-is; from G2968 and G4172; an unwalled city:—town.

G297.definition: ἀμφότερος amphóteros, am-fot'-er-os; comparative of ἀμφί amphí (around); (in plural) both:—both.

G2970.definition: κῶμος kōmos, ko'-mos; from G2749; a carousal (as if letting loose):—revelling, rioting.

G2971.definition:
κώνωψ kṓnōps, ko'-nopes; apparently a derivative of the base of G2759 and a derivative of G3700; 
 a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis):—gnat.

G2972.definition: Κώς Kṓs, koce; of uncertain origin; Cos, an island in the Mediterranean:—Cos.

G2973.definition:
Κωσάμ Kōsám, ko-sam'; of Hebrew origin (compare H7081); Cosam (i.e. Kosam) an
 Israelite:—Cosam.

G2974.definition:
κωφός kōphós, ko-fos'; from G2875; blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech
 (dumb):—deaf, dumb, speechless.

G2975.definition:
λαγχάνω lanchánō, lang-khan'-o; a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate
 in certain tenses; to lot, i.e. determine (by implication, receive)
 especially by lot:—his lot be, cast lots, obtain.

G2976.definition:
Λάζαρος Lázaros, lad'-zar-os; probably of Hebrew origin (H499); Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of
 two Israelites (one imaginary):—Lazarus.

G2977.definition: †λάθρα láthra, lath'-rah; adverb from G2990; privately:—privily, secretly.

G2978.definition: λαῖλαψ laîlaps, lah'-ee-laps; of uncertain derivation; a whirlwind (squall):—storm, tempest.

G2979.definition: λακτίζω laktízō, lak-tid'-zo; from adverb λάξ láx (heelwise); to recalcitrate:—kick.

G298.definition:
ἀμώμητος amṓmētos, am-o'-may-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3469; 
 unblamable:—blameless.

G2980.definition:
λαλέω laléō, lal-eh'-o; a prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, i.e. utter
 words:—preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare G3004.

G2981.definition: λαλιά laliá, lal-ee-ah'; from G2980; talk:—saying, speech.

G2982.definition:
†λαμά lamá, lam-ah'; of Hebrew origin (H4100 with prepositional prefix); 
 lama (i.e. why):—lama.

G2983.definition:
λαμβάνω lambánō, lam-ban'-o; a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate
 in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and
 figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas
 G1209 is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while
 G138 is more violent, to seize or remove)):—accept, + be amazed,
 assay, attain, bring, × when I call, catch, come on (X unto), +
 forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up).

G2984.definition: Λάμεχ Lámech, lam'-ekh; of Hebrew origin (H3929); Lamech (i.e. Lemek), a patriarch:—Lamech.

G2985.definition: λαμπάς lampás, lam-pas'; from G2989; a "lamp" or flambeau:—lamp, light, torch.

G2986.definition:
λαμπρός lamprós, lam-pros'; from the same as G2985; radiant; by analogy, limpid; figuratively,
 magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance):—bright, clear, gay, goodly,
 gorgeous, white.

G2987.definition: λαμπρότης lamprótēs, lam-prot'-ace; from G2986; brilliancy:—brightness.

G2988.definition:
λαμπρῶς lamprōs, lam-proce'; adverb from G2986; brilliantly, i.e. figuratively,
 luxuriously:—sumptuously.

G2989.definition:
λάμπω lámpō, lam'-po; a primary verb; to beam, i.e. radiate brilliancy (literally or
 figuratively):—give light, shine.

G299.definition:
†ἄμωμος ámōmos, am'-o-mos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3470; unblemished (literally or
 figuratively):—without blame (blemish, fault, spot), faultless,
 unblamable.

G2990.definition:
λανθάνω lanthánō, lan-than'-o; a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate
 in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used
 adverbially, unwittingly:—be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.

G2991.definition:
λαξευτός laxeutós, lax-yoo-tos'; from a compound of λᾶς lâs (a stone) and the base of G3584 (in its original
 sense of scraping); rock-quarried:—hewn in stone.

G2992.definition:
†λαός laós, lah-os'; apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from
 G1218, which denotes one's own populace):—people.

G2993.definition:
Λαοδίκεια Laodíkeia, lah-od-ik'-i-ah; from a compound of G2992 and G1349; Laodicia, a place in Asia
 Minor:—Laodicea.

G2994.definition: Λαοδικεύς Laodikeús, lah-od-ik-yooce'; from G2993; a Laodicean, i.e. inhabitant of Laodicia:—Laodicean.

G2995.definition: λάρυγξ lárynx, lar'-oongks; of uncertain derivation; the throat ("larynx"):—throat.

G2996.definition: †Λασαία Lasaía, las-ah'-yah; of uncertain origin; Lasæa, a place in Crete:—Lasea.

G2998.definition:
λατομέω latoméō, lat-om-eh'-o; from the same as the first part of G2991 and the base of G5114; to
 quarry:—hew.

G2999.definition: λατρεία latreía, lat-ri'-ah; from G3000; ministration of God, i.e. worship:—(divine) service.

G3.definition: †Ἀβαδδών Abaddṓn, ab-ad-dohn'; of Hebrew origin (H11); a destroying angel:—Abaddon.

G30.definition:
†ἀγγεῖον angeîon, ang-eye'-on; from ἄγγος ángos (a pail, perhaps as bent; compare the base of G43); a
 receptacle:—vessel.

G3000.definition:
λατρεύω latreúō, lat-ryoo'-o; from λάτρις látris (a hired menial); to minister (to God), i.e. render
 religious homage:—serve, do the service, worship(-per).

G3001.definition: λάχανον láchanon, lakh'-an-on; from λαχαίνω lachaínō (to dig); a vegetable:—herb.

G3003.definition:
†λεγεών legeṓn, leg-eh-ohn'; of Latin origin; a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment
 (figuratively):—legion.

G3004.definition:
†λέγω légō, leg'-o; a primary verb; properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate
 (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas G2036 and
 G5346 generally refer to an individual expression or speech
 respectively; while G4483 is properly to break silence merely, and G2980
 means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean:—ask,
 bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on),
 shew, speak, tell, utter.

G3005.definition: λεῖμμα leîmma, lime'-mah; from G3007; a remainder:—remnant.

G3006.definition: λεῖος leîos, li'-os; apparently a primary word; smooth, i.e. "level":—smooth.

G3007.definition:
λείπω leípō, li'-po; a primary verb; to leave, i.e. (intransitively or passively) to fail
 or be absent:—be destitute (wanting), lack.

G3008.definition:
λειτουργέω leitourgéō, li-toorg-eh'-o; from G3011; to be a public servant, i.e. (by analogy) to perform
 religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve):—minister.

G3009.definition:
λειτουργία leitourgía, li-toorg-ee'-ah; from G3008; public function (as priest ("liturgy") or
 almsgiver):—ministration(-try), service.

G301.definition: Ἀμώς Amṓs, am-oce'; of Hebrew origin (H531); Amos, an Israelite:—Amos.

G3010.definition:
λειτουργικός leitourgikós, li-toorg-ik-os'; from the same as G3008; functional publicly ("liturgic"); i.e.
 beneficient:—ministering.

G3011.definition:
λειτουργός leitourgós, li-toorg-os'; from a derivative of G2992 and G2041; a public servant, i.e. a
 functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (genitive case) a worshipper
 (of God) or benefactor (of man):—minister(-ed).

G3012.definition: λέντιον léntion, len'-tee-on; of Latin origin; a "linen" cloth, i.e. apron:—towel.

G3013.definition: λεπίς lepís, lep-is'; from λέπω lépō (to peel); a flake:—scale.

G3014.definition: λέπρα lépra, lep'-rah; from the same as G3013; scaliness, i.e. "leprosy":—leprosy.

G3015.definition: λεπρός leprós, lep-ros'; from the same as G3014; scaly, i.e. leprous (a leper):—leper.

G3016.definition:
†λεπτόν leptón, lep-ton'; neuter of a derivative of the same as G3013; something scaled (light),
 i.e. a small coin:—mite.

G3017.definition:
†Λευΐ Leuḯ, lyoo'-ee; of Hebrew origin (H3878); Levi, the name of three Israelites:—Levi. 
 Compare G3018.

G3019.definition: †Λευΐτης Leuḯtēs, lyoo-ee'-tace; from G3017; a Levite, i.e. descendant of Levi:—Levite.

G302.definition:
ἄν án, an; a primary particle, denoting a supposition, wish, possibility or
 uncertainty:—(what-, where-, wither-, who-)soever. Usually
 unexpressed except by the subjunctive or potential mood. Also
 contracted for G1437.

G3020.definition: †Λευϊτικός Leuïtikós, lyoo-it'-ee-kos; from G3019; Levitic, i.e. relating to the Levites:—Levitical.

G3021.definition: λευκαίνω leukaínō, lyoo-kah'-ee-no; from G3022; to whiten:—make white, whiten.

G3022.definition: λευκός leukós, lyoo-kos'; from λύκη lýkē ("light"); white:—white.

G3023.definition: †λέων léōn, leh-ohn'; a primary word; a "lion":—lion.

G3024.definition: λήθη lḗthē, lay'-thay; from G2990; forgetfulness:—+ forget.

G3025.definition: ληνός lēnós, lay-nos'; apparently a primary word; a trough, i.e. wine-vat:—winepress.

G3026.definition:
λῆρος lēros, lay'-ros; apparently a primary word; twaddle, i.e. an incredible story:—idle
 tale.

G3027.definition: λῃστής lēistḗs, lace-tace'; from ληΐζομαι lēḯzomai (to plunder); a brigand:—robber, thief.

G3028.definition: †λῆμψις lēmpsis, lape'-sis; from G2983; receipt (the act):—receiving.

G3029.definition:
λίαν lían, lee'-an; of uncertain affinity; much (adverbially):—exceeding, great(-ly),
 sore, very (+ chiefest).

G303.definition:
†ἀνά aná, an-ah'; a primary preposition and adverb; properly, up; but (by extension)
 used (distributively) severally, or (locally) at (etc.):—and, apiece,
 by, each, every (man), in, through.

G3030.definition:
λίβανος líbanos, lib'-an-os; of foreign origin (H3828); the incense-tree, i.e. (by implication)
 incense itself:—frankincense.

G3031.definition:
λιβανωτός libanōtós, lib-an-o-tos'; from G3030; frankincense, i.e. (by extension) a censer for burning
 it:—censer.

G3032.definition: Λιβερτῖνος Libertînos, lib-er-tee'-nos; of Latin origin; a Roman freedman:—Libertine.

G3033.definition: Λιβύη Libýē, lib-oo'-ay; probably from G3047; Libye, a region of Africa:—Libya.

G3034.definition: λιθάζω litházō, lith-ad'-zo; from G3037; to lapidate:—stone.

G3035.definition: λίθινος líthinos, lith-ee'-nos; from G3037; stony, i.e. made of stone:—of stone.

G3036.definition:
λιθοβολέω lithoboléō, lith-ob-ol-eh'-o; from a compound of G3037 and G906; to throw stones, i.e.
 lapidate:—stone, cast stones.

G3037.definition:
λίθος líthos, lee'-thos; apparently a primary word; a stone (literally or
 figuratively):—(mill-, stumbling-)stone.

G3038.definition:
λιθόστρωτος lithóstrōtos, lith-os'-tro-tos; from G3037 and a derivative of G4766; stone-strewed, i.e. a tessellated
 mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed:—Pavement.

G3039.definition:
λικμάω likmáō, lik-mah'-o; from λικμός likmós, the equivalent of λίκνον líknon (a winnowing fan or basket); to
 winnow, i.e. (by analogy), to triturate:—grind to powder.

G304.definition: ἀναβαθμός anabathmós, an-ab-ath-mos'; from G305 (compare G898); a stairway:—stairs.

G3040.definition: λιμήν limḗn, lee-mane'; apparently a primary word; a harbor:—haven. Compare G2568.

G3041.definition:
λίμνη límnē, lim'-nay; probably from G3040 (through the idea of nearness of shore); a pond
 (large or small):—lake.

G3042.definition:
λιμός limós, lee-mos'; probably from G3007 (through the idea of destitution); a scarcity of
 food:—dearth, famine, hunger.

G3043.definition: λίνον línon, lee'-non; probably a primary word; flax, i.e. (by implication) "linen":—linen.

G3044.definition: †Λίνος Línos, lee'-nos; perhaps from G3043; Linus, a Christian:—Linus.

G3045.definition: λιπαρός liparós, lip-ar-os'; from λίπος lípos (grease); fat, i.e. (figuratively) sumptuous:—dainty.

G3046.definition: λίτρα lítra, lee'-trah; of Latin origin (libra); a pound in weight:—pound.

G3047.definition:
λίψ líps, leeps; probably from λείβω leíbō (to pour a "libation"); the south(- west) wind (as
 bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter):—southwest.

G3048.definition:
λογία logía, log-ee'-ah; from G3056 (in the commercial sense); a contribution:—collection,
 gathering.

G3049.definition:
λογίζομαι logízomai, log-id'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G3056; to take an inventory, i.e. estimate (literally
 or figuratively):—conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem,
 impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on).

G305.definition:
ἀναβαίνω anabaínō, an-ab-ah'-ee-no; from G303 and the base of G939; to go up (literally or
 figuratively):—arise, ascend (up), climb (go, grow, rise, spring) up,
 come (up).

G3050.definition: λογικός logikós, log-ik-os'; from G3056; rational ("logical"):—reasonable, of the word.

G3051.definition: λόγιον lógion, log'-ee-on; neuter of G3052; an utterance (of God):—oracle.

G3052.definition: λόγιος lógios, log'-ee-os; from G3056; fluent, i.e. an orator:—eloquent.

G3053.definition:
λογισμός logismós, log-is-mos'; from G3049; computation, i.e. (figuratively) reasoning (conscience,
 conceit):—imagination, thought.

G3054.definition:
λογομαχέω logomachéō, log-om-akh-eh'-o; from a compound of G3056 and G3164; to be disputatious (on
 trifles):—strive about words.

G3055.definition:
λογομαχία logomachía, log-om-akh-ee'-ah; from the same as G3054; disputation about trifles
 ("logomachy"):—strife of words.

G3056.definition:
λόγος lógos, log'-os; from G3004; something said (including the thought); by implication, a
 topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or
 motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in
 John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ):—account, cause,
 communication, × concerning, doctrine, fame, × have to do, intent,
 matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove,
 say(-ing), shew, × speaker, speech, talk, thing, + none of these
 things move me, tidings, treatise, utterance, word, work.

G3057.definition: λόγχη lónchē, long'-khay; perhaps a primary word; a "lance":—spear.

G3058.definition: λοιδορέω loidoréō, loy-dor-eh'-o; from G3060; to reproach, i.e. vilify:—revile.

G3059.definition: λοιδορία loidoría, loy-dor-ee'-ah; from G3060; slander or vituperation:—railing, reproach(-fully).

G306.definition: †ἀναβάλλομαι anabállomai, an-ab-al'-lom-ahee; middle voice from G303 and G906; to put off (for oneself):—defer.

G3060.definition: λοίδορος loídoros, loy'-dor-os; from λοιδός loidós (mischief); abusive, i.e. a blackguard:—railer, reviler.

G3061.definition:
λοιμός loimós, loy'-mos; of uncertain affinity; a plague (literally, the disease, or
 figuratively, a pest):—pestilence(-t).

G3062.definition:
†λοιποί loipoí, loy-poy'; masculine plural of a derivative of G3007; remaining ones:—other,
 which remain, remnant, residue, rest.

G3065.definition: Λουκᾶς Loukâs, loo-kas'; contracted from Latin Lucanus; Lucas, a Christian:—Lucas, Luke.

G3066.definition: Λούκιος Loúkios, loo'-kee-os; of Latin origin; illuminative; Lucius, a Christian:—Lucius.

G3067.definition: λουτρόν loutrón, loo-tron'; from G3068; a bath, i.e. (figuratively), baptism:—washing.

G3068.definition:
λούω loúō, loo'-o; a primary verb; to bathe (the whole person; whereas G3538 means to wet
 a part only, and G4150 to wash, cleanse garments exclusively):—wash.

G3069.definition:
Λύδδα Lýdda, lud'-dah; of Hebrew origin (H3850); Lydda (i.e. Lod), a place in
 Palestine:—Lydda.

G307.definition:
ἀναβιβάζω anabibázō, an-ab-ee-bad'-zo; from G303 and a derivative of the base of G939; to cause to go up, i.e.
 haul (a net):—draw.

G3070.definition:
Λυδία Lydía, loo-dee'-ah; properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia
 Minor); Lydia, a Christian woman:—Lydia.

G3071.definition:
Λυκαονία Lykaonía, loo-kah-on-ee'-ah; perhaps remotely from G3074; Lycaonia, a region of Asia
 Minor:—Lycaonia.

G3072.definition:
Λυκαονιστί Lykaonistí, loo-kah-on-is-tee'; adverb from a derivative of G3071; Lycaonistically, i.e. in the
 language of the Lycaonians:—in the speech of Lycaonia.

G3073.definition: Λυκία Lykía, loo-kee'-ah; probably remotely from G3074; Lycia, a province of Asia Minor:—Lycia.

G3074.definition:
λύκος lýkos, loo'-kos; perhaps akin to the base of G3022 (from the whitish hair); a
 wolf:—wolf.

G3076.definition:
λυπέω lypéō, loo-peh'-o; from G3077; to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad:—cause
 grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow(-ful), be (make) sorry.

G3077.definition:
λύπη lýpē, loo'-pay; apparently a primary word; sadness:—grief, grievous, + grudgingly,
 heaviness, sorrow.

G3078.definition:
Λυσανίας Lysanías, loo-san-ee'-as; from G3080 and ἀνία anía (trouble); grief-dispelling; Lysanias, a governor
 of Abilene:—Lysanias.
