G3079.definition: Λυσίας Lysías, loo-see'-as; of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman:—Lysias.

G308.definition:
ἀναβλέπω anablépō, an-ab-lep'-o; from G303 and G991; to look up; by implication, to recover sight:—look
 (up), see, receive sight.

G3080.definition: λύσις lýsis, loo'-sis; from G3089; a loosening, i.e. (specially), divorce:—to be loosed.

G3081.definition:
†λυσιτελεῖ lysiteleî, loo-sit-el-i'; third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a
 compound of G3080 and G5056; impersonally, it answers the purpose, i.e.
 is advantageous:—it is better.

G3082.definition: Λύστρα Lýstra, loos'-trah; of uncertain origin; Lystra, a place in Asia Minor:—Lystra.

G3083.definition:
λύτρον lýtron, loo'-tron; from G3089; something to loosen with, i.e. a redemption price
 (figuratively, atonement):—ransom.

G3084.definition: λυτρόω lytróō, loo-tro'-o; from G3083; to ransom (literally or figuratively):—redeem.

G3085.definition: λύτρωσις lýtrōsis, loo'-tro-sis; from G3084; a ransoming (figuratively):—+ redeemed, redemption.

G3086.definition: λυτρωτής lytrōtḗs, loo-tro-tace'; from G3084; a redeemer (figuratively):—deliverer.

G3087.definition: λυχνία lychnía, lookh-nee'-ah; from G3088; a lamp-stand (literally or figuratively):—candlestick.

G3088.definition:
λύχνος lýchnos, lookh'-nos; from the base of G3022; a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally
 or figuratively):—candle, light.

G3089.definition:
λύω lýō, loo'-o; a primary verb; to "loosen" (literally or figuratively):—break (up),
 destroy, dissolve, (un-)loose, melt, put off. Compare G4486.

G309.definition: ἀνάβλεψις anáblepsis, an-ab'-lep-sis; from G308; restoration of sight:—recovery of sight.

G3090.definition: Λωΐς Lōḯs, lo-ece'; of uncertain origin; Lois, a Christian woman:—Lois.

G3091.definition: Λώτ Lṓt, lote; of Hebrew origin (H3876); Lot, a patriarch:—Lot.

G3092.definition: Μαάθ Maáth, mah-ath'; probably of Hebrew origin; Maath, an Israelite:—Maath.

G3093.definition:
†Μαγδαλά Magdalá, mag-dal-ah'; of Chaldee origin (compare H4026); the tower; Magdala (i.e. Migdala), a
 place in Palestine:—Magdala.

G3094.definition:
Μαγδαληνή Magdalēnḗ, mag-dal-ay-nay'; feminine of a derivative of G3093; a female Magdalene, i.e. inhabitant
 of Magdala:—Magdalene.

G3096.definition: μαγεύω mageúō, mag-yoo'-o; from G3097; to practice magic:—use sorcery.

G3097.definition:
μάγος mágos, mag'-os; of foreign origin (H7248); a Magian, i.e. Oriental scientist; by
 implication, a magician:—sorcerer, wise man.

G3098.definition:
Μαγώγ Magṓg, mag-ogue'; of Hebrew origin (H4031); Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively)
 an Antichristian party:—Magog.

G3099.definition:
†Μαδιάν Madián, mad-ee-on'; of Hebrew origin (H4080); Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of
 Arabia:—Madian.

G31.definition: ἀγγελία angelía, ang-el-ee'-ah; from G32; an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept:—message.

G310.definition: ἀναβοάω anaboáō, an-ab-o-ah'-o; from G303 and G994; to halloo:—cry (aloud, out).

G3100.definition:
μαθητεύω mathēteúō, math-ayt-yoo'-o; from G3101; intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to
 disciple, i.e. enrol as scholar:—be disciple, instruct, teach.

G3101.definition: μαθητής mathētḗs, math-ay-tes'; from G3129; a learner, i.e. pupil:—disciple.

G3102.definition: μαθήτρια mathḗtria, math-ay'-tree-ah; feminine from G3101; a female pupil:—disciple.

G3103.definition:
†Μαθουσάλα Mathousála, math-oo-sal'-ah; of Hebrew origin (H4968); Mathusala (i.e. Methushelach), an
 antediluvian:—Mathusala.

G3105.definition:
μαίνομαι maínomai, mah'-ee-nom-ahee; middle voice from a primary μάω máō (to long for; through the idea of
 insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac":—be beside self (mad).

G3106.definition:
μακαρίζω makarízō, mak-ar-id'-zo; from G3107; to beatify, i.e. pronounce (or esteem) fortunate:—call
 blessed, count happy.

G3107.definition:
μακάριος makários, mak-ar'-ee-os; a prolonged form of the poetical μάκαρ mákar (meaning the same); supremely
 blest; by extension, fortunate, well off:—blessed, happy(X -ier).

G3108.definition:
μακαρισμός makarismós, mak-ar-is-mos'; from G3106; beatification, i.e. attribution of good
 fortune:—blessedness.

G3109.definition: Μακεδονία Makedonía, mak-ed-on-ee'-ah; from G3110; Macedonia, a region of Greece:—Macedonia.

G311.definition: ἀναβολή anabolḗ, an-ab-ol-ay'; from G306; a putting off:—delay.

G3110.definition:
Μακεδών Makedṓn, mak-ed'-ohn; of uncertain derivation; a Macedon (Macedonian), i.e. inhabitant of
 Macedonia:—of Macedonia, Macedonian.

G3111.definition:
μάκελλον mákellon, mak'-el-lon; of Latin origin (macellum); a butcher's stall, meat market or
 provision-shop:—shambles.

G3112.definition:
μακράν makrán, mak-ran'; feminine accusative case singular of G3117 (G3598 being implied); at a
 distance (literally or figuratively):—(a-)far (off), good (great) way
 off.

G3113.definition: μακρόθεν makróthen, mak-roth'-en; adverb from G3117; from a distance or afar:—afar off, from far.

G3114.definition:
μακροθυμέω makrothyméō, mak-roth-oo-meh'-o; from the same as G3116; to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively)
 forbearing or (subjectively) patient:—bear (suffer) long, be
 longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure.

G3115.definition:
μακροθυμία makrothymía, mak-roth-oo-mee'-ah; from the same as G3116; longanimity, i.e. (objectively) forbearance or
 (subjectively) fortitude:—longsuffering, patience.

G3116.definition:
†μακροθυμώς makrothymṓs, mak-roth-oo-moce'; adverb of a compound of G3117 and G2372; with long (enduring) temper,
 i.e. leniently:—patiently.

G3117.definition:
μακρός makrós, mak-ros'; from G3372; long (in place (distant) or time (neuter plural)):—far,
 long.

G3118.definition: μακροχρόνιος makrochrónios, mak-rokh-ron'-ee-os; from G3117 and G5550; long-timed, i.e. long-lived:—live long.

G3119.definition: μαλακία malakía, mal-ak-ee'-ah; from G3120; softness, i.e. enervation (debility):—disease.

G312.definition:
ἀναγγέλλω anangéllō, an-ang-el'-lo; from G303 and the base of G32; to announce (in detail):—declare,
 rehearse, report, show, speak, tell.

G3120.definition:
μαλακός malakós, mal-ak-os'; of uncertain affinity; soft, i.e. fine (clothing); figuratively, a
 catamite:—effeminate, soft.

G3121.definition:
Μαλελεήλ Maleleḗl, mal-el-eh-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H4111); Maleleel (i.e. Mahalalel), an
 antediluvian:—Maleleel.

G3122.definition:
μάλιστα málista, mal'-is-tah; neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb μάλα mála
 (very); (adverbially) most (in the greatest degree) or
 particularly:—chiefly, most of all, (e-)specially.

G3123.definition:
μᾶλλον mâllon, mal'-lon; neuter of the comparative of the same as G3122; (adverbially) more (in
 a greater degree)) or rather:—+ better, × far, (the) more (and more),
 (so) much (the more), rather.

G3124.definition: Μάλχος Málchos, mal'-khos; of Hebrew origin (H4429); Malchus, an Israelite:—Malchus.

G3125.definition: μάμμη mámmē, mam'-may; of natural origin ("mammy"); a grandmother:—grandmother.

G3126.definition:
μαμμωνᾶς mammōnâs, mam-mo-nas'; of Chaldee origin (confidence, i.e. wealth, personified); mammonas,
 i.e. avarice (deified):—mammon.

G3127.definition: Μαναήν Manaḗn, man-ah-ane'; of uncertain origin; Manaën, a Christian:—Manaen.

G3128.definition:
†Μανασσῆς Manassēs, man-as-sace'; of Hebrew origin (H4519); Mannasses (i.e. Menashsheh), an
 Israelite:—Manasses.

G3129.definition:
μανθάνω manthánō, man-than'-o; prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which,
 μαθέω mathéō, is used as an alternate in certain tenses; to learn
 (in any way):—learn, understand.

G313.definition:
ἀναγεννάω anagennáō, an-ag-en-nah'-o; from G303 and G1080; to beget or (by extension) bear (again):—beget,
 (bear) × (again).

G3130.definition: μανία manía, man-ee'-ah; from G3105; craziness:—(+ make) × mad.

G3131.definition: μάννα mánna, man'-nah; of Hebrew origin (H4478); manna (i.e. man), an edible gum:—manna.

G3132.definition:
μαντεύομαι manteúomai, mant-yoo'-om-ahee; from a derivative of G3105 (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave
 through inspiration); to divine, i.e. utter spells (under pretense of
 foretelling:—by soothsaying.

G3133.definition:
μαραίνω maraínō, mar-ah'-ee-no; of uncertain affinity; to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and
 passively) to pass away:—fade away.

G3134.definition:
†μαρὰν ἀθά maràn athá, mar'-an ath'-ah; of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come); maranatha, i.e. an
 exclamation of the approaching divine judgment:—Maran-atha.

G3135.definition: μαργαρίτης margarítēs, mar-gar-ee'-tace; from μάργαρος márgaros (a pearl-oyster); a pearl:—pearl.

G3136.definition:
Μάρθα Mártha, mar'-thah; probably of Chaldee origin (meaning mistress); Martha, a Christian
 woman:—Martha.

G3137.definition:
†Μαρία María, mar-ee'-ah; of Hebrew origin (H4813); Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of
 six Christian females:—Mary.

G3138.definition: Μάρκος Márkos, mar'-kos; of Latin origin; Marcus, a Christian:—Marcus, Mark.

G3139.definition: μάρμαρος mármaros, mar'-mar-os; from μαρμαίρω marmaírō (to glisten); marble (as sparkling white):—marble.

G314.definition: ἀναγινώσκω anaginṓskō, an-ag-in-oce'-ko; from G303 and G1097; to know again, i.e. (by extension) to read:—read.

G3140.definition:
μαρτυρέω martyréō, mar-too-reh'-o; from G3144; to be a witness, i.e. testify (literally or
 figuratively):—charge, give (evidence), bear record, have (obtain,
 of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have)
 testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness.

G3141.definition:
μαρτυρία martyría, mar-too-ree'-ah; from G3144; evidence given (judicially or genitive case):—record,
 report, testimony, witness.

G3142.definition:
μαρτύριον martýrion, mar-too'-ree-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G3144; something evidential, i.e.
 (genitive case) evidence given or (specially), the Decalogue (in the
 sacred Tabernacle):—to be testified, testimony, witness.

G3143.definition:
μαρτύρομαι martýromai, mar-too'-rom-ahee; middle voice from G3144; to be adduced as a witness, i.e.
 (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation):—take to
 record, testify.

G3144.definition:
μάρτυς mártys, mar'-toos; of uncertain affinity; a witness (literally (judicially) or
 figuratively (genitive case)); by analogy, a "martyr":—martyr,
 record, witness.

G3145.definition: μασσάομαι massáomai, mas-sah'-om-ahee; from a primary μάσσω mássō (to handle or squeeze); to chew:—gnaw.

G3146.definition: μαστιγόω mastigóō, mas-tig-o'-o; from G3148; to flog (literally or figuratively):—scourge.

G3147.definition: μαστίζω mastízō, mas-tid'-zo; from G3149; to whip (literally):—scourge.

G3148.definition:
μάστιξ mástix, mas'-tix; probably from the base of G3145 (through the idea of contact); a whip
 (literally, the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively, a
 disease):—plague, scourging.

G3149.definition:
μαστός mastós, mas-tos'; from the base of G3145; a (properly, female) breast (as if kneaded
 up):—pap.

G315.definition: ἀναγκάζω anankázō, an-ang-kad'-zo; from G318; to necessitate:—compel, constrain.

G3150.definition: ματαιολογία mataiología, mat-ah-yol-og-ee'-ah; from G3151; random talk, i.e. babble:—vain jangling.

G3151.definition:
ματαιολόγος mataiológos, mat-ah-yol-og'-os; from G3152 and G3004; an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker,
 i.e. a wrangler:—vain talker.

G3152.definition:
μάταιος mátaios, mat'-ah-yos; from the base of G3155; empty, i.e. (literally) profitless, or
 (specially), an idol:—vain, vanity.

G3153.definition:
ματαιότης mataiótēs, mat-ah-yot'-ace; from G3152; inutility; figuratively, transientness; morally,
 depravity:—vanity.

G3154.definition:
ματαιόω mataióō, mat-ah-yo'-o; from G3152; to render (passively, become) foolish, i.e. (morally)
 wicked or (specially), idolatrous:—become vain.

G3155.definition:
μάτην mátēn, mat'-ane; accusative case of a derivative of the base of G3145 (through the idea
 of tentative manipulation, i.e. unsuccessful search, or else of
 punishment); folly, i.e. (adverbially) to no purpose:—in vain.

G3157.definition:
†Ματθάν Matthán, mat-than'; of Hebrew origin (H4977); Matthan (i.e. Mattan), an
 Israelite:—Matthan.

G316.definition:
ἀναγκαῖος anankaîos, an-ang-kah'-yos; from G318; necessary; by implication, close (of kin):—near, necessary,
 necessity, needful.

G3160.definition:
Ματταθά Mattathá, mat-tath-ah'; probably a shortened form of G3161 (compare H4992); Mattatha (i.e.
 Mattithjah), an Israelite:—Mattatha.

G3161.definition:
Ματταθίας Mattathías, mat-tath-ee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H4993); Mattathias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite
 and a Christian:—Mattathias.

G3162.definition:
μάχαιρα máchaira, makh'-ahee-rah; probably feminine of a presumed derivative of G3163; a knife, i.e.
 dirk; figuratively, war, judicial punishment:—sword.

G3163.definition:
μάχη máchē, makh'-ay; from G3164; a battle, i.e. (figuratively) controversy:—fighting,
 strive, striving.

G3164.definition:
μάχομαι máchomai, makh'-om-ahee; middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to war, i.e.
 (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute:—fight, strive.

G3165.definition: μέ mé, meh; a shorter (and probably original) form of G1691; me:—I, me, my.

G3167.definition:
μεγαλεῖος megaleîos, meg-al-i'-os; from G3173; magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous
 favor, or (subjectively) perfection:—great things, wonderful works.

G3168.definition:
μεγαλειότης megaleiótēs, meg-al-i-ot'-ace; from G3167; superbness, i.e. glory or splendor:—magnificence, majesty,
 mighty power.

G3169.definition:
μεγαλοπρεπής megaloprepḗs, meg-al-op-rep-ace'; from G3173 and G4241; befitting greatness or magnificence
 (majestic):—excellent.

G317.definition: ἀναγκαστῶς anankastōs, an-ang-kas-toce'; adverb from a derivative of G315; compulsorily:—by constraint.

G3170.definition:
μεγαλύνω megalýnō, meg-al-oo'-no; from G3173; to make (or declare) great, i.e. increase or (figuratively)
 extol:—enlarge, magnify, shew great.

G3171.definition: μεγάλως megálōs, meg-al'-oce; adverb from G3173; much:—greatly.

G3172.definition:
μεγαλωσύνη megalōsýnē, meg-al-o-soo'-nay; from G3173; greatness, i.e. (figuratively) divinity (often God
 himself):—majesty.

G3173.definition:
μέγας mégas, meg'-as; (including the prolonged forms, feminine μεγάλη megálē, plural
 μεγάλοι megáloi, etc.; compare also G3176, G3187); big (literally or
 figuratively, in a very wide application):—(+ fear) exceedingly,
 great(-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong,
 × to years.

G3174.definition: μέγεθος mégethos, meg'-eth-os; from G3173; magnitude (figuratively):—greatness.

G3175.definition: †μεγιστᾶνες megistânes, meg-is-tan'-es; plural from G3176; grandees:—great men, lords.

G3177.definition:
μεθερμηνεύω methermēneúō, meth-er-mane-yoo'-o; from G3326 and G2059; to explain over, i.e. translate:—(by)
 interpret(-ation).

G3178.definition:
μέθη méthē, meth'-ay; apparently a primary word; an intoxicant, i.e. (by implication)
 intoxication:—drunkenness.

G3179.definition:
μεθίστημι methístēmi, meth-is'-tay-mee; from G3326 and G2476; to transfer, i.e. carry away, depose or
 (figuratively) exchange, seduce:—put out, remove, translate, turn
 away.

G3180.definition:
μεθοδεία methodeía, meth-od-i'-ah; from a compound of G3326 and G3593 (compare "method"); travelling over,
 i.e. travesty (trickery):—wile, lie in wait.

G3182.definition: μεθύσκω methýskō, meth-oos'-ko; a prolonged (transitive) form of G3184; to intoxicate:—be drunk(-en).

G3183.definition: μέθυσος méthysos, meth'-oo-sos; from G3184; tipsy, i.e. (as noun) a sot:—drunkard.

G3184.definition:
μεθύω methýō, meth-oo'-o; from another form of G3178; to drink to intoxication, i.e. get
 drunk:—drink well, make (be) drunk(-en).

G3187.definition:
μείζων meízōn, mide'-zone; irregular comparative of G3173; larger (literally or figuratively,
 specially, in age):—elder, greater(-est), more.

G3188.definition: μέλαν mélan, mel'-an; neuter of G3189 as noun; ink:—ink.

G3189.definition: μέλας mélas, mel'-as; apparently a primary word; black:—black.

G319.definition:
†ἀναγνωρίζομαι anagnōrízomai, an-ag-no-rid'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G303 and G1107; to make (oneself) known:—be made
 known.

G3190.definition: †Μελεᾶς Meleâs, mel-eh-as'; of uncertain origin; Meleas, an Israelite:—Meleas.

G3191.definition:
μελετάω meletáō, mel-et-ah'-o; from a presumed derivative of G3199; to take care of, i.e. (by
 implication) revolve in the mind:—imagine, (pre-)meditate.

G3192.definition: μέλι méli, mel'-ee; apparently a primary word; honey:—honey.

G3194.definition: †Μελίτη Melítē, mel-ee'-tay; of uncertain origin; Melita, an island in the Mediterranean:—Melita.

G3195.definition:
μέλλω méllō, mel'-lo; a strengthened form of G3199 (through the idea of expectation); to
 intend, i.e. be about to be, do, or suffer something (of persons or
 things, especially events; in the sense of purpose, duty, necessity,
 probability, possibility, or hesitation):—about, after that, be
 (almost), (that which is, things, + which was for) to come, intend,
 was to (be), mean, mind, be at the point, (be) ready, + return, shall
 (begin), (which, that) should (after, afterwards, hereafter) tarry,
 which was for, will, would, be yet.

G3196.definition: μέλος mélos, mel'-os; of uncertain affinity; a limb or part of the body:—member.

G3197.definition:
Μελχί Melchí, mel-khee'; of Hebrew origin (H4428 with pronominal suffix, my king); Melchi (i.e.
 Malki), the name of two Israelites:—Melchi.

G3198.definition:
Μελχισεδέκ Melchisedék, mel-khis-ed-ek'; of Hebrew origin (H4442); Melchisedek (i.e. Malkitsedek), a
 patriarch:—Melchisedec.

G32.definition:
†ἄγγελος ággelos, ang'-el-os; from ἀγγέλλω aggéllō (probably derived from G71; compare G34) (to bring
 tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a
 pastor:—angel, messenger.

G320.definition: ἀνάγνωσις anágnōsis, an-ag'-no-sis; from G314; (the act of) reading:—reading.

G3200.definition: μεμβράνα membrána, mem-bran'-ah; of Latin origin ("membrane"); a (written) sheep-skin:—parchment.

G3201.definition: μέμφομαι mémphomai, mem'-fom-ahee; middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to blame:—find fault.

G3202.definition:
μεμψίμοιρος mempsímoiros, mem-psim'-oy-ros; from a presumed derivative of G3201 and μοῖρα moîra (fate; akin to the base
 of G3313); blaming fate, i.e. querulous (discontented):—complainer.

G321.definition:
ἀνάγω anágō, an-ag'-o; from G303 and G71; to lead up; by extension to bring out; specially, to
 sail away:—bring (again, forth, up again), depart, launch (forth),
 lead (up), loose, offer, sail, set forth, take up.

G322.definition:
ἀναδείκνυμι anadeíknymi, an-ad-ike'-noo-mee; from G303 and G1166; to exhibit, i.e. (by implication) to indicate,
 appoint:—appoint, shew.

G323.definition: ἀνάδειξις anádeixis, an-ad'-ike-sis; from G322; (the act of) exhibition:—shewing.

G324.definition: ἀναδέχομαι anadéchomai, an-ad-ekh'-om-ahee; from G303 and G1209; to entertain (as a guest):—receive.

G325.definition: ἀναδίδωμι anadídōmi, an-ad-eed'-om-ee; from G303 and G1325; to hand over:—deliver.

G326.definition: ἀναζάω anazáō, an-ad-zah'-o; from G303 and G2198; to recover life (literally or figuratively):—(be a-)live again, revive.

G327.definition: ἀναζητέω anazētéō, an-ad-zay-teh'-o; from G303 and G2212; to search out:—seek.

G328.definition: ἀναζώννυμι anazṓnnymi, an-ad-zone'-noo-mee; from G303 and G2224; to gird afresh:—gird up.

G329.definition:
ἀναζωπυρέω anazōpyréō, an-ad-zo-poor-eh'-o; from G303 and a compound of the base of G2226 and G4442; to
 re-enkindle:—stir up.

G33.definition: ἄγε áge, ag'-eh; imperative of G71; properly, lead, i.e. come on:—go to.

G330.definition: ἀναθάλλω anathállō, an-ath-al'-lo; from G303 and θάλλω thállō (to flourish); to revive:—flourish again.

G3303.definition:
μέν mén, men; a primary particle; properly, indicative of affirmation or concession
 (in fact); usually followed by a contrasted clause with G1161 (this
 one, the former, etc.):—even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily. Often
 compounded with other particles in an intensive or asseverative sense.

G3304.definition:
†μενοῦνγε menoûnge, men-oon'-geh; from G3203 and G3767 and G1065; so then at least:—nay but, yea doubtless
 (rather, verily).

G3305.definition:
μέντοι méntoi, men'-toy; from G3203 and G5104; indeed though, i.e. however:—also, but, howbeit,
 nevertheless, yet.

G3306.definition:
μένω ménō, men'-o; a primary verb; to stay (in a given place, state, relation or
 expectancy):—abide, continue, dwell, endure, be present, remain,
 stand, tarry (for), × thine own.

G3307.definition:
μερίζω merízō, mer-id'-zo; from G3313; to part, i.e. (literally) to apportion, bestow, share, or
 (figuratively) to disunite, differ:—deal, be difference between,
 distribute, divide, give participle

G3308.definition: μέριμνα mérimna, mer'-im-nah; from G3307 (through the idea of distraction); solicitude:—care.

G3309.definition: μεριμνάω merimnáō, mer-im-nah'-o; from G3308; to be anxious about:—(be, have) care(-ful), take thought.

G331.definition:
ἀνάθεμα anáthema, an-ath'-em-ah; from G394; a (religious) ban or (concretely) excommunicated (thing or
 person):—accused, anathema, curse, × great.

G3310.definition:
μερίς merís, mer-ece'; feminine of G3313; a portion, i.e. province, share or (abstractly)
 participation:—part (X -akers).

G3311.definition: μερισμός merismós, mer-is-mos'; from G3307; a separation or distribution:—dividing asunder, gift.

G3312.definition: μεριστής meristḗs, mer-is-tace'; from G3307; an apportioner (administrator):—divider.

G3313.definition:
μέρος méros, mer'-os; from an obsolete but more primary form of μείρομαι meíromai (to get as a
 section or allotment); a division or share (literally or figuratively,
 in a wide application):—behalf, course, coast, craft, particular (+
 -ly), part (+ -ly), piece, portion, respect, side, some sort(-what).

G3314.definition: μεσημβρία mesēmbría, mes-ame-bree'-ah; from G3319 and G2250; midday; by implication, the south:—noon, south.

G3315.definition:
μεσιτεύω mesiteúō, mes-it-yoo'-o; from G3316; to interpose (as arbiter), i.e (by implication) to ratify
 (as surety):—confirm.

G3316.definition:
μεσίτης mesítēs, mes-ee'-tace; from G3319; a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by
 implication) a reconciler (intercessor):—mediator.

G3317.definition:
μεσονύκτιον mesonýktion, mes-on-ook'-tee-on; neuter of compound of G3319 and G3571; midnight (especially as a
 watch):—midnight.

G3318.definition:
Μεσοποταμία Mesopotamía, mes-op-ot-am-ee'-ah; from G3319 and G4215; Mesopotamia (as lying between the Euphrates and
 the Tigris; compare 0763), a region of Asia:—Mesopotamia.

G3319.definition:
μέσος mésos, mes'-os; from G3326; middle (as an adjective or (neuter) noun):—among, × before
 them, between, + forth, mid(-day, -night), midst, way.

G332.definition:
ἀναθεματίζω anathematízō, an-ath-em-at-id'-zo; from G331; to declare or vow under penalty of execration:—(bind under
 a) curse, bind with an oath.

G3320.definition: μεσότοιχον mesótoichon, mes-ot'-oy-khon; from G3319 and G5109; a partition (figuratively):—middle wall.

G3321.definition: μεσουράνημα mesouránēma, mes-oo-ran'-ay-mah; from a presumed compound of G3319 and G3772; mid-sky:—midst of heaven.

G3322.definition:
μεσόω mesóō, mes-o'-o; from G3319; to form the middle, i.e. (in point of time), to be half-way
 over:—be about the midst.

G3323.definition:
Μεσσίας Messías, mes-see'-as; of Hebrew origin (H4899); the Messias (i.e. Mashiach), or
 Christ:—Messias.

G3324.definition: μεστός mestós, mes-tos'; of uncertain derivation; replete (literally or figuratively):—full.

G3325.definition: μεστόω mestóō, mes-to'-o; from G3324; to replenish, i.e. (by implication) to intoxicate:—fill.

G3326.definition:
μετά metá, met-ah'; a primary preposition (often used adverbially); properly, denoting
 accompaniment; "amid" (local or causal); modified variously according
 to the case (genitive association, or accusative succession) with
 which it is joined; occupying an intermediate position between G575 or
 G1537 and G1519 or G4314; less intimate than G1722 and less close than
 G4862):—after(-ward), × that he again, against, among, × and,
 + follow, hence, hereafter, in, of, (up-)on, + our, × and
 setting, since, (un-)to, + together, when, with (+ -out). Often used
 in composition, in substantially the same relations of participation
 or proximity, and transfer or sequence.

G3327.definition:
μεταβαίνω metabaínō, met-ab-ah'-ee-no; from G3326 and the base of G939; to change place:—depart, go, pass,
 remove.

G3328.definition:
μεταβάλλω metabállō, met-ab-al'-lo; from G3326 and G906; to throw over, i.e. (middle voice figuratively) to
 turn about in opinion:—change mind.

G3329.definition: μετάγω metágō, met-ag'-o; from G3326 and G718; to lead over, i.e. transfer (direct):—turn about.

G333.definition:
ἀναθεωρέω anatheōréō, an-ath-eh-o-reh'-o; from G303 and G2334; to look again (i.e. attentively) at (literally or
 figuratively):—behold, consider.

G3330.definition: μεταδίδωμι metadídōmi, met-ad-id'-o-mee; from G3326 and G1325; to give over, i.e. share:—give, impart.

G3331.definition:
μετάθεσις metáthesis, met-ath'-es-is; from G3346; transposition, i.e. transferral (to heaven),
 disestablishment (of a law):—change, removing, translation.

G3332.definition: μεταίρω metaírō, met-ah'-ee-ro; from G3326 and G142; to betake oneself, i.e. remove (locally):—depart.

G3333.definition:
μετακαλέω metakaléō, met-ak-al-eh'-o; from G3326 and G2564; to call elsewhere, i.e. summon:—call (for,
 hither).

G3334.definition:
μετακινέω metakinéō, met-ak-ee-neh'-o; from G3326 and G2795; to stir to a place elsewhere, i.e. remove
 (figuratively):—move away.

G3335.definition:
μεταλαμβάνω metalambánō, met-al-am-ban'-o; from G3326 and G2983; to participate; genitive case, to accept (and
 use):—eat, have, be partaker, receive, take.

G3337.definition: μεταλλάσσω metallássō, met-al-las'-so; from G3326 and G236; to exchange:—change.

G3338.definition:
†μεταμέλλομαι metaméllomai, met-am-el'-lom-ahee; from G3326 and the middle voice of G3199; to care afterwards, i.e.
 regret:—repent (self).

G3339.definition:
μεταμορφόω metamorphóō, met-am-or-fo'-o; from G3326 and G3445; to transform (literally or figuratively,
 "metamorphose"):—change, transfigure, transform.

G3340.definition:
μετανοέω metanoéō, met-an-o-eh'-o; from G3326 and G3539; to think differently or afterwards, i.e.
 reconsider (morally, feel compunction):—repent.

G3341.definition:
μετάνοια metánoia, met-an'-oy-ah; from G3340; (subjectively) compunction (for guilt, including
 reformation); by implication, reversal (of (another's)
 decision):—repentance.

G3342.definition:
μεταξύ metaxý, met-ax-oo'; from G3326 and a form of G4862; betwixt (of place or person); (of time)
 as adjective, intervening, or (by implication) adjoining:—between,
 mean while, next.

G3343.definition:
μεταπέμπω metapémpō, met-ap-emp'-o; from G3326 and G3992; to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to
 summon or invite:—call (send) for.

G3344.definition:
†μεταστρέφω metastréphō, met-as-tref'-o; from G3326 and G4762; to turn across, i.e. transmute or (figuratively)
 corrupt:—pervert, turn.

G3346.definition:
μετατίθημι metatíthēmi, met-at-ith'-ay-mee; from G3326 and G5087; to transfer, i.e. (literally) transport, (by
 implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively)
 pervert:—carry over, change, remove, translate, turn.

G3347.definition: μετέπειτα metépeita, met-ep'-i-tah; from G3326 and G1899; thereafter:—afterward.

G3348.definition:
μετέχω metéchō, met-ekh'-o; from G3326 and G2192; to share or participate; by implication, belong
 to, eat (or drink):—be partaker, pertain, take part, use.

G3349.definition:
μετεωρίζω meteōrízō, met-eh-o-rid'-zo; from a compound of G3326 and a collateral form of G142 or perhaps rather
 G109 (compare "meteor"); to raise in mid-air, i.e. (figuratively)
 suspend (passively, fluctuate or be anxious):—be of doubtful mind.

G335.definition:
ἀναίδεια anaídeia, an-ah'-ee-die-ah'; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle (compare G427)) and G127; 
 impudence, i.e. (by implication) importunity:—importunity.

G3350.definition:
μετοικεσία metoikesía, met-oy-kes-ee'-ah; from a derivative of a compound of G3326 and G3624; a change of abode,
 i.e. (specially), expatriation:—X brought, carried(-ying) away
 (in-)to.

G3351.definition:
μετοικίζω metoikízō, met-oy-kid'-zo; from the same as G3350; to transfer as a settler or captive, i.e
 colonize or exile:—carry away, remove into.

G3352.definition: μετοχή metochḗ, met-okh-ay'; from G3348; participation, i.e. intercourse:—fellowship.

G3353.definition:
μέτοχος métochos, met'-okh-os; from G3348; participant, i.e. (as noun) a sharer; by implication, an
 associate:—fellow, partaker, partner.

G3354.definition:
μετρέω metréō, met-reh'-o; from G3358; to measure (i.e. ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by
 implication, to admeasure (i.e. allot by rule):—figuratively, to
 estimate:—measure, mete.

G3355.definition:
μετρητής metrētḗs, met-ray-tace'; from G3354; a measurer, i.e. (specially), a certain standard measure of
 capacity for liquids:—firkin.

G3356.definition:
μετριοπαθέω metriopathéō, met-ree-op-ath-eh'-o; from a compound of the base of G3357 and G3806; to be moderate in
 passion, i.e. gentle (to treat indulgently):—have compassion.

G3357.definition:
μετρίως metríōs, met-ree'-oce; adverb from a derivative of G3358; moderately, i.e. slightly:—a
 little.

G3358.definition:
μέτρον métron, met'-ron; an apparently primary word; a measure ("metre"), literally or
 figuratively; by implication, a limited portion (degree):—measure.

G3359.definition:
μέτωπον métōpon, met'-o-pon; from G3326 and ops (the face); the forehead (as opposite the
 countenance):—forehead.

G336.definition: ἀναίρεσις anaíresis, an-ah'-ee-res-is; from G337; (the act of) killing:—death.

G3360.definition:
μέχρι méchri, mekh'-ree; from G3372; as far as, i.e. up to a certain point (as a preposition, of
 extent (denoting the terminus, whereas G891 refers especially to the
 space of time or place intervening) or conjunction):—till, (un-)to,
 until.

G3361.definition:
μή mḗ, may; a primary particle of qualified negation (whereas G3756 expresses an
 absolute denial); (adverb) not, (conjunction) lest; also (as an
 interrogative implying a negative answer (whereas G3756 expects an
 affirmative one)) whether:—any but (that), × forbear, + God forbid, +
 lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, (can-)not,
 nothing, that not, un(-taken), without. Often used in compounds in
 substantially the same relations. See also G3362, G3363, G3364, G3372,
 G3373, G3375, G3378.

G3364.definition:
οὐ μή ou mḗ, oo may; i.e. G3756 and G3361; a double negative strengthening the denial; not at
 all:—any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at
 all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise). Compare
 G3378.

G3365.definition:
μηδαμῶς mēdamōs, may-dam-oce'; adverb from a compound of G3361 and ἀμός amós (somebody); by no means:—not
 so.

G3366.definition:
μηδέ mēdé, may-deh'; from G3361 and G1161; but not, not even; in a continued negation,
 nor:—neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as).

G3367.definition:
μηδείς mēdeís, may-dice'; from G3361 and G1520; not even one (man, woman, thing):—any (man,
 thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing,
 + without delay.

G3368.definition: μηδέποτε mēdépote, may-dep'-ot-eh; from G3366 and G4218; not even ever:—never.

G3369.definition: μηδέπω mēdépō, may-dep'-o; from G3366 and G4452; not even yet:—not yet.

G337.definition:
ἀναιρέω anairéō, an-ahee-reh'-o; from G303 and (the active of) G138; to take up, i.e. adopt; by
 implication, to take away (violently), i.e. abolish, murder:—put to
 death, kill, slay, take away, take up.

G3370.definition:
Μῆδος Mēdos, may'-dos; of foreign origin (compare H4074); a Median, or inhabitant of
 Media:—Mede.

G3371.definition:
μηκέτι mēkéti, may-ket'-ee; from G3361 and G2089; no further:—any longer, (not) henceforth,
 hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any more.

G3372.definition: μῆκος mēkos, may'-kos; probably akin to G3173; length (literally or figuratively) length.

G3373.definition: μηκύνω mēkýnō, may-koo'-no; from G3372; to lengthen, i.e. (middle voice) to enlarge:—grow up.

G3374.definition: μηλωτή mēlōtḗ, may-lo-tay'; from μῆλον mēlon (a sheep); a sheep-skin:—sheepskin.

G3375.definition:
μήν mḗn, mane; a stronger form of G3303; a particle of affirmation (only with G2229);
 assuredly:—+ surely.

G3376.definition: μήν mḗn, mane; a primary word; a month:—month.

G3377.definition:
μηνύω mēnýō, may-noo'-o; probably from the same base as G3145 and G3415 (i.e. μάω máō, to strive); to
 disclose (through the idea of mental effort and thus calling to mind),
 i.e. report, declare, intimate:—shew, tell.

G3379.definition:
μήποτε mḗpote, may'-pot-eh; from G3361 and G4218; not ever; also if (or lest) ever (or perhaps):—if
 peradventure, lest (at any time, haply), not at all, whether or not.

G338.definition:
ἀναίτιος anaítios, an-ah'-ee-tee-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G159 (in the sense of G156); 
 innocent:—blameless, guiltless.

G3380.definition: μήπω mḗpō, may'-po; from G3361 and G4452; not yet:—not yet.

G3382.definition: μηρός mērós, may-ros'; perhaps a primary word; a thigh:—thigh.

G3383.definition:
μήτε mḗte, may'-teh; from G3361 and G5037; not too, i.e. (in continued negation) neither or
 nor; also, not even:—neither, (n-)or, so as much.

G3384.definition:
μήτηρ mḗtēr, may'-tare; apparently a primary word; a "mother" (literally or figuratively,
 immediate or remote):—mother.

G3385.definition:
μήτι mḗti, may'-tee; from G3361 and the neuter of G5100; whether at all:—not (the particle
 usually not expressed, except by the form of the question).

G3388.definition: μήτρα mḗtra, may'-trah; from G3384; the matrix:—womb.

G3389.definition:
†μητραλῴας mētralṓias, may-tral-o'-as; from G3384 and the base of G257; a mother-thresher, i.e.
 matricide:—murderer of mothers.

G339.definition:
ἀνακαθίζω anakathízō, an-ak-ath-id'-zo; from G303 and G2523; properly, to set up, i.e. (reflexively) to sit
 up:—sit up.

G3392.definition:
μιαίνω miaínō, me-ah'-ee-no; perhaps a primary verb; to sully or taint, i.e. contaminate
 (ceremonially or morally):—defile.

G3393.definition:
μίασμα míasma, mee'-as-mah; from G3392 ("miasma"); (morally) foulness (properly, the
 effect):—pollution.

G3394.definition: μιασμός miasmós, mee-as-mos'; from G3392; (morally) contamination (properly, the act):—uncleanness.

G3395.definition: †μίγμα mígma, mig'-mah; from G3396; a compound:—mixture.

G3396.definition: μίγνυμι mígnymi, mig'-noo-mee; a primary verb; to mix:—mingle.

G3398.definition:
μικρός mikrós, mik-ros'; apparently a primary word; small (in size, quantity, number or
 (figuratively) dignity):—least, less, little, small.

G3399.definition: Μίλητος Mílētos, mil'-ay-tos; of uncertain origin; Miletus, a city of Asia Minor:—Miletus.

G34.definition: ἀγέλη agélē, ag-el'-ay; from G71 (compare G32); a drove:—herd.

G340.definition: ἀνακαινίζω anakainízō, an-ak-ahee-nid'-zo; from G303 and a derivative of G2537; to restore:—renew.

G3400.definition: μίλιον mílion, mil'-ee-on; of Latin origin; a thousand paces, i.e. a "mile":—mile.

G3401.definition: μιμέομαι miméomai, mim-eh'-om-ahee; middle voice from μῖμος mîmos (a "mimic"); to imitate:—follow.

G3402.definition: μιμητής mimētḗs, mim-ay-tace'; from G3401; an imitator:—follower.

G3404.definition:
μισέω miséō, mis-eh'-o; from a primary μῖσος mîsos (hatred); to detest (especially to persecute); by
 extension, to love less:—hate(-ful).

G3405.definition: μισθαποδοσία misthapodosía, mis-thap-od-os-ee'-ah; from G3406; requital (good or bad):—recompence of reward.

G3406.definition:
μισθαποδότης misthapodótēs, mis-thap-od-ot'-ace; from G3409 and G591; a remunerator[1]:—rewarder.

    
    
        1. Edited by BLB [A spelling error was made in the original document "renumerator"]

G3407.definition: μίσθιος místhios, mis'-thee-os; from G3408; a wage-earner:—hired servant.

G3408.definition:
μισθός misthós, mis-thos'; apparently a primary word; pay for service (literally or
 figuratively), good or bad:—hire, reward, wages.

G3409.definition: μισθόω misthóō, mis-tho'-o; from G3408; to let out for wages, i.e. (middle voice) to hire:—hire.

G341.definition: ἀνακαινόω anakainóō, an-ak-ahee-no'-o; from G303 and a derivative of G2537; to renovate:—renew.

G3410.definition: μίσθωμα místhōma, mis'-tho-mah; from G3409; a rented building:—hired house.

G3411.definition: μισθωτός misthōtós, mis-tho-tos'; from G3409; a wage-worker (good or bad):—hired servant, hireling.

G3412.definition:
Μιτυλήνη Mitylḗnē, mit-oo-lay'-nay; for μυτιλήνη mytilḗnē (abounding in shellfish); Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town
 on the island of Lesbos:—Mitylene.

G3413.definition: Μιχαήλ Michaḗl, mikh-ah-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H4317); Michael, an archangel:—Michael.

G3414.definition: μνᾶ mnâ, mnah; of Latin origin; a mna (i.e. mina), a certain weight:—pound.

G3415.definition:
μνάομαι mnáomai, mnah'-om-ahee; middle voice of a derivative of G3306 or perhaps of the base of G3145
 (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp); to bear
 in mind, i.e. recollect; by implication, to reward or punish:—be
 mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance. Compare G3403.

G3416.definition: Μνάσων Mnásōn, mnah'-sohn; of uncertain origin; Mnason, a Christian:—Mnason.

G3417.definition:
μνεία mneía, mni'-ah; from G3415 or G3403; recollection; by implication, recital:—mention,
 remembrance.

G3418.definition:
μνῆμα mnēma, mnay'-mah; from G3415; a memorial, i.e. sepulchral monument
 (burial-place):—grave, sepulchre, tomb.

G3419.definition:
μνημεῖον mnēmeîon, mnay-mi'-on; from G3420; a remembrance, i.e. cenotaph (place of interment):—grave,
 sepulchre, tomb.

G342.definition: ἀνακαίνωσις anakaínōsis, an-ak-ah'-ee-no-sis; from G341; renovation:—renewing.

G3420.definition: μνήμη mnḗmē, mnay'-may; from G3403; memory:—remembrance.

G3421.definition:
μνημονεύω mnēmoneúō, mnay-mon-yoo'-o; from a derivative of G3420; to exercise memory, i.e. recollect; by
 implication, to punish; also to rehearse:—make mention; be mindful,
 remember.

G3422.definition: μνημόσυνον mnēmósynon, mnay-mos'-oo-non; from G3421; a reminder (memorandum), i.e. record:—memorial.

G3423.definition:
μνηστεύω mnēsteúō, mnace-tyoo'-o; from a derivative of G3415; to give a souvenir (engagement present),
 i.e. betroth:—espouse.

G3424.definition:
μογιλάλος mogilálos, mog-il-al'-os; from G3425 and G2980; hardly talking, i.e. dumb (tongue-tied):—having
 an impediment in his speech.

G3425.definition: μόγις mógis, mog'-is; adverb from a primary μόγος mógos (toil); with difficulty:—hardly.

G3426.definition:
μόδιος módios, mod'-ee-os; of Latin origin; a modius, i.e. certain measure for things dry (the
 quantity or the utensil):—bushel.

G3427.definition: μοί moí, moy; the simpler form of G1698; to me:—I, me, mine, my.

G3428.definition:
μοιχαλίς moichalís, moy-khal-is'; a prolonged form of the feminine of G3432; an adulteress (literally or
 figuratively):—adulteress(-ous, -y).

G3429.definition: †μοιχάω moicháō, moy-khah'-o; from G3432; (middle voice) to commit adultery:—commit adultery.

G343.definition:
ἀνακαλύπτω anakalýptō, an-ak-al-oop'-to; from G303 (in the sense of reversal) and G2572; to unveil:—open,
 (un-)taken away.

G3430.definition: μοιχεία moicheía, moy-khi'-ah; from G3431; adultery:—adultery.

G3431.definition: μοιχεύω moicheúō, moy-khyoo'-o; from G3432; to commit adultery:—commit adultery.

G3432.definition:
μοιχός moichós, moy-khos'; perhaps a primary word; a (male) paramour; figuratively,
 apostate:—adulterer.

G3433.definition:
μόλις mólis, mol'-is; probably by variation for G3425; with difficulty:—hardly, scarce(-ly),
 + with much work.

G3434.definition: Μολόχ Molóch, mol-okh'; of Hebrew origin (H4432); Moloch (i.e. Molek), an idol:—Moloch.

G3435.definition: μολύνω molýnō, mol-oo'-no; probably from G3189; to soil (figuratively):—defile.

G3436.definition: μολυσμός molysmós, mol-oos-mos'; from G3435; a stain; i.e. (figuratively) immorality:—filthiness.

G3437.definition: μομφή momphḗ, mom-fay'; from G3201; blame, i.e. (by implication), a fault:—quarrel.

G3438.definition:
μονή monḗ, mon-ay'; from G3306; a staying, i.e. residence (the act or the place):—abode,
 mansion.

G3439.definition: μονογενής monogenḗs, mon-og-en-ace'; from G3441 and G1096; only-born, i.e. sole:—only (begotten, child).

G344.definition: ἀνακάμπτω anakámptō, an-ak-amp'-to; from G303 and G2578; to turn back:—(re-)turn.

G3441.definition:
μόνος mónos, mon'-os; probably from G3306; remaining, i.e. sole or single; by implication,
 mere:—alone, only, by themselves.

G3442.definition: μονόφθαλμος monóphthalmos, mon-of'-thal-mos; from G3441 and G3788; one-eyed:—with one eye.

G3443.definition: μονόω monóō, mon-o'-o; from G3441; to isolate, i.e. bereave:—be desolate.

G3444.definition:
μορφή morphḗ, mor-fay'; perhaps from the base of G3313 (through the idea of adjustment of
 parts); shape; figuratively, nature:—form.

G3445.definition: μορφόω morphóō, mor-fo'-o; from the same as G3444; to fashion (figuratively):—form.

G3446.definition:
μόρφωσις mórphōsis, mor'-fo-sis; from G3445; formation, i.e. (by implication), appearance (semblance or
 (concretely) formula):—form.

G3447.definition: μοσχοποιέω moschopoiéō, mos-khop-oy-eh'-o; from G3448 and G4160; to fabricate the image of a bullock:—make a calf.

G3448.definition: μόσχος móschos, mos'-khos; probably strengthened for όσχος óschos (a shoot); a young bullock:—calf.

G3449.definition:
†μόχθος móchthos, mokh'-thos; from the base of G3425; toil, i.e. (by implication)
 sadness:—painfulness, travail.

G345.definition:
†ἀνακεῖμαι anakeîmai, an-ak-i'-mahee; from G303 and G2749; to recline (as a corpse or at a meal):—guest,
 lean, lie, sit (down, at meat), at the table.

G3450.definition: μοῦ moû, moo; the simpler form of G1700; of me:—I, me, mine (own), my.

G3451.definition: μουσικός mousikós, moo-sik-os'; from Μοῦσα Moûsa (a Muse); "musical", i.e. (as noun) a minstrel:—musician.

G3452.definition: μυελός myelós, moo-el-os'; perhaps a primary word; the marrow:—marrow.

G3453.definition:
μυέω myéō, moo-eh'-o; from the base of G3466; to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to
 teach:—instruct.

G3454.definition:
μῦθος mŷthos, moo'-thos; perhaps from the same as G3453 (through the idea of tuition); a tale,
 i.e. fiction ("myth"):—fable.

G3455.definition:
μυκάομαι mykáomai, moo-kah'-om-ahee; from a presumed derivative of μύζω mýzō ( to "moo"); to bellow
 (roar):—roar.

G3456.definition:
μυκτηρίζω myktērízō, mook-tay-rid'-zo; from a derivative of the base of G3455 (meaning snout, as that whence
 lowing proceeds); to make mouths at, i.e. ridicule:—mock.

G3457.definition: μυλικός mylikós, moo-lee-kos'; from G3458; belonging to a mill:—mill(-stone).

G3458.definition:
†μύλος mýlos, moo'-los; probably ultimately from the base of G3433 (through the idea of
 hardship); a "mill", i.e. (by implication), a grinder
 (millstone):—millstone.

G346.definition:
†ἀνακεφαλαίομαι anakephalaíomai, an-ak-ef-al-ah'-ee-om-ahee; from G303 and G2775 (in its original sense); to sum up:—briefly
 comprehend, gather together in one.

G3460.definition: Μύρα Mýra, moo'-rah; of uncertain derivation; Myra, a place in Asia Minor:—Myra.

G3461.definition:
†μυριάς myriás, moo-ree'-as; from G3463; a ten-thousand; by extension, a "myriad" or indefinite
 number:—ten thousand.

G3462.definition: μυρίζω myrízō, moo-rid'-zo; from G3464; to apply (perfumed) unguent to:—anoint.

G3463.definition:
μύριοι mýrioi, moo'-ree-oi; plural of an apparently primary word (properly, meaning very many); 
 ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many:—ten thousand.

G3464.definition:
μύρον mýron, moo'-ron; probably of foreign origin (compare H4753, G4666); "myrrh", i.e. (by
 implication) perfumed oil:—ointment.

G3465.definition: Μυσία Mysía, moo-see'-ah; of uncertain origin; Mysia, a region of Asia Minor:—Mysia.

G3466.definition:
μυστήριον mystḗrion, moos-tay'-ree-on; from a derivative of μύω mýō (to shut the mouth); a secret or "mystery"
 (through the idea of silence imposed by initiation into religious
 rites):—mystery.

G3467.definition:
μυωπάζω myōpázō, moo-ope-ad'-zo; from a compound of the base of G3466 and ὤψ ṓps (the face; from G3700); to
 shut the eyes, i.e. blink (see indistinctly):—cannot see far off.

G3468.definition:
μώλωψ mṓlōps, mo'-lopes; from μῶλος mōlos ("moil"; probably akin to the base of G3433) and probably
 ὤψ ṓps (the face; from G3700); a mole ("black eye") or blow-mark:—stripe.

G3469.definition: †μωμάομαι mōmáomai, mo-mah'-om-ahee; from G3470; to carp at, i.e. censure (discredit):—blame.

G347.definition: ἀνακλίνω anaklínō, an-ak-lee'-no; from G303 and G2827; to lean back:—lay, (make) sit down.

G3470.definition:
μῶμος mōmos, mo'-mos; perhaps from G3201; a flaw or blot, i.e. (figuratively) disgraceful
 person:—blemish.

G3471.definition:
μωραίνω mōraínō, mo-rah'-ee-no; from G3474; to become insipid; figuratively, to make (passively, act)
 as a simpleton:—become fool, make foolish, lose savour.

G3472.definition: μωρία mōría, mo-ree'-ah; from G3474; silliness, i.e. absurdity:—foolishness.

G3473.definition:
μωρολογία mōrología, mo-rol-og-ee'-ah; from a compound of G3474 and G3004; silly talk, i.e.
 buffoonery:—foolish talking.

G3474.definition:
μωρός mōrós, mo-ros'; probably from the base of G3466; dull or stupid (as if shut up), i.e.
 heedless, (morally) blockhead, (apparently) absurd:—fool(-ish, X
 -ishness).

G3475.definition:
Μωσεύς Mōseús, moce-yoos'; of Hebrew origin; (H4872); Moseus, Moses, or Mouses (i.e. Mosheh), the
 Hebrew lawgiver:—Moses.

G3476.definition:
Ναασσών Naassṓn, nah-as-sone'; of Hebrew origin (H5177); Naasson (i.e. Nachshon), an
 Israelite:—Naasson.

G3477.definition:
Ναγγαί Nangaí, nang-gah'-ee; probably of Hebrew origin (compare H5052); Nangæ (i.e. perhaps
 Nogach), an Israelite:—Nagge.

G3479.definition: Ναζαρηνός Nazarēnós, nad-zar-ay-nos'; from G3478; a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth:—of Nazareth.

G3480.definition:
Ναζωραῖος Nazōraîos, nad-zo-rah'-yos; from G3478; a Nazoræan, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a
 Christian:—Nazarene, of Nazareth.

G3481.definition: †Ναθάν Nathán, nath-an'; of Hebrew origin (H5416); Nathan, an Israelite:—Nathan.

G3482.definition:
Ναθαναήλ Nathanaḗl, nath-an-ah-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H5417); Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and
 Christian:—Nathanael.

G3483.definition:
ναί naí, nahee; a primary particle of strong affirmation; yes:—even so, surely,
 truth, verily, yea, yes.

G3484.definition:
Ναΐν Naḯn, nah-in'; probably of Hebrew origin (compare H4999); Nain, a place in
 Palestine:—Nain.

G3485.definition:
ναός naós, nah-os'; from a primary ναίω naíō (to dwell); a fane, shrine, temple:—shrine,
 temple. Compare G2411.

G3486.definition: Ναούμ Naoúm, nah-oom'; of Hebrew origin (H5151); Naum (i.e. Nachum), an Israelite:—Naum.

G3487.definition: νάρδος nárdos, nar'dos; of foreign origin (compare H5373); "nard":—(spike-)nard.

G3488.definition:
Νάρκισσος Nárkissos, nar'-kis-sos; a flower of the same name, from νάρκη nárkē (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); 
 Narcissus, a Roman:—Narcissus.

G3489.definition:
ναυαγέω nauagéō, now-ag-eh'-o; from a compound of G3491 and G71; to be shipwrecked (stranded,
 "navigate"), literally or figuratively:—make (suffer) shipwreck.

G349.definition: ἀνακράζω anakrázō, an-ak-rad'-zo; from G303 and G2896; to scream up (aloud):—cry out.

G3490.definition: ναύκληρος naúklēros, now'-klay-ros; from G3491 and G2819 ("clerk"); a captain:—owner of a ship.

G3491.definition: ναῦς naûs, nowce; from νάω náō or νέω néō (to float); a boat (of any size):—ship.

G3492.definition: ναύτης naútēs, now'-tace; from G3491; a boatman, i.e. seaman:—sailor, shipman.

G3493.definition: Ναχώρ Nachṓr, nakh-ore'; of Hebrew origin (H5152); Nachor, the grandfather of Abraham:—Nachor.

G3494.definition:
νεανίας neanías, neh-an-ee'-as; from a derivative of G3501; a youth (up to about forty years):—young
 man.

G3495.definition: νεανίσκος neanískos, neh-an-is'-kos; from the same as G3494; a youth (under forty):—young man.

G3498.definition:
νεκρός nekrós, nek-ros'; from an apparently primary νέκυς nékys (a corpse); dead (literally or
 figuratively; also as noun):—dead.

G3499.definition:
νεκρόω nekróō, nek-ro'-o; from G3498; to deaden, i.e. (figuratively) to subdue:—be dead,
 mortify.

G35.definition:
ἀγενεαλόγητος agenealógētos, ag-en-eh-al-og'-ay-tos; from G1 (as negative particle) and G1075; unregistered as to
 birth:—without descent.

G350.definition:
ἀνακρίνω anakrínō, an-ak-ree'-no; from G303 and G2919; properly, to scrutinize, i.e. (by implication)
 investigate, interrogate, determine:—ask, question, discern, examine,
 judge, search.

G3500.definition: νέκρωσις nékrōsis, nek'-ro-sis; from G3499; decease; figuratively, impotency:—deadness, dying.

G3503.definition: νεότης neótēs, neh-ot'-ace; from G3501; newness, i.e. youthfulness:—youth.

G3504.definition:
νεόφυτος neóphytos, neh-of'-oo-tos; from G3501 and a derivative of G5453; newly planted, i.e. (figuratively)
 a young convert ("neophyte"):—novice.

G3506.definition:
νεύω neúō, nyoo'-o; apparently a primary verb; to "nod", i.e. (by analogy),
 signal:—beckon.

G3507.definition: †νεφέλη nephélē, nef-el'-ay; from G3509; properly, cloudiness, i.e. (concretely) a cloud:—cloud.

G3508.definition:
†Νεφθαλείμ Nephthaleím, nef-thal-ime'; of Hebrew origin (H5321); Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in
 Palestine:—Nephthalim.

G3509.definition: νέφος néphos, nef'-os; apparently a primary word; a cloud:—cloud.

G351.definition: ἀνάκρισις anákrisis, an-ak'-ree-sis; from G350; a (judicial) investigation:—examination.

G3510.definition:
νεφρός nephrós, nef-ros'; of uncertain affinity; a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the
 inmost mind:—reins.

G3511.definition:
νεωκόρος neōkóros, neh-o-kor'-os; from a form of G3485 and κορέω koréō (to sweep); a temple-servant, i.e. (by
 implication) a votary:—worshipper.

G3512.definition:
νεωτερικός neōterikós, neh-o-ter'-ik-os; from the comparative of G3501; appertaining to younger persons, i.e.
 juvenile:—youthful.

G3513.definition:
νή nḗ, nay; probably an intensive form of G3483; a particle of attestation
 (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as
 sure as:—I protest by.

G3514.definition: νήθω nḗthō, nay'-tho; from νέω néō (of like meaning); to spin:—spin.

G3515.definition:
νηπιάζω nēpiázō, nay-pee-ad'-zo; from G3516; to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently:—be a
 child.

G3516.definition:
νήπιος nḗpios, nay'-pee-os; from an obsolete particle νή- nḗ- (implying negation) and G2031; not
 speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded
 person, an immature Christian:—babe, child (+ -ish).

G3517.definition:
Νηρεύς Nēreús, nare-yoos'; apparently from a derivative of the base of G3491 (meaning wet); 
 Nereus, a Christian:—Nereus.

G3518.definition: Νηρί Nērí, nay-ree'; of Hebrew origin (H5374); Neri (i.e. Nerijah), an Israelite:—Neri.

G3519.definition: νησίον nēsíon, nay-see'-on; diminutive of G3520; an islet:—island.

G352.definition:
ἀνακύπτω anakýptō, an-ak-oop'-to; from G303 (in the sense of reversal) and G2955; to unbend, i.e. rise;
 figuratively, be elated:—lift up, look up.

G3520.definition: νῆσος nēsos, nay'-sos; probably from the base of G3491; an island:—island, isle.

G3521.definition:
νηστεία nēsteía, nace-ti'-ah; from G3522; abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious);
 specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement:—fast(-ing).

G3522.definition: νηστεύω nēsteúō, nace-tyoo'-o; from G3523; to abstain from food (religiously):—fast.

G3523.definition:
νῆστις nēstis, nace'-tis; from the inseparable negative particle νή- nḗ- (not) and G2068; not eating,
 i.e. abstinent from food (religiously):—fasting.

G3524.definition: †νηφάλεος nēpháleos, nay-fal'-eh-os; from G3525; sober, i.e. (figuratively) circumspect:—sober.

G3525.definition:
νήφω nḗphō, nay'-fo; of uncertain affinity; to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e.
 (figuratively) be discreet:—be sober, watch.

G3526.definition: Νίγερ Níger, neeg'-er; of Latin origin; black; Niger, a Christian:—Niger.

G3527.definition: Νικάνωρ Nikánōr, nik-an'-ore; probably from G3528; victorious; Nicanor, a Christian:—Nicanor.

G3528.definition:
νικάω nikáō, nik-ah'-o; from G3529; to subdue (literally or figuratively):—conquer, overcome,
 prevail, get the victory.

G3529.definition:
νίκη níkē, nee'-kay; apparently a primary word; conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively)
 the means of success:—victory.

G353.definition: ἀναλαμβάνω analambánō, an-al-am-ban'-o; from G303 and G2983; to take up:—receive up, take (in, unto, up).

G3530.definition:
Νικόδημος Nikódēmos, nik-od'-ay-mos; from G3534 and G1218; victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an
 Israelite:—Nicodemus.

G3531.definition: Νικολαΐτης Nikolaḯtēs, nik-ol-ah-ee'-tace; from G3532; a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus:—Nicolaitane.

G3532.definition:
Νικόλαος Nikólaos, nik-ol'-ah-os; from G3534 and G2994; victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a
 heretic:—Nicolaus.

G3533.definition:
Νικόπολις Nikópolis, nik-op'-ol-is; from G3534 and G4172; victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in
 Macedonia:—Nicopolis.

G3534.definition:
νῖκος nîkos, nee'-kos; from G3529; a conquest (concretely), i.e. (by implication)
 triumph:—victory.

G3536.definition:
†Νινευΐτης Nineuḯtēs, nin-yoo-ee'-tace; from G3535; a Ninevite, i.e. inhabitant of Nineveh:—of Nineve,
 Ninevite.

G3537.definition: νιπτήρ niptḗr, nip-tare'; from G3538; a ewer:—bason.

G3538.definition:
νίπτω níptō, nip'-to; to cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face);
 ceremonially, to perform ablution:—wash. Compare G3068.

G3539.definition:
†νοιέω noiéō, noy-eh'-o; from G3563; to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to
 comprehend, heed:—consider, perceive, think, understand.

G354.definition: †ἀνάληψις análēpsis, an-al'-ape-sis; from G353; ascension:—taking up.

G3540.definition:
νόημα nóēma, no'-ay-mah; from G3539; a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the
 intellect, disposition, itself:—device, mind, thought.

G3541.definition: νόθος nóthos, noth'-os; of uncertain affinity; a spurious or illegitimate son:—bastard.

G3542.definition:
νομή nomḗ, nom-ay'; feminine from the same as G3551; pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding
 (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage:—X
 eat, pasture.

G3543.definition:
νομίζω nomízō, nom-id'-zo; from G3551; properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom
 (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard:—suppose,
 thing, be wont.

G3544.definition:
νομικός nomikós, nom-ik-os'; from G3551; according (or pertaining) to law, i.e. legal
 (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law:—about the
 law, lawyer.

G3545.definition:
νομίμως nomímōs, nom-im'-oce; adverb from a derivative of G3551; legitimately (specially, agreeably
 to the rules of the lists):—lawfully.

G3546.definition:
νόμισμα nómisma, nom'-is-mah; from G3543; what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma),
 i.e. current coin:—money.

G3547.definition:
νομοδιδάσκαλος nomodidáskalos, nom-od-id-as'-kal-os; from G3551 and G1320; an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. a
 Rabbi:—doctor (teacher) of the law.

G3548.definition:
νομοθεσία nomothesía, nom-oth-es-ee'-ah; from G3550; legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic
 code):—giving of the law.

G3549.definition:
νομοθετέω nomothetéō, nom-oth-et-eh'-o; from G3550; to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic)
 enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them):—establish, receive the
 law.

G355.definition:
ἀναλίσκω analískō, an-al-is'-ko; from G303 and a form of the alternate of G138; properly, to use up, i.e.
 destroy:—consume.

G3550.definition: νομοθέτης nomothétēs, nom-oth-et'-ace; from G3551 and a derivative of G5087; a legislator:—lawgiver.

G3551.definition:
νόμος nómos, nom'-os; from a primary νέμω némō (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to
 animals); law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case
 (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the
 Gospel), or figuratively (a principle):—law.

G3552.definition:
νοσέω noséō, nos-eh'-o; from G3554; to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite)
 to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon):—dote.

G3554.definition:
νόσος nósos, nos'-os; of uncertain affinity; a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral
 disability):—disease, infirmity, sickness.

G3555.definition: νοσσιά nossiá, nos-see-ah'; from G3502; a brood (of chickens):—brood.

G3556.definition: νοσσίον nossíon, nos-see'-on; diminutive of G3502; a birdling:—chicken.

G3557.definition:
†νοσφίζομαι nosphízomai, nos-fid'-zom-ahee; middle voice from νοσφί nosphí (apart or clandestinely); to sequestrate for
 oneself, i.e. embezzle:—keep back, purloin.

G3558.definition:
νότος nótos, not'-os; of uncertain affinity; the south(-west) wind; by extension, the
 southern quarter itself:—south (wind).

G3559.definition:
νουθεσία nouthesía, noo-thes-ee'-ah; from G3563 and a derivative of G5087; calling attention to, i.e. (by
 implication) mild rebuke or warning:—admonition.

G356.definition: ἀναλογία analogía, an-al-og-ee'-ah; from a compound of G303 and G3056; proportion:—proportion.

G3560.definition:
νουθετέω nouthetéō, noo-thet-eh'-o; from the same as G3559; to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to
 caution or reprove gently:—admonish, warn.

G3561.definition:
†νουμηνία noumēnía, noo-may-nee'-ah; feminine of a compound of G3501 and G3376 (as noun by implication, of
 G2250); the festival of new moon:—new moon.

G3562.definition:
νουνεχῶς nounechōs, noon-ekh-oce'; adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of G3563 and G2192; in
 a mind-having way, i.e. prudently:—discreetly.

G3563.definition:
νοῦς noûs, nooce; probably from the base of G1097; the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or
 human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning:—mind,
 understanding. Compare G5590.

G3564.definition:
Νυμφᾶς Nymphâs, noom-fas'; probably contracted for a compound of G3565 and G1435; nymph-given (i.e.
 -born); Nymphas, a Christian:—Nymphas.

G3565.definition:
νύμφη nýmphē, noom-fay'; from a primary but obsolete verb νύπτω nýptō (to veil as a bride; compare
 Latin "nupto," to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including
 a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife:—bride, daughter in
 law.

G3566.definition: νυμφίος nymphíos, noom-fee'-os; from G3565; a bride-groom (literally or figuratively):—bridegroom.

G3567.definition: νυμφών nymphṓn, noom-fohn'; from G3565; the bridal room:—bridechamber.

G3568.definition:
†νῦν nŷn, noon; a primary particle of present time; "now" (as adverb of date, a
 transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or
 immediate:—henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this
 (time). See also G3569, G3570.

G357.definition:
ἀναλογίζομαι analogízomai, an-al-og-id'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G356; to estimate, i.e. (figuratively)
 contemplate:—consider.

G3570.definition: νυνί nyní, noo-nee'; a prolonged form of G3568 for emphasis; just now:—now.

G3571.definition: νύξ nýx, noox; a primary word; "night" (literally or figuratively):—(mid-)night.

G3572.definition: νύσσω nýssō, noos'-so; apparently a primary word; to prick ("nudge"):—pierce.

G3573.definition:
νυστάζω nystázō, noos-tad'-zo; from a presumed derivative of G3506; to nod, i.e. (by implication) to
 fall asleep; figuratively, to delay:—slumber.

G3574.definition:
νυχθήμερον nychthḗmeron, nookh-thay'-mer-on; from G3571 and G2250; a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four
 hours:—night and day.

G3575.definition: Νῶε Nōe, no'-eh; of Hebrew origin (H5146); Noë, (i.e. Noäch), a patriarch:—Noe.

G3576.definition:
νωθρός nōthrós, no-thros'; from a derivative of G3541; sluggish, i.e. (literally) lazy, or
 (figuratively) stupid:—dull, slothful.

G3577.definition: νῶτος nōtos, no'-tos; of uncertain affinity; the back:—back.

G3578.definition:
ξενία xenía, xen-ee'-ah; from G3581; hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of
 entertainment:—lodging.

G3579.definition:
ξενίζω xenízō, xen-id'-zo; from G3581; to be a host (passively, a guest); by implication, be
 (make, appear) strange:—entertain, lodge, (think it) strange.

G358.definition:
ἄναλος ánalos, an'-al-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G251; saltless, i.e. insipid:—X
 lose saltness.

G3580.definition: ξενοδοχέω xenodochéō, xen-od-okh-eh'-o; from a compound of G3581 and G1209; to be hospitable:—lodge strangers.

G3581.definition:
ξένος xénos, xen'-os; apparently a primary word; foreign (literally, alien, or figuratively,
 novel); by implication, a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer:—host,
 strange(-r).

G3582.definition:
ξέστης xéstēs, xes'-tace; as if from ξέω xéō (properly, to smooth; by implication, (of friction) to
 boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by
 corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about
 a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by
 analogy, a pitcher):—pot.

G3583.definition:
ξηραίνω xēraínō, xay-rah'-ee-no; from G3584; to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature:—dry
 up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away).

G3584.definition:
ξηρός xērós, xay-ros'; from the base of G3582 (through the idea of scorching); arid; by
 implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water):—dry land,
 withered.

G3585.definition: ξύλινος xýlinos, xoo'-lin-os; from G3586; wooden:—of wood.

G3587.definition:
ξυράω xyráō, xoo-rah'-o; from a derivative of the same as G3586 (meaning a razor); to shave or
 "shear" the hair:—shave.

G3588.definition:
ὁ ho, ho; the definite article; the (sometimes to be
 supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom):—the, this, that, one,
 he, she, it, etc.

G3589.definition: †ὀγδοήκοντα ogdoḗkonta, og-do-ay'-kon-tah; from G3590; ten times eight:—fourscore.

G359.definition: ἀνάλυσις análysis, an-al'-oo-sis; from G360; departure:—departure.

G3590.definition: ὄγδοος ógdoos, og'-do-os; from G3638; the eighth:—eighth.

G3591.definition:
ὄγκος ónkos, ong'-kos; probably from the same as G43; a mass (as bending or bulging by its
 load), i.e. burden (hindrance):—weight.

G3592.definition:
ὅδε hóde, hod'-eh; from G3588 and G1161; the same, i.e. this or that one (plural these or
 those); often used as a personal pronoun:—he, she, such, these, thus.

G3593.definition: ὁδεύω hodeúō, hod-yoo'-o; from G3598; to travel:—journey.

G3594.definition:
ὁδηγέω hodēgéō, hod-ayg-eh'-o; from G3595; to show the way (literally or figuratively
 (teach)):—guide, lead.

G3595.definition:
ὁδηγός hodēgós, hod-ayg-os'; from G3598 and G2233; a conductor (literally or figuratively
 (teacher)):—guide, leader.

G3596.definition:
ὁδοιπορέω hodoiporéō, hod-oy-por-eh'-o; from a compound of G3598 and G4198; to be a wayfarer, i.e. travel:—go
 on a journey.

G3597.definition: ὁδοιπορία hodoiporía, hod-oy-por-ee'-ah; from the same as G3596; travel:—journey(-ing).

G3598.definition:
ὁδός hodós, hod-os'; apparently a primary word; a road; by implication, a progress (the
 route, act or distance); figuratively, a mode or means:—journey,
 (high-)way.

G3599.definition: ὀδούς odoús, od-ooce; perhaps from the base of G2068; a "tooth":—tooth.

G36.definition:
ἀγενής agenḗs, ag-en-ace'; from G1 (as negative particle) and G1085; properly, without kin, i.e.
 (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble:—base things.

G360.definition:
ἀναλύω analýō, an-al-oo'-o; from G303 and G3089; to break up, i.e. depart (literally or
 figuratively):—depart, return.

G3600.definition: ὀδυνάω odynáō, od-oo-nah'-o; from G3601; to grieve:—sorrow, torment.

G3601.definition: ὀδύνη odýnē, od-oo'-nay; from G1416; grief (as dejecting):—sorrow.

G3602.definition:
ὀδυρμός odyrmós, od-oor-mos'; from a derivative of the base of G1416; moaning, i.e.
 lamentation:—mourning.

G3604.definition: Ὀζίας Ozías, od-zee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H5818); Ozias (i.e. Uzzijah), an Israelite:—Ozias.

G3605.definition:
ὄζω ózō, od'-zo; a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to scent (usually an ill
 "odor"):—stink.

G3606.definition:
ὅθεν hóthen, hoth'-en; from G3739 with the directive enclitic of source; from which place or
 source or cause (adverb or conjunction):—from thence, (from) whence,
 where(-by, -fore, -upon).

G3607.definition:
ὀθόνη othónē, oth-on'-ay; of uncertain affinity; a linen cloth, i.e. (especially) a
 sail:—sheet.

G3608.definition:
ὀθόνιον othónion, oth-on'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G3607; a linen bandage:—linen
 clothes.

G3609.definition:
οἰκεῖος oikeîos, oy-ki'-os; from G3624; domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent:—(those) of
 the (his own) house(-hold).

G361.definition:
ἀναμάρτητος anamártētos, an-am-ar'-tay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G264; 
 sinless:—that is without sin.

G3610.definition:
†οἰκέτης oikétēs, oy-ket'-ace; from G3611; a fellow resident, i.e. menial domestic:—(household)
 servant.

G3611.definition:
οἰκέω oikéō, oy-keh'-o; from G3624; to occupy a house, i.e. reside (figuratively, inhabit,
 remain, inhere); by implication, to cohabit:—dwell. See also G3625.

G3612.definition: οἴκημα oíkēma, oy'-kay-mah; from G3611; a tenement, i.e. (specially), a jail:—prison.

G3613.definition:
οἰκητήριον oikētḗrion, oy-kay-tay'-ree-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G3611 (equivalent to G3612); a
 residence (literally or figuratively):—habitation, house.

G3614.definition:
οἰκία oikía, oy-kee'-ah; from G3624; properly, residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely)
 an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication, a family
 (especially domestics):—home, house(-hold).

G3615.definition:
†οἰκιακός oikiakós, oy-kee-ak-os'; from G3614; familiar, i.e. (as noun) relatives:—they (them) of (his
 own) household.

G3616.definition: οἰκοδεσποτέω oikodespotéō, oy-kod-es-pot-eh'-o; from G3617; to be the head of (i.e. rule) a family:—guide the house.

G3617.definition:
οἰκοδεσπότης oikodespótēs, oy-kod-es-pot'-ace; from G3624 and G1203; the head of a family:—goodman (of the house),
 householder, master of the house.

G3618.definition:
οἰκοδομέω oikodoméō, oy-kod-om-eh'-o; from the same as G3619; to be a house-builder, i.e. construct or
 (figuratively) confirm:—(be in) build(-er, -ing, up), edify,
 embolden.

G362.definition: ἀναμένω anaménō, an-am-en'-o; from G303 and G3306; to await:—wait for.

G3620.definition: οἰκοδομία oikodomía, oy-kod-om-ee'-ah; from the same as G3619; confirmation:—edifying.

G3621.definition: †οἰκονομέω oikonoméō, oy-kon-om-eh'-o; from G3623; to manage (a house, i.e. an estate):—be steward.

G3622.definition:
οἰκονομία oikonomía, oy-kon-om-ee'-ah; from G3623; administration (of a household or estate); specially, a
 (religious) "economy":—dispensation, stewardship.

G3623.definition:
οἰκονόμος oikonómos, oy-kon-om'-os; from G3624 and the base of G3551; a house-distributor (i.e. manager), or
 overseer, i.e. an employee in that capacity; by extension, a fiscal
 agent (treasurer); figuratively, a preacher (of the
 Gospel):—chamberlain, governor, steward.

G3624.definition:
οἶκος oîkos, oy'-kos; of uncertain affinity; a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or
 figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally
 or figuratively):—home, house(-hold), temple.

G3625.definition:
οἰκουμένη oikouménē, oy-kou-men'-ay; feminine participle present passive of G3611 (as noun, by implication,
 of G1093); land, i.e. the (terrene part of the) globe; specially, the
 Roman empire:—earth, world.

G3626.definition:
†οἰκουρός oikourós, oy-koo-ros'; from G3624 and οὖρος oûros (a guard; be "ware"); a stayer at home, i.e.
 domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper"):—keeper at home.

G3627.definition: †οἰκτείρω oikteírō, oyk-ti'-ro; from οἶκτος oîktos (pity); to exercise pity:—have compassion on.

G3628.definition: οἰκτιρμός oiktirmós, oyk-tir-mos'; from G3627; pity:—mercy.

G3629.definition: οἰκτίρμων oiktírmōn, oyk-tir'-mone; from G3627; compassionate:—merciful, of tender mercy.

G363.definition:
†ἀναμιμνήσκω anamimnḗskō, an-am-im-nace'-ko; from G303 and G3403; to remind; (reflexively) to recollect:—call to
 mind, (bring to , call to, put in), remember(-brance).

G3630.definition:
οἰνοπότης oinopótēs, oy-nop-ot'-ace; from G3631 and a derivative of the alternate of G4095; a
 tippler:—winebibber.

G3631.definition:
οἶνος oînos, oy'-nos; a primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin (H3196)); "wine" (literally
 or figuratively):—wine.

G3632.definition:
οἰνοφλυγία oinophlygía, oy-nof-loog-ee'-ah; from G3631 and a form of the base of G5397; an overflow (or surplus) of
 wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness):—excess of wine.

G3633.definition:
οἴομαι oíomai, oy'-om-ahee; middle voice apparently from G3634; to make like (oneself), i.e.
 imagine (be of the opinion):—suppose, think.

G3634.definition:
οἷος hoîos, hoy'-os; probably akin to G3588, G3739, and G3745; such or what sort of (as a
 correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverbially) with
 negative, not so:—so (as), such as, what (manner of), which.

G3635.definition: ὀκνέω oknéō, ok-neh'-o; from ὄκνος óknos (hesitation); to be slow (figuratively, loath):—delay.

G3636.definition:
ὀκνηρός oknērós, ok-nay-ros'; from G3635; tardy, i.e. indolent; (figuratively) irksome:—grievous,
 slothful.

G3637.definition: ὀκταήμερος oktaḗmeros, ok-tah-ay'-mer-os; from G3638 and G2250; an eight-day old person or act:—the eighth day.

G3638.definition: ὀκτώ oktṓ, ok-to'; a primary numeral; "eight":—eight.

G3639.definition:
ὄλεθρος ólethros, ol'-eth-ros; from a primary ὄλλυμι óllymi (to destroy; a prolonged form); ruin, i.e.
 death, punishment:—destruction.

G364.definition: ἀνάμνησις anámnēsis, an-am'-nay-sis; from G363; recollection:—remembrance (again).

G3640.definition:
†ὀλιγόπιστος oligópistos, ol-ig-op'-is-tos; from G3641 and G4102; incredulous, i.e. lacking confidence (in
 Christ):—of little faith.

G3641.definition:
†ὀλίγος olígos, ol-ee'-gos; of uncertain affinity; puny (in extent, degree, number, duration or
 value); especially neuter (adverbially) somewhat:—+ almost,
 brief(-ly), few, (a) little, + long, a season, short, small, a while.

G3642.definition:
ὀλιγόψυχος oligópsychos, ol-ig-op'-soo-khos; from G3641 and G6590; little-spirited, i.e.
 faint-hearted:—feebleminded.

G3643.definition:
ὀλιγωρέω oligōréō, ol-ig-o-reh'-o; from a compound of G3641 and ὤρα ṓra ("care"); to have little regard for,
 i.e. to disesteem:—despise.

G3644.definition: ὀλοθρευτής olothreutḗs, ol-oth-ryoo-tace'; from G3645; a ruiner, i.e. (specially), a venomous serpent:—destroyer.

G3645.definition: ὀλοθρεύω olothreúō, ol-oth-ryoo'-o; from G3639; to spoil, i.e. slay:—destroy.

G3646.definition:
ὁλοκαύτωμα holokaútōma, hol-ok-ow'-to-mah; from a derivative of a compound of G3650 and a derivative of G2545; a
 wholly-consumed sacrifice ("holocaust"):—(whole) burnt offering.

G3647.definition: ὁλοκληρία holoklēría, hol-ok-lay-ree'-ah; from G3648; integrity, i.e. physical wholeness:—perfect soundness.

G3648.definition:
ὁλόκληρος holóklēros, hol'-ok'-lay-ros; from G3650 and G2819; complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in
 body):—entire, whole.

G3649.definition:
ὀλολύζω ololýzō, ol-ol-odd'-zo; a reduplicated primary verb; to "howl" or "halloo", i.e.
 shriek:—howl.

G365.definition: ἀνανεόω ananeóō, an-an-neh-o'-o; from G303 and a derivative of G3501; to renovate, i.e. reform:—renew.

G3650.definition:
ὅλος hólos, hol'-os; a primary word; "whole" or "all", i.e. complete (in extent, amount,
 time or degree), especially (neuter) as noun or adverb:—all,
 altogether, every whit, + throughout, whole.

G3651.definition:
ὁλοτελής holotelḗs, hol-ot-el-ace'; from G3650 and G5056; complete to the end, i.e. absolutely
 perfect:—wholly.

G3652.definition:
Ὀλυμπᾶς Olympâs, ol-oom-pas'; probably a contraction from Ὀλυμπιόδωρος Olympiódōros (Olympian-bestowed, i.e.
 heaven-descended); Olympas, a Christian:—Olympas.

G3653.definition:
ὄλυνθος ólynthos, ol'-oon-thos; of uncertain derivation; an unripe (because out of season)
 fig:—untimely fig.

G3654.definition:
ὅλως hólōs, hol'-oce; adverb from G3650; completely, i.e. altogether; (by analogy),
 everywhere; (negatively) not by any means:—at all, commonly, utterly.

G3655.definition: ὄμβρος ómbros, om'-bros; of uncertain affinity; a thunder storm:—shower.

G3656.definition:
ὁμιλέω homiléō, hom-il-eh'-o; from G3658; to be in company with, i.e. (by implication) to
 converse:—commune, talk.

G3657.definition:
ὁμιλία homilía, hom-il-ee'-ah; from G3658; companionship ("homily"), i.e. (by implication)
 intercourse:—communication.

G3658.definition:
ὅμιλος hómilos, hom'-il-os; from the base of G3674 and a derivative of the alternate of G138
 (meaning a crowd); association together, i.e. a multitude:—company.

G3659.definition: ὄμμα ómma, om'-mah; from G3700; a sight, i.e. (by implication) the eye:—eye.

G366.definition:
ἀνανήφω ananḗphō, an-an-ay'-fo; from G303 and G3525; to become sober again, i.e. (figuratively) regain
 (one's) senses:—recover self.

G3660.definition:
ὀμνύω omnýō, om-noo'-o; a prolonged form of a primary,
             but obsolete ὄμω ómō, for which
             another prolonged form
    ὀμόω omóō  om-o'-o  is used in certain tenses; 

 to swear, i.e. take (or declare on) oath:—swear.

G3661.definition:
ὁμοθυμαδόν homothymadón, hom-oth-oo-mad-on'; adverb from a compound of the base of G3674 and G2372; 
 unanimously:—with one accord (mind).

G3663.definition:
ὁμοιοπαθής homoiopathḗs, hom-oy-op-ath-ace'; from G3664 and the alternate of G3958; similarly affected:—of (subject
 to) like passions.

G3664.definition:
ὅμοιος hómoios, hom'-oy-os; from the base of G3674; similar (in appearance or character):—like, +
 manner.

G3665.definition: ὁμοιότης homoiótēs, hom-oy-ot'-ace; from G3664; resemblance:—like as, similitude.

G3666.definition:
ὁμοιόω homoióō, hom-oy-o'-o; from G3664; to assimilate, i.e. compare; passively, to become
 similar:—be (make) like, (in the) liken(-ess), resemble.

G3667.definition:
ὁμοίωμα homoíōma, hom-oy'-o-mah; from G3666; a form; abstractly, resemblance:—made like to, likeness,
 shape, similitude.

G3668.definition: ὁμοίως homoíōs, hom-oy'-oce; adverb from G3664; similarly:—likewise, so.

G3669.definition: ὁμοίωσις homoíōsis, hom-oy'-o-sis; from G3666; assimilation, i.e. resemblance:—similitude.

G367.definition:
Ἀνανίας Ananías, an-an-ee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H2608); Ananias, the name of three
 Israelites:—Ananias.

G3670.definition:
ὁμολογέω homologéō, hom-ol-og-eh'-o; from a compound of the base of G3674 and G3056; to assent, i.e.
 covenant, acknowledge:—con- (pro-)fess, confession is made, give
 thanks, promise.

G3671.definition: ὁμολογία homología, hom-ol-og-ee'-ah; from the same as G3670; acknowledgment:—con- (pro-)fession, professed.

G3672.definition:
ὁμολογουμένως homologouménōs, hom-ol-og-ow-men'-oce; adverb of present passive participle of G3670; confessedly:—without
 controversy.

G3673.definition:
ὁμότεχνος homótechnos, hom-ot'-ekh-nos; from the base of G3674 and G5078; a fellow-artificer:—of the same
 craft.

G3674.definition:
ὁμοῦ homoû, hom-oo'; genitive case of ὁμός homós (the same; akin to G260) as adverb; at the same
 place or time:—together.

G3675.definition:
ὁμόφρων homóphrōn, hom-of'-rone; from the base of G3674 and G5424; like-minded, i.e. harmonious:—of one
 mind.

G3676.definition:
ὅμως hómōs, hom'-oce; adverb from the base of G3674; at the same time, i.e. (conjunctionally)
 notwithstanding, yet still:—and even, nevertheless, though but.

G3677.definition: ὄναρ ónar, on'-ar; of uncertain derivation; a dream:—dream.

G3678.definition: ὀνάριον onárion, on-ar'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G3688; a little ass:—young ass.

G3679.definition:
ὀνειδίζω oneidízō, on-i-did'-zo; from G3681; to defame, i.e. rail at, chide, taunt:—cast in teeth,
 (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid.

G368.definition:
ἀναντίῤῥητος anantírrhētos, an-an-tir'-hray-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a
 compound of G473 and G4483; indisputable:—cannot be spoken against.

G3680.definition: ὀνειδισμός oneidismós, on-i-dis-mos'; from G3679; contumely:—reproach.

G3681.definition:
ὄνειδος óneidos, on'-i-dos; probably akin to the base of G3686; notoriety, i.e. a taunt
 (disgrace):—reproach.

G3682.definition: Ὀνήσιμος Onḗsimos, on-ay'-sim-os; from G3685; profitable; Onesimus, a Christian:—Onesimus.

G3683.definition:
Ὀνησίφορος Onēsíphoros, on-ay-sif'-or-os; from a derivative of G3685 and G5411; profit-bearer; Onesiphorus, a
 Christian:—Onespiphorus.

G3684.definition:
ὀνικός onikós, on-ik-os'; from G3688; belonging to a ass, i.e. large (so as to be turned by a
 ass):—millstone.

G3685.definition:
ὀνίνημι onínēmi, on-in'-ay-mee; a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb ( ὄνομαι ónomai, to slur); 
 for which another prolonged form ( ὀνάω onáō) is used as an alternate in
 some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of G3686
 through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to
 derive pleasure or advantage from:—have joy.

G3686.definition:
ὄνομα ónoma, on'-om-ah; from a presumed derivative of the base of G1097 (compare G3685); a
 "name" (literally or figuratively) (authority, character):—called, (+
 sur-)name(-d).

G3687.definition:
ὀνομάζω onomázō, on-om-ad'-zo; from G3686; to name, i.e. assign an appellation; by extension, to
 utter, mention, profess:—call, name.

G3688.definition: ὄνος ónos, on'-os; apparently a primary word; a donkey:—an ass.

G3689.definition:
ὄντως óntōs, on'-toce; adverb of the oblique cases of G5607; really:—certainly, clean,
 indeed, of a truth, verily.

G369.definition: ἀναντιῤῥήτως anantirrhḗtōs, an-an-tir-hray'-toce; adverb from G368; promptly:—without gainsaying.

G3690.definition: ὄξος óxos, oz-os; from G3691; vinegar, i.e. sour wine:—vinegar.

G3691.definition:
ὀξύς oxýs, oz-oos'; probably akin to the base of G188 ("acid"); keen; by analogy,
 rapid:—sharp, swift.

G3692.definition:
ὀπή opḗ, op-ay'; probably from G3700; a hole (as if for light), i.e. cavern; by analogy,
 a spring (of water):—cave, place.

G3693.definition:
ὄπισθεν ópisthen, op'-is-then; from ὄπις ópis (regard; from G3700) with enclitic of source; from the rear
 (as a secure aspect), i.e. at the back (adverb and preposition of
 place or time):—after, backside, behind.

G3694.definition:
ὀπίσω opísō, op-is'-o; from the same as G3693 with enclitic of direction; to the back, i.e.
 aback (as adverb or preposition of time or place; or as noun):—after,
 back(-ward), (+ get) behind, + follow.

G3695.definition:
ὁπλίζω hoplízō, hop-lid'-zo; from G3696; to equip (with weapons (middle voice and
 figuratively)):—arm self.

G3696.definition:
ὅπλον hóplon, hop'-lon; probably from a primary ἕπω hépō (to be busy about); an implement or
 utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially, offensive for
 war):—armour, instrument, weapon.

G3697.definition:
ὁποῖος hopoîos, hop-oy'-os; from G3739 and G4169; of what kind that, i.e. how (as) great (excellent)
 (specially, as an indefinite correlative to the definite antecedent
 G5108 of quality):—what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever.

G3699.definition:
ὅπου hópou, hop'-oo; from G3739 and G4225; what(-ever) where, i.e. at whichever spot:—in
 what place, where(-as, -soever), whither (+ soever).

G37.definition:
ἁγιάζω hagiázō, hag-ee-ad'-zo; from G40; to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate;
 (mentally) to venerate:—hallow, be holy, sanctify.
