 hold, × journeying, keep, + lay wait, + lighten the ship, make, X
 mean, + none of these things move me, observe, ordain, perform,
 provide, + have purged, purpose, put, + raising up, × secure, shew, X
 shoot out, spend, take, tarry, + transgress the law, work, yield. 
 Compare G4238.

G4161.definition:
ποίημα poíēma, poy'-ay-mah; from G4160; a product, i.e. fabric (literally or figuratively):—thing
 that is made, workmanship.

G4162.definition: ποίησις poíēsis, poy'-ay-sis; from G4160; action, i.e. performance (of the law):—deed.

G4163.definition: ποιητής poiētḗs, poy-ay-tace'; from G4160; a performer; specially, a "poet"; --doer, poet.

G4164.definition:
ποικίλος poikílos, poy-kee'-los; of uncertain derivation; motley, i.e. various in character:—divers,
 manifold.

G4165.definition:
ποιμαίνω poimaínō, poy-mah'-ee-no; from G4166; to tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser):—feed
 (cattle), rule.

G4166.definition:
ποιμήν poimḗn, poy-mane'; of uncertain affinity; a shepherd (literally or
 figuratively):—shepherd, pastor.

G4167.definition:
ποίμνη poímnē, poym'-nay; contraction from G4165; a flock (literally or figuratively):—flock,
 fold.

G4168.definition:
ποίμνιον poímnion, poym'-nee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G4167; a flock, i.e. (figuratively)
 group (of believers):—flock.

G4169.definition:
ποῖος poîos, poy'-os; from the base of G4226 and G3634; individualizing interrogative (of
 character) what sort of, or (of number) which one:—what (manner of),
 which.

G417.definition:
ἄνεμος ánemos, an'-em-os; from the base of G109; wind; (plural) by implication, (the four)
 quarters (of the earth):—wind.

G4170.definition:
πολεμέω poleméō, pol-em-eh'-o; from G4171; to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or
 figuratively):—fight, (make) war.

G4171.definition:
πόλεμος pólemos, pol'-em-os; from πέλομαι pélomai (to bustle); warfare (literally or figuratively; a single
 encounter or a series):—battle, fight, war.

G4172.definition:
πόλις pólis, pol'-is; probably from the same as G4171, or perhaps from G4183; a town
 (properly, with walls, of greater or less size):—city.

G4173.definition:
πολιτάρχης politárchēs, pol-it-ar'-khace; from G4172 and G757; a town-officer, i.e. magistrate:—ruler of the
 city.

G4174.definition:
πολιτεία politeía, pol-ee-ti'-ah; from G4177 ("polity"); citizenship; concretely, a
 community:—commonwealth, freedom.

G4175.definition:
πολίτευμα políteuma, pol-it'-yoo-mah; from G4176; a community, i.e. (abstractly) citizenship
 (figuratively):—conversation.

G4176.definition:
†πολιτεύομαι politeúomai, pol-it-yoo'-om-ahee; middle voice of a derivative of G4177; to behave as a citizen
 (figuratively):—let conversation be, live.

G4177.definition: πολίτης polítēs, pol-ee'-tace; from G4172; a townsman:—citizen.

G4178.definition:
πολλάκις pollákis, pol-lak'-is; multiplicative adverb from G4183; many times, i.e.
 frequently:—oft(-en, -entimes, -times).

G4179.definition:
πολλαπλασίων pollaplasíōn, pol-lap-las-ee'-ohn; from G4183 and probably a derivative of G4120; manifold, i.e. (neuter as
 noun) very much more:—manifold more.

G418.definition:
ἀνένδεκτος anéndektos, an-en'-dek-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of the same as G1735; 
 unadmitted, i.e. (by implication) not supposable:—impossible.

G4180.definition:
πολυλογία polylogía, pol-oo-log-ee'-ah; from a compound of G4183 and G3056; loquacity, i.e. prolixity:—much
 speaking.

G4181.definition:
πολυμερῶς polymerōs, pol-oo-mer'-oce; adverb from a compound of G4183 and G3313; in many portions, i.e.
 variously as to time and agency (piecemeal):—at sundry times.

G4182.definition: πολυποίκιλος polypoíkilos, pol-oo-poy'-kil-os; from G4183 and G4164; much variegated, i.e. multifarious:—manifold.

G4183.definition:
πολύς polýs, pol-oos'; including the forms from the alternate πολλός pollós; (singular) much (in any
 respect) or (plural) many; neuter (singular) as adverbial, largely;
 neuter (plural) as adverb or noun often, mostly, largely:—abundant, +
 altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age,
 deal, -ly, while), long, many, much, oft(-en (-times)), plenteous,
 sore, straitly. Compare G4118, G4119.

G4184.definition:
πολύσπλαγχνος polýsplanchnos, pol-oo'-splankh-nos; from G4183 and G4698 (figuratively); extremely compassionate:—very
 pitiful.

G4185.definition:
πολυτελής polytelḗs, pol-oo-tel-ace'; from G4183 and G5056; extremely expensive:—costly, very precious, of
 great price.

G4186.definition: πολύτιμος polýtimos, pol-oot'-ee-mos; from G4183 and G5092; extremely valuable:—very costly, of great price.

G4187.definition:
πολυτρόπως polytrópōs, pol-oot-rop'-oce; adverb from a compound of G4183 and G5158; in many ways, i.e. variously
 as to method or form:—in divers manners.

G4188.definition: πόμα póma, pom'-ah; from the alternate of G4095; a beverage:—drink.

G4189.definition:
πονηρία ponēría, pon-ay-ree'-ah; from G4190; depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely)
 plots, sins:—iniquity, wickedness.

G419.definition:
†ἀνεξερεύνητος anexereúnētos, an-ex-er-yoo'-nay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1830; not
 searched out, i.e. (by implication) inscrutable:—unsearchable.

G4190.definition:
πονηρός ponērós, pon-ay-ros'; from a derivative of G4192; hurtful, i.e. evil (properly, in effect or
 influence, and thus differing from G2556, which refers rather to
 essential character, as well as from G4550, which indicates degeneracy
 from original virtue); figuratively, calamitous; also (passively) ill,
 i.e. diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, i.e. derelict,
 vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural)
 guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners:—bad,
 evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked(-ness). See also G4191.

G4192.definition: πόνος pónos, pon'-os; from the base of G3993; toil, i.e. (by implication) anguish:—pain.

G4193.definition: Ποντικός Pontikós, pon-tik-os'; from G4195; a Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus:—born in Pontus.

G4194.definition: Πόντιος Póntios, pon'-tee-os; of Latin origin; apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman:—Pontius.

G4195.definition:
Πόντος Póntos, pon'-tos; of Latin origin; 

 a sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor:—Pontus.

G4196.definition:
Πόπλιος Póplios, pop'-lee-os; of Latin origin; apparently "popular"; Poplius (i.e. Publius), a
 Roman:—Publius.

G4197.definition:
πορεία poreía, por-i'-ah; from G4198; travel (by land); figuratively (plural) proceedings, i.e.
 career:—journey(-ing), ways.

G4198.definition:
πορεύομαι poreúomai, por-yoo'-om-ahee; middle voice from a derivative of the same as G3984; to traverse, i.e.
 travel (literally or figuratively; especially to remove (figuratively,
 die), live, etc.); --depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a,
 take a) journey, walk.

G4199.definition:
πορθέω porthéō, por-theh'-o; prolongation from πέρθω pérthō (to sack); to ravage
 (figuratively):—destroy, waste.

G42.definition: ἁγιωσύνη hagiōsýnē, hag-ee-o-soo'-nay; from G40; sacredness (i.e. properly, the quality):—holiness.

G420.definition: ἀνεξίκακος anexíkakos, an-ex-ik'-ak-os; from G430 and G2556; enduring of ill, i.e. forbearing:—patient.

G4200.definition:
πορισμός porismós, por-is-mos'; from a derivative of πόρος póros (a way, i.e. means); furnishing
 (procuring), i.e. (by implication) money-getting (acquisition):—gain.

G4201.definition: Πόρκιος Pórkios, por'-kee-os; of Latin origin; apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman:—Porcius.

G4202.definition:
πορνεία porneía, por-ni'-ah; from G4203; harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively,
 idolatry:—fornication.

G4203.definition:
πορνεύω porneúō, porn-yoo'-o; from G4204; to act the harlot, i.e. (literally) indulge unlawful lust
 (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry:—commit
 (fornication).

G4204.definition:
πόρνη pórnē, por'-nay; feminine of G4205; a strumpet; figuratively, an idolater:—harlot,
 whore.

G4205.definition:
πόρνος pórnos, por'-nos; from πέρνημι pérnēmi (to sell; akin to the base of G4097); a (male) prostitute
 (as venal), i.e. (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine):—fornicator,
 whoremonger.

G4206.definition:
πόῤῥω pórrhō, por'-rho; adverb from G4253; forwards, i.e. at a distance:—far, a great way off. 
 See also G4207.

G4207.definition:
πόῤῥωθεν pórrhōthen, por'-rho-then; from G4206 with adverbial enclitic of source; from far, or (by
 implication) at a distance, i.e. distantly:—afar off.

G4208.definition:
†ποῤῥωτέρω porrhōtérō, por-rho-ter'-o; adverb comparative of G4206; further, i.e. a greater
 distance:—farther.

G4209.definition:
πορφύρα porphýra, por-foo'-rah; of Latin origin; the "purple" mussel, i.e. (by implication) the
 red-blue color itself, and finally a garment dyed with it:—purple.

G421.definition:
ἀνεξιχνίαστος anexichníastos, an-ex-ikh-nee'-as-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a
 compound of G1537 and a derivative of G2487; not tracked out, i.e. (by
 implication) untraceable:—past finding out; unsearchable.

G4210.definition: †πορφυροῦς porphyroûs, por-foo-rooce'; from G4209; purpureal, i.e. bluish red:—purple.

G4211.definition:
πορφυρόπωλις porphyrópōlis, por-foo-rop'-o-lis; feminine of a compound of G4209 and G4453; a female trader in purple
 cloth:—seller of purple.

G4212.definition: ποσάκις posákis, pos-ak'-is; multiplicative from G4214; how many times:—how oft(-en).

G4213.definition:
πόσις pósis, pos'-is; from the alternate of G4095; a drinking (the act), i.e. (concretely) a
 draught:—drink.

G4214.definition:
πόσος pósos, pos'-os; from an absolute πός pós (who, what) and G3739; interrogative pronoun (of
 amount) how much (large, long or (plural) many):—how great (long,
 many), what.

G4215.definition:
ποταμός potamós, pot-am-os'; probably from a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (compare G4224); a
 current, brook or freshet (as drinkable), i.e. running water:—flood,
 river, stream, water.

G4216.definition:
ποταμοφόρητος potamophórētos, pot-am-of-or'-ay-tos; from G4215 and a derivative of G5409; river-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a
 stream:—carried away of the flood.

G4217.definition:
ποταπός potapós, pot-ap-os'; apparently from G4219 and the base of G4226; interrogatively, whatever,
 i.e. of what possible sort:—what (manner of).

G4218.definition:
ποτέ poté, pot-eh'; from the base of G4225 and G5037; indefinite adverb, at some time,
 ever:—afore-(any, some-)time(-s), at length (the last), (+ n- )ever,
 in the old time, in time past, once, when.

G4219.definition:
πότε póte, pot'-eh; from the base of G4226 and G5037; interrogative adverb, at what time:—+
 how long, when.

G422.definition:
ἀνεπαίσχυντος anepaíschyntos, an-ep-ah'-ee-skhoon-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a
 compound of G1909 and G153; not ashamed, i.e. irreprehensible: --that
 needeth not to be ashamed.

G4220.definition:
†πότερον póteron, pot'-er-on; neuter of a comparative of the base of G4226; interrogative as adverb,
 which (of two), i.e. is it this or that:—whether.

G4222.definition:
ποτίζω potízō, pot-id'-zo; from a derivative of the alternate of G4095; to furnish drink,
 irrigate:—give (make) to drink, feed, water.

G4223.definition:
Ποτίολοι Potíoloi, pot-ee'-ol-oy; of Latin origin; little wells, i.e. mineral springs; Potioli (i.e.
 Puteoli), a place in Italy:—Puteoli.

G4224.definition: πότος pótos, pot'-os; from the alternate of G4095; a drinking-bout or carousal:—banqueting.

G4225.definition:
†πού poú, poo; genitive case of an indefinite pronoun πός pós (some) otherwise obsolete
 (compare G4214); as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly:—about, a
 certain place.

G4226.definition:
ποῦ poû, poo; genitive case of an interrogative pronoun πός pós (what) otherwise
 obsolete (perhaps the same as G4225 used with the rising slide of
 inquiry); as adverb of place; at (by implication, to) what
 locality:—where, whither.

G4227.definition: Πούδης Poúdēs, poo'-dace; of Latin origin; modest; Pudes (i.e. Pudens), a Christian:—Pudens.

G4228.definition: πούς poús, pooce; a primary word; a "foot" (figuratively or literally):—foot(-stool).

G4229.definition:
πρᾶγμα prâgma, prag'-mah; from G4238; a deed; by implication, an affair; by extension, an object
 (material):—business, matter, thing, work.

G423.definition:
†ἀνεπίληπτος anepílēptos, an-ep-eel'-ape-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1949; not
 arrested, i.e. (by implication) inculpable:—blameless, unrebukeable.

G4230.definition: πραγματεία pragmateía, prag-mat-i'-ah; from G4231; a transaction, i.e. negotiation:—affair.

G4231.definition: πραγματεύομαι pragmateúomai, prag-mat-yoo'-om-ahee; from G4229; to busy oneself with, i.e. to trade:—occupy.

G4232.definition:
πραιτώριον praitṓrion, prahee-to'-ree-on; of Latin origin; the prætorium or governor's courtroom (sometimes
 including the whole edifice and camp):—(common, judgment) hall (of
 judgment), palace, prætorium.

G4233.definition:
πράκτωρ práktōr, prak'-tor; from a derivative of G4238; a practiser, i.e. (specially), an official
 collector:—officer.

G4234.definition:
πρᾶξις prâxis, prax'-is; from G4238; practice, i.e. (concretely) an act; by extension, a
 function:—deed, office, work.

G4237.definition:
πρασιά prasiá, pras-ee-ah'; perhaps from πράσον práson (a leek, and so an onion-patch); a garden plot,
 i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by
 Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement):—in ranks.

G4238.definition:
πράσσω prássō, pras'-so; a primary verb; to "practise", i.e. perform repeatedly or habitually
 (thus differing from G4160, which properly refers to a single act); by
 implication, to execute, accomplish, etc.; specially, to collect
 (dues), fare (personally):—commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require,
 use arts.

G4239.definition:
πραΰς praÿs, prah-ooce'; apparently a primary word; mild, i.e. (by implication) humble:—meek. 
 See also G4235.

G424.definition: ἀνέρχομαι anérchomai, an-erkh'-om-ahee; from G303 and G2064; to ascend:—go up.

G4240.definition: πραΰτης praÿtēs, prah-oo'-tace; from G4239; mildness, i.e. (by implication) humility:—meekness.

G4241.definition:
†πρέπω prépō, prep'-o; apparently a primary verb; to tower up (be conspicuous), i.e. (by
 implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present
 indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right):—become,
 comely.

G4242.definition:
πρεσβεία presbeía, pres-bi'-ah; from G4243; seniority (eldership), i.e. (by implication) an embassy
 (concretely, ambassadors):—ambassage, message.

G4243.definition:
πρεσβεύω presbeúō, pres-byoo'-o; from the base of G4245; to be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a
 representative (figuratively, preacher):—be an ambassador.

G4244.definition:
πρεσβυτέριον presbytérion, pres-boo-ter'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G4245; the order of elders, i.e.
 (specially), Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian "presbytery":—(estate
 of) elder(-s), presbytery.

G4245.definition:
πρεσβύτερος presbýteros, pres-boo'-ter-os; comparative of πρέσβυς présbys (elderly); older; as noun, a senior; specially,
 an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial
 council) or Christian "presbyter":—elder(-est), old.

G4246.definition: πρεσβύτης presbýtēs, pres-boo'-tace; from the same as G4245; an old man:—aged (man), old man.

G4247.definition: πρεσβῦτις presbŷtis, pres-boo'-tis; feminine of G4246; an old woman:—aged woman.

G4248.definition:
πρηνής prēnḗs, pray-nace'; from G4253; leaning (falling) forward ("prone"), i.e. head
 foremost:—headlong.

G4249.definition:
πρίζω prízō, prid'-zo; a strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw); to saw in two:—saw
 asunder.

G425.definition: ἄνεσις ánesis, an'-es-is; from G447; relaxation or (figuratively) relief:—eased, liberty, rest.

G4250.definition: πρίν prín, prin; adverb from G4253; prior, sooner:—before (that), ere.

G4251.definition:
Πρίσκα Príska, pris'-kah; of Latin origin; feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian
 woman:—Prisca. See also G4252.

G4253.definition:
πρό pró, pro; a primary preposition; "fore", i.e. in front of, prior (figuratively,
 superior) to:—above, ago, before, or ever.

G4254.definition:
προάγω proágō, pro-ag'-o; from G4253 and G71; to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to
 precede (in place or time (participle, previous)):—bring (forth,
 out), go before.

G4255.definition:
προαιρέομαι proairéomai, pro-ahee-reh'-om-ahee; from G4253 and G138; to choose for oneself before another thing
 (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend):—purpose.

G4256.definition:
προαιτιάομαι proaitiáomai, pro-ahee-tee-ah'-om-ahee; from G4253 and a derivative of G156; to accuse already, i.e. previously
 charge:—prove before.

G4257.definition: προακούω proakoúō, pro-ak-oo'-o; from G4253 and G191; to hear already,i.e. anticipate:—hear before.

G4258.definition:
προαμαρτάνω proamartánō, pro-am-ar-tan'-o; from G4253 and G264; to sin previously (to conversion):—sin already,
 heretofore sin.

G4259.definition:
προαύλιον proaúlion, pro-ow'-lee-on; neuter of a presumed compound of G4253 and G833; a forecourt, i.e.
 vestibule (alley-way):—porch.

G426.definition:
ἀνετάζω anetázō, an-et-ad'-zo; from G303 and ἐτάζω etázō (to test); to investigate (judicially):—(should
 have) examined(-d).

G4260.definition:
προβαίνω probaínō, prob-ah'-ee-no; from G4253 and the base of G939; to walk forward, i.e. advance
 (literally, or in years):—+ be of a great age, go farther (on), be
 well stricken.

G4261.definition:
προβάλλω probállō, prob-al'-lo; from G4253 and G906; to throw forward, i.e. push to the front,
 germinate:—put forward, shoot forth.

G4262.definition:
προβατικός probatikós, prob-at-ik-os'; from G4263; relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were
 led into Jerusalem:—sheep (market).

G4263.definition:
†πρόβατον próbaton, prob'-at-on; probably neuter of a presumed derivative of G4260; something that walks
 forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or
 figuratively):—sheep(-fold).

G4264.definition:
προβιβάζω probibázō, prob-ib-ad'-zo; from G4253 and a reduplicated form of G971; to force forward, i.e. bring
 to the front, instigate:—draw, before instruct.

G4265.definition:
προβλέπω problépō, prob-lep'-o; from G4253 and G991; to look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in
 advance:—provide.

G4266.definition:
προγίνομαι progínomai, prog-in'-om-ahee; from G4253 and G1096; to be already, i.e. have previousy transpired:—be
 past.

G4267.definition:
προγινώσκω proginṓskō, prog-in-oce'-ko; from G4253 and G1097; to know beforehand, i.e. foresee:—foreknow
 (ordain), know (before).

G4268.definition: πρόγνωσις prógnōsis, prog'-no-sis; from G4267; forethought:—foreknowledge.

G4269.definition: πρόγονος prógonos, prog'-on-os; from G4266; an ancestor, (grand-)parent:—forefather, parent.

G427.definition: ἄνευ áneu, an'-yoo; a primary particle; without:—without. Compare G1.

G4270.definition:
προγράφω prográphō, prog-raf'-o; from G4253 and G1125; to write previously; figuratively, to announce,
 prescribe:—before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore,
 aforetime).

G4271.definition:
πρόδηλος pródēlos, prod'-ay-los; from G4253 and G1212; plain before all men, i.e. obvious:—evident,
 manifest (open) beforehand.

G4272.definition:
προδίδωμι prodídōmi, prod-id'-o-mee; from G4253 and G1325; to give before the other party has given:—first
 give.

G4273.definition:
προδότης prodótēs, prod-ot'-ace; from G4272 (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's)
 hands); a surrender:—betrayer, traitor.

G4274.definition:
πρόδρομος pródromos, prod'-rom-os; from the alternate of G4390; a runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively,
 precursor):—forerunner.

G4276.definition:
προελπίζω proelpízō, pro-el-pid'-zo; from G4253 and G1679; to hope in advance of other confirmation:—first
 trust.

G4278.definition: προενάρχομαι proenárchomai, pro-en-ar'-khom-ahee; from G4253 and G1728; to commence already:—begin (before).

G4279.definition: προεπαγγέλλομαι proepangéllomai, pro-ep-ang-ghel'-lom-ahee; middle voice from G4253 and G1861; to promise of old:—promise before.

G428.definition:
ἀνεύθετος aneúthetos, an-yoo'-the-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2111; not well set, i.e.
 inconvenient:—not commodious.

G4281.definition:
προέρχομαι proérchomai, pro-er'-khom-ahee; from G4253 and G2064 (including its alternate); to go onward, precede
 (in place or time):—go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on.

G4282.definition:
προετοιμάζω proetoimázō, pro-et-oy-mad'-zo; from G4253 and G2090; to fit up in advance (literally or
 figuratively):—ordain before, prepare afore.

G4283.definition:
προευαγγελίζομαι proeuangelízomai, pro-yoo-ang-ghel-id'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G4253 and G2097; to announce glad news in
 advance:—preach before the gospel.

G4284.definition:
†προέχομαι proéchomai, pro-ekh-om-ahee; middle voice from G4253 and G2192; to hold oneself before others, i.e.
 (figuratively) to excel:—be better.

G4285.definition:
προηγέομαι proēgéomai, pro-ay-geh'-om-ahee; from G4253 and G2233; to lead the way for others, i.e. show
 deference:—prefer.

G4287.definition:
προθέσμιος prothésmios, proth-es'-mee-os; from G4253 and a derivative of G5087; fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine
 with G2250 implied) a designated day:—time appointed.

G4288.definition:
προθυμία prothymía, proth-oo-mee'-ah; from G4289; predisposition, i.e. alacrity:—forwardness of mind,
 readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind.

G4289.definition:
πρόθυμος próthymos, proth'-oo-mos; from G4253 and G2372; forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as
 noun) alacrity:—ready, willing.

G429.definition: ἀνευρίσκω aneurískō, an-yoo-ris'-ko; from G303 and G2147; to find out:—find.

G4290.definition: προθύμως prothýmōs, proth-oo'-moce; adverb from G4289; with alacrity:—willingly.

G4291.definition:
προΐστημι proḯstēmi, pro-is'-tay-mee; from G4253 and G2476; to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by
 implication) to practise:—maintain, be over, rule.

G4292.definition:
†προκαλέομαι prokaléomai, prok-al-eh'-om-ahee; middle voice from G4253 and G2564; to call forth to oneself (challenge),
 i.e. (by implication) to irritate:—provoke.

G4293.definition:
προκαταγγέλλω prokatangéllō, prok-at-ang-ghel'-lo; from G4253 and G2605; to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict,
 promise:—foretell, have notice, (shew) before.

G4294.definition: προκαταρτίζω prokatartízō, prok-at-ar-tid'-zo; from G4253 and G2675; to prepare in advance:—make up beforehand.

G4295.definition:
πρόκειμαι prókeimai, prok'-i-mahee; from G4253 and G2749; to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be
 present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward):—be
 first, set before (forth).

G4296.definition:
προκηρύσσω prokērýssō, prok-ay-rooce'-so; from G4253 and G2784; to herald (i.e. proclaim) in advance:—before
 (first) preach.

G4297.definition:
προκοπή prokopḗ, prok-op-ay'; from G4298; progress, i.e. advancement (subjectively or
 objectively):—furtherance, profit.

G4298.definition:
προκόπτω prokóptō, prok-op'-to; from G4253 and G2875; to drive forward (as if by beating), i.e.
 (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in
 time, to be well along):—increase, proceed, profit, be far spent,
 wax.

G4299.definition:
πρόκριμα prókrima, prok'-ree-mah; from a compound of G4253 and G2919; a prejudgment (prejudice), i.e.
 prepossession:—prefer one before another.

G43.definition: ἀγκάλη ankálē, ang-kal'-ay; from ἄγκος ánkos (a bend, "ache"); an arm (as curved):—arm.

G430.definition:
ἀνέχομαι anéchomai, an-ekh'-om-ahee; middle voice from G303 and G2192; to hold oneself up against, i.e.
 (figuratively) put up with:—bear with, endure, forbear, suffer.

G4300.definition: προκυρόω prokyróō, prok-oo-ro'-o; from G4253 and G2964; to ratify previously:—confirm before.

G4301.definition:
προλαμβάνω prolambánō, prol-am-ban'-o; from G4253 and G2983; to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before
 others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate,
 surprise:—come aforehand, overtake, take before.

G4302.definition:
προλέγω prolégō, prol-eg'-o; from G4253 and G3004; to say beforehand, i.e. predict,
 forewarn:—foretell, tell before.

G4303.definition:
προμαρτύρομαι promartýromai, prom-ar-too'-rom-ahee; from G4253 and G3143; to be a witness in advance i.e. predict:—testify
 beforehand.

G4304.definition: προμελετάω promeletáō, prom-el-et-ah'-o; from G4253 and G3191; to premeditate:—meditate before.

G4305.definition:
προμεριμνάω promerimnáō, prom-er-im-nah'-o; from G4253 and G3309; to care (anxiously) in advance:—take thought
 beforehand.

G4306.definition:
προνοέω pronoéō, pron-o-eh'-o; from G4253 and G3539; to consider in advance, i.e. look out for
 beforehand (actively, by way of maintenance for others; middle voice
 by way of circumspection for oneself):—provide (for).

G4307.definition:
πρόνοια prónoia, pron'-oy-ah; from G4306; forethought, i.e. provident care or supply:—providence,
 provision.

G4308.definition:
προοράω prooráō, pro-or-ah'-o; from G4253 and G3708; to behold in advance, i.e. (actively) to notice
 (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own)
 view:—foresee, see before.

G4309.definition:
προορίζω proorízō, pro-or-id'-zo; from G4253 and G3724; to limit in advance, i.e. (figuratively)
 predetermine:—determine before, ordain, predestinate.

G431.definition:
†ἀνεψιός anepsiós, an-eps'-ee-os; from G1 (as a particle of union) and an obsolete νέπος népos (a brood); 
 properly, akin, i.e. (specially) a cousin:—sister's son.

G4310.definition: προπάσχω propáschō, prop-as'-kho; from G4253 and G3958; to undergo hardship previously:—suffer before.

G4311.definition:
προπέμπω propémpō, prop-em'-po; from G4253 and G3992; to send forward, i.e. escort or aid in
 travel:—accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth.

G4312.definition:
προπετής propetḗs, prop-et-ace'; from a compound of G4253 and G4098; falling forward, i.e. headlong
 (figuratively, precipitate):—heady, rash(-ly).

G4313.definition: προπορεύομαι proporeúomai, prop-or-yoo'-om-ahee; from G4253 and G4198; to precede (as guide or herald):—go before.

G4314.definition:
πρός prós, pros; a strengthened form of G4253; a preposition of direction; forward to,
 i.e. toward (with the genitive case, the side of, i.e. pertaining to;
 with the dative case, by the side of, i.e. near to; usually with the
 accusative case, the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the
 destination of the relation, i.e. whither or for which it is
 predicated):—about, according to , against, among, at, because of,
 before, between, (where-)by, for, × at thy house, in, for intent, nigh
 unto, of, which pertain to, that, to (the end that), × together, to
 (you) -ward, unto, with(-in). In the comparative case, it denotes
 essentially the same applications, namely, motion towards, accession
 to, or nearness at.

G4315.definition:
προσάββατον prosábbaton, pros-ab'-bat-on; from G4253 and G4521; a fore-sabbath, i.e. the Sabbath-eve:—day before
 the sabbath. Compare G3904.

G4316.definition:
προσαγορεύω prosagoreúō, pros-ag-or-yoo'-o; from G4314 and a derivative of G58 (mean to harangue); to address, i.e.
 salute by name:—call.

G4317.definition:
προσάγω proságō, pros-ag'-o; from G4314 and G71; to lead towards, i.e. (transitively) to conduct near
 (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach:—bring, draw near.

G4318.definition: προσαγωγή prosagōgḗ, pros-ag-ogue-ay'; from G4317 (compare G72); admission:—access.

G4319.definition: προσαιτέω prosaitéō, pros-ahee-teh'-o; from G4314 and G154; to ask repeatedly (importune), i.e. solicit:—beg.

G432.definition: ἄνηθον ánēthon, an'-ay-thon; probably of foreign origin; dill:—anise.

G4320.definition:
προσαναβαίνω prosanabaínō, pros-an-ab-ah'-ee-no; from G4314 and G305; to ascend farther, i.e. be promoted (take an upper
 (more honorable) seat):—go up.

G4321.definition: προσαναλίσκω prosanalískō, pros-an-al-is'-ko; from G4314 and G355; to expend further:—spend.

G4322.definition: προσαναπληρόω prosanaplēróō, pros-an-ap-lay-ro'-o; from G4314 and G378; to fill up further, i.e. furnish fully:—supply.

G4323.definition:
προσανατίθημι prosanatíthēmi, pros-an-at-ith'-ay-mee; from G4314 and G394; to lay up in addition, i.e. (middle voice and
 figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult:—in conference
 add, confer.

G4324.definition: προσαπειλέω prosapeiléō, pros-ap-i-leh'-o; from G4314 and G546; to menace additionally:—i. e. threaten further.

G4325.definition: προσδαπανάω prosdapanáō, pros-dap-an-ah'-o; from G4314 and G1159; to expend additionally:—spend more.

G4326.definition: προσδέομαι prosdéomai, pros-deh'-om-ahee; from G4314 and G1189; to require additionally, i.e. want further:—need.

G4327.definition:
προσδέχομαι prosdéchomai, pros-dekh'-om-ahee; from G4314 and G1209; to admit (to intercourse, hospitality, credence,
 or (figuratively) endurance); by implication, to await (with
 confidence or patience):—accept, allow, look (wait) for, take.

G4328.definition:
προσδοκάω prosdokáō, pros-dok-ah'-o; from G4314 and dokeuo (to watch); to anticipate (in thought, hope or
 fear); by implication, to await:—(be in) expect(-ation), look (for),
 when looked, tarry, wait for.

G4329.definition:
προσδοκία prosdokía, pros-dok-ee'-ah; from G4328; apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction
 anticipated:—expectation, looking after.

G433.definition:
ἀνήκω anḗkō, an-ay'-ko; from G303 and G2240; to attain to, i.e. (figuratively) be
 proper:—convenient, be fit.

G4330.definition: προσεάω proseáō, pros-eh-ah'-o; from G4314 and G1439; to permit further progress:—suffer.

G4331.definition: προσεγγίζω prosengízō, pros-eng-ghid'-zo; from G4314 and G1448; to approach near:—come nigh.

G4333.definition:
προσεργάζομαι prosergázomai, pros-er-gad'-zom-ahee; from G4314 and G2038; to work additionally, i.e. (by implication)
 acquire besides:—gain.

G4334.definition:
προσέρχομαι prosérchomai, pros-er'-khom-ahee; from G4314 and G2064 (including its alternate); to approach, i.e.
 (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent
 to:—(as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near,
 go (near, to, unto).

G4335.definition:
προσευχή proseuchḗ, pros-yoo-khay'; from G4336; prayer (worship); by implication, an oratory (chapel):—X
 pray earnestly, prayer.

G4336.definition:
προσεύχομαι proseúchomai, pros-yoo'-khom-ahee; from G4314 and G2172; to pray to God, i.e. supplicate, worship:—pray (X
 earnestly, for), make prayer.

G4337.definition:
προσέχω proséchō, pros-ekh'-o; from G4314 and G2192; (figuratively) to hold the mind (3563 implied)
 towards, i.e. pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to,
 adhere to:—(give) attend(-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be
 given to, give (take) heed (to unto); have regard.

G4338.definition:
προσηλόω prosēlóō, pros-ay-lo'-o; from G4314 and a derivative of G2247; to peg to, i.e. spike fast:—nail
 to.

G4339.definition:
προσήλυτος prosḗlytos, pros-ay'-loo-tos; from the alternate of G4334; an arriver from a foreign region, i.e.
 (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism
 ("proselyte"):—proselyte.

G434.definition: ἀνήμερος anḗmeros, an-ay'-mer-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and ἥμερος hḗmeros (lame); savage:—fierce.

G4340.definition:
πρόσκαιρος próskairos, pros'-kahee-ros; from G4314 and G2540; for the occasion only, i.e. temporary:—dur-(eth)
 for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal.

G4341.definition:
†προσκαλέομαι proskaléomai, pros-kal-eh'-om-ahee; middle voice from G4314 and G2564; to call toward oneself, i.e. summon,
 invite:—call (for, to, unto).

G4342.definition:
προσκαρτερέω proskarteréō, pros-kar-ter-eh'-o; from G4314 and G2594; to be earnest towards, i.e. (to a thing) to
 persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend
 assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to
 (as a servitor):—attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in,
 instant in, with), wait on (continually).

G4343.definition: προσκαρτέρησις proskartérēsis, pros-kar-ter'-ay-sis; from G4342; persistancy:—perseverance.

G4344.definition:
προσκεφάλαιον proskephálaion, pros-kef-al'-ahee-on; neuter of a presumed compound of G4314 and G2776; something for the
 head, i.e. a cushion:—pillow.

G4345.definition:
προσκληρόω prosklēróō, pros-klay-ro'-o; from G4314 and G2820; to give a common lot to, i.e. (figuratively) to
 associate with:—consort with.

G4346.definition:
†πρόσκλισις prósklisis, pros'-klis-is; from a compound of G4314 and G2827; a leaning towards, i.e.
 (figuratively) proclivity (favoritism):—partiality.

G4347.definition:
†προσκολλάω proskolláō, pros-kol-lah'-o; from G4314 and G2853; to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to
 adhere:—cleave, join (self).

G4348.definition:
πρόσκομμα próskomma, pros'-kom-mah; from G4350; a stub, i.e. (figuratively) occasion of apostasy:—offence,
 stumbling(-block, (-stone)).

G4349.definition:
προσκοπή proskopḗ, pros-kop-ay'; from G4350; a stumbling, i.e. (figuratively and concretely) occasion of
 sin:—offence.

G435.definition:
ἀνήρ anḗr, an'-ayr; a primary word (compare G444); a man (properly as an individual
 male):—fellow, husband, man, sir.

G4351.definition: προσκυλίω proskylíō, pros-koo-lee'-o; from G4314 and G2947; to roll towards, i.e. block against:—roll (to).

G4352.definition:
προσκυνέω proskynéō, pros-koo-neh'-o; from G4314 and a probable derivative of G2965 (meaning to kiss, like a
 dog licking his master's hand); to fawn or crouch to, i.e. (literally
 or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to,
 adore):—worship.

G4353.definition: προσκυνητής proskynētḗs, pros-koo-nay-tace'; from G4352; an adorer:—worshipper.

G4354.definition: προσλαλέω proslaléō, pros-lal-eh'-o; from G4314 and G2980; to talk to, i.e. converse with:—speak to (with).

G4355.definition:
προσλαμβάνω proslambánō, pros-lam-ban'-o; from G4314 and G2983; to take to oneself, i.e. use (food), lead (aside),
 admit (to friendship or hospitality):—receive, take (unto).

G4357.definition:
προσμένω prosménō, pros-men'-o; from G4314 and G3306; to stay further, i.e. remain in a place, with a
 person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in:—abide still, be
 with, cleave unto, continue in (with).

G4358.definition:
προσορμίζω prosormízō, pros-or-mid'-zo; from G4314 and a derivative of the same as G3730 (meaning to tie
 (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at:—draw to
 the shore.

G4359.definition: προσοφείλω prosopheílō, pros-of-i'-lo; from G4314 and G3784; to be indebted additionally:—over besides.

G436.definition: ἀνθίστημι anthístēmi, anth-is'-tay-mee; from G473 and G2476; to stand against, i.e. oppose:—resist, withstand.

G4360.definition:
προσοχθίζω prosochthízō, pros-okh-thid'-zo; from G4314 and a form of ὀχθέω ochthéō (to be vexed with something irksome); 
 to feel indignant at:—be grieved at.

G4361.definition:
πρόσπεινος próspeinos, pros'-pi-nos; from G4314 and the same as G3983; hungering further, i.e. intensely
 hungry:—very hungry.

G4362.definition:
προσπήγνυμι prospḗgnymi, pros-payg'-noo-mee; from G4314 and G4078; to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a
 cross):—crucify.

G4363.definition:
προσπίπτω prospíptō, pros-pip'-to; from G4314 and G4098; to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself
 (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in
 storm):—beat upon, fall (down) at (before).

G4364.definition:
†προσποιέομαι prospoiéomai, pros-poy-eh'-om-ahee; middle voice from G4314 and G4160; to do forward for oneself, i.e.
 pretend (as if about to do a thing):—make as though.

G4365.definition:
προσπορεύομαι prosporeúomai, pros-por-yoo'-om-ahee; from G4314 and G4198; to journey towards, i.e. approach (not the same as
 G4313):—go before.

G4366.definition:
προσρήγνυμι prosrḗgnymi, pros-rayg'-noo-mee; from G4314 and G4486; to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or
 flood):—beat vehemently against (upon).

G4367.definition:
προστάσσω prostássō, pros-tas'-so; from G4314 and G5021; to arrange towards, i.e. (figuratively)
 enjoin:—bid, command.

G4368.definition:
προστάτις prostátis, pros-tat'-is; feminine of a derivative of G4291; a patroness, i.e.
 assistant:—succourer.

G4369.definition:
προστίθημι prostíthēmi, pros-tith'-ay-mee; from G4314 and G5087; to place additionally, i.e. lay beside, annex,
 repeat:—add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further,
 speak to any more.

G437.definition:
ἀνθομολογέομαι anthomologéomai, anth-om-ol-og-eh'-om-ahee; from G473 and the middle voice of G3670; to confess in turn, i.e.
 respond in praise:—give thanks.

G4370.definition:
προστρέχω prostréchō, pros-trekh'-o; from G4314 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run towards, i.e.
 hasten to meet or join:—run (thither to, to).

G4372.definition:
πρόσφατος prósphatos, pros'-fat-os; from G4253 and a derivative of G4969; previously (recently) slain
 (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made:—new.

G4373.definition: προσφάτως prosphátōs, pros-fat'-oce; adverb from G4372; recently:—lately.

G4374.definition:
προσφέρω prosphérō, pros-fer'-o; from G4314 and G5342 (including its alternate); to bear towards, i.e.
 lead to, tender (especially to God), treat:—bring (to, unto), deal
 with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to.

G4375.definition:
προσφιλής prosphilḗs, pros-fee-lace'; from a presumed compound of G4314 and G5368; friendly towards, i.e.
 acceptable:—lovely.

G4376.definition:
προσφορά prosphorá, pros-for-ah'; from G4374; presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or
 sacrifice:—offering (up).

G4377.definition:
προσφωνέω prosphōnéō, pros-fo-neh'-o; from G4314 and G5455; to sound towards, i.e. address, exclaim,
 summon:—call unto, speak (un-)to.

G4378.definition:
πρόσχυσις próschysis, pros'-khoo-sis; from a comparative of G4314 and χέω chéō (to pour); a shedding forth, i.e.
 affusion:—sprinkling.

G4379.definition:
προσψαύω prospsaúō, pros-psow'-o; from G4314 and ψαύω psaúō (to touch); to impinge, i.e. lay a finger on (in
 order to relieve):—touch.

G438.definition: ἄνθος ánthos, anth'-os; a primary word; a blossom:—flower.

G4380.definition:
†προσωποληπτέω prosōpolēptéō, pros-o-pol-ape-teh'-o; from G4381; to favor an individual, i.e. show partiality:—have respect
 to persons.

G4381.definition:
†προσωπολήπτης prosōpolḗptēs, pros-o-pol-ape'-tace; from G4383 and G2983; an accepter of a face (individual), i.e.
 (specially), one exhibiting partiality:—respecter of persons.

G4382.definition: †προσωποληψία prosōpolēpsía, pros-o-pol-ape-see'-ah; from G4381; partiality, i.e. favoritism:—respect of persons.

G4383.definition:
πρόσωπον prósōpon, pros'-o-pon; from G4314 and ὤψ ṓps (the visage, from G3700); the front (as being towards
 view), i.e. the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by
 implication, presence, person:—(outward) appearance, × before,
 countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence.

G4385.definition:
προτείνω proteínō, prot-i'-no; from G4253 and τείνω teínō (to stretch); to protend, i.e. tie prostrate (for
 scourging):—bind.

G4387.definition: πρότερος próteros, prot'-er-os; comparative of G4253; prior or previous:—former.

G4389.definition:
†προτρέπομαι protrépomai, prot-rep'-om-ahee; middle voice from G4253 and the base of G5157; to turn forward for
 oneself, i.e. encourage:—exhort.

G439.definition: ἀνθρακιά anthrakiá, anth-rak-ee-ah'; from G440; a bed of burning coals:—fire of coals.

G4390.definition:
προτρέχω protréchō, prot-rekh'-o; from G4253 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run forward, i.e.
 outstrip, precede:—outrun, run before.

G4391.definition:
προϋπάρχω proÿpárchō, pro-oop-ar'-kho; from G4253 and G5225; to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do
 something previously:—+ be before(-time).

G4392.definition:
πρόφασις próphasis, prof'-as-is; from a compound of G4253 and G5316; an outward showing, i.e.
 pretext:—cloke, colour, pretence, show.

G4393.definition: προφέρω prophérō, prof-er'-o; from G4253 and G5342; to bear forward, i.e. produce:—bring forth.

G4394.definition:
προφητεία prophēteía, prof-ay-ti'-ah; from G4396 ("prophecy"); prediction (scriptural or other):—prophecy,
 prophesying.

G4395.definition:
προφητεύω prophēteúō, prof-ate-yoo'-o; from G4396; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration,
 exercise the prophetic office:—prophesy.

G4396.definition:
προφήτης prophḗtēs, prof-ay'-tace; from a compound of G4253 and G5346; a foreteller ("prophet"); by
 analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet:—prophet.

G4397.definition:
προφητικός prophētikós, prof-ay-tik-os'; from G4396; pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic"):—of prophecy, of
 the prophets.

G4398.definition:
προφῆτις prophētis, prof-ay'-tis; feminine of G4396; a female foreteller or an inspired
 woman:—prophetess.

G4399.definition:
προφθάνω prophthánō, prof-than'-o; from G4253 and G5348; to get an earlier start of, i.e.
 anticipate:—prevent.

G44.definition: ἄγκιστρον ánkistron, ang'-kis-tron; from the same as G43; a hook (as bent):—hook.

G440.definition: ἄνθραξ ánthrax, anth'-rax; of uncertain derivation; a live coal:—coal of fire.

G4400.definition:
προχειρίζομαι procheirízomai, prokh-i-rid'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G4253 and a derivative of G5495; to handle for oneself
 in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose:—choose, make.

G4401.definition: προχειροτονέω procheirotonéō, prokh-i-rot-on-eh'-o; from G4253 and G5500; to elect in advance:—choose before.

G4402.definition:
Πρόχορος Próchoros, prokh'-or-os; from G4253 and G5525; before the dance; Prochorus, a
 Christian:—Prochorus.

G4403.definition:
πρύμνα prýmna, proom'-nah; feminine of πρυμνύς prymnýs (hindmost); the stern of a ship:—hinder part,
 stern.

G4404.definition:
πρωΐ prōḯ, pro-ee'; adverb from G4253; at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch:—early
 (in the morning), (in the) morning.

G4405.definition: πρωΐα prōḯa, pro-ee'-ah; feminine of a derivative of G4404 as noun; day-dawn:—early, morning.

G4407.definition: πρωϊνός prōïnós, pro-ee-nos'; from G4404; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal:—morning.

G4408.definition:
†πρῶρα prōra, pro'-ra; feminine of a presumed derivative of G4253 as noun; the prow, i.e.
 forward part of a vessel:—forepart(-ship).

G4409.definition: πρωτεύω prōteúō, prote-yoo'-o; from G4413; to be first (in rank or influence):—have the preeminence.

G441.definition: ἀνθρωπάρεσκος anthrōpáreskos, anth-ro-par'-es-kos; from G444 and G700; man-courting, i.e. fawning:—men-pleaser.

G4410.definition:
πρωτοκαθεδρία prōtokathedría, pro-tok-ath-ed-ree'-ah; from G4413 and G2515; a sitting first (in the front row), i.e.
 preeminence in council:—chief (highest, uppermost) seat.

G4411.definition:
πρωτοκλισία prōtoklisía, pro-tok-lis-ee'-ah; from G4413 and G2828; a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the
 dinner-bed, i.e. preeminence at meals:—chief (highest, uppermost)
 room.

G4413.definition:
†πρῶτος prōtos, pro'-tos; contracted superlative of G4253; foremost (in time, place, order or
 importance):—before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all),
 former.

G4414.definition:
πρωτοστάτης prōtostátēs, pro-tos-tat'-ace; from G4413 and G2476; one standing first in the ranks, i.e. a captain
 (champion):—ringleader.

G4415.definition: πρωτοτόκια prōtotókia, pro-tot-ok'-ee-ah; from G4416; primogeniture (as a privilege):—birthright.

G4416.definition:
πρωτότοκος prōtótokos, pro-tot-ok'-os; from G4413 and the alternate of G5088; first-born (usually as noun,
 literally or figuratively):—firstbegotten(-born).

G4417.definition:
πταίω ptaíō, ptah'-yo; a form of G4098; to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of
 salvation):—fall, offend, stumble.

G4418.definition: πτέρνα ptérna, pter'-nah; of uncertain derivation; the heel (figuratively):—heel.

G4419.definition:
πτερύγιον pterýgion, pter-oog'-ee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G4420; a winglet, i.e.
 (figuratively) extremity (top corner):—pinnacle.

G442.definition:
ἀνθρώπινος anthrṓpinos, anth-ro'-pee-nos; from G444; human:—human, common to man, man(-kind), (man-)kind, men's,
 after the manner of men.

G4420.definition: πτέρυξ ptéryx, pter'-oox; from a derivative of G4072 (meaning a feather); a wing:—wing.

G4421.definition: πτηνόν ptēnón, ptay-non'; contraction for G4071; a bird:—bird.

G4422.definition:
πτοέω ptoéō, pto-eh'-o; probably akin to the alternate of G4098 (through the idea of causing to
 fall) or to G4072 (through that of causing to fly away); to
 scare:—frighten.

G4423.definition: πτόησις ptóēsis, pto'-ay-sis; from G4422; alarm:—amazement.

G4424.definition:
Πτολεμαΐς Ptolemaḯs, ptol-em-ah-is'; from Πτολεμαῖος Ptolemaîos (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); Ptolemais, a place
 in Palestine:—Ptolemais.

G4425.definition: πτύον ptýon, ptoo'-on; from G4429; a winnowing-fork (as scattering like spittle):—fan.

G4426.definition:
πτύρω ptýrō, ptoo'-ro; from a presumed derivative of G4429 (and thus akin to G4422); to
 frighten:—terrify.

G4427.definition: πτύσμα ptýsma, ptoos'-mah; from G4429; saliva:—spittle.

G4428.definition:
πτύσσω ptýssō, ptoos'-so; probably akin to πετάννυμι petánnymi (to spread; and thus apparently allied to
 G4072 through the idea of expansion, and to 4429 through that of
 flattening; compare G3961); to fold, i.e. furl a scroll:—close.

G4429.definition: πτύω ptýō, ptoo'-o; a primary verb (compare G4428); to spit:—spit.

G443.definition: ἀνθρωποκτόνος anthrōpoktónos, anth-ro-pok-ton'-os; from G444 and κτείνω kteínō(to kill); a manslayer:—murderer. Compare G5406.

G4430.definition:
πτῶμα ptōma, pto'-mah; from the alternate of G4098; a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body
 (corpse, carrion):—dead body, carcase, corpse.

G4431.definition:
πτῶσις ptōsis, pto'-sis; from the alternate of G4098; a crash, i.e. downfall (literally or
 figuratively):—fall.

G4432.definition:
πτωχεία ptōcheía, pto-khi'-ah; from G4433; beggary, i.e. indigence (literally or
 figuratively):—poverty.

G4433.definition:
πτωχεύω ptōcheúō, pto-khyoo'-o; from G4434; to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent
 (figuratively):—become poor.

G4434.definition:
πτωχός ptōchós, pto-khos'; from πτώσσω ptṓssō (to crouch); akin to G4422 and the alternate of G4098); a
 beggar (as cringing), i.e. pauper (strictly denoting absolute or
 public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative
 sense; whereas G3993 properly means only straitened circumstances in
 private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively
 (distressed):—beggar(-ly), poor.

G4435.definition:
πυγμή pygmḗ, poog-may'; from a primary πύξ pýx (the fist as a weapon); the clenched hand, i.e.
 (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing):—oft.

G4436.definition:
Πύθων Pýthōn, poo'-thone; from Πυθώ Pythṓ (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the
 famous oracle, was located); a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the
 supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying):—divination.

G4437.definition:
πυκνός pyknós, pook-nos'; from the same as G4635; clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent;
 neuter plural (as adverb) frequently:—often(-er).

G4438.definition:
†πυκτέω pyktéō, pook-teh'-o; from a derivative of the same as G4435; to box (with the fist), i.e.
 contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively):—fight.

G4439.definition:
πύλη pýlē, poo'-lay; apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding
 entrance (literally or figuratively):—gate.

G444.definition:
ἄνθρωπος ánthrōpos, anth'-ro-pos; from G435 and ὤψ ṓps (the countenance; from G3700); man-faced, i.e. a human
 being:—certain, man.

G4440.definition:
πυλών pylṓn, poo-lone'; from G4439; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication,
 a portal or vestibule:—gate, porch.

G4441.definition:
πυνθάνομαι pynthánomai, poon-than'-om-ahee; middle voice prolonged from a primary πύθω pýthō (which occurs only as an
 alternate in certain tenses); to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry
 (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from G2065,
 which properly means a request as a favor; and from G154, which is
 strictly a demand for something due; as well as from G2212, which
 implies a search for something hidden; and from G1189, which involves
 the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual
 intelligence):—ask, demand, enquire, understand.

G4442.definition:
πῦρ pŷr, poor; a primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially,
 lightning):—fiery, fire.

G4443.definition: πυρά pyrá, poo-rah'; from G4442; a fire (concretely):—fire.

G4444.definition: πύργος pýrgos, poor'-gos; apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle:—tower.

G4445.definition:
πυρέσσω pyréssō, poo-res'-so; from G4443; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever:—be sick
 of a fever.

G4446.definition:
πυρετός pyretós, poo-ret-os'; from G4445; inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun,
 fever):—fever.

G4447.definition: πύρινος pýrinos, poo'-ree-nos; from G4443; fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming:—of fire.

G4448.definition:
πυρόω pyróō, poo-ro'-o; from G4442; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow
 (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be
 inflamed (with anger, grief, lust):—burn, fiery, be on fire, try.

G4449.definition: πυῤῥάζω pyrrházō, poor-hrad'-zo; from G4450; to redden (intransitively):—be red.

G4450.definition: †πυῤῥός pyrrhós, poor-hros'; from G4442; fire-like, i.e. (specially), flame- colored:—red.

G4451.definition:
πύρωσις pýrōsis, poo'-ro-sis; from G4448; ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively,
 conflagration, calamity as a test):—burning, trial.

G4453.definition:
πωλέω pōléō, po-leh'-o; probably ultimately from πέλομαι pélomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as
 a pedlar), i.e. to sell:—sell, whatever is sold.

G4454.definition:
πῶλος pōlos, po'-los; apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a
 young ass:—colt.

G4455.definition:
πώποτε pṓpote, po'-pot-e; from G4452 and G4218; at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no
 time:—at any time, + never (…to any man),
 + yet, never man.

G4456.definition:
πωρόω pōróō, po-ro'-o; apparently from πῶρος pōros (a kind of stone); to petrify, i.e.
 (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous):—blind,
 harden.

G4457.definition: πώρωσις pṓrōsis, po'-ro-sis; from G4456; stupidity or callousness:—blindness, hardness.

G4458.definition:
-πώς -pṓs, poce; adverb from the base of G4225; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness
 of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition:—haply, by any
 (some) means, perhaps. See G1513, G3381. Compare G4459.

G4459.definition:
πῶς pōs, poce; adverb from the base of G4226; an interrogative particle of manner; in
 what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as
 exclamation, how much!:—how, after (by) what manner (means), that. 
 (Occasionally unexpressed in English).

G446.definition:
ἀνθύπατος anthýpatos, anth-oo'-pat-os; from G473 and a superlative of G5228; instead of the highest officer,
 i.e. (specially) a Roman proconsul:—deputy.

G4460.definition: Ῥαάβ Rhaáb, hrah-ab'; of Hebrew origin (H7343); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess:—Rahab. See also H4477.

G4461.definition:
ῥαββί rhabbí, hrab-bee'; of Hebrew origin (H7227 with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi,
 as an official title of honor:—Master, Rabbi.

G4462.definition: ῥαββονί rhabboní, hrab-bon-ee'; of Chaldee origin; corresponding to G4461:—Lord, Rabboni.

G4463.definition: ῥαβδίζω rhabdízō, hrab-did'-zo; from G4464; to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado:—beat (with rods).

G4464.definition:
ῥάβδος rhábdos, hrab'-dos; from the base of G4474; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton
 of royalty):—rod, sceptre, staff.

G4465.definition:
ῥαβδοῦχος rhabdoûchos, hrab-doo'-khos; from G4464 and G2192; a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman
 lictor (constable or executioner):—serjeant.

G4466.definition: †Ῥαγαῦ Rhagaû, hrag-ow'; of Hebrew origin (H7466); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch:—Ragau.

G4467.definition:
ῥᾳδιούργημα rhaidioúrgēma, hrad-ee-oorg'-ay-mah; from a comparative of ῥᾴδιος rháidios (easy, i.e. reckless) and G2041; 
 easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime:—lewdness.

G4468.definition:
ῥᾳδιουργία rhaidiourgía, hrad-ee-oorg-ee'-a; from the same as G4467; recklessness, i.e. (by extension)
 malignity:—mischief.

G4469.definition:
ῥακά rhaká, rhak-ah'; of Chaldee origin (compare H7386); O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as
 a term of utter vilification):—Raca.

G447.definition:
ἀνίημι aníēmi, an-ee'-ay-mee; from G303 and ἵημι híēmi (to send); to let up, i.e. (literally) slacken or
 (figuratively) desert, desist from:—forbear, leave, loose.

G4470.definition: ῥάκος rhákos, hrak'-os; from G4486; a "rag," i.e. piece of cloth:—cloth.

G4471.definition:
Ῥαμᾶ Rhamâ, hram-ah'; of Hebrew origin (H7414); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in
 Palestine:—Rama.

G4472.definition:
ῥαντίζω rhantízō, hran-tid'-zo; from a derivative of ῥαίνω rhaínō (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, i.e.
 asperse (ceremonially or figuratively):—sprinkle.

G4473.definition: ῥαντισμός rhantismós, hran-tis-mos'; from G4472; aspersion (ceremonially or figuratively):—sprinkling.

G4474.definition:
ῥαπίζω rhapízō, hrap-id'-zo; from a derivative of a primary ῥέπω rhépō (to let fall, "rap"); to
 slap:—smite (with the palm of the hand). Compare G5180.

G4475.definition:
ῥάπισμα rhápisma, hrap'-is-mah; from G4474; a slap:—(+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with
 the hand.

G4476.definition:
†ῥαφίς rhaphís, hraf-ece'; from a primary ῥάπτω rháptō (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474
 through the idea of puncturing); a needle:—needle.

G4477.definition: Ῥαχάβ Rhacháb, hrakh-ab'; from the same as G4460; Rachab, a Canaanitess:—Rachab.

G4478.definition: Ῥαχήλ Rhachḗl, hrakh-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H7354); Rachel, the wife of Jacob:—Rachel.

G4479.definition:
Ῥεβέκκα Rhebékka, hreb-bek'-kah; of Hebrew origin (H7259); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of
 Isaac:—Rebecca.

G4480.definition:
†ῥέδα rhéda, hred'-ah; of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for
 riding):—chariot.

G4482.definition:
ῥέω rhéō, hreh'-o; a primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form
    ῥεύω rheúō  hryoo'-o is used

 to flow ("run"; as water):—flow.

G4484.definition: Ῥήγιον Rhḗgion, hrayg'-ee-on; of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy:—Rhegium.

G4485.definition:
ῥῆγμα rhēgma, hrayg'-mah; from G4486; something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and
 abstractly, a fall):—ruin.

G4486.definition:
ῥήγνυμι rhḗgnymi, hrayg'-noo-mee; both prolonged forms of ῥήκω rhḗkō (which appears only in certain forms,
 and is itself probably a strengthened form of ἄγνυμι ágnymi (see in G2608)) to
 "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by
 separation of the parts; G2608 being its intensive (with the
 preposition in composition), and G2352 a shattering to minute
 fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like
 G3089) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms);
 figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions:—break (forth), burst,
 rend, tear.

G4487.definition:
ῥῆμα rhēma, hray'-mah; from G4483; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by
 implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or
 dispute); with a negative naught whatever:—+ evil, + nothing, saying,
 word.

G4488.definition:
Ῥησά Rhēsá, hray-sah'; probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for H7509); Resa (i.e. Rephajah),
 an Israelite:—Rhesa.

G4489.definition:
ῥήτωρ rhḗtōr, hray'-tore; from G4483; a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic
 advocate:—orator.

G449.definition:
ἄνιπτος ániptos, an'-ip-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3538; 
 without ablution:—unwashen.

G4490.definition:
ῥητῶς rhētōs, hray-toce'; adverb from a derivative of G4483; out-spokenly, i.e.
 distinctly:—expressly.

G4491.definition:
ῥίζα rhíza, hrid'-zah; apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or
 figuratively):—root.

G4492.definition: ῥιζόω rhizóō, hrid-zo'-o; from G4491; to root (figuratively, become stable):—root.

G4493.definition:
ῥιπή rhipḗ, hree-pay'; from G4496; a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an
 instant):—twinkling.

G4494.definition:
ῥιπίζω rhipízō, hrip-id'-zo; from a derivative of G4496 (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up,
 i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves):—toss.

G4496.definition:
ῥίπτω rhíptō, hrip'-to; a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474, through the
 idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus
 differing from G906, which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from τείνω teínō
 (see in G1614), which indicates an extended projection); by
 qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to
 disperse:—cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw.

G4497.definition:
Ῥοβοάμ Rhoboám, hrob-o-am'; of Hebrew origin (H7346); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an
 Israelite:—Roboam.

G4498.definition: Ῥόδη Rhódē, hrod'-ay; probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl:—Rhoda.

G4499.definition:
Ῥόδος Rhódos, hrod'-os; probably from ῥόδον rhódon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the
 Mediterranean:—Rhodes.

G45.definition: ἄγκυρα ánkyra, ang'-koo-rah; from the same as G43; an "anchor" (as crooked):—anchor.

G450.definition:
†ἀνίστημι anístēmi, an-is'-tay-mee; from G303 and G2476; to stand up (literal or figurative, transitive or
 intransitive):—arise, lift up, raise up (again), rise (again), stand
 up(-right).

G4500.definition:
ῥοιζηδόν rhoizēdón, hroyd-zay-don'; adverb from a derivative of ῥοῖζος rhoîzos (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a
 crash:—with a great noise.

G4501.definition:
ῥομφαία rhomphaía, hrom-fah'-yah; probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass
 (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively):—sword.

G4502.definition: Ῥουβήν Rhoubḗn, hroo-bane'; of Hebrew origin (H7205); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite:—Reuben.

G4503.definition: Ῥούθ Rhoúth, hrooth; of Hebrew origin (H7327); Ruth, a Moabitess:—Ruth.

G4504.definition: Ῥοῦφος Rhoûphos, hroo'-fos; of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian:—Rufus.

G4505.definition:
ῥύμη rhýmē, hroo'-may; prolongation from G4506 in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as
 crowded):—lane, street.

G4506.definition:
ῥύομαι rhýomai, rhoo'-om-ahee; middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to G4482 (through the idea of a
 current; compare G4511); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e.
 rescue:—deliver(-er).

G4507.definition: ῥυπαρία rhyparía, hroo-par-ee'-ah; from G4508; dirtiness (morally):—turpitude.

G4508.definition:
ῥυπαρός rhyparós, rhoo-par-os'; from G4509; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally,
 wicked:—vile.

G4509.definition: ῥύπος rhýpos, hroo'-pos; of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity:—filth.

G451.definition: Ἄννα Ánna, an'-nah; of Hebrew origin (H2584); Anna, an Israelitess:—Anna.

G4511.definition:
ῥύσις rhýsis, hroo'-sis; from G4506 in the sense of its congener G4482; a flux (of
 blood):—issue.

G4512.definition:
ῥυτίς rhytís, hroo-tece'; from G4506; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on
 the face):—wrinkle.

G4514.definition: Ῥωμαῖος Rhōmaîos, hro-mah'-yos; from G4516; Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun):—Roman, of Rome.

G4515.definition:
Ῥωμαϊστί Rhōmaïstí, hro-mah-is-tee'; adverb from a presumed derivative of G4516; Romaistically, i.e. in the
 Latin language:—Latin.

G4516.definition: Ῥώμη Rhṓmē, hro'-may; from the base of G4517; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy:—Rome.

G4517.definition:
ῥώννυμι rhṓnnymi, hrone'-noo-mee; prolongation from ῥώομαι rhṓomai (to dart; probably akin to G4506); to
 strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting
 exclamation, good-bye):—farewell.

G4518.definition:
σαβαχθάνι sabachtháni, sab-akh-than-ee'; of Chaldee or (H7662 with pronominal suffix); thou hast left me;
 sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress:—sabachthani.

G4519.definition:
σαβαώθ sabaṓth, sab-ah-owth'; of Hebrew origin (H6635 in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e.
 tsebaoth), a military epithet of God:—sabaoth.

G452.definition: Ἄννας Ánnas, an'-nas; of Hebrew origin (H2608); Annas (i.e. G367), an Israelite:—Annas.

G4520.definition:
σαββατισμός sabbatismós, sab-bat-is-mos'; from a derivative of G4521; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the
 repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven):—rest.

G4521.definition:
σάββατον sábbaton, sab'-bat-on; of Hebrew origin (H7676); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly
 repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution
 itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two
 Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications:—sabbath
 (day), week.

G4522.definition:
σαγήνη sagḗnē, sag-ay'-nay; from a derivative of σάττω sáttō (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a
 pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a
 "seine" for fishing:—net.

G4523.definition:
Σαδδουκαῖος Saddoukaîos, sad-doo-kah'-yos; probably from G4524; a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a
 certain heretical Israelite:—Sadducee.

G4524.definition: Σαδώκ Sadṓk, sad-oke'; of Hebrew origin (H6659); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite:—Sadoc.

G4525.definition:
σαίνω saínō, sah'-ee-no; akin to G4579; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally)
 to shake (figuratively, disturb):—move.

G4526.definition:
σάκκος sákkos, sak'-kos; of Hebrew origin (H8242); "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or
 garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief):—sackcloth.

G4527.definition: Σαλά Salá, sal-ah'; of Hebrew origin (H7974); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch:—Sala.

G4528.definition:
Σαλαθιήλ Salathiḗl, sal-ath-ee-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H7597); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an
 Israelite:—Salathiel.

G4529.definition:
Σαλαμίς Salamís, sal-am-ece'; probably from G4535 (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in
 Cyprus:—Salamis.

G453.definition:
ἀνόητος anóētos, an-o'-ay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3539; 
 unintelligent; by implication, sensual:—fool(-ish), unwise.

G4530.definition: Σαλείμ Saleím, sal-ime'; probably from the same as G4531; Salim, a place in Palestine:—Salim.

G4531.definition:
σαλεύω saleúō, sal-yoo'-o; from G4535; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication)
 destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite:—move, shake (together),
 which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.

G4532.definition:
Σαλήμ Salḗm, sal-ame'; of Hebrew origin (H8004); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in
 Palestine:—Salem.

G4533.definition: Σαλμών Salmṓn, sal-mone'; of Hebrew origin (H8012); Salmon, an Israelite:—Salmon.

G4534.definition:
Σαλμώνη Salmṓnē, sal-mo'-nay; perhaps of similar origin to G4529; Salmone, a place in
 Crete:—Salmone.

G4535.definition:
σάλος sálos, sal'-os; probably from the base of G4525; a vibration, i.e. (specially),
 billow:—wave.

G4536.definition:
σάλπιγξ sálpinx, sal'-pinx; perhaps from G4535 (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a
 trumpet:—trump(-et).

G4537.definition:
σαλπίζω salpízō, sal-pid'-zo; from G4536; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or
 figuratively):—(which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).

G4538.definition: σαλπιστής salpistḗs, sal-pis-tace'; from G4537; a trumpeter:—trumpeter.

G4539.definition:
Σαλώμη Salṓmē, sal-o'-may; probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from H7965); Salome (i.e.
 Shelomah), an Israelitess:—Salome.

G454.definition:
ἄνοια ánoia, an'-oy-ah; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and G3563; stupidity; by
 implication, rage:—folly, madness.

G4540.definition:
Σαμάρεια Samáreia, sam-ar'-i-ah; of Hebrew origin (H8111); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of
 Palestine:—Samaria.

G4541.definition: †Σαμαρείτης Samareítēs, sam-ar-i'-tace; from G4540; a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria:—Samaritan.

G4542.definition: †Σαμαρεῖτις Samareîtis, sam-ar-i'-tis; feminine of G4541; a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria:—of Samaria.

G4543.definition:
Σαμοθρᾴκη Samothráikē, sam-oth-rak'-ay; from G4544 and Θτρᾴκη Thtráikē (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an
 island in the Mediterranean:—Samothracia.

G4544.definition: Σάμος Sámos, sam'-os; of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean:—Samos.

G4545.definition: Σαμουήλ Samouḗl, sam-oo-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H8050); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite:—Samuel.

G4546.definition:
Σαμψών Sampsṓn, samp-sone'; of Hebrew origin (H8123); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an
 Israelite:—Samson.

G4547.definition:
σανδάλιον sandálion, san-dal'-ee-on; neuter of a derivative of σάνδαλον sándalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin);
 a slipper or sole-pad:—sandal.

G4548.definition: σανίς sanís, san-ece'; of uncertain affinity; a plank:—board.

G4549.definition:
Σαούλ Saoúl, sah-ool'; of Hebrew origin (H7586); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of
 Paul:—Saul. Compare G4569.

G455.definition:
ἀνοίγω anoígō, an-oy'-go; from G303 and οἴγω oígō (to open); to open up (literally or figuratively, in
 various applications):—open.

G4550.definition:
σαπρός saprós, sap-ros'; from G4595; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally):—bad,
 corrupt. Compare G4190.

G4551.definition: †Σαπφείρη Sappheírē, sap-fi'-ray; feminine of G4552; Sapphire, an Israelitess:—Sapphira.

G4552.definition: †σάπφειρος sáppheiros, sap'-fi-ros; of Hebrew origin (H5601); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem:—sapphire.

G4553.definition:
σαργάνη sargánē, sar-gan'-ay; apparently of Hebrew origin (H8276); a basket (as interwoven or
 wicker-work:—basket.

G4554.definition:
Σάρδεις Sárdeis, sar'-dice; plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia
 Minor:—Sardis.

G4556.definition:
†σάρδιος sárdios, sar'-dee-os; properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (3037 being
 implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called:—sardius.

G4557.definition:
σαρδόνυξ sardónyx, sar-don'-oox; from the base of G4556 and ὄνυξ ónyx (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx"
 stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called:—sardonyx.

G4558.definition:
Σάρεπτα Sárepta, sar'-ep-tah; of Hebrew origin (H6886); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in
 Palestine:—Sarepta.

G4559.definition:
σαρκικός sarkikós, sar-kee-kos'; from G4561; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal,
 or (by implication) animal, unregenerate:—carnal, fleshly.

G456.definition: ἀνοικοδομέω anoikodoméō, an-oy-kod-om-eh'-o; from G303 and G3618; to rebuild:—build again.

G4560.definition: σάρκινος sárkinos, sar'-kee-nos; from G4561; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft:—fleshly.

G4561.definition:
σάρξ sárx, sarx; probably from the base of G4563; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e.
 (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body
 (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is
 external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human
 nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or
 (specially), a human being (as such):—carnal(-ly, + -ly minded),
 flesh(-ly).

G4562.definition: †Σαρούχ Saroúch, sar-ooch'; of Hebrew origin (H8286); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch:—Saruch.

G4563.definition:
σαρόω saróō, sar-o'-o; from a derivative of σαίρω saírō (to brush off; akin to G4951); meaning a
 broom; to sweep:—sweep.

G4564.definition:
Σάῤῥα Sárrha, sar'-hrah; of Hebrew origin (H8283); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of
 Abraham:—Sara, Sarah.

G4565.definition:
†Σάρων Sárōn, sar'-one; of Hebrew origin (H8289); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of
 Palestine:—Saron.

G4567.definition:
Σατανᾶς Satanâs, sat-an-as'; of Chaldee origin corresponding to H4566 (with the definite affix); the
 accuser, i.e. the devil:—Satan.

G4568.definition: σάτον sáton, sat'-on; of Hebrew origin (H5429); a certain measure for things dry:—measure.

G4569.definition:
Σαῦλος Saûlos, sow'-los; of Hebrew origin, the same as G4549; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish
 name of Paul:—Saul.

G457.definition: ἄνοιξις ánoixis, an'-oix-is; from G455; opening (throat):—X open.

G4570.definition:
σβέννυμι sbénnymi, sben'-noo-mee; a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish
 (literally or figuratively):—go out, quench.

G4572.definition:
σεαυτοῦ seautoû, seh-ow-too'; genitive case from G4571 and G846,
               also dative case of the same,
    σεαυτῷ seautōi  seh-ow-to', and accusative case
    σεαυτόν seautón  seh-ow-ton', likewise contracted
    σαυτοῦ sautoû  sow-too',
    σαυτῷ sautōi  sow-to',   and
    σαυτόν sautón  sow-ton',  respectively; 

 of (with, to) thyself:—thee, thine own self, (thou) thy(-self).

G4573.definition:
σεβάζομαι sebázomai, seb-ad'-zom-ahee; middle voice from a derivative of G4576; to venerate, i.e.
 adore:—worship.

G4574.definition:
σέβασμα sébasma, seb'-as-mah; from G4573; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar,
 etc):—devotion, that is worshipped.

G4575.definition:
σεβαστός sebastós, seb-as-tos'; from G4573; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman
 Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial:—Augustus(-').

G4576.definition:
σέβομαι sébomai, seb'-om-ahee; middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e.
 adore:—devout, religious, worship.

G4577.definition:
†σειρά seirá, si-rah'; probably from G4951 through its congener εἴρω eírō (to fasten; akin to G138);
 a chain (as binding or drawing):—chain.

G4578.definition:
σεισμός seismós, sice-mos'; from G4579; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an
 earthquake:—earthquake, tempest.

G4579.definition:
σείω seíō, si'-o; apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to
 and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to
 tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or
 concern):—move, quake, shake.

G458.definition:
ἀνομία anomía, an-om-ee'-ah; from G459; illegality, i.e. violation of law or (genitive case)
 wickedness:—iniquity, × transgress(-ion of) the law, unrighteousness.

G4580.definition: Σεκοῦνδος Sekoûndos, sek-oon'-dos; of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian:—Secundus.

G4581.definition:
Σελεύκεια Seleúkeia, sel-yook'-i-ah; from Σέλευκος Séleukos (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in
 Syria:—Seleucia.

G4582.definition:
σελήνη selḗnē, sel-ay'-nay; from σέλας sélas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of G138, through
 the idea of attractiveness); the moon:—moon.

G4583.definition:
σεληνιάζομαι selēniázomai, sel-ay-nee-ad'-zom-ahee; middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of G4582; to be
 moon-struck, i.e. crazy:—be a lunatic.

G4584.definition: †Σεμεΐ Semeḯ, sem-eh-ee'; of Hebrew origin (H8096); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite:—Semei.

G4585.definition: σεμίδαλις semídalis, sem-id'-al-is; probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour:—fine flour.

G4586.definition: σεμνός semnós, sem-nos'; from G4576; venerable, i.e. honorable:—grave, honest.

G4587.definition: σεμνότης semnótēs, sem-not'-ace; from G4586; venerableness, i.e. probity:—gravity, honesty.

G4588.definition: Σέργιος Sérgios, serg'-ee-os; of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman:—Sergius.

G4589.definition: Σήθ Sḗth, sayth; of Hebrew origin (H8352); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch:—Seth.

G459.definition:
ἄνομος ánomos, an'-om-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3551; lawless, i.e. (negatively)
 not subject to (the Jewish) law; (by implication, a Gentile), or
 (positively) wicked:—without law, lawless, transgressor, unlawful,
 wicked.

G4590.definition: Σήμ Sḗm, same; of Hebrew origin (H8035); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch:—Sem.

G4591.definition: σημαίνω sēmaínō, say-mah'-ee-no; from σῆμα sēma (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate:—signify.

G4592.definition:
σημεῖον sēmeîon, say-mi'-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4591; an indication,
 especially ceremonially or supernaturally:—miracle, sign, token,
 wonder.

G4593.definition: σημειόω sēmeióō, say-mi-o'-o; from G4592; to distinguish, i.e. mark (for avoidance):—note.

G4594.definition:
σήμερον sḗmeron, say'-mer-on; neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article G3588 (t
 changed to s) and G2250; on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or
 just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto):—this
 (to-)day.

G4595.definition:
σήπω sḗpō, say'-po; apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish:—be
 corrupted.

G4597.definition: σής sḗs, sace; apparently of Hebrew origin (H5580); a moth:—moth.

G4598.definition: σητόβρωτος sētóbrōtos, say-tob'-ro-tos; from G4597 and a derivative of G977; moth-eaten:—motheaten.

G4599.definition:
σθενόω sthenóō, sthen-o'-o; from σθένος sthénos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of G2476); to
 strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and
 power):—strengthen.

G46.definition:
ἄγναφος ágnaphos, ag'-naf-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and the same as G1102; properly,
 unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth):—new.

G460.definition:
ἀνόμως anómōs, an-om'-oce; adverb from G459; lawlessly, i.e. (specially) not amenable to (the
 Jewish) law:—without law.

G4600.definition:
σιαγών siagṓn, see-ag-one'; of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek
 or side of the face:—cheek.

G4601.definition:
σιγάω sigáō, see-gah'-o; from G4602; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively):—keep
 close (secret, silence), hold peace.

G4602.definition:
σιγή sigḗ, see-gay'; apparently from σίζω sízō (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush); silence:—silence. 
 Compare G4623.

G4604.definition: σίδηρος sídēros, sid'-ay-ros; of uncertain derivation; iron:—iron.

G4605.definition:
Σιδών Sidṓn, sid-one'; of Hebrew origin (H6721); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in
 Palestine:—Sidon.

G4606.definition: †Σιδώνιος Sidṓnios, sid-o'-nee-os; from G4605; a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon:—of Sidon.

G4607.definition:
σικάριος sikários, sik-ar'-ee-os; of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish
 fanatic outlawed by the Romans):—murderer. Compare G5406.

G4608.definition:
σίκερα síkera, sik'-er-ah; of Hebrew origin (H7941); an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented
 liquor:—strong drink.

G4609.definition: †Σίλας Sílas, see'-las; contraction for G4610; Silas, a Christian:—Silas.

G461.definition:
ἀνορθόω anorthóō, an-orth-o'-o; from G303 and a derivative of the base of G3717; to straighten up:—lift
 (set) up, make straight.

G4610.definition:
Σιλουανός Silouanós, sil-oo-an-os'; of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian:—Silvanus. Compare
 G4609.

G4611.definition:
Σιλωάμ Silōám, sil-o-am'; of Hebrew origin (H7975); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of
 Jerusalem:—Siloam.

G4612.definition:
σιμικίνθιον simikínthion, sim-ee-kin'-thee-on; of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering
 (apron):—apron.

G4613.definition:
Σίμων Símōn, see'-mone; of Hebrew origin (H8095); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine
 Israelites:—Simon. Compare G4826.

G4614.definition:
Σινᾶ Sinâ, see-nah'; of Hebrew origin (H5514); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in
 Arabia:—Sina.

G4615.definition:
σίναπι sínapi, sin'-ap-ee; perhaps from σίνομαι sínomai (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the
 plant):—mustard.

G4616.definition:
σινδών sindṓn, sin-done'; of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. bleached linen
 (the cloth or a garment of it):—(fine) linen (cloth).

G4617.definition: σινιάζω siniázō, sin-ee-ad'-zo; from σινίον siníon (a sieve); to riddle (figuratively):—sift.

G4618.definition: σιτευτός siteutós, sit-yoo-ros'; from a derivative of G4621; grain-fed, i.e. fattened:—fatted.

G4619.definition: σιτιστός sitistós, sit-is-tos'; from a derivative of G4621; grained, i.e. fatted:—fatling.

G462.definition: ἀνόσιος anósios, an-os'-ee-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3741; wicked:—unholy.

G4620.definition:
†σιτόμετρον sitómetron, sit-om'-et-ron; from G4621 and G3358; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration
 (allowance of food):—portion of meat.

G4621.definition: †σῖτος sîtos, see'-tos; of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat:—corn, wheat.

G4622.definition:
Σιών Siṓn, see-own'; of Hebrew origin (H6726); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem;
 figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant):—Sion.

G4623.definition: σιωπάω siōpáō, see-o-pah'-o; from σιωπή siōpḗ (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from G4602, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like G2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water):—dumb, (hold) peace.

G4624.definition:
σκανδαλίζω skandalízō, skan-dal-id'-zo; from G4625; to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble
 (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure):—(make to)
 offend.

G4625.definition:
σκάνδαλον skándalon, skan'-dal-on; ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of G2578; a trap-stick (bent
 sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or
 sin):—occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends,
 stumblingblock.

G4626.definition: σκάπτω skáptō, skap'-to; apparently a primary verb; to dig:—dig.

G4627.definition:
σκάφη skáphē, skaf'-ay; a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for
 landing):—boat.

G4628.definition:
σκέλος skélos, skel'-os; apparently from σκέλλω skéllō (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the
 leg (as lank):—leg.

G4629.definition:
σκέπασμα sképasma, skep'-as-mah; from a derivative of σκέπας sképas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of
 G4649 through the idea of noticeableness); clothing:—raiment.

G463.definition: ἀνοχή anochḗ, an-okh-ay'; from G430; self-restraint, i.e. tolerance:—forbearance.

G4630.definition:
Σκευᾶς Skeuâs, skyoo-as'; apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an
 Israelite:—Sceva.

G4631.definition: σκευή skeuḗ, skyoo-ay'; from G4632; furniture, i.e. spare tackle:—tackling.

G4632.definition:
σκεῦος skeûos, skyoo'-os; of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus
 (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the
 usefulness of the husband]):—goods, sail, stuff, vessel.

G4633.definition:
σκηνή skēnḗ, skay-nay'; apparently akin to G4632 and G4639; a tent or cloth hut (literally or
 figuratively):—habitation, tabernacle.

G4634.definition:
σκηνοπηγία skēnopēgía, skay-nop-ayg-ee'-ah; from G4636 and G4078; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the
 custom of erecting booths for temporary homes):—tabernacles.

G4635.definition: σκηνοποιός skēnopoiós, skay-nop-oy-os'; from G4633 and G4160; a manufacturer of tents:—tent-maker.

G4636.definition:
σκῆνος skēnos, skay'-nos; from G4633; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human
 body (as the abode of the spirit):—tabernacle.

G4637.definition:
σκηνόω skēnóō, skay-no'-o; from G4636; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a
 mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of
 old, a symbol of protection and communion):—dwell.

G4638.definition:
σκήνωμα skḗnōma, skay'-no-mah; from G4637; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's
 residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul):—tabernacle.

G4639.definition:
σκιά skiá, skee'-ah; apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or
 figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)):—shadow.

G464.definition:
ἀνταγωνίζομαι antagōnízomai, an-tag-o-nid'-zom-ahee; from G473 and G75; to struggle against (figuratively)
 ("antagonize"):—strive against.

G4640.definition:
σκιρτάω skirtáō, skeer-tah'-o; akin to σκαίρω skaírō (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the
 quickening of a fetus):—leap (for joy).

G4641.definition:
