τολμάω tolmáō, tol-mah'-o; from τόλμα tólma (boldness; probably itself from the base of G5056 through
 the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while
 G2292 is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be
 courageous:—be bold, boldly, dare, durst.

G5112.definition: †τολμηρότερον tolmēróteron, tol-may-rot'-er-on; neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of G5111 (as adverb); more daringly, i.e. with greater confidence than otherwise:—the more boldly.

G5113.definition: τολμητής tolmētḗs, tol-may-tace'; from G5111; a daring (audacious) man:—presumptuous.

G5114.definition:
τομώτερος tomṓteros, tom-o'-ter-os; comparative of a derivative of the primary τέμνω témnō (to cut; more
 comprehensive or decisive than G2875, as if by a single stroke; whereas
 that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen:—sharper.

G5115.definition:
τόξον tóxon, tox'-on; from the base of G5088; a bow (apparently as the simplest
 fabric):—bow.

G5116.definition:
τοπάζιον topázion, top-ad'-zee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of τόπαζος tópazos (a "topaz"; 
 of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite:—topaz.

G5117.definition:
τόπος tópos, top'-os; apparently a primary word; a spot (general in space, but limited by
 occupancy; whereas G5561 is a large but participle locality), i.e.
 location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition,
 opportunity; specially, a scabbard:—coast, licence, place, × plain,
 quarter, + rock, room, where.

G5118.definition:
τοσοῦτος tosoûtos, tos-oo'-tos; from τόσος tósos (so much; apparently from G3588 and G3739) and G3778
 (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. such (in quantity,
 amount, number of space):—as large, so great (long, many, much),
 these many.

G5119.definition:
τότε tóte, tot'-eh; from (the neuter of) G3588 and G3753; the when, i.e. at the time that
 (of the past or future, also in consecution):—that time, then.

G512.definition:
†ἀνωφελής anōphelḗs, an-o-fel'-ace; from G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G5624; useless or
 (neuter) inutility:—unprofitable(-ness).

G5121.definition:
τοὐναντίον tounantíon, too-nan-tee'-on; contraction for the neuter of G3588 and G1726; on the
 contrary:—contrariwise.

G5122.definition: τοὔνομα toúnoma, too'-no-mah; contraction for the neuter of G3588 and G3686; the name (is):—named.

G5123.definition: τουτέστι toutésti, toot-es'-tee; contraction for G5124 and G2076; that is:—that is (to say).

G5124.definition:
τοῦτο toûto, too'-to; neuter singular nominative or accusative case of G3778; that
 thing:—here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the
 same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore).

G5126.definition:
τοῦτον toûton, too'-ton; accusative case singular masculine of G3778; this (person, as objective
 of verb or preposition):—him, the same, that, this.

G5128.definition:
τούτους toútous, too'-tooce; accusative case plural masculine of G3778; these (persons, as objective
 of verb or preposition):—such, them, these, this.

G513.definition: ἀξίνη axínē, ax-ee'-nay; probably from ἄγνυμι ágnymi (to break; compare G4486); an axe:—axe.

G5131.definition: τράγος trágos, trag'-os; from the base of G5176; a he-goat (as a gnawer):—goat.

G5132.definition:
τράπεζα trápeza, trap'-ed-zah; probably contracted from G5064 and G3979; a table or stool (as being
 four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter
 for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at
 interest):—bank, meat, table.

G5133.definition: τραπεζίτης trapezítēs, trap-ed-zee'-tace; from G5132; a money-broker or banker:—exchanger.

G5134.definition:
τραῦμα traûma, trow'-mah; from the base of τιτρώσκω titrṓskō (to wound; akin to the base of G2352, G5147,
 G5149, etc.); a wound:—wound.

G5135.definition: τραυματίζω traumatízō, trow-mat-id'-zo; from G5134; to inflict a wound:—wound.

G5136.definition:
τραχηλίζω trachēlízō, trakh-ay-lid'-zo; from G5137; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet
 of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare):—opened.

G5137.definition:
τράχηλος tráchēlos, trakh'-ay-los; probably from G5143 (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck),
 i.e. (figuratively) life:—neck.

G5138.definition:
τραχύς trachýs, trakh-oos'; perhaps strengthened from the base of G4486 (as if jagged by rents); 
 uneven, rocky (reefy):—rock, rough.

G5139.definition:
Τραχωνῖτις Trachōnîtis, trakh-o-nee'-tis; from a derivative of G5138; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of
 Syria:—Trachonitis.

G514.definition:
ἄξιος áxios, ax'-ee-os; probably from G71; deserving, comparable or suitable (as if drawing
 praise):—due reward, meet, (un-)worthy.

G5140.definition: τρεῖς treîs, trice; a primary (plural) number; "three":—three.

G5141.definition:
τρέμω trémō, trem'-o; strengthened from a primary τρέω tréō (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble"
 or fear:—be afraid, trembling.

G5142.definition:
τρέφω tréphō, tref'-o; a primary verb (properly, τρέφω tréphō; but perhaps strengthened from the
 base of G5157 through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen,
 i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper,
 rear):—bring up, feed, nourish.

G5144.definition: τριάκοντα triákonta, tree-ak'-on-tah; the decade of G5140; thirty:—thirty.

G5145.definition: τριακόσιοι triakósioi, tree-ak-os'-ee-oy; plural from G5140 and G1540; three hundred:—three hundred.

G5146.definition:
τρίβολος tríbolos, trib'-ol-os; from G5140 and G956; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in
 war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop):—brier, thistle.

G5147.definition:
τρίβος tríbos, tree'-bos; from τρίβω tríbō (to "rub"; akin to τείρω teírō, τρύω trýō, and the base of G5131,
 G5134); a rut or worn track:—path.

G5148.definition:
τριετία trietía, tree-et-ee'-ah; from a compound of G5140 and G2094; a three years' period
 (triennium):—space of three years.

G5149.definition:
τρίζω trízō, trid'-zo; apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to
 grate the teeth (in frenzy):—gnash.

G515.definition:
ἀξιόω axióō, ax-ee-o'-o; from G514; to deem entitled or fit:—desire, think good, count (think)
 worthy.

G5150.definition:
†τρίμηνον trímēnon, trim'-ay-non; neuter of a compound of G5140 and G3376 as noun; a three months'
 space:—three months.

G5151.definition: τρίς trís, trece; adverb from G5140; three times:—three times, thrice.

G5152.definition:
τρίστεγον trístegon, tris'-teg-on; neuter of a compound of G5140 and G4721 as noun; a third roof
 (story):—third loft.

G5153.definition: τρισχίλιοι trischílioi, tris-khil'-ee-oy; from G5151 and G5507; three times a thousand:—three thousand.

G5154.definition:
τρίτος trítos, tree'-tos; ordinal from G5140; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as
 adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly:—third(-ly).

G5155.definition: τρίχινος tríchinos, trikh'-ee-nos; from G2359; hairy, i.e. made of hair (mohair):—of hair.

G5156.definition: τρόμος trómos, trom'-os; from G5141; a "trembling", i.e. quaking with fear:—+ tremble(-ing).

G5157.definition:
τροπή tropḗ, trop-ay'; from an apparently primary τρέπω trépō to turn; a turn ("trope"), i.e.
 revolution (figuratively, variation):—turning.

G5158.definition:
τρόπος trópos, trop'-os; from the same as G5157; a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style
 (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like);
 figuratively, deportment or character:—(even) as, conversation, (+
 like) manner, (+ by any) means, way.

G5159.definition: τροποφορέω tropophoréō, trop-of-or-eh'-o; from G5158 and G5409; to endure one's habits:—suffer the manners.

G516.definition:
ἀξίως axíōs, ax-ee'-oce; adverb from G514; appropriately:—as becometh, after a godly sort,
 worthily(-thy).

G5160.definition:
τροφή trophḗ, trof-ay'; from G5142; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication,
 rations (wages):—food, meat.

G5161.definition: Τρόφιμος Tróphimos, trof'-ee-mos; from G5160; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian:—Trophimus.

G5162.definition: τροφός trophós, trof-os'; from G5142; a nourisher, i.e. nurse:—nurse.

G5163.definition:
τροχιά trochiá, trokh-ee-ah'; from G5164; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of
 conduct:—path.

G5164.definition:
τροχός trochós, trokh-os'; from G5143; a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of
 physical effects:—course.

G5165.definition: †τρύβλιον trýblion, troob'-lee-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl:—dish.

G5166.definition:
τρυγάω trygáō, troo-gah'-o; from a derivative of τρύγω trýgō (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to
 collect the vintage:—gather.

G5167.definition:
τρυγών trygṓn, troo-gone'; from τρύζω trýzō (to murmur; akin to G5149, but denoting a duller sound); a
 turtle-dove (as cooing):—turtle-dove.

G5168.definition:
†τρυμαλιά trymaliá, troo-mal-ee-ah'; from a derivative of τρύω trýō (to wear away; akin to the base of G5134,
 G5147 and G5176); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye:—eye. Compare G5169.

G5169.definition:
τρύπημα trýpēma, troo'-pay-mah; from a derivative of the base of G5168; an aperture, i.e. a needle's
 eye:—eye.

G517.definition:
ἀόρατος aóratos, ah-or'-at-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3707; invisible:—invisible
 (thing).

G5170.definition: Τρύφαινα Trýphaina, troo'-fahee-nah; from G5172; luxurious; Tryphæna, a Christian woman:—Tryphena.

G5171.definition: τρυφάω trypháō, troo-fah'-o; from G5172; to indulge in luxury:—live in pleasure.

G5172.definition:
τρυφή tryphḗ, troo-fay'; from θρύπτω thrýptō (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the
 mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, i.e. luxury or
 debauchery:—delicately, riot.

G5173.definition: Τρυφῶσα Tryphōsa, troo-fo'-sah; from G5172; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female:—Tryphosa.

G5174.definition:
†Τρωάς Trōás, tro-as'; from Τρός Trós (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a
 place in Asia Minor:—Troas.

G5176.definition:
τρώγω trṓgō, tro'-go; probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of G5134 and
 G5147 through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a
 base of G5167 and G5149 through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw
 or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat:—eat.

G5177.definition:
τυγχάνω tynchánō, toong-khan'-o; probably for an obsolete τύχω týchō (for which the middle voice of another
 alternate τεύχω teúchō (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain
 tenses; akin to the base of G5088 through the idea of effecting;
 properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark
 to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or
 end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the
 latter application only impersonal (with G1487), i.e. perchance; or
 (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with,
 with G3756, extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with
 another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were):—be, chance, enjoy,
 little, obtain, × refresh…self, + special. Compare G5180.

G5178.definition:
τυμπανίζω tympanízō, toom-pan-id'-zo; from a derivative of G5180 (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on
 an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to
 death:—torture.

G5179.definition:
†τύπος týpos, too'-pos; from G5180; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar;
 by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or
 resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for
 imitation) or instance (for warning):—en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure,
 form, manner, pattern, print.

G518.definition:
ἀπαγγέλλω apangéllō, ap-ang-el'-lo; from G575 and the base of G32; to announce:—bring word (again),
 declare, report, shew (again), tell.

G5180.definition:
τύπτω týptō, toop'-to; a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. cudgel or
 pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by
 repeated blows; thus differing from G3817 and G3960, which denote a
 (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or G4141 with
 the fist (or a hammer), or G4474 with the palm; as well as from G5177,
 an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to
 offend (the conscience):—beat, smite, strike, wound.

G5181.definition:
Τύραννος Týrannos, too'-ran-nos; a provincial form of the derivative of the base of G2962; a "tyrant";
 Tyrannus, an Ephesian:—Tyrannus.

G5183.definition: Τύριος Týrios, too'-ree-os; from G5184; a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus:—of Tyre.

G5184.definition:
Τύρος Týros, too'-ros; of Hebrew origin (H6865): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in
 Palestine:—Tyre.

G5185.definition:
†τυφλός typhlós, toof-los'; from, G5187; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically
 or mentally):—blind.

G5186.definition: τυφλόω typhlóō, toof-lo'-o; from G5185; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure:—blind.

G5187.definition:
τυφόω typhóō, toof-o'-o; from a derivative of G5188; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively)
 to inflate with self-conceit:—high-minded, be lifted up with pride,
 be proud.

G5188.definition:
†τύφω týphō, too'-fo; apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume
 without flame:—smoke.

G5189.definition: τυφωνικός typhōnikós, too-fo-nee-kos'; from a derivative of G5188; stormy (as if smoky):—tempestuous.

G519.definition:
†ἀπάγχομαι apánchomai, ap-ang'-khom-ahee; from G575 and ἄγχω ánchō (to choke; akin to the base of G43); to strangle
 oneself off (i.e. to death):—hang himself.

G5190.definition:
Τυχικός Tychikós, too-khee-kos'; from a derivative of G5177; fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a
 Christian:—Tychicus.

G5191.definition: ὑακίνθινος hyakínthinos, hoo-ak-in'-thee-nos; from G5192; "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", i.e. deep blue:—jacinth.

G5192.definition:
ὑάκινθος hyákinthos, hoo-ak'-in-thos; of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of
 a deep blue color, probably the zirkon:—jacinth.

G5193.definition: ὑάλινος hyálinos, hoo-al'-ee-nos; from G5194; glassy, i.e. transparent:—of glass.

G5194.definition:
ὕαλος hýalos, hoo'-al-os; perhaps from the same as G5205 (as being transparent like rain); 
 glass:—glass.

G5195.definition:
ὑβρίζω hybrízō, hoo-brid'-zo; from G5196; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse:—use despitefully,
 reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).

G5196.definition:
ὕβρις hýbris, hoo'-bris; from G5228; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury:—harm,
 hurt, reproach.

G5197.definition: ὑβριστής hybristḗs, hoo-bris-tace'; from G5195; an insulter, i.e. maltreater:—despiteful, injurious.

G5198.definition:
ὑγιαίνω hygiaínō, hoog-ee-ah'-ee-no; from G5199; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively,
 to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine):—be in health, (be safe and)
 sound, (be) whole(-some).

G5199.definition:
ὑγιής hygiḗs, hoog-ee-ace'; from the base of G837; healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true
 (in doctrine):—sound, whole.

G52.definition: ἄγνοια ágnoia, ag'-noy-ah; from G50; ignorance (properly, the quality):—ignorance.

G520.definition:
ἀπάγω apágō, ap-ag'-o; from G575 and G71; to take off (in various senses):—bring, carry away,
 lead (away), put to death, take away.

G5200.definition:
ὑγρός hygrós, hoo-gros'; from the base of G5205; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication)
 sappy (fresh):—green.

G5201.definition: ὑδρία hydría, hoo-dree-ah'; from G5204; a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply:—water-pot.

G5202.definition:
ὑδροποτέω hydropotéō, hoo-drop-ot-eh'-o; from a compound of G5204 and a derivative of G4095; to be a
 water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages:—drink water.

G5203.definition:
ὑδρωπικός hydrōpikós, hoo-dro-pik-os'; from a compound of G5204 and a derivative of G3700 (as if looking
 watery); to be "dropsical":—have the dropsy.

G5204.definition:
ὕδωρ hýdōr, hoo'-dore; from the base of G5205; water (as if rainy) literally or
 figuratively:—water.

G5205.definition: ὑετός hyetós, hoo-et-os'; from a primary ὕω hýō (to rain); rain, especially a shower:—rain.

G5206.definition:
υἱοθεσία huiothesía, hwee-oth-es-ee'-ah; from a presumed compound of G5207 and a derivative of G5087; the placing
 as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to
 God):—adoption (of children, of sons).

G5207.definition:
υἱός huiós, hwee-os'; apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very
 widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship:—child, foal,
 son.

G5208.definition: ὕλη hýlē, hoo-lay'; perhaps akin to G3586; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel:—matter.

G5209.definition:
ὑμᾶς hymâs, hoo-mas'; accusative case of G5210; you (as the objective of a verb or
 preposition):—ye, you (+ -ward), your (+ own).

G521.definition:
ἀπαίδευτος apaídeutos, ap-ah'-ee-dyoo-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3811; 
 uninstructed, i.e. (figuratively) stupid:—unlearned.

G5210.definition:
ὑμεῖς hymeîs, hoo-mice'; irregular plural of G4771; you (as subjective of verb):—ye
 (yourselves), you.

G5211.definition:
†Ὑμεναῖος Hymenaîos, hoo-men-ah'-yos; from Ὑμήν Hymḗn (the god of weddings); "hymenæal"; Hymenæus, an opponent of
 Christianity:—Hymenæus.

G5212.definition: ὑμέτερος hyméteros, hoo-met'-er-os; from G5210; yours, i.e. pertaining to you:—your (own).

G5213.definition:
ὑμῖν hymîn, hoo-min'; irregular dative case of G5210; to (with or by) you:—ye, you,
 your(-selves).

G5214.definition:
ὑμνέω hymnéō, hoom-neh'-o; from G5215; to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to
 celebrate (God) in song:—sing a hymn (praise unto).

G5216.definition:
ὑμῶν hymōn, hoo-mone'; genitive case of G5210; of (from or concerning) you:—ye, you, your
 (own, -selves).

G5217.definition:
ὑπάγω hypágō, hoop-ag'-o; from G5259 and G71; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as
 if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively:—depart, get
 hence, go (a-)way.

G5218.definition:
ὑπακοή hypakoḗ, hoop-ak-o-ay'; from G5219; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or
 submission:—obedience, (make) obedient, obey(-ing).

G5219.definition:
ὑπακούω hypakoúō, hoop-ak-oo'-o; from G5259 and G191; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen
 attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or
 authority:—hearken, be obedient to, obey.

G522.definition: ἀπαίρω apaírō, ap-ah'-ee-ro; from G575 and G142; to lift off, i.e. remove:—take (away).

G5220.definition:
ὕπανδρος hýpandros, hoop'-an-dros; from G5259 and G435; in subjection under a man, i.e. a married
 woman:—which hath an husband.

G5221.definition:
ὑπαντάω hypantáō, hoop-an-tah'-o; from G5259 and a derivative of G473; to go opposite (meet) under
 (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with:—(go to) meet.

G5222.definition:
ὑπάντησις hypántēsis, hoop-an'-tay-sis; from G5221; an encounter or concurrence (with G1519 for infinitive, in
 order to fall in with):—meeting.

G5223.definition:
ὕπαρξις hýparxis, hoop'-arx-is; from G5225; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property,
 wealth:—goods, substance.

G5225.definition:
ὑπάρχω hypárchō, hoop-ar'-kho; from G5259 and G756; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence
 (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or
 subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as
 an auxiliary to a principal (verb):—after, behave, live.

G5226.definition: ὑπείκω hypeíkō, hoop-i'-ko; from G5259 and εἴκω eíkō (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender:—submit self.

G5227.definition:
ὑπεναντίος hypenantíos, hoop-en-an-tee'-os; from G5259 and G1727; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as
 noun) an opponent:—adversary, against.

G5228.definition:
†ὑπέρ hypér, hoop-er'; a primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place,
 above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding;
 with the accusative case superior to, more than:—(+ exceeding,
 abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest,
 concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than),
 of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward),
 very.

G5229.definition:
†ὑπεραίρομαι hyperaíromai, hoop-er-ah'-ee-rom-ahee; middle voice from G5228 and G142; to raise oneself over, i.e.
 (figuratively) to become haughty:—exalt self, be exalted above
 measure.

G523.definition: ἀπαιτέω apaitéō, ap-ah'-ee-teh-o; from G575 and G154; to demand back:—ask again, require.

G5230.definition:
ὑπέρακμος hypérakmos, hoop-er'-ak-mos; from G5228 and the base of G188; beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively
 (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth:—+ pass the flower of
 (her) age.

G5231.definition:
ὑπεράνω hyperánō, hoop-er-an'-o; from G5228 and G507; above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or
 rank):—far above, over.

G5232.definition:
ὑπεραυξάνω hyperauxánō, hoop-er-owx-an'-o; from G5228 and G837; to increase above ordinary degree:—grow
 exceedingly.

G5233.definition:
ὑπερβαίνω hyperbaínō, hoop-er-bah'-ee-no; from G5228 and the base of G939; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to
 overreach:—go beyond.

G5234.definition:
ὑπερβαλλόντως hyperballóntōs, hoop-er-bal-lon'-toce; adverb from present participle active of G5235; excessively:—beyond
 measure.

G5235.definition:
ὑπερβάλλω hyperbállō, hoop-er-bal'-lo; from G5228 and G906; to throw beyond the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively)
 to surpass (only active participle supereminent):—exceeding, excel,
 pass.

G5236.definition:
ὑπερβολή hyperbolḗ, hoop-er-bol-ay'; from G5235; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively)
 supereminence; adverbially (with G1519 or G2596) pre-
 eminently:—abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more
 excellent, beyond (out of) measure.

G5238.definition:
ὑπερέκεινα hyperékeina, hoop-er-ek'-i-nah; from G5228 and the neuter plural of G1565; above those parts, i.e. still
 farther:—beyond.

G5239.definition: ὑπερεκτείνω hyperekteínō, hoop-er-ek-ti'-no; from G5228 and G1614; to extend inordinately:—stretch beyond.

G524.definition:
ἀπαλγέω apalgéō, ap-alg-eh'-o; from G575 and ἀλγέω algéō (to smart); to grieve out, i.e. become
 apathetic:—be past feeling.

G5240.definition:
ὑπερεκχύνω hyperekchýnō, hoop-er-ek-khoo'-no; from G5228 and the alternate form of G1632; to pour out over, i.e.
 (passively) to overflow:—run over.

G5241.definition: ὑπερεντυγχάνω hyperentynchánō, hoop-er-en-toong-khan'-o; from G5228 and G1793; to intercede in behalf of:—make intercession for.

G5242.definition:
ὑπερέχω hyperéchō, hoop-er-ekh'-o; from G5228 and G2192; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to
 excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior,
 superiority:—better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.

G5243.definition: ὑπερηφανία hyperēphanía, hoop-er-ay-fan-ee'-ah; from G5244; haughtiness:—pride.

G5244.definition:
ὑπερήφανος hyperḗphanos, hoop-er-ay'-fan-os; from G5228 and G5316; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e.
 (figuratively) haughty:—proud.

G5245.definition:
ὑπερνικάω hypernikáō, hoop-er-nik-ah'-o; from G5228 and G3528; to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive
 victory:—more than conquer.

G5246.definition:
ὑπέρογκος hypéronkos, hoop-er'-ong-kos; from G5228 and G3591; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent:—great
 swelling.

G5247.definition:
ὑπεροχή hyperochḗ, hoop-er-okh-ay'; from G5242; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or
 character):—authority, excellency.

G5248.definition: ὑπερπερισσεύω hyperperisseúō, hoop-er-per-is-syoo'-o; from G5228 and G4052; to super-abound:—abound much more, exceeding.

G5249.definition:
ὑπερπερισσῶς hyperperissōs, hoop-er-per-is-soce'; from G5228 and G4057; superabundantly, i.e. exceedingly:—beyond
 measure.

G525.definition:
ἀπαλλάσσω apallássō, ap-al-las'-so; from G575 and G236; to change away, i.e. release, (reflexively)
 remove:—deliver, depart.

G5250.definition: ὑπερπλεονάζω hyperpleonázō, hoop-er-pleh-on-ad'-zo; from G5228 and G4121; to superabound:—be exceeding abundant.

G5251.definition:
ὑπερυψόω hyperypsóō, hoop-er-oop-so'-o; from G5228 and G5312; to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest
 position:—highly exalt.

G5252.definition:
ὑπερφρονέω hyperphronéō, hoop-er-fron-eh'-o; from G5228 and G5426; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or
 arrogant:—think more highly.

G5253.definition:
ὑπερῷον hyperōion, hoop-er-o'-on; neuter of a derivative of G5228; a higher part of the house, i.e.
 apartment in the third story:—upper chamber (room).

G5254.definition:
ὑπέχω hypéchō, hoop-ekh'-o; from G5259 and G2192; to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with
 patience:—suffer.

G5255.definition:
ὑπήκοος hypḗkoos, hoop-ay'-ko-os; from G5219; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication)
 submissive:—obedient.

G5256.definition:
ὑπηρετέω hypēretéō, hoop-ay-ret-eh'-o; from G5257; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication)
 subserve:—minister (unto), serve.

G5257.definition:
ὑπηρέτης hypērétēs, hoop-ay-ret'-ace; from G5259 and a derivative of ἐρέσσω eréssō (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e.
 (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable):—minister,
 officer, servant.

G5258.definition:
ὕπνος hýpnos, hoop'-nos; from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to G5259 through the idea of
 subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor:—sleep.

G5259.definition:
ὑπό hypó, hoop-o'; a primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place
 (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the
 accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or
 time (when (at)):—among, by, from, in, of, under, with.

G526.definition:
ἀπαλλοτριόω apallotrióō, ap-al-lot-ree-o'-o; from G575 and a derivative of G245; to estrange away, i.e. (passively
 and figuratively) to be non-participant:—alienate, be alien.

G5260.definition:
ὑποβάλλω hypobállō, hoop-ob-al'-lo; from G5259 and G906; to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by
 collusion:—suborn.

G5261.definition:
ὑπογραμμός hypogrammós, hoop-og-ram-mos'; from a compound of G5259 and G1125; an underwriting, i.e. copy for
 imitation (figuratively):—example.

G5262.definition:
ὑπόδειγμα hypódeigma, hoop-od'-igue-mah; from G5263; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively,
 specimen, adumbration):—en-(ex-)ample, pattern.

G5263.definition:
ὑποδείκνυμι hypodeíknymi, hoop-od-ike'-noo-mee; from G5259 and G1166; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to
 exemplify (instruct, admonish):—show, (fore-)warn.

G5264.definition:
ὑποδέχομαι hypodéchomai, hoop-od-ekh'-om-ahee; from G5259 and G1209; to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain
 hospitably:—receive.

G5265.definition:
ὑποδέω hypodéō, hoop-od-eh'-o; from G5259 and G1210; to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or
 sandals:—bind on, (be) shod.

G5266.definition:
ὑπόδημα hypódēma, hoop-od'-ay-mah; from G5265; something bound under the feet, i.e. a shoe or
 sandal:—shoe.

G5267.definition:
ὑπόδικος hypódikos, hoop-od'-ee-kos; from G5259 and G1349; under sentence, i.e. (by implication)
 condemned:—guilty.

G5268.definition:
ὑποζύγιον hypozýgion, hoop-od-zoog'-ee-on; neuter of a compound of G5259 and G2218; an animal under the yoke
 (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey:—ass.

G5269.definition:
ὑποζώννυμι hypozṓnnymi, hoop-od-zone'-noo-mee; from G5259 and G2224; to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables
 across the keel, sides and deck):—undergirt.

G527.definition: ἀπαλός apalós, ap-al-os'; of uncertain derivation; soft:—tender.

G5270.definition: ὑποκάτω hypokátō, hoop-ok-at'-o; from G5259 and G2736; down under, i.e. beneath:—under.

G5271.definition:
ὑποκρίνομαι hypokrínomai, hoop-ok-rin'-om-ahee; middle voice from G5259 and G2919; to decide (speak or act) under a
 false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend):—feign.

G5272.definition:
ὑπόκρισις hypókrisis, hoop-ok'-ree-sis; from G5271; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit
 ("hypocrisy"):—condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy.

G5273.definition:
ὑποκριτής hypokritḗs, hoop-ok-ree-tace'; from G5271; an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e.
 (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite":—hypocrite.

G5275.definition:
ὑπολείπω hypoleípō, hoop-ol-i'-po; from G5295 and G3007; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to
 remain (survive):—be left.

G5276.definition:
ὑπολήνιον hypolḗnion, hoop-ol-ay'-nee-on; neuter of a presumed compound of G5259 and G3025; vessel or receptacle
 under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat:—winefat.

G5277.definition: ὑπολιμπάνω hypolimpánō, hoop-ol-im-pan'-o; a prolonged form for G5275; to leave behind, i.e. bequeath:—leave.

G5278.definition:
ὑπομένω hypoménō, hoop-om-en'-o; from G5259 and G3306; to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively,
 to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere:—abide,
 endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind.

G5279.definition:
†ὑπομιμνήσκω hypomimnḗskō, hoop-om-im-nace'-ko; from G5259 and G3403; to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle
 voice, one's own) memory:—put in mind, remember, bring to (put in)
 remembrance.

G528.definition: ἀπαντάω apantáō, ap-an-tah'-o; from G575 and a derivative of G473; to meet away, i.e. encounter:—meet.

G5280.definition: ὑπόμνησις hypómnēsis, hoop-om'-nay-sis; from G5279; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection:—remembrance.

G5281.definition:
ὑπομονή hypomonḗ, hoop-om-on-ay'; from G5278; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy:—enduring,
 patience, patient continuance (waiting).

G5282.definition:
ὑπονοέω hyponoéō, hoop-on-o-eh'-o; from G5259 and G3539; to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or
 conjecture:—think, suppose, deem.

G5283.definition: ὑπόνοια hypónoia, hoop-on'-oy-ah; from G5282; suspicion:—surmising.

G5284.definition: ὑποπλέω hypopléō, hoop-op-leh'-o; from G5259 and G4126; to sail under the lee of:—sail under.

G5285.definition: ὑποπνέω hypopnéō, hoop-op-neh'-o; from G5259 and G4154; to breathe gently, i.e. breeze:—blow softly.

G5286.definition:
ὑποπόδιον hypopódion, hoop-op-od'-ee-on; neuter of a compound of G5259 and G4228; something under the feet, i.e.
 a foot-rest (figuratively):—footstool.

G5287.definition:
ὑπόστασις hypóstasis, hoop-os'-tas-is; from a compound of G5259 and G2476; a setting under (support), i.e.
 (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance
 (objectively or subjectively):—confidence, confident, person,
 substance.

G5288.definition:
ὑποστέλλω hypostéllō, hoop-os-tel'-lo; from G5259 and G4724; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e.
 (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal
 (reserve):—draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw.

G5289.definition:
ὑποστολή hypostolḗ, hoop-os-tol-ay'; from G5288; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy:—draw
 back.

G529.definition: ἀπάντησις apántēsis, ap-an'-tay-sis; from G528; a (friendly) encounter:—meet.

G5290.definition:
ὑποστρέφω hypostréphō, hoop-os-tref'-o; from G5259 and G4762; to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally
 or figuratively):—come again, return (again, back again), turn back
 (again).

G5291.definition:
ὑποστρώννυμι hypostrṓnnymi, hoop-os-trone'-noo-mee; from G5259 and G4766; to strew underneath (the feet as a
 carpet):—spread.

G5292.definition: ὑποταγή hypotagḗ, hoop-ot-ag-ay'; from G5293; subordination:—subjection.

G5293.definition:
ὑποτάσσω hypotássō, hoop-ot-as'-so; from G5259 and G5021; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey:—be under
 obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to,
 unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.

G5294.definition:
ὑποτίθημι hypotíthēmi, hoop-ot-ith'-ay-mee; from G5259 and G5087; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to
 hazard, (reflexively) to suggest:—lay down, put in remembrance.

G5295.definition:
ὑποτρέχω hypotréchō, hoop-ot-rekh'-o; from G5259 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run under, i.e.
 (specially), to sail past:—run under.

G5296.definition:
ὑποτύπωσις hypotýpōsis, hoop-ot-oop'-o-sis; from a compound of G5259 and a derivative of G5179; typification under
 (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for
 imitation:—form, pattern.

G5297.definition:
ὑποφέρω hypophérō, hoop-of-er'-o; from G5259 and G5342; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to
 undergo hardship:—bear, endure.

G5298.definition:
ὑποχωρέω hypochōréō, hoop-okh-o-reh'-o; from G5259 and G5562; to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly:—go aside,
 withdraw self.

G5299.definition:
ὑπωπιάζω hypōpiázō, hoop-o-pee-ad'-zo; from a compound of G5259 and a derivative of G3700; to hit under the eye
 (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively)
 to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions):—keep
 under, weary.

G53.definition:
ἁγνός hagnós, hag-nos'; from the same as G40; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent,
 modest, perfect:—chaste, clean, pure.

G530.definition:
ἅπαξ hápax, hap'-ax; probably from G537; one (or a single) time (numerically or
 conclusively):—once.

G5300.definition: ὗς hŷs, hoos; apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine"):—sow.

G5301.definition: ὕσσωπος hýssōpos, hoos'-so-pos; of foreign origin (H231); "hyssop":—hyssop.

G5303.definition:
ὑστέρημα hystérēma, hoos-ter'-ay-mah; from G5302; a deficit; specially, poverty:—that which is behind, (that
 which was) lack(-ing), penury, want.

G5304.definition:
ὑστέρησις hystérēsis, hoos-ter'-ay-sis; from G5302; 

 a falling short, i.e. (specially), penury:—want.

G5306.definition: ὕστερος hýsteros, hoos'-ter-os; comparative from G5259 (in the sense of behind); later:—latter.

G5307.definition: ὑφαντός hyphantós, hoo-fan-tos'; from ὑφαίνω hyphaínō to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted:—woven.

G5308.definition: ὑψηλός hypsēlós, hoop-say-los'; from G5311; lofty (in place or character):—high(-er, -ly) (esteemed).

G5309.definition:
ὑψηλοφρονέω hypsēlophronéō, hoop-say-lo-fron-eh'-o; from a compound of G5308 and G5424; to be lofty in mind, i.e.
 arrogant:—be highminded.

G531.definition:
ἀπαράβατος aparábatos, ap-ar-ab'-at-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3845; not passing
 away, i.e. untransferable (perpetual):—unchangeable.

G5310.definition:
ὕψιστος hýpsistos, hoop'-sis-tos; superlative from the base of G5311; highest, i.e. (masculine singular)
 the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens:—most high,
 highest.

G5311.definition:
ὕψος hýpsos, hoop'-sos; from a derivative of G5228; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude,
 (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity:—be exalted, height,
 (on) high.

G5312.definition: ὑψόω hypsóō, hoop-so'-o; from G5311; to elevate (literally or figuratively):—exalt, lift up.

G5313.definition:
ὕψωμα hýpsōma, hoop'-so-mah; from G5312; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or
 (by implication) a barrier (figuratively):—height, high thing.

G5314.definition: φάγος phágos, fag'-os; from G5315; a glutton:—gluttonous.

G5316.definition:
φαίνω phaínō, fah'-ee-no; prolongation for the base of G5457; to lighten (shine), i.e. show
 (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative):—appear, seem,
 be seen, shine, × think.

G5317.definition: †Φάλεκ Phálek, fal'-ek; of Hebrew origin (H6389); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch:—Phalec.

G5318.definition:
φανερός phanerós, fan-er-os'; from G5316; shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter
 (as adverb) publicly, externally:—abroad, + appear, known, manifest,
 open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).

G5319.definition:
φανερόω phaneróō, fan-er-o'-o; from G5318; to render apparent (literally or figuratively):—appear,
 manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self).

G532.definition:
ἀπαρασκεύαστος aparaskeúastos, ap-ar-ask-yoo'-as-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3903; 
 unready:—unprepared.

G5320.definition:
φανερῶς phanerōs, fan-er-oce'; adverb from G5318; plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly:—evidently,
 openly.

G5321.definition:
φανέρωσις phanérōsis, fan-er'-o-sis; from G5319; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension)
 a bestowment:—manifestation.

G5322.definition: φανός phanós, fan-os'; from G5316; a lightener, i.e. light; lantern:—lantern.

G5323.definition:
Φανουήλ Phanouḗl, fan-oo-ale'; of Hebrew origin (H6439); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an
 Israelite:—Phanuel.

G5324.definition:
φαντάζω phantázō, fan-tad'-zo; from a derivative of G5316; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to
 appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle):—sight.

G5325.definition:
φαντασία phantasía, fan-tas-ee'-ah; from a derivative of G5324; (properly abstract) a (vain) show
 ("fantasy"):—pomp.

G5326.definition:
φάντασμα phántasma, fan'-tas-mah; from G5324; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e.
 spectre:—spirit.

G5327.definition:
φάραγξ pháranx, far'-anx; properly, strengthened from the base of G4008 or rather of G4486; a gap
 or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent):—valley.

G5328.definition:
Φαραώ Pharaṓ, far-ah-o'; of foreign origin (H6547); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian
 king:—Pharaoh.

G5329.definition: Φάρες Pháres, far-es'; of Hebrew origin (H6557); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite:—Phares.

G533.definition: ἀπαρνέομαι aparnéomai, ap-ar-neh'-om-ahee; from G575 and G720; to deny utterly, i.e. disown, abstain:—deny.

G5330.definition:
†Φαρισαῖος Pharisaîos, far-is-ah'-yos; of Hebrew origin (compare H6567); a separatist, i.e. exclusively
 religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary:—Pharisee.

G5331.definition:
†φαρμακεία pharmakeía, far-mak-i'-ah; from G5332; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic
 (literally or figuratively):—sorcery, witchcraft.

G5332.definition:
φαρμακεύς pharmakeús, far-mak-yoos'; from φάρμακον phármakon (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist
 ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician:—sorcerer.

G5333.definition: φάρμακος phármakos, far-mak-os'; the same as G5332:—sorcerer.

G5334.definition:
φάσις phásis, fas'-is; from G5346 (not the same as "phase", which is from G5316); a saying,
 i.e. report:—tidings.

G5335.definition: φάσκω pháskō, fas'-ko; prolongation from the same as G5346; to assert:—affirm, profess, say.

G5336.definition: φάτνη phátnē, fat'-nay; from πατέομαι patéomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder):—manager, stall.

G5337.definition:
φαῦλος phaûlos, fow'-los; apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively)
 wicked:—evil.

G5338.definition: φέγγος phéngos, feng'-gos; probably akin to the base of G5457 (compare G5350); brilliancy:—light.

G5339.definition:
φείδομαι pheídomai, fi'-dom-ahee; of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain
 or (objectively) to treat leniently:—forbear, spare.

G534.definition:
ἀπάρτι apárti, ap-ar'-tee; from G575 and G737; from now, i.e. henceforth (already):—from
 henceforth.

G5340.definition:
φειδομένως pheidoménōs, fi-dom-en'-oce; adverb from participle of G5339; abstemiously, i.e.
 stingily:—sparingly.

G5341.definition:
†φελόνης phelónēs, fel-on'-ace; by transposition for a derivative probably of G5316 (as showing outside
 the other garments); a mantle (surtout):—cloke.

G5343.definition:
φεύγω pheúgō, fyoo'-go; apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by
 implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish:—escape, flee (away).

G5344.definition: Φῆλιξ Phēlix, fay'-lix; of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman:—Felix.

G5345.definition: φήμη phḗmē, fay'-may; from G5346; a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"):—fame.

G5346.definition:
φημί phēmí, fay-mee'; properly, the same as the base of G5457 and G5316; to show or make known
 one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say:—affirm, say. Compare G3004.

G5347.definition: Φῆστος Phēstos, face'-tos; of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman:—Festus.

G5348.definition:
φθάνω phthánō, fthan'-o; apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or
 precede; by extension, to have arrived at:—(already) attain, come,
 prevent.

G5349.definition: φθαρτός phthartós, fthar-tos'; from G5351; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable:—corruptible.

G535.definition: ἀπαρτισμός apartismós, ap-ar-tis-mos'; from a derivative of G534; completion:—finishing.

G5350.definition:
φθέγγομαι phthéngomai, ftheng'-gom-ahee; probably akin to G5338 and thus to G5346; to utter a clear sound, i.e.
 (generally) to proclaim:—speak.

G5351.definition:
φθείρω phtheírō, fthi'-ro; probably strengthened from φθίω phthíō (to pine or waste); properly, to
 shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to
 ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to
 deprave):—corrupt (self), defile, destroy.

G5352.definition:
φθινοπωρινός phthinopōrinós, fthin-op-o-ree-nos'; from derivative of φθίνω phthínō (to wane; akin to the base of G5351) and
 G3703 (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves):—whose
 fruit withereth.

G5353.definition:
φθόγγος phthóngos, ftong'-gos; from G5350; utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or
 instrumental):—sound.

G5354.definition: φθονέω phthonéō, fthon-eh'-o; from G5355; to be jealous of:—envy.

G5355.definition:
φθόνος phthónos, fthon'-os; probably akin to the base of G5351; ill-will (as detraction), i.e.
 jealousy (spite):—envy.

G5356.definition:
φθορά phthorá, fthor-ah'; from G5351; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or
 figuratively):—corruption, destroy, perish.

G5357.definition: φιάλη phiálē, fee-al'-ay; of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"):—vial.

G5358.definition:
φιλάγαθος philágathos, fil-ag'-ath-os; from G5384 and G18; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue:—love of
 good men.

G5359.definition:
Φιλαδέλφεια Philadélpheia, fil-ad-el'-fee-ah; from Φιλάδελφος Philádelphos (the same as G5361), a king of Pergamos; 
 Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor:—Philadelphia.

G536.definition:
ἀπαρχή aparchḗ, ap-ar-khay'; from a compound of G575 and G756; a beginning of sacrifice, i.e. the
 (Jewish) first-fruit (figuratively):—first-fruits.

G5360.definition:
φιλαδελφία philadelphía, fil-ad-el-fee'-ah; from G5361; fraternal affection:—brotherly love (kindness), love of
 the brethren.

G5361.definition: φιλάδελφος philádelphos, fil-ad'-el-fos; from G5384 and G80; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal:—love as brethren.

G5362.definition:
φίλανδρος phílandros, fil'-an-dros; from G5384 and G435; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife:—love
 their husbands.

G5363.definition:
φιλανθρωπία philanthrōpía, fil-an-thro-pee'-ah; from the same as G5364; fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence
 ("philanthropy"):—kindness, love towards man.

G5364.definition:
φιλανθρώπως philanthrṓpōs, fil-an-thro'-poce; adverb from a compound of G5384 and G444; fondly to man
 ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely:—courteously.

G5365.definition: φιλαργυρία philargyría, fil-ar-goo-ree'-ah; from G5366; avarice:—love of money.

G5366.definition: φιλάργυρος philárgyros, fil-ar'-goo-ros; from G5384 and G696; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious:—covetous.

G5367.definition: φίλαυτος phílautos, fil'-ow-tos; from G5384 and G846; fond of self, i.e. selfish:—lover of own self.

G5368.definition:
φιλέω philéō, fil-eh'-o; from G5384; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)),
 i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of
 sentiment or feeling; while G25 is wider, embracing especially the
 judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of
 principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as
 G2309 and G1014, or as G2372 and G3563 respectively; the former being
 chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss
 (as a mark of tenderness):—kiss, love.

G5369.definition:
φιλήδονος philḗdonos, fil-ay'-don-os; from G5384 and G2237; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous:—lover of
 pleasure.

G537.definition:
ἅπας hápas, hap'-as; from G1 (as a particle of union) and G3956; absolutely all or (singular)
 every one:—all (things), every (one), whole.

G5370.definition: φίλημα phílēma, fil'-ay-mah; from G5368; a kiss:—kiss.

G5371.definition: Φιλήμων Philḗmōn, fil-ay'-mone; from G5368; friendly; Philemon, a Christian:—Philemon.

G5372.definition: Φίλητος Phílētos, fil-ay-tos'; from G5368; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity:—Philetus.

G5373.definition: φιλία philía, fil-ee'-ah; from G5384; fondness:—friendship.

G5374.definition:
Φιλιππήσιος Philippḗsios, fil-ip-pay'-see-os; from G5375; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of
 Philippi:—Philippian.

G5375.definition: Φίλιπποι Phílippoi, fil'-ip-poy; plural of G5376; Philippi, a place in Macedonia:—Philippi.

G5376.definition:
Φίλιππος Phílippos, fil'-ip-pos; from G5384 and G2462; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four
 Israelites:—Philip.

G5377.definition: φιλόθεος philótheos, fil-oth'-eh-os; from G5384 and G2316; fond of God, i.e. pious:—lover of God.

G5378.definition:
Φιλόλογος Philólogos, fil-ol'-og-os; from G5384 and G3056; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative,
 learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian:—Philologus.

G5379.definition: φιλονεικία philoneikía, fil-on-i-kee'-ah; from G5380; quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute:—strife.

G538.definition: ἀπατάω apatáō, ap-at-ah'-o; of uncertain derivation; to cheat, i.e. delude:—deceive.

G5380.definition:
φιλόνεικος philóneikos, fil-on'-i-kos; from G5384 and νεῖκος neîkos (a quarrel; probably akin to G3534); fond of
 strife, i.e. disputatious:—contentious.

G5381.definition: †φιλονεξία philonexía, fil-on-ex-ee'-ah; from G5382; hospitableness:—entertain stranger, hospitality.

G5382.definition:
φιλόξενος philóxenos, fil-ox'-en-os; from G5384 and G3581; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable:—given to (lover
 of, use) hospitality.

G5383.definition:
φιλοπρωτεύω philoprōteúō, fil-op-rote-yoo'-o; from a compound of G5384 and G4413; to be fond of being first, i.e.
 ambitious of distinction:—love to have the preeminence.

G5384.definition:
†φίλος phílos, fee'-los; properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as
 a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.):—friend.

G5385.definition:
φιλοσοφία philosophía, fil-os-of-ee'-ah; from G5386; "philosophy", i.e. (specially), Jewish
 sophistry:—philosophy.

G5386.definition:
φιλόσοφος philósophos, fil-os'-of-os; from G5384 and G4680; fond of wise things, i.e. a
 "philosopher":—philosopher.

G5387.definition:
φιλόστοργος philóstorgos, fil-os'-tor-gos; from G5384 and στοργή storgḗ (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or
 children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow
 Christian:—kindly affectioned.

G5388.definition:
φιλότεκνος philóteknos, fil-ot'-ek-nos; from G5384 and G5043; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal:—love their
 children.

G5389.definition:
φιλοτιμέομαι philotiméomai, fil-ot-im-eh'-om-ahee; middle voice from a compound of G5384 and G5092; to be fond of honor,
 i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something):—labour, strive,
 study.

G539.definition: ἀπάτη apátē, ap-at'-ay; from G538; delusion:—deceit(-ful, -fulness), deceivableness(-ving).

G5390.definition:
φιλοφρόνως philophrónōs, fil-of-ron'-oce; adverb from G5391; with friendliness of mind, i.e.
 kindly:—courteously.

G5392.definition: †φιμόω phimóō, fee-mo'-o; from φιμός phimós (a muzzle); to muzzle:—muzzle.

G5393.definition:
Φλέγων Phlégōn, fleg'-one; active participle of the base of G5395; blazing; Phlegon, a
 Christian:—Phlegon.

G5394.definition:
φλογίζω phlogízō, flog-id'-zo; from G5395; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame
 with passion):—set on fire.

G5395.definition: φλόξ phlóx, flox; from a primary φλέγω phlégō (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze:—flame(-ing).

G5396.definition:
φλυαρέω phlyaréō, floo-ar-eh'-o; from G5397; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate
 idly or mischievously:—prate against.

G5397.definition: φλύαρος phlýaros, floo'-ar-os; from φλύω phlýō (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater:—tattler.

G5398.definition:
φοβερός phoberós, fob-er-os'; from G5401; frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable:—fearful,
 terrible.

G5399.definition:
φοβέω phobéō, fob-eh'-o; from G5401; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to
 be in awe of, i.e. revere:—be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly),
 reverence.

G54.definition:
ἁγνότης hagnótēs, hag-not'-ace; from G53; cleanness (the state), i.e. (figuratively)
 blamelessness:—pureness.

G540.definition:
ἀπάτωρ apátōr, ap-at'-ore; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3962; fatherless, i.e. of
 unrecorded paternity:—without father.

G5400.definition:
φόβητρον phóbētron, fob'-ay-tron; neuter of a derivative of G5399; a frightening thing, i.e. terrific
 portent:—fearful sight.

G5401.definition:
φόβος phóbos, fob'-os; from a primary φέβομαι phébomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright:—be
 afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.

G5402.definition:
Φοίβη Phoíbē, foy'-bay; feminine of φοῖβος phoîbos (bright; probably akin to the base of G5457);
 Phœbe, a Christian woman:—Phebe.

G5403.definition:
Φοινίκη Phoiníkē, foy-nee'-kay; from G5404; palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of
 Palestine:—Phenice, Phenicia.

G5404.definition: †φοῖνιξ phoînix, foy'-nix; of uncertain derivation; a palm-tree:—palm (tree).

G5405.definition: Φοῖνιξ Phoînix, foy'-nix; probably the same as G5404; Phœnix, a place in Crete:—Phenice.

G5406.definition:
φονεύς phoneús, fon-yooce'; from G5408; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional)
 homicide; which G443 does not necessarily imply; while G4607 is a
 special term for a public bandit):—murderer.

G5407.definition: φονεύω phoneúō, fon-yoo'-o; from G5406; to be a murderer (of):—kill, do murder, slay.

G5408.definition:
φόνος phónos, fon'-os; from an obsolete primary φένω phénō (to slay); murder:—murder, + be slain
 with, slaughter.

G5409.definition:
φορέω phoréō, for-eh'-o; from G5411; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or
 a constant accompaniment:—bear, wear.

G541.definition:
ἀπαύγασμα apaúgasma, ap-ow'-gas-mah; from a compound of G575 and G826; an off-flash, i.e.
 effulgence:—brightness.

G5411.definition:
φόρος phóros, for'-os; from G5342; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an
 individual assessment on persons or property; whereas G5056 is usually
 a general toll on goods or travel):—tribute.

G5412.definition:
φορτίζω phortízō, for-tid'-zo; from G5414; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e.
 (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual
 anxiety):—lade, by heavy laden.

G5413.definition:
φορτίον phortíon, for-tee'-on; diminutive of G5414; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e.
 (figuratively) a task or service:—burden.

G5415.definition: Φορτουνᾶτος Phortounâtos, for-too-nat'-os; of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian:—Fortunatus.

G5416.definition:
φραγέλλιον phragéllion, frag-el'-le-on; neuter of a derivative from the base of G5417; a whip, i.e. Roman lash
 as a public punishment:—scourge.

G5417.definition:
φραγελλόω phragellóō, frag-el-lo'-o; from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash
 as a public punishment:—scourge.

G5418.definition:
φραγμός phragmós, frag-mos'; from G5420; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or
 figuratively):—hedge (+ round about), partition.

G5419.definition:
φράζω phrázō, frad'-zo; probably akin to G5420 through the idea of defining; to indicate (by
 word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound:—declare.

G5420.definition:
φράσσω phrássō, fras'-so; apparently a strengthening form of the base of G5424; to fence or
 inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to
 silence):—stop.

G5422.definition: φρεναπατάω phrenapatáō, fren-ap-at-ah'-o; from G5423; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude:—deceive.

G5423.definition: φρεναπάτης phrenapátēs, fren-ap-at'-ace; from G5424 and G539; a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer:—deceiver.

G5424.definition:
φρήν phrḗn, frane; probably from an obsolete φράω phráō (to rein in or curb; compare G5420); 
 the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by
 implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by
 extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive
 faculties):—understanding.

G5425.definition:
φρίσσω phríssō, fris'-so; apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder
 (fear):—tremble.

G5426.definition:
φρονέω phronéō, fron-eh'-o; from G5424; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or
 opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less
 earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in
 (with concern or obedience):—set the affection on, (be) care(-ful),
 (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed),
 regard, savour, think.

G5427.definition:
φρόνημα phrónēma, fron'-ay-mah; from G5426; (mental) inclination or purpose:—(be, + be carnally, + be
 spiritually) mind(-ed).

G5428.definition:
φρόνησις phrónēsis, fron'-ay-sis; from G5426; mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral
 insight:—prudence, wisdom.

G5429.definition:
φρόνιμος phrónimos, fron'-ee-mos; from G5424; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious
 character; while G4680 denotes practical skill or acumen; and G4908
 indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense
 conceited (also in the comparative):—wise(-r).

G543.definition:
ἀπείθεια apeítheia, ap-i'-thi-ah; from G545; disbelief (obstinate and rebellious):—disobedience,
 unbelief.

G5430.definition: φρονίμως phronímōs, fron-im'-oce; adverb from G5429; prudently:—wisely.

G5431.definition:
φροντίζω phrontízō, fron-tid'-zo; from a derivative of G5424; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious:—be
 careful.

G5432.definition:
φρουρέω phrouréō, froo-reh'-o; from a compound of G4253 and G3708; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to
 mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem
 in, protect:—keep (with a garrison). Compare G5083.

G5433.definition:
φρυάσσω phryássō, froo-as'-so; akin to G1032, G1031; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e.
 (figuratively) to make a tumult:—rage.

G5434.definition:
φρύγανον phrýganon, froo'-gan-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of φρύγω phrýgō (to roast or parch; akin to
 the base of G5395); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig:—stick.

G5435.definition: Φρυγία Phrygía, froog-ee'-ah; probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor:—Phrygia.

G5436.definition:
†Φύγελλος Phýgellos, foog'-el-los; probably from G5343; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate
 Christian:—Phygellus.

G5437.definition: φυγή phygḗ, foog-ay'; from G5343; a fleeing, i.e. escape:—flight.

G5438.definition:
φυλακή phylakḗ, foo-lak-ay'; from G5442; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person;
 figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a
 division of day or night), literally or figuratively:—cage, hold,
 (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch.

G5439.definition: φυλακίζω phylakízō, foo-lak-id'-zo; from G5441; to incarcerate:—imprison.

G544.definition:
ἀπειθέω apeithéō, ap-i-theh'-o; from G545; to disbelieve (wilfully and perversely):—not believe,
 disobedient, obey not, unbelieving.

G5440.definition:
φυλακτήριον phylaktḗrion, foo-lak-tay'-ree-on; neuter of a derivative of G5442; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for
 wearing slips of Scripture texts:—phylactery.

G5441.definition: φύλαξ phýlax, foo'-lax; from G5442; a watcher or sentry:—keeper.

G5442.definition:
φυλάσσω phylássō, foo-las'-so; probably from G5443 through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on
 guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey,
 avoid:—beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare G5083.

G5443.definition:
φυλή phylḗ, foo-lay'; from G5453 (compare G5444); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan:—kindred,
 tribe.

G5444.definition: φύλλον phýllon, fool'-lon; from the same as G5443; a sprout, i.e. leaf:—leaf.

G5445.definition:
φύραμα phýrama, foo'-ram-ah; from a prolonged form of φύρω phýrō (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps
 akin to G5453 through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a
 mass of dough:—lump.

G5446.definition:
φυσικός physikós, foo-see-kos'; from G5449; "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive:—natural. 
 Compare G5591.

G5447.definition:
φυσικῶς physikōs, foo-see-koce'; adverb from G5446; "physically", i.e. (by implication)
 instinctively:—naturally.

G5448.definition:
φυσιόω physióō, foo-see-o'-o; from G5449 in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e.
 (figuratively) make proud (haughty):—puff up.

G5449.definition:
φύσις phýsis, foo'-sis; from G5453; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication)
 natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort;
 figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage:—(man-)kind,
 nature(-al).

G545.definition:
ἀπειθής apeithḗs, ap-i-thace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3982; unpersuadable, i.e.
 contumacious:—disobedient.

G5450.definition: φυσίωσις physíōsis, foo-see'-o-sis; from G5448; inflation, i.e. (figuratively) haughtiness:—swelling.

G5451.definition:
φυτεία phyteía, foo-ti'-ah; from G5452; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or
 vegetable:—plant.

G5452.definition:
φυτεύω phyteúō, foot-yoo'-o; from a derivative of G5453; to set out in the earth, i.e. implant;
 figuratively, to instil doctrine:—plant.

G5453.definition:
φύω phýō, foo'-o; a primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell
 up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout,
 produce), literally or figuratively:—spring (up).

G5454.definition: φωλεός phōleós, fo-leh-os'; of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place:—hole.

G5455.definition:
φωνέω phōnéō, fo-neh'-o; from G5456; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by
 implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation:—call
 (for), crow, cry.

G5456.definition:
φωνή phōnḗ, fo-nay'; probably akin to G5316 through the idea of disclosure; a tone
 (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for
 any purpose), saying or language:—noise, sound, voice.

G5457.definition:
φῶς phōs, foce; from an obsolete φάω pháō (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; 
 compare G5316, G5346); luminousness (in the widest application, natural
 or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative):—fire,
 light.

G5458.definition:
φωστήρ phōstḗr, foce-tare'; from G5457; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or
 (abstractly) brilliancy:—light.

G5459.definition:
φωσφόρος phōsphóros, foce-for'-os; from G5457 and G5342; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially),
 the morning-star (figuratively):—day star.

G546.definition:
ἀπειλέω apeiléō, ap-i-leh'-o; of uncertain derivation; to menace; by implication, to
 forbid:—threaten.

G5460.definition:
φωτεινός phōteinós, fo-ti-nos'; from G5457; lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated
 (figuratively):—bright, full of light.

G5461.definition:
φωτίζω phōtízō, fo-tid'-zo; from G5457; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten
 up (literally or figuratively):—enlighten, illuminate, (bring to,
 give) light, make to see.

G5462.definition: φωτισμός phōtismós, fo-tis-mos'; from G5461; illumination (figuratively):—light.

G5463.definition:
χαίρω chaírō, khah'-ee-ro; a primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off;
 impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be
 well:—farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hail, joy(- fully),
 rejoice.

G5464.definition: χάλαζα chálaza, khal'-ad-zah; probably from G5465; hail:—hail.

G5465.definition: χαλάω chaláō, khal-ah'-o; from the base of G5490; to lower (as into a void):—let down, strike.

G5466.definition:
Χαλδαῖος Chaldaîos, khal-dah'-yos; probably of Hebrew or (H3778); a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or
 the region of the lower Euphrates:—Chaldæan.

G5468.definition:
χαλιναγωγέω chalinagōgéō, khal-in-ag-ogue-eh'-o; from a compound of G5469 and the reduplicated form of G71; to be a
 bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively):—bridle.

G5469.definition: χαλινός chalinós, khal-ee-nos'; from G5465; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit):—bit, bridle.

G547.definition: ἀπειλή apeilḗ, ap-i-lay'; from G546; a menace:—X straitly, threatening.

G5471.definition: χαλκεύς chalkeús, khalk-yooce'; from G5475; a copper-worker or brazier:—coppersmith.

G5472.definition:
χαλκηδών chalkēdṓn, khal-kay-dohn'; from G5475 and perhaps G1491; copper-like, i.e.
 "chalcedony":—chalcedony.

G5473.definition: χαλκίον chalkíon, khal-kee'-on; diminutive from G5475; a copper dish:—brazen vessel.

G5474.definition:
χαλκολίβανον chalkolíbanon, khal-kol-ib'-an-on; neuter of a compound of G5475 and G3030 (in the implied mean of
 whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or
 gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre:—fine brass.

G5475.definition:
χαλκός chalkós, khal-kos'; perhaps from G5465 through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this
 metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or
 some implement or coin made of it):—brass, money.

G5476.definition:
χαμαί chamaí, kham-ah'-ee; adverb perhaps from the base of G5490 through the idea of a fissure in
 the soil; earthward, i.e. prostrate:—on (to) the ground.

G5477.definition:
Χαναάν Chanaán, khan-ah-an'; of Hebrew origin (H3667); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of
 Palestine:—Chanaan.

G5478.definition:
†Χανααναῖος Chanaanaîos, khan-ah-an-ah'-yos; from G5477; a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile
 Palestine:—of Canaan.

G5479.definition:
χαρά chará, khar-ah'; from G5463; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight:—gladness, × greatly, (X
 be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).

G548.definition: ἄπειμι ápeimi, ap'-i-mee; from G575 and G1510; to be away:—be absent. Compare G549.

G5480.definition:
χάραγμα cháragma, khar'-ag-mah; from the same as G5482; a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of
 servitude), or scupltured figure (statue):—graven, mark.

G5481.definition:
χαρακτήρ charaktḗr, khar-ak-tare'; from the same as G5482; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by
 implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an
 exact copy or (figuratively) representation):—express image.

G5482.definition:
χάραξ chárax, khar'-ax; from χαράσσω charássō (to sharpen to a point; akin to G1125 through the idea of
 scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart
 (military mound for circumvallation in a siege):—trench.

G5483.definition:
χαρίζομαι charízomai, khar-id'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G5485; to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in
 kindness, pardon or rescue:—deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely)
 give, grant.

G5484.definition:
χάριν chárin, khar'-in; accusative case of G5485 as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on
 account of:—be-(for) cause of, for sake of,
 +…fore, × reproachfully.

G5485.definition:
χάρις cháris, khar'-ece; from G5463; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or
 concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine
 influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including
 gratitude):—acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy,
 liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy).

G5486.definition:
χάρισμα chárisma, khar'-is-mah; from G5483; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or
 passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively)
 religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty:—(free)
 gift.

G5487.definition:
χαριτόω charitóō, khar-ee-to'-o; from G5485; to grace, i.e. indue with special honor:—make accepted, be
 highly favoured.

G5488.definition:
Χαῤῥάν Charrhán, khar-hran'; of Hebrew origin (H2771); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in
 Mesopotamia:—Charran.

G5489.definition:
χάρτης chártēs, khar'-tace; from the same as G5482; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be
 scribbled over):—paper.

G5490.definition:
χάσμα chásma, khas'-mah; from a form of an obsolete primary χάω cháō (to "gape" or "yawn"); a
 "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval):—gulf.

G5491.definition:
χεῖλος cheîlos, khi'-los; from a form of the same as G5490; a lip (as a pouring place);
 figuratively, a margin (of water):—lip, shore.

G5492.definition:
χειμάζω cheimázō, khi-mad'-zo; from the same as G5494; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a
 gale:—be tossed with tempest.

G5493.definition:
χείμαῤῥος cheímarrhos, khi'-mar-hros; from the base of G5494 and G4482; a storm-runlet, i.e.
 winter-torrent:—brook.

G5494.definition: χειμών cheimṓn, khi-mone'; from a derivative of χέω chéō (to pour; akin to the base of G5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter:—tempest, foul weather, winter.

G5495.definition:
χείρ cheír, khire; perhaps from the base of G5494 in the sense of its congener the base of
 G5490 (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand
 (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means
 or instrument):—hand.

G5496.definition:
χειραγωγέω cheiragōgéō, khi-rag-ogue-eh'-o; from G5497; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person):—lead
 by the hand.

G5497.definition:
χειραγωγός cheiragōgós, khi-rag-o-gos'; from G5495 and a reduplicated form of G71; a hand-leader, i.e. personal
 conductor (of a blind person):—some to lead by the hand.

G5498.definition:
χειρόγραφον cheirógraphon, khi-rog'-raf-on; neuter of a compound of G5495 and G1125; something hand-written
 ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond
 (figuratively)):—handwriting.

G5499.definition:
χειροποίητος cheiropoíētos, khi-rop-oy'-ay-tos; from G5495 and a derivative of G4160; manufactured, i.e. of human
 construction:—made by (make with) hands.

G55.definition: ἁγνῶς hagnōs, hag-noce'; adverb from G53; purely, i.e. honestly:—sincerely.

G550.definition:
†ἀπειπόμην apeipómēn, ap-i-pom'-ane; reflexive past of a compound of G575 and G2036; to say off for oneself,
 i.e. disown:—renounce.

G5500.definition:
χειροτονέω cheirotonéō, khi-rot-on-eh'-o; from a comparative of G5495 and τείνω teínō (to stretch); to be a
 hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to
 select or appoint:—choose, ordain.

G5501.definition:
χείρων cheírōn, khi'-rone; irregular comparative of G2556; from an obsolete equivalent
 χέρης chérēs (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated
 (physically, mentally or morally):—sorer, worse.

G5502.definition:
†χερουβίμ cheroubím, kher-oo-beem'; plural of Hebrew origin (H3742); "cherubim" (i.e. cherubs or
 kerubim):—cherubims.

G5503.definition:
χήρα chḗra, khay'-rah; feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of G5490
 through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband),
 literally or figuratively:—widow.

G5505.definition: χιλιάς chiliás, khil-ee-as'; from G5507; one thousand ("chiliad"):—thousand.

G5506.definition:
†χιλίαρχος chilíarchos, khil-ee'-ar-khos; from G5507 and G757; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch";
 i.e. colonel:—(chief, high) captain.

G5507.definition: χίλιοι chílioi, khil'-ee-oy; plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand:—thousand.

G5508.definition:
Χίος Chíos, khee'-os; of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the
 Mediterranean:—Chios.

G5509.definition: χιτών chitṓn, khee-tone'; of foreign origin (H3801); a tunic or shirt:—clothes, coat, garment.

G551.definition:
ἀπείραστος apeírastos, ap-i'-ras-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3987; 
 untried, i.e. not temptable:—not to be tempted.

G5510.definition:
χιών chiṓn, khee-one'; perhaps akin to the base of G5490 (G5465) or G5494 (as descending or
 empty); snow:—snow.

G5511.definition: χλαμύς chlamýs, khlam-ooce'; of uncertain derivation; a military cloak:—robe.

G5512.definition:
†χλευάζω chleuázō, khlyoo-ad'-zo; from a derivative probably of G5491; to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer
 at:—mock.

G5513.definition: χλιαρός chliarós, khlee-ar-os'; from χλίω chlíō (to warm); tepid:—lukewarm.

G5514.definition:
Χλόη Chlóē, khlo'-ay; feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloë, a Christian
 female:—Chloe.

G5515.definition:
χλωρός chlōrós, khlo-ros'; from the same as G5514; greenish, i.e. verdant, dun-colored:—green,
 pale.

G5517.definition:
χοϊκός choïkós, kho-ik-os'; from G5522; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication)
 terrene:—earthy.

G5518.definition: χοῖνιξ choînix, khoy'-nix; of uncertain derivation; a chœnix or certain dry measure:—measure.

G5519.definition: χοῖρος choîros, khoy'-ros; of uncertain derivation; a hog:—swine.

G552.definition:
ἄπειρος ápeiros, ap'-i-ros; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3984; inexperienced, i.e.
 ignorant:—unskilful.

G5520.definition:
χολάω choláō, khol-ah'-o; from G5521; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged,
 "choleric"):—be angry.

G5521.definition:
χολή cholḗ, khol-ay'; feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the
 greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne
 (wormwood, poppy, etc.):—gall.

G5523.definition: †Χοραζίν Chorazín, khor-ad-zin'; of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine:—Chorazin.

G5524.definition:
χορηγέω chorēgéō, khor-ayg-eh'-o; from a compound of G5525 and G71; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally)
 to furnish:—give, minister.

G5525.definition: χορός chorós, khor-os'; of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. round dance ("choir":—dancing.

G5526.definition:
χορτάζω chortázō, khor-tad'-zo; from G5528; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in
 abundance):—feed, fill, satisfy.

G5527.definition: χόρτασμα chórtasma, khor'-tas-mah; from G5526; forage, i.e. food:—sustenance.

G5528.definition:
χόρτος chórtos, khor'-tos; apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by
 implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation:—blade, grass, hay.

G5529.definition: Χουζᾶς Chouzâs, khood-zas'; of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod:—Chuza.

G553.definition: ἀπεκδέχομαι apekdéchomai, ap-ek-dekh'-om-ahee; from G575 and G1551; to expect fully:—look (wait) for.

G5532.definition:
χρεία chreía, khri'-ah; from the base of G5530 or G5534; employment, i.e. an affair; also (by
 implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution:—business,
 lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want.

G5533.definition:
†χρεωφειλέτης chreōpheilétēs, khreh-o-fi-let'-ace; from a derivative of G5531 and G3781; a loan-ower, i.e. indebted
 person:—debtor.

G5534.definition:
χρή chrḗ, khray; third person singular of the same as G5530 or G5531 used impersonally; 
 it needs (must or should) be:—ought.

G5535.definition:
χρῄζω chrḗizō, khrade'-zo; from G5532; to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of:—(have)
 need.

G5536.definition: χρῆμα chrēma, khray'-mah; something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price:—money, riches.

G5537.definition:
χρηματίζω chrēmatízō, khray-mat-id'-zo; from G5536; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of G5530),
 i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of
 G5532) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a
 title:—be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak.

G5538.definition: χρηματισμός chrēmatismós, khray-mat-is-mos'; from G5537; a divine response or revelation:—answer of God.

G5539.definition: χρήσιμος chrḗsimos, khray'-see-mos; from G5540; serviceable:—profit.

G554.definition:
ἀπεκδύομαι apekdýomai, ap-ek-doo'-om-ahee; middle voice from G575 and G1562; to divest wholly oneself, or (for
 oneself) despoil:—put off, spoil.

G5540.definition:
χρῆσις chrēsis, khray'-sis; from G5530; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an
 occupation of the body):—use.

G5541.definition:
χρηστεύομαι chrēsteúomai, khraste-yoo'-om-ahee; middle voice from G5543; to show oneself useful, i.e. act
 benevolently:—be kind.

G5542.definition:
χρηστολογία chrēstología, khrase-tol-og-ee'-ah; from a compound of G5543 and G3004; fair speech, i.e.
 plausibility:—good words.

G5543.definition:
χρηστός chrēstós, khrase-tos'; from G5530; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or
 morals):—better, easy, good(-ness), gracious, kind.

G5544.definition:
χρηστότης chrēstótēs, khray-stot'-ace; from G5543; usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or
 demeanor):—gentleness, good(-ness), kindness.

G5545.definition:
χρῖσμα chrîsma, khris'-mah; from G5548; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special
 endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit:—anointing, unction.

G5546.definition: Χριστιανός Christianós, khris-tee-an-os'; from G5547; a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ:—Christian.

G5547.definition: Χριστός Christós, khris-tos'; from G5548; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus:—Christ.

G5548.definition:
χρίω chríō, khree'-o; probably akin to G5530 through the idea of contact; to smear or rub
 with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or
 religious service:—anoint.

G5549.definition: χρονίζω chronízō, khron-id'-zo; from G5550; to take time, i.e. linger:—delay, tarry.

G555.definition: ἀπέκδυσις apékdysis, ap-ek'-doo-sis; from G554; divestment:—putting off.

G5550.definition:
χρόνος chrónos, khron'-os; of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus
 properly distinguished from G2540, which designates a fixed or special
 occasion; and from G165, which denotes a particular period) or
 interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication,
 delay:—+ years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while.

G5551.definition:
χρονοτριβέω chronotribéō, khron-ot-rib-eh'-o; from a presumed compound of G5550 and the base of G5147; to be a
 time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger):—spend time.

G5552.definition: χρύσεος chrýseos, khroo'-seh-os; from G5557; made of gold:—of gold, golden.

G5553.definition:
χρυσίον chrysíon, khroo-see'-on; diminutive of G5557; a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or
 coin:—gold.

G5554.definition:
χρυσοδακτύλιος chrysodaktýlios, khroo-sod-ak-too'-lee-os; from G5557 and G1146; gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or
 similar jewelry:—with a gold ring.

G5555.definition:
χρυσόλιθος chrysólithos, khroo-sol'-ee-thos; from G5557 and G3037; gold-stone, i.e. a yellow gem
 ("chrysolite"):—chrysolite.

G5556.definition:
χρυσόπρασος chrysóprasos, khroo-sop'-ras-os; from G5557 and πράσον práson (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem
 ("chrysoprase"):—chrysoprase.

G5557.definition:
χρυσός chrysós, khroo-sos'; perhaps from the base of G5530 (through the idea of the utility of the
 metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or
 coin:—gold.

G5558.definition: χρυσόω chrysóō, khroo-so'-o; from G5557; to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments:—deck.

G5559.definition:
χρώς chrṓs, khroce; probably akin to the base of G5530 through the idea of handling; the
 body (properly, its surface or skin):—body.

G556.definition: ἀπελαύνω apelaúnō, ap-el-ow'-no; from G575 and G1643; to dismiss:—drive.

G5560.definition: χωλός chōlós, kho-los'; apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. limping:—cripple, halt, lame.

G5561.definition:
χώρα chṓra, kho'-rah; feminine of a derivative of the base of G5490 through the idea of empty
 expanse; room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive;
 often including its inhabitants):—coast, county, fields, ground,
 land, region. Compare G5117.

G5562.definition:
χωρέω chōréō, kho-reh'-o; from G5561; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass,
 enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or
 figuratively):—come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to)
 receive.

G5563.definition:
χωρίζω chōrízō, kho-rid'-zo; from G5561; to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go
 away:—depart, put asunder, separate.

G5564.definition:
χωρίον chōríon, kho-ree'-on; diminutive of G5561; a spot or plot of ground:—field, land, parcel of
 ground, place, possession.

G5565.definition:
χωρίς chōrís, kho-rece'; adverb from G5561; at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as
 preposition):—beside, by itself, without.

G5566.definition: χῶρος chōros, kho'-ros; of Latin origin; the north-west wind:—north west.

G5567.definition:
ψάλλω psállō, psal'-lo; probably strengthened from ψάω psáō (to rub or touch the surface; compare
 G5597); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument
 (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes):—make
 melody, sing (psalms).

G5568.definition:
ψαλμός psalmós, psal-mos'; from G5567; a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with
 the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the
 book of the Psalms:—psalm. Compare G5603.

G5569.definition:
ψευδάδελφος pseudádelphos, psyoo-dad'-el-fos; from G5571 and G80; a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate:—false
 brethren.

G557.definition:
ἀπελεγμός apelegmós, ap-el-eg-mos'; from a compound of G575 and G1651; refutation, i.e. (by implication)
 contempt:—nought.

G5570.definition:
ψευδαπόστολος pseudapóstolos, psyoo-dap-os'-tol-os; from G5571 and G652; a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher:—false
 teacher.

G5571.definition: ψευδής pseudḗs, psyoo-dace'; from G5574; untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked:—false, liar.

G5572.definition:
ψευδοδιδάσκαλος pseudodidáskalos, psyoo-dod-id-as'-kal-os; from G5571 and G1320; a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous
 Christian doctrine:—false teacher.

G5573.definition:
ψευδολόγος pseudológos, psyoo-dol-og'-os; from G5571 and G3004; mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian
 doctrine:—speaking lies.

G5574.definition:
†ψεύδομαι pseúdomai, psyoo'-dom-ahee; middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or
 attempt to deceive by falsehood:—falsely, lie.

G5576.definition:
ψευδομαρτυρέω pseudomartyréō, psyoo-dom-ar-too-reh'-o; from G5575; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in
 evidence:—be a false witness.

G5577.definition: ψευδομαρτυρία pseudomartyría, psyoo-dom-ar-too-ree'-ah; from G5575; untrue testimony:—false witness.

G5578.definition:
ψευδοπροφήτης pseudoprophḗtēs, psyoo-dop-rof-ay'-tace; from G5571 and G4396; a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or
 religious impostor:—false prophet.

G5579.definition: ψεῦδος pseûdos, psyoo'-dos; from G5574; a falsehood:—lie, lying.

G558.definition: ἀπελεύθερος apeleútheros, ap-el-yoo'-ther-os; from G575 and G1658; one freed away, i.e. a freedman:—freeman.

G5580.definition: ψευδόχριστος pseudóchristos, psyoo-dokh'-ris-tos; from G5571 and G5547; a spurious Messiah:—false Christ.

G5581.definition: ψευδώνυμος pseudṓnymos, psyoo-do'-noo-mos; from G5571 and G3686; untruly named:—falsely so called.

G5582.definition: ψεῦσμα pseûsma, psyoos'-mah; from G5574; a fabrication, i.e. falsehood:—lie.

G5583.definition: ψεύστης pseústēs, psyoos-tace'; from G5574; a falsifier:—liar.

G5584.definition:
ψηλαφάω psēlapháō, psay-laf-ah'-o; from the base of G5567 (compare G5586); to manipulate, i.e. verify by
 contact; figuratively, to search for:—feel after, handle, touch.

G5585.definition:
ψηφίζω psēphízō, psay-fid'-zo; from G5586; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to
 compute:—count.

G5586.definition:
ψῆφος psēphos, psay'-fos; from the same as G5584; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by
 implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal)
 or ticket (of admission); a vote:—stone, voice.

G5588.definition: ψιθυριστής psithyristḗs, psith-oo-ris-tace'; from the same as G5587; a secret calumniator:—whisperer.

G5589.definition:
ψιχίον psichíon, psikh-ee'-on; diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5567 (meaning a crumb); a
 little bit or morsel:—crumb.

G559.definition: Ἀπελλῆς Apellēs, ap-el-lace'; of Latin origin; Apelles, a Christian:—Apelles.

G5590.definition:
ψυχή psychḗ, psoo-khay'; from G5594; breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or
 concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on
