 the one hand from G4151, which is the rational and immortal soul; and
 on the other from G2222, which is mere vitality, even of plants: these
 terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew H5315, H7307
 and H2416):—heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you.

G5591.definition:
ψυχικός psychikós, psoo-khee-kos'; from G5590; sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand
 from G4152, which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other
 from G5446, which is the lower or bestial nature):—natural, sensual.

G5592.definition: ψύχος psýchos, psoo'-khos; from G5594; coolness:—cold.

G5593.definition: ψυχρός psychrós, psoo-chros'; from G5592; chilly (literally or figuratively):—cold.

G5594.definition:
ψύχω psýchō, psoo'-kho; a primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on
 the one hand from G4154, which denotes properly a forcible respiration;
 and on the other from the base of G109, which refers properly to an
 inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature
 by evaporation) to chill (figuratively):—wax cold.

G5595.definition:
ψωμίζω psōmízō, pso-mid'-zo; from the base of G5596; to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to
 nourish:—(bestow to) feed.

G5596.definition:
ψωμίον psōmíon, pso-mee'-on; diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5597; a crumb or morsel
 (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful:—sop.

G5597.definition:
ψώχω psṓchō, pso'-kho; prolongation from the same base as G5567; to triturate, i.e. (by
 analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or
 hand):—rub.

G5598.definition:
Ω Ō, o'-meg-ah; the last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the
 finality:—Omega.

G5599.definition:
ὦ ō, o; a primary interjection; as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note
 of exclamation, oh:—O.

G56.definition:
ἀγνωσία agnōsía, ag-no-see'-ah; from G1 (as negative particle) and G1108; ignorance (properly, the
 state):—ignorance, not the knowledge.

G560.definition: ἀπελπίζω apelpízō, ap-el-pid'-zo; from G575 and G1679; to hope out, i.e. fully expect:—hope for again.

G5600.definition:
ὦ ō, o; the subjunctive of G1510; (may, might, can, could, would, should, must,
 etc.; also with G1487 and its comparative, as well as with other
 particles) be:—+ appear, are, (may, might, should) be, × have, is, +
 pass the flower of her age, should stand, were.

G5601.definition: †Ὠβήδ Ōbḗd, o-bade'; of Hebrew origin (H5744); Obed, an Israelite:—Obed.

G5602.definition:
ὧδε hōde, ho'-deh; from an adverb form of G3592; in this same spot, i.e. here or
 hither:—here, hither, (in) this place, there.

G5603.definition:
ᾠδή ōidḗ, o-day'; from G103; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while
 G5215 denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and G5568
 still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation):—song.

G5604.definition:
ὠδίν ōdín, o-deen'; akin to G3601; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth:—pain,
 sorrow, travail.

G5605.definition:
ὠδίνω ōdínō, o-dee'-no; from G5604; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or
 figuratively):—travail in (birth).

G5606.definition:
ὦμος ōmos, o'-mos; perhaps from the alternate of G5342; the shoulder (as that on which
 burdens are borne):—shoulder.

G5607.definition: ὤν ṓn, oan; present participle of G1510; being:—be, come, have.

G5608.definition:
ὠνέομαι ōnéomai, o-neh'-om-ahee; middle voice from an apparently primary ὦνος ōnos (a sum or price); to
 purchase (synonymous with the earlier G4092):—buy.

G5609.definition: ὠόν ōón, o-on'; apparently a primary word; an "egg":—egg.

G561.definition:
ἀπέναντι apénanti, ap-en'-an-tee; from G575 and G1725; from in front, i.e. opposite, before or
 against:—before, contrary, over against, in the presence of.

G5610.definition:
ὥρα hṓra, ho'-rah; apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or
 figuratively):—day, hour, instant, season, × short, (even-)tide,
 (high) time.

G5611.definition:
ὡραῖος hōraîos, ho-rah'-yos; from G5610; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by
 implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)):—beautiful.

G5612.definition: ὠρύομαι ōrýomai, o-roo'-om-ahee; middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar":—roar.

G5613.definition:
ὡς hōs, hoce; probably adverb of comparative from G3739; which how, i.e. in that
 manner (very variously used, as follows):—about, after (that),
 (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like),
 for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit,
 unto, when(-soever), while, × with all speed.

G5614.definition:
ὡσαννά hōsanná, ho-san-nah'; of Hebrew origin (H3467 and H4994); oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na),
 an exclamation of adoration:—hosanna.

G5615.definition:
ὡσαύτως hōsaútōs, ho-sow'-toce; from G5613 and an adverb from G846; as thus, i.e. in the same way:—even
 so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner.

G5616.definition:
ὡσεί hōseí, ho-si'; from G5613 and G1487; as if:—about, as (it had been, it were), like
 (as).

G5617.definition: Ὡσηέ Hōsēé, ho-say-eh'; of Hebrew origin (H1954); Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite:—Osee.

G5618.definition: ὥσπερ hṓsper, hoce'-per; from G5613 and G4007; just as, i.e. exactly like:—(even, like) as.

G5619.definition: ὡσπερεί hōspereí, hoce-per-i'; from G5618 and G1487; just as if, i.e. as it were:—as.

G562.definition:
ἀπέραντος apérantos, ap-er'-an-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a secondary derivative of G4008; 
 unfinished, i.e. (by implication) interminable:—endless.

G5620.definition:
ὥστε hṓste, hoce'-teh; from G5613 and G5037; so too, i.e. thus therefore (in various relations
 of consecution, as follow):—(insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch)
 that, therefore, to, wherefore.

G5621.definition:
ὠτίον ōtíon, o-tee'-on; diminutive of G3775; an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the
 lobe of the ear:—ear.

G5622.definition:
ὠφέλεια ōphéleia, o-fel'-i-ah; from a derivative of the base of G5624; usefulness, i.e.
 benefit:—advantage, profit.

G5623.definition:
ὠφελέω ōpheléō, o-fel-eh'-o; from the same as G5622; to be useful, i.e. to benefit:—advantage,
 better, prevail, profit.

G5624.definition:
ὠφέλιμος ōphélimos, o-fel'-ee-mos; from a form of G3786; helpful or serviceable, i.e.
 advantageous:—profit(-able).

G563.definition:
ἀπερισπάστως aperispástōs, ap-er-is-pas-toce'; adverb from a compound of G1 (as a negative participle) and a presumed
 derivative of G4049; undistractedly, i.e. free from (domestic)
 solicitude:—without distraction.

G564.definition:
ἀπερίτμητος aperítmētos, ap-er-eet'-may-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4059; 
 uncircumcised (figuratively):—uncircumcised.

G565.definition:
ἀπέρχομαι apérchomai, ap-erkh'-om-ahee; from G575 and G2064; to go off (i.e. depart), aside (i.e. apart) or
 behind (i.e. follow), literally or figuratively:—come, depart, go
 (aside, away, back, out, … ways), pass away, be past.

G569.definition:
ἀπιστέω apistéō, ap-is-teh'-o; from G571; to be unbelieving, i.e. (transitively) disbelieve, or (by
 implication) disobey:—believe not.

G57.definition: ἄγνωστος ágnōstos, ag'-noce-tos'; from G1 (as negative particle) and G1110; unknown:—unknown.

G570.definition:
ἀπιστία apistía, ap-is-tee'-ah; from G571; faithlessness, i.e. (negatively) disbelief (lack of
 Christian faith), or (positively) unfaithfulness
 (disobedience):—unbelief.

G571.definition:
ἄπιστος ápistos, ap'-is-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G4103; (actively) disbelieving,
 i.e. without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively)
 untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing):—that believeth not,
 faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing).

G572.definition:
ἁπλότης haplótēs, hap-lot'-ace; from G573; singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without
 dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious
 bestowal):—bountifulness, liberal(-ity), simplicity, singleness.

G573.definition:
ἁπλοῦς haploûs, hap-looce'; probably from G1 (as a particle of union) and the base of G4120; 
 properly, folded together, i.e. single (figuratively, clear):—single.

G574.definition:
ἁπλῶς haplōs, hap-loce'; adverb from G573 (in the objective sense of G572); bountifully;
 --liberally.

G575.definition:
ἀπό apó, apo'; a primary particle; "off," i.e. away (from something near), in various
 senses (of place, time, or relation; literal or figurative):—(X
 here-)after, ago, at, because of, before, by (the space of), for(-th),
 from, in, (out) of, off, (up-)on(-ce), since, with.

G576.definition:
ἀποβαίνω apobaínō, ap-ob-ah'-ee-no; from G575 and the base of G939; literally, to disembark; figuratively,
 to eventuate:—become, go out, turn.

G577.definition: ἀποβάλλω apobállō, ap-ob-al'-lo; from G575 and G906; to throw off; figuratively, to lose:—cast away.

G578.definition:
ἀποβλέπω apoblépō, ap-ob-lep'-o; from G575 and G991; to look away from everything else, i.e.
 (figuratively) intently regard:—have respect.

G579.definition:
ἀπόβλητος apóblētos, ap-ob'-lay-tos; from G577; cast off, i.e. (figuratively) such as to be rejected:—be
 refused.

G58.definition:
ἀγορά agorá, ag-or-ah'; from ἀγείρω ageírō (to gather; probably akin to G1453); properly, the
 town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or
 thoroughfare:—market(-place), street.

G580.definition: ἀποβολή apobolḗ, ap-ob-ol-ay'; from G577; rejection; figuratively, loss:—casting away, loss.

G581.definition:
†ἀπογενόμενος apogenómenos, ap-og-en-om'-en-os; past participle of a compound of G575 and G1096; absent, i.e. deceased
 (figuratively, renounced):—being dead.

G582.definition: ἀπογραφή apographḗ, ap-og-raf-ay'; from G583; an enrollment; by implication, an assessment:—taxing.

G583.definition:
ἀπογράφω apográphō, ap-og-raf'-o; from G575 and G1125; to write off (a copy or list), i.e. enrol:—tax,
 write.

G584.definition:
ἀποδείκνυμι apodeíknymi, ap-od-ike'-noo-mee; from G575 and G1166; to show off, i.e. exhibit; figuratively, to
 demonstrate, i.e. accredit:—(ap-)prove, set forth, shew.

G585.definition: ἀπόδειξις apódeixis, ap-od'-ike-sis; from G584; manifestation:—demonstration.

G586.definition:
†ἀποδεκατόω apodekatóō, ap-od-ek-at-o'-o; from G575 and G1183; to tithe (as debtor or creditor):—(give, pay,
 take) tithe.

G587.definition: ἀπόδεκτος apódektos, ap-od'-ek-tos; from G588; accepted, i.e. agreeable:—acceptable.

G588.definition:
ἀποδέχομαι apodéchomai, ap-od-ekh'-om-ahee; from G575 and G1209; to take fully, i.e. welcome (persons), approve
 (things):—accept, receive (gladly).

G589.definition:
ἀποδημέω apodēméō, ap-od-ay-meh'-o; from G590; to go abroad, i.e. visit a foreign land:—go (travel) into a
 far country, journey.

G59.definition:
ἀγοράζω agorázō, ag-or-ad'-zo; from G58; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase;
 specially, to redeem:—buy, redeem.

G590.definition:
ἀπόδημος apódēmos, ap-od'-ay-mos; from G575 and G1218; absent from one's own people, i.e. a foreign
 traveller:—taking a far journey.

G591.definition:
ἀποδίδωμι apodídōmi, ap-od-eed'-o-mee; from G575 and G1325; to give away, i.e. up, over, back, etc. (in various
 applications):—deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be
 made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell,
 yield.

G592.definition:
ἀποδιορίζω apodiorízō, ap-od-ee-or-id'-zo; from G575 and a compound of G223 and G3724; to disjoin (by a boundary,
 figuratively, a party):—separate.

G593.definition:
ἀποδοκιμάζω apodokimázō, ap-od-ok-ee-mad'-zo; from G575 and G1381; to disapprove, i.e. (by implication) to
 repudiate:—disallow, reject.

G594.definition: ἀποδοχή apodochḗ, ap-od-okh-ay'; from G588; acceptance:—acceptation.

G595.definition:
ἀπόθεσις apóthesis, ap-oth'-es-is; from G659; a laying aside (literally or figuratively):—putting away
 (off).

G596.definition: ἀποθήκη apothḗkē, ap-oth-ay'-kay; from G659; a repository, i.e. granary:—barn, garner.

G597.definition: ἀποθησαυρίζω apothēsaurízō, ap-oth-ay-sow-rid'-zo; from G575 and G2343; to treasure away:—lay up in store.

G598.definition: ἀποθλίβω apothlíbō, ap-oth-lee'-bo; from G575 and G2346; to crowd (from every side):—press.

G599.definition:
†ἀποθνήσκω apothnḗskō, ap-oth-nace'-ko; from G575 and G2348; to die off (literally or figuratively):—be dead,
 death, die, lie a-dying, be slain (X with).

G6.definition: †Ἄβελ Ábel, ab'-el; of Hebrew origin (H1893); Abel, the son of Adam:—Abel.

G60.definition:
ἀγοραῖος agoraîos, ag-or-ah'-yos; from G58; relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by
 implication, vulgar:—baser sort, low.

G600.definition:
ἀποκαθίστημι apokathístēmi, ap-ok-ath-is'-tay-mee; from G575 and G2525; to reconstitute (in health, home or
 organization):—restore (again).

G601.definition: ἀποκαλύπτω apokalýptō, ap-ok-al-oop'-to; from G575 and G2572; to take off the cover, i.e. disclose:—reveal.

G602.definition:
ἀποκάλυψις apokálypsis, ap-ok-al'-oop-sis; from G601; disclosure:—appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be
 revealed, revelation.

G603.definition:
ἀποκαραδοκία apokaradokía, ap-ok-ar-ad-ok-ee'-ah; from a comparative of G575 and a compound of κάρα kára (the head) and G1380
 (in the sense of watching); intense anticipation:—earnest
 expectation.

G604.definition: ἀποκαταλλάσσω apokatallássō, ap-ok-at-al-las'-so; from G575 and G2644; to reconcile fully:—reconcile.

G605.definition: ἀποκατάστασις apokatástasis, ap-ok-at-as'-tas-is; from G600; reconstitution:—restitution.

G606.definition:
ἀπόκειμαι apókeimai, ap-ok'-i-mahee; from G575 and G2749; to be reserved; figuratively, to await:—be
 appointed, (be) laid up.

G607.definition: ἀποκεφαλίζω apokephalízō, ap-ok-ef-al-id'-zo; from G575 and G2776; to decapitate:—behead.

G608.definition: ἀποκλείω apokleíō, ap-ok-li'-o; from G575 and G2808; to close fully:—shut up.

G609.definition:
ἀποκόπτω apokóptō, ap-ok-op'-to; from G575 and G2875; to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate
 (the privy parts):—cut off. Compare G2699.

G61.definition:
ἄγρα ágra, ag'-rah; from G71; (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul
 (of fish):—draught.

G610.definition:
ἀπόκριμα apókrima, ap-ok'-ree-mah; from G611 (in its original sense of judging); a judicial
 decision:—sentence.

G611.definition:
ἀποκρίνομαι apokrínomai, ap-ok-ree'-nom-ahee; from G575 and κρίνω krínō; to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to
 respond; by Hebraism (compare H6030) to begin to speak (where an
 address is expected):—answer.

G612.definition: ἀπόκρισις apókrisis, ap-ok'-ree-sis; from G611; a response:—answer.

G613.definition:
ἀποκρύπτω apokrýptō, ap-ok-roop'-to; from G575 and G2928; to conceal away (i.e. fully); figuratively, to keep
 secret:—hide.

G614.definition: ἀπόκρυφος apókryphos, ap-ok'-roo-fos; from G613; secret; by implication, treasured:—hid, kept secret.

G615.definition:
†ἀποκτείνω apokteínō, ap-ok-ti'-no; from G575 and κτείνω kteínō (to slay); to kill outright; figuratively, to
 destroy:—put to death, kill, slay.

G616.definition:
ἀποκυέω apokyéō, ap-ok-oo-eh'-o; from G575 and the base of G2949; to breed forth, i.e. (by transference)
 to generate (figuratively):—beget, produce.

G617.definition: †ἀποκυλίω apokylíō, ap-ok-oo-lee'-o; from G575 and G2947; to roll away:—roll away (back).

G618.definition:
ἀπολαμβάνω apolambánō, ap-ol-am-ban'-o; from G575 and G2983; to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also
 to take aside:—receive, take.

G619.definition:
ἀπόλαυσις apólausis, ap-ol'-ow-sis; from a comparative of G575 and λαύω laúō (to enjoy); full
 enjoyment:—enjoy(-ment).

G62.definition:
ἀγράμματος agrámmatos, ag-ram-mat-os; from G1 (as negative particle) and G1121; unlettered, i.e.
 illiterate:—unlearned.

G620.definition:
ἀπολείπω apoleípō, ap-ol-ipe'-o; from G575 and G3007; to leave behind (passively, remain); by
 implication, to forsake:—leave, remain.

G622.definition:
ἀπόλλυμι apóllymi, ap-ol'-loo-mee; from G575 and the base of G3639; to destroy fully (reflexively, to
 perish, or lose), literally or figuratively:—destroy, die, lose, mar,
 perish.

G623.definition: Ἀπολλύων Apollýōn, ap-ol-loo'-ohn; active participle of G622; a destroyer (i.e. Satan):—Apollyon.

G624.definition:
Ἀπολλωνία Apollōnía, ap-ol-lo-nee'-ah; from the pagan deity Ἀπόλλων Apóllōn (i.e. the sun; from G622); Apollonia, a
 place in Macedonia:—Apollonia.

G625.definition: †Ἀπολλῶς Apollōs, ap-ol-loce'; probably from the same as G624; Apollos, an Israelite:—Apollos.

G626.definition:
ἀπολογέομαι apologéomai, ap-ol-og-eh'-om-ahee; middle voice from a compound of G575 and G3056; to give an account
 (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self):—answer (for self),
 make defence, excuse (self), speak for self.

G627.definition:
ἀπολογία apología, ap-ol-og-ee'-ah; from the same as G626; a plea ("apology"):—answer (for self), clearing
 of self, defence.

G628.definition:
ἀπολούω apoloúō, ap-ol-oo'-o; from G575 and G3068; to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted
 (reflexively):—wash (away).

G629.definition:
ἀπολύτρωσις apolýtrōsis, ap-ol-oo'-tro-sis; from a compound of G575 and G3083; (the act) ransom in full, i.e.
 (figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian
 salvation:—deliverance, redemption.

G63.definition:
ἀγραυλέω agrauléō, ag-row-leh'-o; from G68 and G832 (in the sense of G833); to camp out:—abide in the
 field.

G630.definition:
ἀπολύω apolýō, ap-ol-oo'-o; from G575 and G3089; to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release,
 dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or
 (specially) divorce:—(let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go,
 loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty.

G631.definition:
†ἀπομάσσομαι apomássomai, ap-om-as'-som-ahee; middle voice from G575 and μάσσω mássō (to squeeze, knead, smear); to scrape
 away:—wipe off.

G632.definition: ἀπονέμω aponémō, ap-on-em'-o; from G575 and the base of G3551; to apportion, i.e. bestow:—give.

G633.definition:
ἀπονίπτω aponíptō, ap-on-ip'-to; from G575 and G3538; to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands
 symbolically):—wash.

G634.definition: ἀποπίπτω apopíptō, ap-op-ip'-to; from G575 and G4098; to fall off:—fall.

G635.definition:
ἀποπλανάω apoplanáō, ap-op-lan-ah'-o; from G575 and G4105; to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray
 (from truth):—err, seduce.

G636.definition: ἀποπλέω apopléō, ap-op-leh'-o; from G575 and G4126; to set sail:—sail away.

G638.definition: ἀποπνίγω apopnígō, ap-op-nee'-go; from G575 and G4155; to stifle (by drowning or overgrowth):—choke.

G639.definition:
ἀπορέω aporéō, ap-or-eh'-o; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G4198; to
 have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally):—(stand in) doubt, be
 perplexed.

G64.definition: ἀγρεύω agreúō, ag-rew'-o; from G61; to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap:—catch.

G640.definition: ἀπορία aporía, ap-or-ee'-a; from the same as G639; a (state of) quandary:—perplexity.

G641.definition: †ἀποῤῥίπτω aporrhíptō, ap-or-hrip'-to; from G575 and G4496; to hurl off, i.e. precipitate (oneself):—cast.

G642.definition:
ἀπορφανίζω aporphanízō, ap-or-fan-id'-zo; from G575 and a derivative of G3737; to bereave wholly, i.e.
 (figuratively) separate (from intercourse):—take.

G644.definition:
ἀποσκίασμα aposkíasma, ap-os-kee'-as-mah; from a compound of G575 and a derivative of G4639; a shading off, i.e.
 obscuration:—shadow.

G645.definition:
ἀποσπάω apospáō, ap-os-pah'-o; from G575 and G4685; to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a
 sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire
 (personally or factiously):—(with-)draw (away), after we were gotten
 from.

G646.definition:
ἀποστασία apostasía, ap-os-tas-ee'-ah; feminine of the same as G647; defection from truth (properly, the
 state) ("apostasy"):—falling away, forsake.

G647.definition:
ἀποστάσιον apostásion, ap-os-tas'-ee-on; neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of G868; properly,
 something separative, i.e. (specially) divorce:—(writing of)
 divorcement.

G648.definition: ἀποστεγάζω apostegázō, ap-os-teg-ad'-zo; from G575 and a derivative of G4721; to unroof:—uncover.

G649.definition:
ἀποστέλλω apostéllō, ap-os-tel'-lo; from G575 and G4724; set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out
 (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively:—put in, send
 (away, forth, out), set (at liberty).

G65.definition: ἀγριέλαιος agriélaios, ag-ree-el'-ah-yos; from G66 and G1636; an oleaster:—olive tree (which is) wild.

G650.definition:
†ἀποστερέω aposteréō, ap-os-ter-eh'-o; from G575 and στερέω steréō (to deprive); to despoil:—defraud, destitute,
 kept back by fraud.

G651.definition: ἀποστολή apostolḗ, ap-os-tol-ay'; from G649; commission, i.e. (specially) apostolate:—apostleship.

G653.definition:
ἀποστοματίζω apostomatízō, ap-os-tom-at-id'-zo; from G575 and a (presumed) derivative of G4750; to speak off-hand
 (properly, dictate), i.e. to catechize (in an invidious
 manner):—provoke to speak.

G654.definition:
ἀποστρέφω apostréphō, ap-os-tref'-o; from G575 and G4762; to turn away or back (literally or
 figuratively):—bring again, pervert, turn away (from).

G655.definition: ἀποστυγέω apostygéō, ap-os-toog-eh'-o; from G575 and the base of G4767; to detest utterly:—abhor.

G656.definition: ἀποσυνάγωγος aposynágōgos, ap-os-oon-ag'-o-gos; from G575 and G4864; excommunicated:—(put) out of the synagogue(-s).

G657.definition:
ἀποτάσσομαι apotássomai, ap-ot-as'-som-ahee; middle voice from G575 and G5021; literally, to say adieu (by departing
 or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce:—bid farewell, forsake,
 take leave, send away.

G658.definition: ἀποτελέω apoteléō, ap-ot-el-eh'-o; from G575 and G5055; to complete entirely, i.e. consummate:—finish.

G659.definition:
ἀποτίθημι apotíthēmi, ap-ot-eeth'-ay-mee; from G575 and G5087; to put away (literally or figuratively):—cast off,
 lay apart (aside, down), put away (off).

G66.definition:
ἄγριος ágrios, ag'-ree-os; from G68; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or
 figuratively (fierce):—wild, raging.

G660.definition: ἀποτινάσσω apotinássō, ap-ot-in-as'-so; from G575 and τινάσσω tinássō (to jostle); to brush off:—shake off.

G661.definition: ἀποτίνω apotínō, ap-ot-ee'-no; from G575 and G5099; to pay in full:—repay.

G662.definition: ἀποτολμάω apotolmáō, ap-ot-ol-mah'-o; from G575 and G5111; to venture plainly:—be very bold.

G663.definition:
ἀποτομία apotomía, ap-ot-om-ee'-ah; from the base of G664; (figuratively) decisiveness, i.e.
 rigor:—severity.

G664.definition:
ἀποτόμως apotómōs, ap-ot-om'-oce; adverb from a derivative of a comparative of G575 and τέμνω témnō (to cut); 
 abruptly, i.e. peremptorily:—sharply(-ness).

G665.definition:
ἀποτρέπω apotrépō, ap-ot-rep'-o; from G575 and the base of G5157; to deflect, i.e. (reflexively)
 avoid:—turn away.

G666.definition: ἀπουσία apousía, ap-oo-see'-ah; from the participle of G548; a being away:—absence.

G667.definition:
ἀποφέρω apophérō, ap-of-er'-o; from G575 and G5342; to bear off (literally or relatively):—bring,
 carry (away).

G668.definition: ἀποφεύγω apopheúgō, ap-of-yoo'-go; from G575 and G5343; (figuratively) to escape:—escape.

G669.definition:
ἀποφθέγγομαι apophthéngomai, ap-of-theng'-om-ahee; from G575 and G5350; to enunciate plainly, i.e. declare:—say, speak
 forth, utterance.

G67.definition:
Ἀγρίππας Agríppas, ag-rip'-pas; apparently from G66 and G2462; wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the
 Herods:—Agrippa.

G670.definition: ἀποφορτίζομαι apophortízomai, ap-of-or-tid'-zom-ahee; from G575 and the middle voice of G5412; to unload:—unlade.

G671.definition:
ἀπόχρησις apóchrēsis, ap-okh'-ray-sis; from a compound of G575 and G5530; the act of using up, i.e.
 consumption:—using.

G672.definition: ἀποχωρέω apochōréō, ap-okh-o-reh'-o; from G575 and G5562; to go away:—depart.

G673.definition:
ἀποχωρίζω apochōrízō, ap-okh-o-rid'-zo; from G575 and G5563; to rend apart; reflexively, to separate:—depart
 (asunder).

G674.definition: ἀποψύχω apopsýchō, ap-ops-oo'-kho; from G575 and G5594; to breathe out, i.e. faint:—hearts failing.

G675.definition:
Ἄππιος Áppios, ap'-pee-os; of Latin origin; (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius,
 the name of a Roman:—Appii.

G676.definition:
ἀπρόσιτος aprósitos, ap-ros'-ee-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of
 G4314 and εἶμι eîmi (to go); inaccessible:—which no man can approach.

G678.definition:
ἀπροσωπολήπτως aprosōpolḗptōs, ap-ros-o-pol-ape'-tos; adverb from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed
 derivative of a presumed compound of G4383 and G2983 (compare G4381); in
 a way not accepting the person, i.e. impartially:—without respect of
 persons.

G679.definition:
ἄπταιστος áptaistos, ap-tah'-ee-stos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4417; not
 stumbling, i.e. (figuratively) without sin:—from falling.

G68.definition:
ἀγρός agrós, ag-ros'; from G71; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country;
 specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet:—country, farm, piece of ground, land.

G681.definition:
†ἅπτω háptō, hap'-to; a primary verb; properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on
 fire:—kindle, light.

G682.definition: Ἀπφία Apphía, ap-fee'-a; probably of foreign origin; Apphia, a woman of Collosæ:—Apphia.

G683.definition:
†ἀπωθέομαι apōthéomai, ap-o-theh'-om-ahee; from G575 and the middle voice of ὠθέω ōthéō or ὤθω ṓthō (to shove); to push
 off, figuratively, to reject:—cast away, put away (from), thrust away
 (from).

G684.definition:
ἀπώλεια apṓleia, ap-o'-li-a; from a presumed derivative of G622; ruin or loss (physical, spiritual
 or eternal):—damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X
 perish, pernicious ways, waste.

G685.definition:
ἀρά ará, ar-ah'; probably from G142; properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by
 implication) imprecation:—curse.

G686.definition:
ἄρα ára, ar'-ah; probably from G142 (through the idea of drawing a conclusion); a
 particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as
 follows):—haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be,
 then, therefore, truly, wherefore. Often used in connection with other
 particles, especially G1065 or G3767 (after) or G1487 (before). Compare
 also G687.

G687.definition:
ἆρα âra, ar'-ah; a form of G686, denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is
 presumed:—therefore.

G688.definition: Ἀραβία Arabía, ar-ab-ee'-ah; of Hebrew origin (H6152); Arabia, a region of Asia:—Arabia.

G689.definition: †Ἀράμ Arám, ar-am'; of Hebrew origin (H7410); Aram (i.e. Ram), an Israelite:—Aram.

G69.definition:
ἀγρυπνέω agrypnéō, ag-roop-neh'-o; ultimately from G1 (as negative particle) and G5258; to be sleepless,
 i.e. keep awake:—watch.

G690.definition: Ἄραψ Áraps, ar'-aps; from G688; an Arab or native of Arabia:—Arabian.

G691.definition: ἀργέω argéō, arg-eh'-o; from G692; to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay:—linger.

G692.definition:
ἀργός argós, ar-gos'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2041; inactive, i.e. unemployed;
 (by implication) lazy, useless:—barren, idle, slow.

G693.definition: †ἀργύρεος argýreos, ar-goo'-reh-os; from G696; made of silver:—(of) silver.

G694.definition:
ἀργύριον argýrion, ar-goo'-ree-on; neuter of a presumed derivative of G696; silvery, i.e. (by implication)
 cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel):—money, (piece
 of) silver (piece).

G695.definition: ἀργυροκόπος argyrokópos, ar-goo-rok-op'-os; from G696 and G2875; a beater (i.e. worker) of silver:—silversmith.

G696.definition:
ἄργυρος árgyros, ar'-goo-ros; from ἀργός argós (shining); silver (the metal, in the articles or
 coin):—silver.

G697.definition:
†Ἄρειος Πάγος Áreios Págos, ar'-i-os pag'-os; from Ἄρης Árēs (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of
 G4078; rock of Ares, a place in Athens:—Areopagus, Mars' Hill.

G698.definition:
Ἀρεοπαγίτης Areopagítēs, ar-eh-op-ag-ee'-tace; from G697; an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars'
 Hill:—Areopagite.

G699.definition: †ἀρεσκεία areskeía, ar-es'-ki-ah; from a derivative of G700; complaisance:—pleasing.

G7.definition: Ἀβιά Abiá, ab-ee-ah'; of Hebrew origin (H29); Abijah, the name of two Israelites:—Abia.

G70.definition: ἀγρυπνία agrypnía, ag-roop-nee'-ah; from G69; sleeplessness, i.e. a keeping awake:—watch.

G700.definition:
ἀρέσκω aréskō, ar-es'-ko; probably from G142 (through the idea of exciting emotion); to be
 agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so):—please.

G701.definition:
ἀρεστός arestós, ar-es-tos'; from G700; agreeable; by implication, fit:—(things that) please(-ing),
 reason.

G702.definition: Ἀρέτας Arétas, ar-et'-as; of foreign origin; Aretas, an Arabian:—Aretas.

G703.definition:
ἀρέτη arétē, ar-et'-ay; from the same as G730; properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence
 (intrinsic or attributed):—praise, virtue.

G704.definition: ἀρήν arḗn, ar-ane'; perhaps the same as G730; a lamb (as a male):—lamb.

G705.definition: ἀριθμέω arithméō, ar-ith-meh'-o; from G706; to enumerate or count:—number.

G706.definition: ἀριθμός arithmós, ar-ith-mos'; from G142; a number (as reckoned up):—number.

G707.definition:
Ἀριμαθαία Arimathaía, ar-ee-math-ah'-ee-ah; of Hebrew origin (H7414); Arimathæa (or Ramah), a place in
 Palestine:—Arimathæa.

G708.definition:
Ἀρίσταρχος Arístarchos, ar-is'-tar-khos; from the same as G712 and G757; best ruling; Aristarchus, a
 Macedonian:—Aristarchus.

G709.definition: ἀριστάω aristáō, ar-is-tah'-o; from G712; to take the principle meal:—dine.

G71.definition:
ἄγω ágō, ag'-o; a primary verb; properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive,
 (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively)
 induce:—be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open.

G710.definition:
ἀριστερός aristerós, ar-is-ter-os'; apparently a comparative of the same as G712; the left hand (as
 second-best):—left (hand).

G711.definition:
Ἀριστόβουλος Aristóboulos, ar-is-tob'-oo-los; from the same as G712 and G1012; best counselling; Aristoboulus, a
 Christian:—Aristobulus.

G712.definition:
ἄριστον áriston, ar'-is-ton; apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as G730; the best meal
 (or breakfast; perhaps from ἦρι ēri ("early")), i.e. luncheon:—dinner.

G713.definition: ἀρκετός arketós, ar-ket-os'; from G714; satisfactory:—enough, suffice (-ient).

G714.definition:
ἀρκέω arkéō, ar-keh'-o; apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to G142 through the idea
 of raising a barrier); properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to
 avail (figuratively, be satisfactory):—be content, be enough,
 suffice, be sufficient.

G715.definition: †ἄρκτος árktos, ark'-tos; probably from G714; a bear (as obstructing by ferocity):—bear.

G716.definition:
ἅρμα hárma, har'-mah; probably from G142 (perhaps with G1 (as a particle of union) prefixed); 
 a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare G719)):—chariot.

G717.definition:
†Ἀρμαγεδδών Armageddṓn, ar-mag-ed-dohn'; of Hebrew origin (H2022 and H4023); Armageddon (or Har-Meggiddon), a
 symbolic name:—Armageddon.

G718.definition:
ἁρμόζω harmózō, har-mod'-zo; from G719; to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to
 betroth):—espouse.

G719.definition: ἁρμός harmós, har-mos'; from the same as G716; an articulation (of the body):—joint.

G72.definition:
ἀγωγή agōgḗ, ag-o-gay'; reduplicated from G71; a bringing up, i.e. mode of living:—manner of
 life.

G720.definition:
ἀρνέομαι arnéomai, ar-neh'-om-ahee; perhaps from G1 (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of G4483; 
 to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate:—deny, refuse.

G721.definition: ἀρνίον arníon, ar-nee'-on; diminutive from G704; a lambkin:—lamb.

G722.definition: †ἀροτριόω arotrióō, ar-ot-ree-o'-o; from G723; to plow:—plough.

G723.definition: ἄροτρον árotron, ar'-ot-ron; from ἀρόω aróō (to till); a plow:—plough.

G724.definition: ἁρπαγή harpagḗ, har-pag-ay'; from G726; pillage (properly abstract):—extortion, ravening, spoiling.

G725.definition: ἁρπαγμός harpagmós, har-pag-mos'; from G726; plunder (properly concrete):—robbery.

G726.definition:
ἁρπάζω harpázō, har-pad'-zo; from a derivative of G138; to seize (in various applications):—catch
 (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force).

G727.definition: ἅρπαξ hárpax, har'-pax; from G726; rapacious:—extortion, ravening.

G728.definition:
ἀῤῥαβών arrhabṓn, ar-hrab-ohn'; of Hebrew origin (H6162); a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or
 property given in advance as security for the rest:—earnest.

G73.definition:
ἀγών agṓn, ag-one'; from G71; properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by
 implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or
 anxiety:—conflict, contention, fight, race.

G731.definition:
ἄῤῥητος árrhētos, ar'-hray-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and the same as G4490; unsaid, i.e. (by
 implication) inexpressible:—unspeakable.

G732.definition:
ἄῤῥωστος árrhōstos, ar'-hroce-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4517; 
 infirm:—sick (folk, -ly).

G733.definition:
ἀρσενοκοίτης arsenokoítēs, ar-sen-ok-oy'-tace; from G730 and G2845; a sodomite:—abuser of (that defile) self with
 mankind.

G734.definition:
Ἀρτεμάς Artemás, ar-tem-as'; contracted from a compound of G735 and G1435; gift of Artemis; Artemas
 (or Artemidorus), a Christian:—Artemas.

G735.definition:
Ἄρτεμις Ártemis, ar'-tem-is; probably from the same as G736; prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian
 goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities:—Diana.

G736.definition:
ἀρτέμων artémōn, ar-tem'-ohn; from a derivative of G737; properly, something ready (or else more
 remotely from G142 (compare G740); something hung up), i.e. (specially)
 the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel:—mainsail.

G737.definition:
ἄρτι árti, ar'-tee; adverb from a derivative of G142 (compare G740) through the idea of
 suspension; just now:—this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after),
 hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present.

G738.definition:
ἀρτιγέννητος artigénnētos, ar-teeg-en'-nay-tos; from G737 and G1084; just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young
 convert:—new born.

G739.definition: ἄρτιος ártios, ar'-tee-os; from G737; fresh, i.e. (by implication) complete:—perfect.

G74.definition:
ἀγωνία agōnía, ag-o-nee'-ah; from G73; a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively)
 anguish:—agony.

G740.definition: ἄρτος ártos, ar'-tos; from G142; bread (as raised) or a loaf:—(shew-)bread, loaf.

G741.definition:
ἀρτύω artýō, ar-too'-o; from a presumed derivative of G142; to prepare, i.e. spice (with
 stimulating condiments):—season.

G742.definition:
Ἀρφαξάδ Arphaxád, ar-fax-ad'; of Hebrew origin (H775); Arphaxad, a post-diluvian
 patriarch:—Arphaxad.

G743.definition: ἀρχάγγελος archángelos, ar-khang'-el-os; from G757 and G32; a chief angel:—archangel.

G744.definition: ἀρχαῖος archaîos, ar-khah'-yos; from G746; original or primeval:—(them of) old (time).

G745.definition:
Ἀρχέλαος Archélaos, ar-khel'-ah-os; from G757 and G2994; people-ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish
 king:—Archelaus.

G746.definition:
ἀρχή archḗ, ar-khay'; from G756; (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief
 (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank):—beginning,
 corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality,
 principle, rule.

G747.definition: ἀρχηγός archēgós, ar-khay-gos'; from G746 and G71; a chief leader:—author, captain, prince.

G748.definition: ἀρχιερατικός archieratikós, ar-khee-er-at-ee-kos'; from G746 and a derivative of G2413; high-priestly:—of the high-priest.

G749.definition:
ἀρχιερεύς archiereús, ar-khee-er-yuce'; from G746 and G2409; the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically,
 Christ); by extension a chief priest:—chief (high) priest, chief of
 the priests.

G75.definition:
ἀγωνίζομαι agōnízomai, ag-o-nid'-zom-ahee; from G73; to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively
 (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to
 accomplish something):—fight, labor fervently, strive.

G750.definition: ἀρχιποίμην archipoímēn, ar-khee-poy'-mane; from G746 and G4166; a head shepherd:—chief shepherd.

G751.definition: Ἄρχιππος Árchippos, ar'-khip-pos; from G746 and G2462; horse-ruler; Archippus, a Christian:—Archippus.

G752.definition:
ἀρχισυνάγωγος archisynágōgos, ar-khee-soon-ag'-o-gos; from G746 and G4864; director of the synagogue services:—(chief) ruler
 of the synagogue.

G753.definition:
ἀρχιτέκτων architéktōn, ar-khee-tek'-tone; from G746 and G5045; a chief constructor, i.e.
 "architect":—masterbuilder.

G754.definition:
ἀρχιτελώνης architelṓnēs, ar-khee-tel-o'-nace; from G746 and G5057; a principle tax-gatherer:—chief among the
 publicans.

G755.definition:
ἀρχιτρίκλινος architríklinos, ar-khee-tree'-klee-nos; from G746 and a compound of G5140 and G2827 (a dinner-bed, because
 composed of three couches); director of the entertainment:—governor
 (ruler) of the feast.

G757.definition:
ἄρχω árchō, ar'-kho; a primary verb; to be first (in political rank or power):—reign
 (rule) over.

G758.definition:
ἄρχων árchōn, ar'-khone; present participle of G757; a first (in rank or power):—chief (ruler),
 magistrate, prince, ruler.

G759.definition:
ἄρωμα árōma, ar'-o-mah; from G142 (in the sense of sending off scent); an aromatic:—(sweet)
 spice.

G76.definition:
Ἀδάμ Adám, ad-am'; of Hebrew origin (H121); Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man
 (as his representative):—Adam.

G760.definition: †Ἀσά Asá, as-ah'; of Hebrew origin (H609); Asa, an Israelite:—Asa.

G761.definition:
ἀσάλευτος asáleutos, as-al'-yoo-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4531; unshaken,
 i.e. (by implication) immovable (figuratively):—which cannot be
 moved, unmovable.

G762.definition:
ἄσβεστος ásbestos, as'-bes-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4570; not
 extinguished, i.e. (by implication) perpetual:—not to be quenched,
 unquenchable.

G763.definition:
ἀσέβεια asébeia, as-eb'-i-ah; from G765; impiety, i.e. (by implication)
 wickedness:—ungodly(-liness).

G764.definition:
ἀσεβέω asebéō, as-eb-eh'-o; from G765; to be (by implied act) impious or wicked:—commit (live,
 that after should live) ungodly.

G765.definition:
ἀσεβής asebḗs, as-eb-ace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4576; 
 irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked:—ungodly (man).

G766.definition:
ἀσέλγεια asélgeia, as-elg'-i-a; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed
 σελγής selgḗs (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning
 continent); licentiousness (sometimes including other
 vices):—filthy, lasciviousness, wantonness.

G767.definition:
ἄσημος ásēmos, as'-ay-mos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G4591; unmarked, i.e.
 (figuratively) ignoble:—mean.

G768.definition: Ἀσήρ Asḗr, as-ayr'; of Hebrew origin (H836); Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe:—Aser.

G769.definition:
ἀσθένεια asthéneia, as-then'-i-ah; from G772; feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady;
 morally, frailty:—disease, infirmity, sickness, weakness.

G77.definition:
ἀδάπανος adápanos, ad-ap'-an-os; from G1 (as negative particle); and G1160; costless, i.e.
 gratuitous:—without expense.

G770.definition:
ἀσθενέω asthenéō, as-then-eh'-o; from G772; to be feeble (in any sense):—be diseased, impotent folk
 (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak.

G771.definition: ἀσθένημα asthénēma, as-then'-ay-mah; from G770; a scruple of conscience:—infirmity.

G772.definition:
ἀσθενής asthenḗs, as-then-ace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G4599; strengthless (in
 various applications, literal, figurative and moral):—more feeble,
 impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing).

G773.definition:
Ἀσία Asía, as-ee'-ah; of uncertain derivation; Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its
 western shore:—Asia.

G774.definition: Ἀσιανός Asianós, as-ee-an-os'; from G773; an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia:—of Asia.

G775.definition:
Ἀσιάρχης Asiárchēs, as-ee-ar'-khace; from G773 and G746; an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in
 a city of Asia Minor:—chief of Asia.

G776.definition: ἀσιτία asitía, as-ee-tee'-ah; from G777; fasting (the state):—abstinence.

G777.definition:
ἄσιτος ásitos, as'-ee-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G4621; without (taking)
 food:—fasting.

G778.definition:
ἀσκέω askéō, as-keh'-o; probably from the same as G4632; to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively)
 train (by implication, strive):—exercise.

G779.definition:
ἀσκός askós, as-kos'; from the same as G778; a leathern (or skin) bag used as a
 bottle:—bottle.

G78.definition: Ἀδδί Addí, ad-dee'; probably of Hebrew origin (compare H5716); Addi, an Israelite:—Addi.

G780.definition: ἀσμένως asménōs, as-men'-oce; adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237; with pleasure:—gladly.

G781.definition: ἄσοφος ásophos, as'-of-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G4680; unwise:—fool.

G782.definition:
†ἀσπάζομαι aspázomai, as-pad'-zom-ahee; from G1 (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of G4685; to enfold
 in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to
 welcome:—embrace, greet, salute, take leave.

G783.definition: ἀσπασμός aspasmós, as-pas-mos'; from G782; a greeting (in person or by letter):—greeting, salutation.

G784.definition:
ἄσπιλος áspilos, as'-pee-los; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G4695; unblemished (physically or
 morally):—without spot, unspotted.

G785.definition:
ἀσπίς aspís, as-pece'; of uncertain derivation; a buckler (or round shield); used of a
 serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp":—asp.

G786.definition:
ἄσπονδος áspondos, as'-pon-dos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4689; literally,
 without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by
 implication) truceless:—implacable, truce-breaker.

G787.definition: ἀσσάριον assárion, as-sar'-ee-on; of Latin origin; an assarius or as, a Roman coin:—farthing.

G788.definition:
ἆσσον âsson, as'-son; neuter comparative of the base of G1451; more nearly, i.e. very
 near:—close.

G789.definition: Ἄσσος Ássos, as'-sos; probably of foreign origin; Assus, a city of Asia MInor:—Assos.

G79.definition: ἀδελφή adelphḗ, ad-el-fay'; feminine of G80; a sister (naturally or ecclesiastically):—sister.

G790.definition:
ἀστατέω astatéō, as-tat-eh'-o; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2476; to be
 non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless:—have no certain
 dwelling-place.

G791.definition: ἀστεῖος asteîos, as-ti'-os; from ἄστυ ásty (a city); urbane, i.e. (by implication) handsome:—fair.

G792.definition:
ἀστήρ astḗr, as-tare'; probably from the base of G4766; a star (as strown over the sky),
 literally or figuratively:—star.

G793.definition:
ἀστήρικτος astḗriktos, as-tay'-rik-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4741; 
 unfixed, i.e. (figuratively) vacillating:—unstable.

G794.definition:
ἄστοργος ástorgos, as'-tor-gos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of
 στέργω stérgō (to cherish affectionately); hard-hearted towards
 kindred:—without natural affection.

G796.definition: ἀστραπή astrapḗ, as-trap-ay'; from G797; lightning; by analogy, glare:—lightning, bright shining.

G797.definition: ἀστράπτω astráptō, as-trap'-to; probably from G792; to flash as lightning:—lighten, shine.

G798.definition:
ἄστρον ástron, as'-tron; neuter from G792; properly, a constellation; put for a single star
 (natural or artificial):—star.

G799.definition:
Ἀσύγκριτος Asýnkritos, as-oong'-kree-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4793; 
 incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian:—Asyncritos.

G8.definition: †Ἀβιαθάρ Abiathár, ab-ee-ath'-ar; of Hebrew origin (H54); Abiathar, an Israelite:—Abiathar.

G80.definition:
ἀδελφός adelphós, ad-el-fos'; from G1 (as a connective particle) and δελφύς delphýs (the womb); a brother
 (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like G1):—brother.

G800.definition:
ἀσύμφωνος asýmphōnos, as-oom'-fo-nos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G4859; inharmonious
 (figuratively):—agree not.

G801.definition:
ἀσύνετος asýnetos, as-oon'-ay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G4908; unintelligent; by
 implication, wicked:—foolish, without understanding.

G802.definition:
ἀσύνθετος asýnthetos, as-oon'-thet-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4934; properly,
 not agreed, i.e. treacherous to compacts:—covenant-breaker.

G803.definition: ἀσφάλεια aspháleia, as-fal'-i-ah; from G804; security (literally or figuratively):—certainty, safety.

G804.definition:
ἀσφαλής asphalḗs, as-fal-ace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail"); secure
 (literally or figuratively):—certain(-ty), safe, sure.

G805.definition: ἀσφαλίζω asphalízō, as-fal-id'-zo; from G804; to render secure:—make fast (sure).

G806.definition:
ἀσφαλῶς asphalōs, as-fal-oce'; adverb from G804; securely (literally or figuratively):—assuredly,
 safely.

G807.definition:
ἀσχημονέω aschēmonéō, as-kay-mon-eh'-o; from G809; to be (i.e. act) unbecoming:—behave self uncomely
 (unseemly).

G808.definition:
ἀσχημοσύνη aschēmosýnē, as-kay-mos-oo'-nay; from G809; an indecency; by implication, the pudenda:—shame, that
 which is unseemly.

G809.definition:
ἀσχήμων aschḗmōn, as-kay'-mone; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2192 (in
 the sense of its congener G4976); properly, shapeless, i.e.
 (figuratively) inelegant:—uncomely.

G81.definition:
ἀδελφότης adelphótēs, ad-el-fot'-ace; from G80; brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e.
 the (Christian) fraternity:—brethren, brotherhood.

G810.definition:
ἀσωτία asōtía, as-o-tee'-ah; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed
 derivative of G4982; properly, unsavedness, i.e. (by implication)
 profligacy:—excess, riot.

G811.definition: ἀσώτως asṓtōs, as-o'-toce; adverb from the same as G810; dissolutely:—riotous.

G812.definition: ἀτακτέω ataktéō, at-ak-teh'-o; from G813; to be (i.e. act) irregular:—behave self disorderly.

G813.definition:
ἄτακτος átaktos, at'-ak-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5021; unarranged,
 i.e. (by implication) insubordinate (religiously):—unruly.

G814.definition: ἀτάκτως atáktōs, at-ak'-toce; adverb from G813, irregularly (morally):—disorderly.

G815.definition:
ἄτεκνος áteknos, at'-ek-nos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5043; childless:—childless,
 without children.

G817.definition:
ἄτερ áter, at'-er; a particle probably akin to G427; aloof, i.e. apart from (literally or
 figuratively):—in the absence of, without.

G818.definition:
ἀτιμάζω atimázō, at-im-ad'-zo; from G820; to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or
 maltreat:—despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully.

G819.definition:
ἀτιμία atimía, at-ee-mee'-ah; from G820; infamy, i.e. (subjectively) comparative indignity,
 (objectively) disgrace:—dishonour, reproach, shame, vile.

G82.definition:
ἄδηλος ádēlos, ad'-ay-los; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1212; hidden, figuratively,
 indistinct:—appear not, uncertain.

G820.definition:
ἄτιμος átimos, at'-ee-mos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5092; (negatively) unhonoured or
 (positively) dishonoured:—despised, without honour, less honourable
 (comparative degree).

G821.definition: †ἀτιμόω atimóō, at-ee-mo'-o; from G820; used like G818, to maltreat:—handle shamefully.

G822.definition: ἀτμίς atmís, at-mece'; from the same as G109; mist:—vapour.

G823.definition:
ἄτομος átomos, at'-om-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G5114; uncut, i.e. (by
 implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time):—moment.

G824.definition:
ἄτοπος átopos, at'-op-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5117; out of place, i.e.
 (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked:—amiss, harm,
 unreasonable.

G825.definition:
Ἀττάλεια Attáleia, at-tal'-i-ah; from Ἄτταλος Áttalos (a king of Pergamus); Attaleia, a place in
 Pamphylia:—Attalia.

G826.definition: αὐγάζω augázō, ow-gad'-zo; from G827; to beam forth (figuratively):—shine.

G827.definition:
αὐγή augḗ, owg'-ay; of uncertain derivation; a ray of light, i.e. (by implication)
 radiance, dawn:—break of day.

G828.definition:
Αὔγουστος Augoûstos, ow'-goos-tos; from Latin ("august"); Augustus, a title of the Roman
 emperor:—Augustus.

G829.definition:
αὐθάδης authádēs, ow-thad'-ace; from G846 and the base of G2237; self-pleasing, i.e.
 arrogant:—self-willed.

G83.definition: ἀδηλότης adēlótēs, ad-ay-lot'-ace; from G82; uncertainty:—X uncertain.

G830.definition:
αὐθαίρετος authaíretos, ow-thah'-ee-ret-os; from G846 and the same as G140; self-chosen, i.e. (by implication)
 voluntary:—of own accord, willing of self.

G831.definition:
αὐθεντέω authentéō, ow-then-teh'-o; from a compound of G846 and an obsolete ἕντης héntēs (a worker); to act of
 oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate:—usurp authority over.

G832.definition: αὐλέω auléō, ow-leh'-o; from G836; to play the flute:—pipe.

G833.definition:
αὐλή aulḗ, ow-lay'; from the same as G109; a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a
 mansion:—court, (sheep-)fold, hall, palace.

G834.definition: αὐλητής aulētḗs, ow-lay-tace'; from G832; a flute-player:—minstrel, piper.

G835.definition:
αὐλίζομαι aulízomai, ow-lid'-zom-ahee; middle voice from G833; to pass the night (properly, in the open
 air):—abide, lodge.

G836.definition: αὐλός aulós, ow-los'; from the same as G109; a flute (as blown):—pipe.

G837.definition:
αὐξάνω auxánō, owx-an'-o; a prolonged form of a primary verb; to grow ("wax"), i.e. enlarge
 (literal or figurative, active or passive):—grow (up), (give the)
 increase.

G838.definition: αὔξησις aúxēsis, owx'-ay-sis; from G837; growth:—increase.

G839.definition:
αὔριον aúrion, ow'-ree-on; from a derivative of the same as G109 (meaning a breeze, i.e. the
 morning air); properly, fresh, i.e. (adverb with ellipsis of G2250)
 to-morrow:—(to-)morrow, next day.

G84.definition: ἀδήλως adḗlōs, ad-ay'-loce; adverb from G82; uncertainly:—uncertainly.

G840.definition:
αὐστηρός austērós, ow-stay-ros'; from a (presumed) derivative of the same as G109 (meaning blown); rough
 (properly as a gale), i.e. (figuratively) severe:—austere.

G841.definition:
αὐτάρκεια autárkeia, ow-tar'-ki-ah; from G842; self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or
 (concretely) a competence:—contentment, sufficiency.

G842.definition: αὐτάρκης autárkēs, ow-tar'-kace; from G846 and G714; self-complacent, i.e. contented:—content.

G843.definition: αὐτοκατάκριτος autokatákritos, ow-tok-at-ak'-ree-tos; from G846 and a derivative or G2632; self-condemned:—condemned of self.

G844.definition:
αὐτόματος autómatos, ow-tom'-at-os; from G846 and the same as G3155; self-moved ("automatic"), i.e.
 spontaneous:—of own accord, of self.

G845.definition: αὐτόπτης autóptēs, ow-top'-tace; from G846 and G3700; self-seeing, i.e. an eye-witness:—eye-witness.

G846.definition:
αὐτός autós, ow-tos'; from the particle αὖ aû (perhaps akin to the base of G109 through the idea
 of a baffling wind) (backward); the reflexive pronoun self, used
 (alone or in the comparative G1438) of the third person , and (with the
 proper personal pronoun) of the other persons:—her, it(-self), one,
 the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy-
 )self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at,
 - by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they, (these) things, this (man),
 those, together, very, which. Compare G848.

G848.definition:
αὑτοῦ hautoû, how-too'; contracted for G1438; self (in some oblique case or reflexively,
 relation):—her (own), (of) him(-self), his (own), of it, thee, their
 (own), them(-selves), they.

G849.definition:
αὐτόχειρ autócheir, ow-tokh'-ire; from G846 and G5495; self-handed, i.e. doing personally:—with … own
 hands.

G85.definition:
ἀδημονέω adēmonéō, ad-ay-mon-eh'-o; from a derivative of ἀδέω adéō (to be sated to loathing); to be in distress
 (of mind):—be full of heaviness, be very heavy.

G850.definition:
αὐχμηρός auchmērós, owkh-may-ros'; from αὐχμός auchmós (probably from a base akin to that of G109) (dust, as
 dried by wind); properly, dirty, i.e. (by implication) obscure:—dark.

G851.definition:
ἀφαιρέω aphairéō, af-ahee-reh'-o; from G575 and G138; to remove (literally or figuratively):—cut (smite)
 off, take away.

G852.definition:
ἀφανής aphanḗs, af-an-ace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5316; non-apparent):—that is not
 manifest.

G853.definition:
ἀφανίζω aphanízō, af-an-id'-zo; from G852; to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or
 (passively) disappear (be destroyed):—corrupt, disfigure, perish,
 vanish away.

G854.definition: ἀφανισμός aphanismós, af-an-is-mos'; from G853; disappearance, i.e. (figuratively) abrogation:—vanish away.

G855.definition:
ἄφαντος áphantos, af'-an-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5316; 
 non-manifested, i.e. invisible:—vanished out of sight.

G856.definition:
ἀφεδρών aphedrṓn, af-ed-rone'; from a compound of G575 and the base of G1476; a place of sitting apart,
 i.e. a privy:—draught.

G857.definition:
ἀφειδία apheidía, af-i-dee'-ah; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and G5339; unsparingness,
 i.e. austerity (asceticism):—neglecting.

G858.definition:
ἀφελότης aphelótēs, af-el-ot'-ace; from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and φέλλος phéllos (in the
 sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); smoothness, i.e.
 (figuratively) simplicity:—singleness.

G859.definition:
ἄφεσις áphesis, af'-es-is; from G863; freedom; (figuratively) pardon:—deliverance, forgiveness,
 liberty, remission.

G86.definition:
†ᾅδης háidēs, hah'-dace; from G1 (as negative particle) and G1492; properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades"
 or the place (state) of departed souls:—grave, hell.

G860.definition: ἁφή haphḗ, haf-ay'; from G680; probably a ligament (as fastening):—joint.

G861.definition:
ἀφθαρσία aphtharsía, af-thar-see'-ah; from G862; incorruptibility; genitive, unending existence;
 (figuratively) genuineness:—immortality, incorruption, sincerity.

G862.definition:
ἄφθαρτος áphthartos, af'-thar-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5351; undecaying
 (in essence or continuance):—not (in-, un-)corruptible, immortal.

G863.definition:
ἀφίημι aphíēmi, af-ee'-ay-mee; from G575 and ἵημι híēmi (to send; an intensive form of εἶμι eîmi, to go); to
 send forth, in various applications (as follow):—cry, forgive,
 forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send)
 away, remit, suffer, yield up.

G864.definition:
ἀφικνέομαι aphiknéomai, af-ik-neh'-om-ahee; from G575 and the base of G2425; to go (i.e. spread) forth (by
 rumor):—come abroad.

G865.definition:
ἀφιλάγαθος aphilágathos, af-il-ag'-ath-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5358; hostile to virtue:—despiser
 of those that are good.

G866.definition:
ἀφιλάργυρος aphilárgyros, af-il-ar'-goo-ros; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5366; unavaricious:—without
 covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre.

G867.definition:
ἄφιξις áphixis, af'-ix-is; from G864; properly, arrival, i.e. (by implication)
 departure:—departing.

G869.definition: ἄφνω áphnō, af'-no; adverb from G852 (contraction); unawares, i.e. unexpectedly:—suddenly.

G87.definition:
ἀδιάκριτος adiákritos, ad-ee-ak'-ree-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1252; properly,
 undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial:—without partiality.

G870.definition:
ἀφόβως aphóbōs, af-ob'-oce; adverb from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and G5401; 
 fearlessly:—without fear.

G871.definition: ἀφομοιόω aphomoióō, af-om-oy-o'-o; from G575 and G3666; to assimilate closely:—make like.

G872.definition: ἀφοράω aphoráō, af-or-ah'-o; from G575 and G3708; to consider attentively:—look.

G873.definition:
ἀφορίζω aphorízō, af-or-id'-zo; from G575 and G3724; to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit,
 exclude, appoint, etc.:—divide, separate, sever.

G874.definition:
ἀφορμή aphormḗ, af-or-may'; from a compound of G575 and G3729; a starting-point, i.e. (figuratively)
 an opportunity:—occasion.

G875.definition: ἀφρίζω aphrízō, af-rid'-zo; from G876; to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy):—foam.

G876.definition: ἀφρός aphrós, af-ros'; apparently a primary word; froth, i.e. slaver:—foaming.

G877.definition:
ἀφροσύνη aphrosýnē, af-ros-oo'-nay; from G878; senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally)
 recklessness:—folly, foolishly(-ness).

G878.definition:
ἄφρων áphrōn, af'-rone; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5424; properly, mindless, i.e.
 stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic,
 (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving:—fool(-ish), unwise.

G879.definition:
ἀφυπνόω aphypnóō, af-oop-no'-o; from a compound of G575 and G5258; properly, to become awake, i.e. (by
 implication) to drop (off) in slumber:—fall asleep.

G88.definition:
ἀδιάλειπτος adiáleiptos, ad-ee-al'-ipe-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G1223
 and G3007; unintermitted, i.e. permanent:—without ceasing, continual.

G880.definition:
ἄφωνος áphōnos, af'-o-nos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5456; voiceless, i.e. mute (by
 nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning:—dumb, without
 signification.

G881.definition: †Ἀχάζ Acház, akh-adz'; of Hebrew origin (H271); Achaz, an Israelite:—Achaz.

G882.definition:
Ἀχαΐα Achaḯa, ach-ah-ee'-ah; of uncertain derivation; Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of
 Europe:—Achaia.

G883.definition: Ἀχαϊκός Achaïkós, ach-ah-ee-kos'; from G882; an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian:—Achaicus.

G884.definition:
ἀχάριστος acháristos, ach-ar'-is-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5483; 
 thankless, i.e. ungrateful:—unthankful.

G885.definition: †Ἀχείμ Acheím, akh-ime'; probably of Hebrew origin (compare H3137); Achim, an Israelite:—Achim.

G886.definition:
ἀχειροποίητος acheiropoíētos, akh-i-rop-oy'-ay-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5499; unmanufactured, i.e.
 inartificial:—made without (not made with) hands.

G887.definition:
ἀχλύς achlýs, akh-looce'; of uncertain derivation; dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a
 cataract:—mist.

G888.definition:
ἀχρεῖος achreîos, akh-ri'-os; from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5534 (compare
 G5532); useless, i.e. (euphemistically) unmeritorious:—unprofitable.

G889.definition: ἀχρειόω achreióō, akh-ri-o'-o; from G888; to render useless, i.e. spoil:—become unprofitable.

G89.definition:
ἀδιαλείπτως adialeíptōs, ad-ee-al-ipe'-toce; adverb from G88; uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an
 appropriate occasion):—without ceasing.

G890.definition:
ἄχρηστος áchrēstos, akh'-race-tos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5543; inefficient, i.e. (by
 implication) detrimental:—unprofitable.

G891.definition:
ἄχρι áchri, akh'-ree; akin to G206 (through the idea of a terminus); (of
 time) until or (of place) up to:—as far as, for, in(-to), till,
 (even, un-)to, until, while. Compare G3360.

G892.definition:
ἄχυρον áchyron, akh'-oo-ron; perhaps remotely from χέω chéō (to shed forth); chaff (as
 diffusive):—chaff.

G893.definition: ἀψευδής apseudḗs, aps-yoo-dace'; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5579; veracious:—that cannot lie.

G894.definition:
ἄψινθος ápsinthos, ap'-sin-thos; of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e.
 (figuratively) calamity):—wormwood.

G895.definition:
ἄψυχος ápsychos, ap'-soo-khos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5590; lifeless, i.e. inanimate
 (mechanical):—without life.

G896.definition:
Βάαλ Báal, bah'-al; of Hebrew origin (H1168); Baal, a Phœnician deity (used as a symbol of
 idolatry):—Baal.

G897.definition:
Βαβυλών Babylṓn, bab-oo-lone'; of Hebrew origin (H894); Babylon, the capitol of Chaldæa (literally or
 figuratively (as a type of tyranny)):—Babylon.

G898.definition:
βαθμός bathmós, bath-mos'; from the same as G899; a step, i.e. (figuratively) grade (of
 dignity):—degree.

G899.definition:
βάθος báthos, bath'-os; from the same as G901; profundity, i.e. (by implication) extent;
 (figuratively) mystery:—deep(-ness, things), depth.

G9.definition: Ἀβιληνή Abilēnḗ, ab-ee-lay-nay'; of foreign origin (compare H58); Abilene, a region of Syria:—Abilene.

G900.definition: βαθύνω bathýnō, bath-oo'-no; from G901; to deepen:—deep.

G901.definition:
βαθύς bathýs, bath-oos'; from the base of G939; profound (as going down), literally or
 figuratively:—deep, very early.

G902.definition:
βαΐον baḯon, bah-ee'-on; a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of G939; a palm twig
 (as going out far):—branch.

G903.definition:
Βαλαάμ Balaám, bal-ah-am'; of Hebrew origin (H1109); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false
 teacher):—Balaam.

G904.definition: Βαλάκ Balák, bal-ak'; of Hebrew origin (H1111); Balak, a Moabite:—Balac.

G905.definition:
†βαλάντιον balántion, bal-an'-tee-on; probably remotely from G906 (as a depository); a pouch (for
 money):—bag, purse.

G906.definition:
†βάλλω bállō, bal'-lo; a primary verb; to throw (in various applications, more or less
 violent or intense):—arise, cast (out), × dung, lay, lie, pour, put
 (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust. Compare G4496.

G907.definition:
βαπτίζω baptízō, bap-tid'-zo; from a derivative of G911; to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e.
 fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution,
 especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian
 baptism:—Baptist, baptize, wash.

G908.definition: βάπτισμα báptisma, bap'-tis-mah; from G907; baptism (technically or figuratively):—baptism.

G909.definition: βαπτισμός baptismós, bap-tis-mos'; from G907; ablution (ceremonial or Christian):—baptism, washing.

G91.definition:
ἀδικέω adikéō, ad-ee-keh'-o; from G94; to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or
 physically):—hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer,
 take) wrong.

G910.definition: Βαπτιστής Baptistḗs, bap-tis-tace'; from G907; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner:—Baptist.

G911.definition:
βάπτω báptō, bap'-to; a primary verb; to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New
 Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to
 moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as
 with dye):—dip.

G912.definition:
Βαραββᾶς Barabbâs, bar-ab-bas'; of Chaldee origin (H1347 and H5); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an
 Israelite:—Barabbas.

G913.definition: Βαράκ Barák, bar-ak'; of Hebrew origin (H1301); Barak, an Israelite:—Barak.

G914.definition:
Βαραχίας Barachías, bar-akh-ee'-as; of Hebrew origin (H1296); Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an
 Israelite:—Barachias.

G915.definition:
βάρβαρος bárbaros, bar'-bar-os; of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (i.e.
 non-Greek):—barbarian(-rous).

G916.definition: †βαρέω baréō, bar-eh'-o; from G926; to weigh down (figuratively):—burden, charge, heavy, press.

G917.definition: βαρέως baréōs, bar-eh'-oce; adverb from G926; heavily (figuratively):—dull.

G918.definition:
Βαρθολομαῖος Bartholomaîos, bar-thol-om-ah'-yos; of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H8526); son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomæus, a
 Christian apostle:—Bartholomeus.

G919.definition:
Βαριησοῦς Bariēsoûs, bar-ee-ay-sooce'; of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H3091); son of Jesus (or Joshua);
 Bar-jesus, an Israelite:—Barjesus.

G92.definition: ἀδίκημα adíkēma, ad-eek'-ay-mah; from G91; a wrong done:—evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong.

G920.definition:
†Βαριωνᾶς Bariōnâs, bar-ee-oo-nas'; of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H3124); son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas,
 an Israelite:—Bar-jona.

G921.definition:
Βαρνάβας Barnábas, bar-nab'-as; of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H5029); son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy);
 Barnabas, an Israelite:—Barnabas.

G923.definition:
Βαρσαβᾶς Barsabâs, bar-sab-as'; of Chaldee origin (H1247 and probably H6634); son of Sabas (or Tsaba);
 Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites:—Barsabas.

G924.definition:
Βαρτιμαῖος Bartimaîos, bar-tim-ah'-yos; of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H2931); son of Timæus (or the unclean);
 Bar-timæus, an Israelite:—Bartimæus.

G926.definition:
βαρύς barýs, bar-ooce'; from the same as G922; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome,
 grave:—grievous, heavy, weightier.

G927.definition: βαρύτιμος barýtimos, bar-oo'-tim-os; from G926 and G5092; highly valuable:—very precious.

G928.definition: βασανίζω basanízō, bas-an-id'-zo; from G931; to torture:—pain, toil, torment, toss, vex.

G929.definition: βασανισμός basanismós, bas-an-is-mos'; from G928; torture:—torment.

G93.definition:
ἀδικία adikía, ad-ee-kee'-ah; from G94; (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the
 act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act):—iniquity,
 unjust, unrighteousness, wrong.

G930.definition: βασανιστής basanistḗs, bas-an-is-tace'; from G928; a torturer:—tormentor.

G931.definition:
βάσανος básanos, bas'-an-os; perhaps remotely from the same as G939 (through the notion of going to
 the bottom); a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture:—torment.

G932.definition:
βασιλεία basileía, bas-il-i'-ah; from G935; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a
 realm (literally or figuratively):—kingdom,
 + reign.

G934.definition: βασίλειος basíleios, bas-il'-i-os; from G935; kingly (in nature):—royal.

G935.definition:
βασιλεύς basileús, bas-il-yooce'; probably from G939 (through the notion of a foundation of power); a
 sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively):—king.

G936.definition: βασιλεύω basileúō, bas-il-yoo'-o; from G935; to rule (literally or figuratively):—king, reign.

G937.definition:
βασιλικός basilikós, bas-il-ee-kos'; from G935; regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or
 befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or
 (figuratively) preeminent:—king's, nobleman, royal.

G938.definition: βασίλισσα basílissa, bas-il'-is-sah; feminine from G936; a queen:—queen.

G939.definition:
βάσις básis, bas'-ece; from βαίνω baínō (to walk); a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the
 foot:—foot.

G94.definition:
ἄδικος ádikos, ad'-ee-kos; from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1349; unjust; by extension wicked;
 by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen:—unjust, unrighteous.

G940.definition:
βασκαίνω baskaínō, bas-kah'-ee-no; akin to G5335; to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false
 representations):—bewitch.

G941.definition:
βαστάζω bastázō, bas-tad'-zo; perhaps remotely derived from the base of G939 (through the idea of
 removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare,
 sustain, receive, etc.):—bear, carry, take up.

G942.definition: βάτος bátos, bat'-os; of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub:—bramble, bush.

G944.definition: βάτραχος bátrachos, bat'-rakh-os; of uncertain derivation; a frog:—frog.

G945.definition:
βαττολογέω battologéō, bat-tol-og-eh'-o; from Βάττος Báttos (a proverbial stammerer) and G3056; to stutter, i.e. (by
 implication) to prate tediously:—use vain repetitions.

G946.definition: βδέλυγμα bdélygma, bdel'-oog-mah; from G948; a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry:—abomination.

G947.definition: βδελυκτός bdelyktós, bdel-ook-tos'; from G948; detestable, i.e. (specially) idolatrous:—abominable.

G948.definition:
†βδελύσσω bdelýssō, bdel-oos'-so; from a (presumed) derivative of βδέω bdéō (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e.
 (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry):—abhor, abominable.

G949.definition:
βέβαιος bébaios, beb'-ah-yos; from the base of G939 (through the idea of basality); stable (literally
 or figuratively):—firm, of force, stedfast, sure.

G95.definition: ἀδίκως adíkōs, ad-ee'-koce; adverb from G94; unjustly:—wrongfully.

G950.definition: βεβαιόω bebaióō, beb-ah-yo'-o; from G949; to stabilitate (figuratively):—confirm, (e-)stablish.

G9501.definition:
†Α A, al'-fah; of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only
 (from its use as a numeral) the first:—Alpha. Often used (usually
 ἄν án, before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from G427) in
 the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter;
 occasionally in the sense of union (as a contraction of G260).

G951.definition: βεβαίωσις bebaíōsis, beb-ah'-yo-sis; from G950; stabiliment:—confirmation.

G952.definition:
βέβηλος bébēlos, beb'-ay-los; from the base of G939 and βηλός bēlós (a threshold); accessible (as by
 crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions)
 heathenish, wicked:—profane (person).

G953.definition: βεβηλόω bebēlóō, beb-ay-lo'-o; from G952; to desecrate:—profane.

G954.definition:
†Βεελζεβούλ Beelzeboúl, beh-el-zeb-ool'; of Chaldee origin (by parody on H1176); dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of
 Satan:—Beelzebub.

G955.definition:
Βελίαλ Belíal, bel-ee'-al; of Hebrew origin (H1100); worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of
 Satan:—Belial.

G956.definition: βέλος bélos, bel'-os; from G906; a missile, i.e. spear or arrow:—dart.

G957.definition:
†βελτίον beltíon, bel-tee'-on; neuter of a compound of a derivative of G906 (used for the comparative
 of G18); better:—very well.

G958.definition: Βενιαμίν Beniamín, ben-ee-am-een'; of Hebrew origin (H1144); Benjamin, an Israelite:—Benjamin.

G959.definition:
Βερνίκη Berníkē, ber-nee'-kay; from a provincial form of G5342 and G3529; victorious; Bernice, a member
 of the Herodian family:—Bernice.

G960.definition:
Βέροια Béroia, ber'-oy-ah; perhaps a provincial from a derivative of G4008 (Perœa, i.e. the
 region beyond the coast-line); Berœa, a place in Macedonia:—Berea.

G961.definition: Βεροιαῖος Beroiaîos, ber-oy-ah'-yos; from G960; a Berœoean or native of Berœa:—of Berea.

G963.definition:
Βηθανία Bēthanía, bay-than-ee'-ah; of Chaldee origin; date-house; Beth-any, a place in
 Palestine:—Bethany.

G964.definition:
†Βηθεσδά Bēthesdá, bay-thes-dah'; of Chaldee origin (compare H1004 and H2617); house of kindness;
 Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem:—Bethesda.

G965.definition:
†Βηθλεέμ Bēthleém, bayth-leh-em'; of Hebrew origin (H1036); Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in
 Palestine:—Bethlehem.

G966.definition:
Βηθσαϊδά Bēthsaïdá, bayth-sahee-dah'; of Chaldee origin (compare H1004 and H6719); fishing-house; Bethsaida, a
 place in Palestine:—Bethsaida.

G967.definition:
†Βηθφαγή Bēthphagḗ, bayth-fag-ay'; of Chaldee origin (compare H1004 and H6291); fig-house; Beth-phage, a
 place in Palestine:—Bethphage.

G968.definition:
βῆμα bēma, bay'-ma; from the base of G939; a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a
 rostrum, i.e. a tribunal:—judgment-seat, set (foot) on, throne.

G969.definition: βήρυλλος bḗryllos, bay'-rool-los; of uncertain derivation; a "beryl":—beryl.

G97.definition:
ἄδολος ádolos, ad'-ol-os; from G1 (as a negative particle); and G1388; undeceitful, i.e.
 (figuratively) unadulterated:—sincere.

G970.definition:
βία bía, bee'-ah; probably akin to G979 (through the idea of vital activity); 
 force:—violence.

G971.definition:
βιάζω biázō, bee-ad'-zo; from G979; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or
 (passively) to be seized:—press, suffer violence.

G972.definition: βίαιος bíaios, bee'-ah-yos; from G970; violent:—mighty.

G973.definition: βιαστής biastḗs, bee-as-tace'; from G971; a forcer, i.e. (figuratively) energetic:—violent.

G974.definition: βιβλιαρίδιον bibliarídion, bib-lee-ar-id'-ee-on; a diminutive of G975; a booklet:—little book.

G975.definition: βιβλίον biblíon, bib-lee'-on; a diminutive of G976; a roll:—bill, book, scroll, writing.

G976.definition:
βίβλος bíblos, bib'-los; properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a
 sheet or scroll of writing:—book.

G977.definition:
βιβρώσκω bibrṓskō, bib-ro'-sko; a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps
 causative of G1006); to eat:—eat.

G978.definition: Βιθυνία Bithynía, bee-thoo-nee'-ah; of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia:—Bithynia.

G979.definition:
βίος bíos, bee'-os; a primary word; life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence;
 by implication, the means of livelihood:—good, life, living.

G98.definition:
Ἀδραμυττηνός Adramyttēnós, ad-ram-oot-tay-nos'; from Ἀδραμύττειον Adramýtteion (a place in Asia Minor); Adramyttene or belonging to
 Adramyttium:—of Adramyttium.

G980.definition: βιόω bióō, bee-o'-o; from G979; to spend existence:—live.

G981.definition:
βίωσις bíōsis, bee'-o-sis; from G980; living (properly, the act, by implication, the
 mode):—manner of life.

G982.definition:
βιωτικός biōtikós, bee-o-tee-kos'; from a derivative of G980; relating to the present existence:—of
 (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life.

G983.definition: βλαβερός blaberós, blab-er-os'; from G984; injurious:—hurtful.

G984.definition:
βλάπτω bláptō, blap'-to; a primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to
 injure:—hurt.

G985.definition:
βλαστάνω blastánō, blas-tan'-o; from βλαστός blastós (a sprout); to germinate; by implication, to yield
 fruit:—bring forth, bud, spring (up).

G986.definition:
Βλάστος Blástos, blas'-tos; perhaps the same as the base of G985; Blastus, an officer of Herod
 Agrippa:—Blastus.

G987.definition:
†βλασφημέω blasphēméō, blas-fay-meh'-o; from G989; to vilify; specially, to speak impiously:—(speak)
 blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil.

G988.definition:
βλασφημία blasphēmía, blas-fay-me'-ah; from G989; vilification (especially against God):—blasphemy, evil
 speaking, railing.

G989.definition:
βλάσφημος blásphēmos, blas'-fay-mos; from a derivative of G984 and G5345; scurrilious, i.e. calumnious
 (against men), or (specially) impious (against
 God):—blasphemer(-mous), railing.

G99.definition:
Ἀδρίας Adrías, ad-ree'-as; from Ἀδρία Adría (a place near its shore); the Adriatic sea (including the
 Ionian):—Adria.

G990.definition:
βλέμμα blémma, blem'-mah; from G991; vision (properly concrete; by implication,
 abstract):—seeing.

G991.definition:
βλέπω blépō, blep'-o; a primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively):—behold,
 beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed. 
 Compare G3700.

G992.definition: βλητέος blētéos, blay-teh'-os; from G906; fit to be cast (i.e. applied):—must be put.

G993.definition:
Βοανεργές Boanergés, bo-an-erg-es'; of Chaldee origin (H1123 and H7266); sons of commotion; Boanerges, an
 epithet of two of the apostles:—Boanerges.

G994.definition:
βοάω boáō, bo-ah'-o; apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; to halloo, i.e. shout
 (for help or in a tumultuous way):—cry.

G995.definition: βοή boḗ, bo-ay'; from G994; a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.):—cry.

G996.definition:
βοήθεια boḗtheia, bo-ay'-thi-ah; from G998; aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a
 vessel:—help.

G997.definition: βοηθέω boēthéō, bo-ay-theh'-o; from G998; to aid or relieve:—help, succor.

G998.definition: βοηθός boēthós, bo-ay-thos'; from G995 and theo (to run); a succorer:—helper.

G999.definition:
βόθυνος bóthynos, both'-oo-nos; akin to G900; a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern:—ditch,
 pit.

G5125.definition: to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things). such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those

G2448.definition: Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine. Judah

G4833.definition: to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate. make conformable unto

G2700.definition: to shoot down with an arrow or other missile. thrust through

G2743.definition: to brand ("cauterize"), i.e. (by implication) to render unsensitive (figuratively). sear with a hot iron

G3176.definition: greatest or very great. exceeding great

G4481.definition: Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol. Remphan

G3836.definition: from all directions. from every quarter

G2544.definition: and yet indeed, i.e. although really. nevertheless, though

G680.definition: properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. to touch (in many implied relations). touch

G5024.definition: in the same way. even thus, (manner) like, so

G3166.definition: akin to G837 (αὐξάνω) and G2744 (καυχάομαι)); to talk big, i.e. be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic). boast great things

G2045.definition: to seek, i.e. (figuratively) to investigate. search

G4894.definition: to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of. consider, know, be privy, be ware of

G471.definition: to refute or deny. gainsay, say against

G1888.definition: in theft itself, i.e. (by analogy) in actual crime. in the very act

G5414.definition: something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship. lading

G3363.definition: in order (or so) that not. albeit not, lest, that, no(-t, (-thing))

G4412.definition: firstly (in time, place, order, or importance). before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all)

G2568.definition: Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete. fair havens

G3818.definition: Pacatianian, a section of Phrygia. Pacatiana

G4252.definition: Priscilla (i.e. little Prisca), a Christian woman. Priscilla

G3063.definition: something remaining (adverbially). besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then

G1068.definition: oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem. Gethsemane

G2276.definition: worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb). less, worse

G3386.definition: not at all then, i.e. not to say (the rather still). how much more

G729.definition: unsewed, i.e. of a single piece. without seam

G2802.definition: Claude, an island near Crete. Clauda

G5129.definition: to (in, with or by) this (person or thing). here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this

G3603.definition: which is. called, which is (make), that is (to say)

G1548.definition: the same as 1547. give in marriage

G5410.definition: a forum or market-place; only in comparative with G675 (Ἄππιος); a station on the Appian road. forum

G4118.definition: the largest number or very large. very great, most

G5104.definition: an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth. (used only with other particles in the comparative, as G2544 (καίτοιγε), G3305 (μέντοι), G5105 (τοιγαροῦν), G5106 (τοίνυν), etc

G3158.definition: Matthat (i.e. Mattithjah), the name of two Israelites. Mathat

G4671.definition: to thee. thee, thine own, thou, thy

G4555.definition: sardine (G3037 (λίθος) being implied), i.e. a gem, so called. sardine

G1547.definition: to marry off a daughter. give in marriage

G3755.definition: during which same time, i.e. whilst. whiles

G5130.definition: of (from or concerning) these (persons or things). such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those

G1749.definition: an ambush, i.e. (figuratively) murderous design. lying in wait

G2148.definition: a storm from the East (or southeast), i.e. (in modern phrase) a Levanter. Euroklydon

G730.definition: male (as stronger for lifting). male, man

G3505.definition: Neron (i.e. Nero), a Roman emperor. Nero

G2781.definition: a cell for honey, i.e. (collectively) the comb. (honey-)comb

G4280.definition: used as alternate of G4277 (προέπω); to say already, predict. foretell, say (speak, tell) before

G2534.definition: and at least (or even, indeed). and, at least

G1181.definition: a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically) tithe. tenth (part), tithe

G4388.definition: to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine). purpose, set forth

G5522.definition: a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt. dust

G1489.definition: if indeed, seeing that, unless, (with negative) otherwise. if (so be that, yet)

G1221.definition: a particle of generalization; indeed, at any time. (what-)soever

G4839.definition: to remain in company, i.e. still live. continue with

G3496.definition: new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia. Neapolis

G445.definition: to act as proconsul. be the deputy

G3378.definition: as interrogative and negative, is it not that?. neither (followed by no), + never, not

G4708.definition: more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise. more carefully

G5182.definition: akin to G2351 (θόρυβος)); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb. trouble

G5026.definition: (towards or of) this. her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same)

G1573.definition: to be (bad or) weak, i.e. (by implication) to fail (in heart). faint, be weary

G508.definition: above the ground, i.e. (properly) the second floor of a building; used for a dome or a balcony on the upper story. upper room

G2581.definition: zealous; Cananites, an epithet. Canaanite (by mistake for a derivative from G5477 (Χαναάν))

G4900.definition: to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation). + set at one again

G1508.definition: if not. but, except (that), if not, more than, save (only) that, saving, till

G1827.definition: to convict fully, i.e. (by implication) to punish. convince

G1647.definition: far less. less than the least

G4746.definition: a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed. branch

G5224.definition: things extant or in hand, i.e. property or possessions. goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast

G5575.definition: a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony. false witness

G3801.transliteration: ho ṑn kaí ho ēn kaí ho erchómenos
G3801.definition: the one being and the one that was and the one coming, i.e. the Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ. which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be)

G1444.definition: Hebraic or the Jewish language. Hebrew

G2208.definition: a Zealot, i.e. (specially) partisan for Jewish political independence. Zelotes

G943.definition: a bath, or measure for liquids. measure

G5063.definition: of forty years of age. (+ full, of) forty years (old)

G3193.definition: relating to honey, i.e. bee (comb). honeycomb

G4696.definition: a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace. spot

G2640.definition: a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few. remnant

G5504.definition: "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto. yesterday

G4571.definition: thee. thee, thou, X thy house

G3478.definition: Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine. Nazareth

G1999.definition: a conspiracy, i.e. concourse (riotous or friendly). that which cometh upon, + raising up

G3872.definition: something put down alongside, i.e. a deposit (sacred trust). that (thing) which is committed (un-)to (trust)

G4332.definition: to sit near, i.e. attend as a servant. wait at

G1970.definition: to throttle upon, i.e. (figuratively) overgrow. choke

G4406.definition: dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season). early

G1513.definition: if somehow. if by any means

G2444.definition: for what reason ?, i.e. why?. wherefore, why

G2046.definition: an alternate for G2036 (ἔπω) in certain tenses; to utter, i.e. speak or say. call, say, speak (of), tell
